# Change requests

A change request is a PO-ordered change to something already **built and
signed**. It is not a defect (the product does what was agreed and the
agreement changed) and it is not an open question (nothing was undecided).
Both of those have their own registers — `10-defect-log.csv` and
`01-open-questions.md` — and putting a CR in either one loses the thing that
matters most about it: **which signed statement is being reversed, and why the
reversal is sound.**

Format: `CR-###` · what changed · what it reverses · the case · what moves ·
what it costs · **the version it landed in** · status. Every row cites the ruling
verbatim, because a paraphrase of a PO sentence is how the next agent rebuilds the
wrong thing.


---

## ➜ THE INDEX — every change request, and where its text lives

⚠ **PO RULING 2026-09-03: ONE FILE PER CHANGE REQUEST FROM HERE, AND THIS PAGE BECOMES THE INDEX.**
Verbatim: ***"one file per CR from here. `12-governance/change-requests/CR-068-customer-portal.md`,
with `11-change-requests.md` kept as the index — the CR number, its title, its status, and a link."***

**WHY, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED.** This file reached **2.5 MB and 30,491 lines across 80 change
requests** before the ruling. At that size GitHub refuses to render it in a browser; every lane that
touches any CR contends for the same file, which is the shared-file hazard hard-won law 11 exists for
and which tripped the register-deletion guard three times on 2026-09-03 alone; and `CR-068` by itself
is 815 lines. **A register that cannot be opened is not a register.**

**WHAT MOVED AND WHAT DID NOT.** `CR-001`–`CR-067` stay exactly where they are, in this file, at the
line they have always been at — **no citation anywhere in the repository breaks.** `CR-068` moved to
its own file, because it is the one being built from right now and the PO's ruling names it by path.
**Every CR from `CR-069` onward is written to `12-governance/change-requests/CR-###-<slug>.md` and
appears here only as a row.**

⚠ **THE STATUS COLUMN IS DELIBERATELY NOT FILLED FOR THE EIGHTY BELOW.** Filling it would mean
reading eighty CRs and judging each, and a status inferred from a heading is exactly what both source
documents this repository works from warn against in the same words: *"a status guessed from a change
log, or from a memory of having written something, is worse than no status at all."* **A row's status
is filled in when somebody reads that CR against the code.** Until then the row says where the text
is, which is what the index is for.

## CR-071 — What the customer portal must feel like, and the load it holds at

**Arrived** 2026-09-03, in two messages. First the requirement — *"there can be 500 users or 100 users
from various tulities using customer portal … it should not hamper performance of back office user"* —
and then, when told no agreed response time existed anywhere in the repository, the delegation:
*"Figure that out and write it as response time specifications"*.

**Classified a requirement, and urgent**, because `CR-068`'s first wave was being built the same hour.
It supersedes one line of B6's planning table (*"Concurrency: low (1–2 staff/tenant)"*) for the
platform while leaving it true of staff, adds `NFR-38`–`NFR-41`, and closes `OQ-CWP-1510`.

**The specification is `04-docs/05-modules/15-portal/11-response-times.md`** — ten targets by errand,
two rules that outrank them, five prohibitions, and how each is proved. ⚠ **Its figures are OURS by
delegation, not a PO ruling, and must never be cited as one.**

**Status: written, rules in force, no version of its own** — `CR-068`'s waves carry them.
| **CR-074** | *"Can we write a cr with phases to enable them?"* — turning the test suite on. Measured 2026-09-05 at `2.196.0`: **9,810 backend test functions, 367 front-end test files and 116 gates** run continuously, while the only two surfaces that exercise the product END TO END run not at all — **347 journey specifications** (prose; exactly one executable spec exists for all of them) and **54 browser walkthroughs** (~1,672 assertions, no runner, every CI workflow `.disabled`). Five walkthroughs run by hand that day found four faults invisible to all ~10,300 automated checks. **Five phases: 1–3 are days and give most of the value; 4 is a programme, and its estimate is stated honestly because the design forbids hand-typed expectations** | [`change-requests/CR-074-turning-the-test-suite-on.md`](change-requests/CR-074-turning-the-test-suite-on.md) |
| **CR-075** | *"I want you to read 3 documents from artifacts. and confirm whether you ahve all the etails to write details in 04 folder as new module; Runbook; also here please note each runbook details should be save in seperate folder or file so that later himan developer can edit them easily"* — **the Runbooks module.** One engine that walks a set of things, applies a utility's own declared process, and either reports what needs fixing or does the work — a dry run before anything happens and an audit row after everything does. **Two kinds, and the distinction is enforced rather than promised: a Check is constructed with no writer, so a write is unavailable rather than refused at runtime; an Action writes behind a dry run, a batch approval carrying the count, a cap that refuses rather than truncating, and a stop button.** 34 runbooks numbered 1–35 with no 7 (21 fully defined, 5 drafted, 8 named), **8 screens for all of them** because two are renderers over a runbook's definition and its report, 7 tables, 18 routes, 41 stories, 39 rules, 25 tests. Five phases, each ending with something a utility can open. ⚠ **THE ORDER WAS RE-CUT ON 2026-09-06 BY TWO FURTHER PO RULINGS** — *"once you have foundation I want to prioritise runbook related to integration first and then rest"*, then *"For me integration related to accounting, payment provider, emails, GIS are important - over other"*. **Every integration-driven runbook is an ACTION, and an Action cannot run before the acting half exists, so the acting half moved into the foundation as PHASE 2**: 1 the foundation, it can look (`A`–`E`) · 2 the foundation, it can act (`L` `M` `N`) · 3 the integration runbooks (`O` `P` `Q′` — runbooks 10, 14, 20, 22) · 4 prove it on their data and the scheduled Checks (`F`–`K`) · 5 the rest (`R′` `S` `T`). **Nothing is renumbered — no wave letter, no task id, no epic**; `Q′` and `R′` change contents only. **Phase 2 ships the dangerous half with sending switched OFF** and turns it on only after a full cycle in production, and **wave `M` — that cycle, with its written go/no-go — stays at full length between `L` and `N`, because it is now the whole safety argument.** The price, named rather than sold: **the coverage grid, the go-live and sales artefact, lands in phase 4 instead of phase 2.** The questions no longer all sit in phases 4 and 5 — **three moved to phase 2 and one to phase 4, because the waves they hang on moved and they came with it** — and not one of them blocks anything. ⚠ **TWO DEPENDENCIES ARE NOW URGENT AND ONE IS UNOWNED**: the audit actor (`BR-AUD-003` — a NULL actor means *a system job*) blocks phase 2 and through it 3 and 5; and **integrations emits neither `batch.landed` nor `feedback.landed` — zero occurrences in the backend, integrations' half under `BR-INT-054`, CR-069's work, scoped to nobody — without which phase 3 has no trigger.** ⚠ **AND ONE STATED ABSENCE SITS IN THE FIRST AREA THE PO NAMED: nothing builds the ACCOUNTING FILE's contents.** CR-069 wave `J` builds the envelope; runbook 9 is a Check that produces a tie-out, not an export; no port writes a file. **The card is not invented here and not dropped either.** Three PO rulings arrived with it and are in the decision log: the section is **called Runbooks, coined deliberately** against the market's own word *checklist*; screens are **`RBS-001`–`RBS-008`**, not `S147`–`S154`, which reverses this lane's own recommendation; and the 60,000–80,000 account figure is **an illustration, not a scope change** — the ICP stays at 40,000. ⚠ **Three errors were found inside the source documents and corrected as it was written:** the ports are **thirteen, not four**, and *raise a work item* is not one of them (it is an engine act, which is the only thing that lets a Check populate the work list while holding no writer); `BR-RBS-029` was used for two different rules; and the numeric error codes collide with the new screen series and become message keys. **Specification: `12-governance/change-requests/CR-075-runbooks-module.md`.** Module: `04-docs/05-modules/17-runbooks/`, with one file per runbook in `11-catalogue/` — the PO's own requirement — and 75 wireframes each paired with its build sheet. **Status: BUILDING. Phase 1 (`A`–`F`), phase 2's `L`/`M`, and phase 3's `P` and `Q′` have landed; version **2.215.0** carries `Q′` — runbooks 20 and 22. ⚠ **AND THAT SENTENCE WAS STALE AGAIN BY 2026-09-07, WHICH IS THE SECOND TIME AND THE REASON THE WARNING BELOW IS KEPT.** Waves `I`, `J`, `K`, `R′`, `S` and `T` have landed since, and on 2026-09-07 the FIRST TWO OF THE EIGHT *named only* cards were built as well — **runbook 28** (`US-RBS-043`, the Assets category's first, so that category stops being empty) and **runbook 33** (`US-RBS-044`), at version **2.218.0**, placed in the execution plan as wave `U`. **Six named-only cards remain: 29, 30, 31, 32, 34 and 35.** ⚠ **THIS LANE IS NAMING ONLY WHAT IT BUILT.** The waves listed above are read from their own execution-plan rows and the version numbers on their commits; a status line that claimed the whole change request on one lane's authority is how this sentence went stale the first time. ⚠ **THIS SENTENCE READ *"written 2026-09-06, nothing built"* UNTIL 2026-09-06 AND FIFTEEN WAVES HAD LANDED UNDER IT** — a status column nobody walked while every wave updated its own execution-plan row instead, which is the stale-body shape CLAUDE.md warns a lane will act on. Per-wave detail is in `04-docs/05-modules/17-runbooks/10-execution-plan.md` and the rulings are in the decision log.** |

**`CR-077`'s row is above. PARTS IS NOW BUILT — 2026-09-07, version `2.229.0`.** It is the
SEVENTH target of the one importer and not an importer of its own (`BR-MET-096`), the load
calls Work's own `apps/work/import_writer.py` through the `import_writer` seam kind — the
door `accounts` already uses — and nothing outside `apps/work` names the `parts` table, so
`G78` stays satisfied by construction. Five columns, seven stage-3 rules, a rollback branch,
and the sample file's headers all map themselves. Proved end to end on PostgreSQL and then
clicked: `10-scripts/cr083_integrations_and_parts_walkthrough.mjs`, 24 checks, and the
decision log of the same day carries the figures and the one thing the file could not carry.

**THE READS STARTERS ARE BUILT — 2026-09-08, version `2.231.0`.** `CR-077` is now complete.
The reads importer keeps its ONE published template (`BR-MET-032`): the header row and the
column mapping are identical for all four, and what differs is the worked ROWS.
`GET /reads/template?shape=flat|tou|demand|net` picks them, `read_import.READ_SHAPES`
declares them, and **the same address with no `shape` still serves the exact bytes it has
served since CR-038 W4** — the spec and the front end name `reads_template.csv`, and
changing what an unchanged address serves is how a bookmark starts lying. S28 offers four
buttons where it offered one: **Flat or tiered · Time of use · Demand · Net metering.**

**THE COUNT IS FOUR AND SEASONAL IS NOT A FIFTH**, which is the measurement `CR-077`'s row
already carried: flat AND tiered are one row (a tier is a bracket in the price list), time
of use is three registers on one date, demand is energy plus a peak row with the reset
noted only on the peak (`BR-MET-049`/`BR-MET-051`), and net metering is energy plus
`export` (`BR-AST-029`). A season is a property of the price list resolved from the date on
the reading, so a seasonal read is a flat read on a date; a fifth starter would teach a
file layout that does not exist. Capacity services read no meter at all and get none.

⚠ **THE PARTS TRAP IS CLOSED BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY CARE.** Every starter row is built by
`_shape_row` from `TEMPLATE_COLUMNS` — the same dict `parse_csv` maps a header against — and
a row naming a column the parser does not read RAISES at import time.
`tests/test_cr077_read_starters.py` reads that dict rather than a copy of it, and puts all
four files through the real parser: zero parse errors, every published header mapped to its
own target. Clicked end to end in `10-scripts/po20260908_walkthrough.mjs`, which downloads
each file from the real button, pastes it back into the real screen and reads the mapping
the SERVER answered with — **9 columns detected, 9 matched, on all four** — with a negative
control that renames one optional header and confirms the check can still see an unmatched
column.

⚠ **AND THE STALE CITATION IS FIXED.** `import_runs.py` and `tests/test_cr025_sample_csv.py`
both cited `reads_template.csv` as *"header plus ONE worked row"*; that stopped being true
at CR-038 W4, and `template_csv`'s docstring had been REPORTING the drift for a fortnight
instead of closing it (hard-won law 1). Both now say what the file ships.

A capacity service reads nothing, so the entry goes and `tests/test_cr062_j_addendum.py::test_pure_j1_only_thermal_moves` moves with it. (d) `METERED_ESTATE_SERVICES` loses `thermal_heat` and `CAPACITY_ESTATE_SERVICES` gains it; `SERVICE_METER_PREFIX["thermal_heat"] = "TH"` and `BACKBONE_BASE["thermal_heat"]` go with it. **A thermal tenant stops getting 48 meters, an opening read and three months of readings, and starts getting a service point per unit with its tonnage on the unit.** (e) The three `TH-CW-*` bands are WITHDRAWN and replaced by a catalogue of connected-tonnage capacities — this is the half the 2026-08-27 ruling actually ordered. Each of the three is a RANGE (*"≤25 tons"*, *"25–100"*), which is precisely why they cannot be capacities: a range has no single value to multiply. Their mirror rows in `apps/tenancy/fixtures/lookup_defaults.json` and the three codes listed in `07-frontend/e2e/CR-004-reference-crud.spec.ts` move with them, behind a `BR-TEN-077` version bump. ⚠ **NO ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 FIGURE MOVES, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** `04-docs/02-decisions/04-money-math-rules.md` contains no thermal figure at all; B5's single mention of `thermal_heat` is the revenue-account addendum, which is a GL designation and not an amount. `GT-1`–`GT-61` price no thermal line. **So this needs no re-sign under HUMAN-GUIDE §6** — but (b) above still has to be put to the PO, because a figure they personally approved is being retired. **WHAT IT COSTS, MEASURED ON THE DEVELOPMENT DATABASE RATHER THAN ESTIMATED:** across all four seeded tenants there are **4 `tenant_services` rows for thermal, every one of them `metered` and every one of them `enabled = false`**, with **0 thermal service points, 0 thermal assets and 0 thermal invoice lines**. **Nothing is billing thermal today, so no customer is re-billed and no issued invoice is contradicted** — the data migration moves four dormant rows. That is the cheapest this change will ever be, and it is the argument for doing it now rather than after a thermal utility goes live. **WHAT IS STILL OPEN AND MUST NOT BE CLOSED BY THIS WORK.** `OQ-560` — thermal STEAM's size bands — stays open; it was put to the PO as a dimension with no boundaries and `steam_size_classes()` still raises. The unit code is `ton`. **Status: BUILT 2026-09-07 (version `2.227.0`), HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING.** **WHAT SHIPPED, and every figure below was measured or cited rather than assumed.** `SERVICE_DEFAULT_UOMS["thermal_heat"]` is `ServiceDefault("ton", "klb", capacity)` — basis and unit moved in ONE edit, which the map's own comment requires. Researched: **Lansing Board of Water & Light** (municipal, MI) Rate CW1 FY2024-25 charges **`$50.00` per ton** of Contract Demand (`$49.49` in FY2023-24), and its Capacity Charge IS the minimum monthly charge; **City of Mesa AZ** (municipal) bills district cooling on a monthly charge per **Rated-Ton** and defines a Ton-Hour as 12,000 BTU; **District Energy St. Paul** and **JEA** (Jacksonville, municipal) both set demand on TONS. ⚠ **`$50.00` IS NOT COPIED ACROSS AND THAT IS THE JUDGMENT:** Lansing bills it on *"the maximum instantaneous demand (tons) supplied during the billing period"* — a MEASURED summer peak, near zero in a Michigan January — while the PO's model is Mesa's, a charge on CONNECTED tonnage twelve months a year. `$50.00 × 3 ÷ 12` = **`$12.50`**, i.e. `$150` per ton-year. ⚠ **What could not be verified, stated rather than smoothed over:** both rate PDFs are blocked by this environment's network egress policy, so the cents are quoted from search results rather than read off the tariff; the STRUCTURE is corroborated by four municipal utilities, the exact cent is one utility's at one remove. **`$0.045` per ton-hour is RETIRED.** ⚠ **A sibling lane seeded `gas` at `$1.15/ccf` into that same map hours earlier the same day** (`DEF-RAT-4516`, closing `OQ-1290`) — both changes stand and the map's own rule decides it: it holds a flat price for a METERED service, so gas belongs and thermal no longer does. A first draft of this CR asserted the map would be EMPTY, which would have gone red on a sibling's correct change. Their row's worked figure *"thermal billed 30,000 × $0.045 = $1,350.00"* retires with it. **THE TONNAGE IS A UNIT FACT, NOT A DEVICE.** `connections.UNIT_CAPACITY_CHARACTERISTIC` gains `"thermal_heat": "connected_capacity"` — storm water's shape, for storm water's own reason: **nobody installs a ton**, the chiller is the utility's, in the plant. A thermal tenant stops getting **48 `TH-` meters, an opening read and three months of readings** and gets a service point per unit with its tonnage on it: 45 houses at 5 tons, two commercial at **100**, the depot at **200**, the mill at 400, and `THERMAL_UNIT_WITH_NONE` deliberately unconnected so `BR-MET-108`'s ruled `$0.00` stands beside real numbers. **1,025 connected tons = `$12,812.50` a month** before `BR-RAT-101`'s outside-city 1.5x. **`klb` STAYS and `OQ-560` IS UNTOUCHED — decided, not overlooked.** It is thermal STEAM's unit and `steam_size_classes()` still raises. ⚠ **AND THE BRIEFING'S WORRY ABOUT `_derive_uom_service_scope()` DOES NOT HOLD, WHICH IS WORTH RECORDING:** dropping a unit from `SERVICE_DEFAULT_UOMS` cannot silently rescope `klb` OR `ton-hr`, because `_seed_uoms` resolves `stated or SEEDED_UOM_SERVICE_SCOPE.get(code)` and BOTH units STATE `"service": "thermal_heat"` in `lookup_defaults.json`, where the fixture wins. `ton-hr` therefore leaves the map and stays in the catalogue at its stated scope. `klb` is kept anyway, so the derived and stated statements still agree in both directions and the map is not silent about steam. **NO ❄️ FROZEN FIGURE MOVED, CHECKED NOT ASSUMED:** `04-docs/02-decisions/04-money-math-rules.md` contains no thermal figure at all; B5's only `thermal_heat` mention is revenue account **4170**, a GL designation; and `GT-1`–`GT-61` price no thermal line. **MIGRATION** `tenancy/0043_cr080_thermal_capacity_basis.py` — DATA ONLY per `0031`'s measured rule (a migration that writes rows and then ALTERs the same table fails on PostgreSQL and passes the whole SQLite suite). It moves the BASIS and deliberately **not** the stored UoM, because a seeded default is never a backfill (`BR-TEN-1180` clause 6). 🔒 `HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING`, ledger row appended. **RE-MEASURED BEFORE MIGRATING, on a seeded database at the tip:** thermal is `metered` and `enabled = false` on every row, with **0 thermal service points, 0 assets and 0 invoice lines**. Nothing bills thermal, so nobody is re-billed and no issued invoice is contradicted. ⚠ **ONE THING FOUND THAT THIS CR DID NOT GO LOOKING FOR:** `07-frontend/e2e/CR-004-reference-crud.spec.ts` had been missing fire's six `FL-*` codes since 2026-09-02 — its count assertion read **53** where the fixture held **59**. | **CR-081** | **SEWER STOPS BEING A PERCENTAGE OF THE WATER *CHARGE* AND BECOMES A PERCENTAGE OF THE WATER *QUANTITY*, PRICED ON A SEWER RATE SCHEDULE OF ITS OWN.** PO verbatim, 2026-09-07: *"we ahve to apply this method - Way 2 — what you described: a percentage of the gallons. * Water bill: same $39.50 * Sewer quantity: 40% of 8,000 gallons = 3,200 gallons * Sewer bill: 3,200 gallons at sewer's own rate — say $5.00 per thousand = $16.00 - pleas emake the changes"*. ⚠ **THIS REVERSES A RULING THE SAME PO MADE, AND THE SUPERSESSION IS STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** `BR-RAT-010` — *"Sewer '% of water': volume vs charge basis"* — was put to them and answered **`PO R1 Q8`: % of water usage-charge dollars**, and `BR-RAT-015` is the rule written from that answer. **`BR-RAT-015` is SUPERSEDED by this CR; `BR-RAT-010` reopens and is answered the other way.** ⚠ **AND IT MOVES ❄️ FROZEN B5 FIGURES, SO THE CHANGE PROCESS'S STEP 2 APPLIES: STOP AND RE-SIGN THROUGH HUMAN-GUIDE §6. NO CODE MOVES UNTIL THAT SIGNATURE EXISTS** — *"please make the changes"* is the instruction to proceed, not the signature, because a signature covers only what was SHOWN and the PO has so far been shown ONE of the affected figures. **SIX SEWER AMOUNTS MOVE, ACROSS FIVE WORKED EXAMPLES, and every one is computed here from the workbook's own water quantities so the PO can check each by hand:** `WE-1`/`GT-17` water **8 kgal** → sewer qty **3.2 kgal** (today **`$15.80`**) · `WE-4`/`GT-20` water **12 kgal** → **4.8 kgal** (today **`$24.96`**) · `WE-9`/`GT-25` water **6 kgal** → **2.4 kgal** (today **`$10.60`**) · `WE-10`/`GT-26` Jan–Mar water **6 kgal** → **2.4 kgal** (today **`$10.60`**) · `WE-10` Apr–Jun on tariff v4 → **2.4 kgal** (today **`$11.24`**) · `WE-12` water **3.1 kgal** → **1.24 kgal** (today **`$4.96`**). **At the PO's illustrative `$5.00` per kgal those become `$16.00` · `$24.00` · `$12.00` · `$12.00` · `$12.00` · `$6.20`** — and **every taxable subtotal, tax split and bill total on those five examples moves with them** and must be recomputed by `10-scripts/03-golden-verify.py` rather than by hand. ⚠ **NOTE WHICH WAY THEY MOVE, BECAUSE IT IS NOT ONE DIRECTION: residential goes UP and commercial goes DOWN.** `WE-1` gains `$0.20` while `WE-4` loses `$0.96`, because commercial water is flat `$5.20`/kgal against residential's tiered average of `$4.9375`/kgal — so today's percentage-of-money quietly charges a commercial customer more sewer per gallon than a residential one, and the volume basis stops it. **THREE THINGS ARE NOT SETTLED BY THE PO's MESSAGE AND EVERY FIGURE ABOVE DEPENDS ON THEM.** **(a) THE SEWER RATE IS NOT RULED. `$5.00` WAS THE LANE'S OWN ILLUSTRATION — the word *"say"* is in the sentence they quoted back — so it is NOT a signed rate and must not be seeded as one.** To hold `WE-1` at today's `$15.80` the rate would be **`$4.9375`**/kgal; a round `$5.00` gives `$16.00`. **(b) FLAT OR TIERED?** Water is tiered residentially (`0–5 $4.00 / 5–15 $6.50 / 15+ $8.00`) and flat commercially (`$5.20`); sewer may now have its own ladder or a single rate, and the two give different answers for a heavy user. **(c) ⚠ THE `40%` NOW MEANS SOMETHING PHYSICALLY DIFFERENT AND `40%` IS LOW FOR IT.** On the charge basis it was a PRICE RATIO — what sewer costs relative to water. On the volume basis it is a **RETURN-TO-SEWER FACTOR** — the fraction of metered water that actually goes down the drain — and typical North American factors are **80–95%** for a residential account without irrigation, with a lower figure used precisely to allow for outdoor watering. **Keeping `40%` is lawful and may be deliberate, but it is no longer the same number doing the same job**, and a lane must not carry it forward as if the ruling did not change its meaning. **WHAT ELSE MOVES IN CODE:** `apps/rating/pricing/models/percent_of_service.py` 🔒 (its `basis_amount` becomes a QUANTITY, not dollars) · `apps/rating/engine.py` 🔒 second pass · **`SERVICE_DEFAULT_UOMS["sewer"]` — today `ServiceDefault(None, None, share)` with the comment *"No unit, by the ruling: a share of another service's money has no quantity"*, which this ruling reverses: sewer now HAS a quantity and must carry the basis service's unit, so a utility metering water in `ccf` bills sewer in `ccf`** · sewer needs a `tariff_versions` row with a real rate, which it has never had on any tenant · `BR-RAT-015`, `BR-RAT-010`, `OQ-232` and every citing document. **Status: DONE 2026-09-08 at version `2.230.0`.** The finance re-sign landed the same day (decision log, *"THE PO RE-SIGNS SIX FROZEN SEWER FIGURES"*) and answered all three of (a), (b) and (c) in one sentence — **(a) the rate is `$5.00`**, **(b) FLAT, not tiered**, and **(c) the factor is `90%` and is now a RETURN-TO-SEWER FACTOR rather than a price ratio**. ⚠ **THE SIX FIGURES ARE NOT THE ONES THIS ROW ESTIMATED**, because the factor moved with the basis: `WE-1` **`$36.00`** (not `$16.00`), `WE-4` **`$54.00`**, `WE-9` **`$27.00`**, `WE-10` **`$27.00`** in BOTH halves, `WE-12` **`$13.95`** — and the direction is no longer mixed, every one more than doubles. **Recomputed by `10-scripts/03-golden-verify.py`, never by hand: 33 PASS / 0 FAIL** with `WE-1` taxable `$242.10` → tax `$22.87` → total **`$314.97`** · `WE-2` **`$292.10`** · prices a VOLUME and the line carries a quantity, the basis service's unit and sewer's own rate · `engine.py`'s second pass hands across `basis_quantity` + `basis_unit` (the field was RENAMED from `basis_amount` so an unconverted caller fails loudly instead of multiplying kgal by a price-per-kgal) · `selectors.pricing_inputs` publishes sewer's rate the way `flat`'s is published (BR-RAT-032, one 0→∞ tier — no new column) · `rating/0028_cr081_sewer_volume_basis.py` backfills it per tenant under `app.tenant_id` with a savepoint each and LOGS THE COUNTS · `SERVICE_DEFAULT_UOMS["sewer"]` mirrors water's `kgal`/`ccf` (so `kgal` widens back to All services) · `BR-RAT-015` ❄️ SUPERSEDED by the new **`BR-RAT-1015`** and `BR-RAT-010` reopened and answered the other way. ⚠ **TWO THINGS THE RE-SIGN ⚠ **NUMBERS ARE NO LONGER TAKEN FROM A SENTENCE ON THIS PAGE — PO RULING 2026-09-10.**
A change request raised from here carries the branch that raised it: **`CR-<nnn>-<BRCnn>`**,
e.g. `CR-090-BRC01`, in its own file `change-requests/CR-090-BRC01-<slug>.md`. **`CR-001`–`CR-089`
keep their bare form and nothing is renumbered.** Each concurrent branch owns a DISJOINT block of
numbers, recorded in [`14-id-reservations.md`](14-id-reservations.md) before that branch starts —
`CR-090`–`094` is `BRC01`, `095`–`099` is `BRC02`, `100`–`104` is `BRC03`. **Take your number from
your own block, not from this page**, verify it at push time with `10-scripts/allocate.py cr
--verify <n>`, and know that `G17` fails a duplicate **number** even when the suffixes differ — two
branches both calling something ninety merge clean and go red at the gate rather than in the register.
The whole rule, with its reasoning, is `13-change-process.md` step 0. Allocate at the moment a change
ARRIVES, not when work starts.

## CR-001 · Settings: "Reference data" becomes "Configure", and three tabs move inside it

**Raised:** 2026-08-11, Product Owner, from the running app.
**Release:** R1 (Settings is R1 scope; the app is deployed and this is live).
**Status:** ACCEPTED — implemented 2026-08-11.

### What the PO asked for, verbatim

> "Rooutes and Cycle, Numbering, templates - move under Reference data - we can
> call Reference data = Configure - can you take this as change request for R1,
> write entire case, make changes"

### The change, concretely

The Settings tab strip today (screenshot, `/silver-creek-water/settings/routes-cycles`):

```
Company · Users & roles · Services & UoM · Routes & Cycles · Reference data ·
Numbering · Templates · Notifications · Integrations · Security · Billing plan
```

Eleven tabs, wrapping onto a second line at 1920px — which is itself part of
the case: a strip that wraps has stopped being a strip.

After:

```
Company · Users & roles · Services & UoM · Configure · Notifications ·
Integrations · Security · Billing plan
```

Eight tabs, one line, with **Configure** carrying a second-level strip:

```
Reference data · Routes & Cycles · Numbering · Templates
```

### What this reverses, and why the reversal is sound

**A1 Addendum r6 (2026-08-07) says the opposite, in as many words:**

> *"Lookup tables" tab renamed to **Reference data** (clearer for business
> users). **Routes & Cycles, Numbering, and Security remain their own tabs
> (they are configuration/security, not editable reference lists).**"*

That is a signed decision with a stated reason, and the reason is good: Routes
& Cycles and Numbering are not lists a clerk edits row by row, so filing them
under a heading that promises *reference lists* would have misdescribed them.

**The rename is what dissolves the objection.** r6's argument is against the
word "Reference data", not against the grouping. "Configure" describes all four
accurately: reference lists, read routes and billing cycles, number formats and
document templates are every one of them *things you set up once and change
rarely*. The PO's two sentences are therefore one move, not two — and it only
works because the rename comes with it. Moving three tabs under a heading still
called "Reference data" would have been the mistake r6 correctly refused.

**Security deliberately does NOT move.** r6 named three tabs and the PO named
three tabs, and they are not the same three: r6 said Routes & Cycles, Numbering
and Security; the PO said Routes & Cycles, Numbering and Templates. Security
stays a top-level tab, and r6's reason for it is untouched — it is security,
not configuration, and a password policy is not a thing you file next to a list
of meter types. This is recorded because "the PO moved three tabs" invites
someone to assume it was r6's three.

### The supporting case, beyond the PO's preference

1. **Eleven tabs wrap.** The screenshot shows the strip breaking onto a second
   row with "Billing plan" alone underneath, on a 1920px display. Eight fit.
2. **The three tabs being moved are the three a tenant touches least.** Routes,
   cycles, number formats and templates are configured during onboarding and
   then left alone for months. The tabs a clerk uses weekly — Company, Users,
   Services — keep their top-level position.
3. **The second level already exists and is proved.** `Company` has carried a
   sub-tab strip (Profile · Regional) since it was built, with the route
   `/settings/:tab/:sub` and a tested fallback. This CR uses the same mechanism
   rather than inventing a second one.
4. **It shortens no URL a human typed.** The four moved tabs keep their own URL
   segments (see below), so nothing anyone bookmarked stops working.

### What moves, file by file

| What | Change |
|---|---|
| `SETTINGS_TABS` | Four entries become one; `reference-data` stays as the id and gains sub-tabs |
| `settings.tab.referenceData` (5 catalogues) | Value becomes **Configure**. The KEY is unchanged — renaming it would touch every catalogue for no gain and break nothing usefully |
| `CONFIGURE_SUB_TABS` | New, mirroring `COMPANY_SUB_TABS`: reference-data · routes-cycles · number-series · templates |
| `SettingsPage` body switch | Routes to the sub-tab, defaulting to Reference data |
| S8 checklist targets (`US-TEN-003`) | `settings/number-series` still resolves — see the URL note |
| `01-screen-inventory.md` | **A1 Addendum r9** recording this, and stamping r6 as superseded in part |
| `12-governance/02-decision-log.md` | The ruling verbatim |
| G14 (prototype conformance) | See below — this is the part that needs care |

### URLs: nothing breaks, deliberately

The four sub-tabs keep the segments they have today, because
`/settings/:tab/:sub` reads the SECOND segment when the first is `Configure`'s
id — and `Configure`'s id stays `reference-data`. So:

| Old URL | After |
|---|---|
| `/settings/reference-data` | works — Configure, defaulting to Reference data |
| `/settings/routes-cycles` | redirects to `/settings/reference-data/routes-cycles` |
| `/settings/number-series` | redirects to `/settings/reference-data/number-series` |
| `/settings/templates` | redirects to `/settings/reference-data/templates` |

The redirects are not decoration. `US-TEN-003`'s onboarding checklist targets
`settings/number-series` by name, the Reference data screen links to
`/settings/templates` for the BR-TEN-033 document-template pointer, and the
deployed app has been serving all four for weeks. A tab move that 404s a
checklist link would be this CR causing a defect.

### What it costs

**G14 does NOT go red — and the reason is a hole worth naming.** I predicted in
the first draft of this case that the prototype-conformance gate would fail on
the label "Configure", and then ran it: **PASS, 9 tab labels matched.** The
prediction was wrong because G14's `TAB_LABEL_KEYS` guards the Plans & Rates
tabs, the Assets tabs and Company's two SUB-tabs — and **not one Settings
top-level tab label.** The correction is recorded rather than quietly edited,
because "I claimed a gate would catch this and did not run it" is the exact
shape of hard-won law 1, and this file is the wrong place to repeat it.

So the position is: **the divergence is real and nothing guards it.** The
prototype draws eleven Settings tabs and knows no label "Configure"; the app
now draws eight. A previous lane already reported the same hole from the other
side — Company's sub-tab labels were prototype-verbatim but absent from
`TAB_LABEL_KEYS`, and adding them was outside that lane's territory. Two
reports of one gap is enough: **adding the Settings top-level labels to G14 is
now scheduled work**, and it will go red on this CR the moment it lands, which
is correct and is the point. The divergence is recorded here and in A1
Addendum r9 so the gate has something to be told about.

**The prototype file is NOT edited.** It is the design of record for R1, and
rewriting it to match the product destroys the only thing that catches drift
(law 6 — nine defects were found this way and by nothing else). When the
prototype and a ruling disagree, the ruling wins and the divergence is written
down; the prototype stays as it was drawn.

This is the third prototype-vs-ruling divergence in two days — DEF-018 (nav
order), DEF-033 (draft bill numbers, which reversed the other way and proved
the prototype right), and this one. The pattern is worth stating plainly:
**the prototype is older than every ruling made since, so a disagreement is
evidence about dates, not about correctness.** Each one has to be judged, and
each judgement has to be written down, because a silent divergence is
indistinguishable from a mistake and someone eventually "fixes" it back.

### What actually ran

⚠ **The first version of this block was WRONG, and the way it was wrong is the
same mistake this file already corrects one section up.** It reported
`vitest run  53 files, 738 passed` — a number copied from the run BEFORE the
change. The suite was backgrounded, its output was never read, and green was
assumed. **Four tests were failing, all of them mine**, and every one was a
test correctly pinning the pre-CR contract:

| Test | What it pinned |
|---|---|
| the ratified tab order | `number-series` must be a top-level tab id |
| honest states | `templates` must render its "arrives with" as a TOP-LEVEL tab |
| an Executive's tab set | the strip must contain the words "Reference data" |
| the checklist contract | `/settings/number-series` must match `settings/:tab` |

Each was updated to the new contract rather than deleted, and the fourth grew a
partner that asserts what the CR actually promises: **the three moved segments
resolve to their redirects.** That assertion did not exist before, so the
redirect work — the part of this change most likely to break a live checklist
link — had nothing defending it. The failure produced a better test than the
pass would have.

Measured, after the fix:

```
tsc --noEmit                    clean
eslint --max-warnings 0         clean
vitest run                      54 files, 751 passed / 175 todo
                                (2 unrelated failures, another lane's, waiting
                                 on i18n keys it is not permitted to add)
pytest tests                    1343 passed, 83 skipped, 1 xfailed
run_gates.py                    15 PASS / 0 FAIL / 1 SKIP
trace_lint                      OK - 250 stories, 559 BR refs
```

**Kept rather than tidied away**, because two unverified claims in one document
is a pattern and not an accident: a backgrounded check is not a passing check
until somebody reads it.

## CR-002 · A new UI bundle (prototype r10) with a module the module map does not have

**Raised:** 2026-08-16, Product Owner, as a file handed over in the working chat
session (`SMARTBillHub_UI_Mockups.zip`, 20 MB, 67 files).
**Release:** R2 (undecided — see OQ-249; the scope answer is the PO's).
**Status:** ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-18 — OQ-249 IS ANSWERED AND THIS HEADER WAS
WRONG FOR TWO DAYS.** It read *"awaiting OQ-249 for scope"* until 2026-08-18,
and OQ-249 was answered on **2026-08-16**: PO verbatim *"Yes it is sensitive; we
will build as version 2 of the product; I ahve made the design ; but it is not
part of R4 ; it will be R5 ; you dont need to do anything right now"*. **Field
work IS in the product and it is R5** — scope YES, release R5, nothing built
now. Three sub-questions stay open by the PO's own instruction (own module vs
tabs on `assets`, its place in the build order, whether `btm` is R4 or rides
R5); they are deliberately not pressed. **This CR ships no code**, so the
2026-08-18 browser closure bar is N/A to it (§8 — nothing for a person to do on
a screen). **One follow-up is owed and is not a blocker:** the `/work` rail
entry and the four SET-04 Work cards say the feature is missing without saying
WHEN — they should name R5, because a placeholder that states its release is
information and one that does not is a broken promise. Deleting them is NOT the
correct response to "it is R5".
**Supersedes:** nothing signed. It does not reverse a business rule; it proposes
new surface and changes which prototype file lanes read.

### What the PO asked for, verbatim

> "This updated file of UI; we have made many cahnges to it including new
> module; save this as  new version. When we update the UI/Scrren you can refer
> this new file ; how you will ahndle this?"

and, in the same exchange:

> "give me link where you ahve save this prortype that I just gave you"

### 1 · Classify

**New requirement**, not a defect. The product does what was agreed; the design
changed. The harsh rule in §1 of the change process ("when it is ambiguous it is
a DEFECT") does not fire here — nothing suggests we built the wrong thing, and
the bundle adds surface rather than correcting it.

**But one part of it is not classified yet and must not be guessed:** whether
the Work module is in scope at all. That is OQ-249, raised the same day.

### 2 · What is being reversed

**Nothing signed.** Checked against the two places a design change usually
collides:

* **B4 / B5 money math (❄️ FROZEN).** No rate, rounding rule, tax base or worked
  figure appears in the bundle. No finance re-sign is triggered. If a later
  reading of the Work module's `parts` or `cost` surfaces turns out to price
  anything, that is a STOP and a re-sign via HUMAN-GUIDE §6 — it is not this row.
* **BR-SHL-001 (sidebar order, PO-ruled 2026-08-10, Settings last).** The

### 4 · What is already built and is now in question

**`UI-RULES.md` is the live risk in this bundle, and it is not the new module.**
Its own first line: *"The binding conventions for every screen. Anything new
must follow these; anything found violating them is a bug."* That sentence
converts twenty conventions into acceptance criteria over screens that are
**already shipped and deployed**. Three that are near-certain to bite:

* **Rule 16** — a pagination footer on *every* list table, `Showing 1–50 of N`,
  page sizes 50/100/200/500/1000, **page size remembered per table**.
* **Rule 15** — row actions are icons with tooltips, **never text links**, max 2
  visible plus `…` overflow, against a fixed icon vocabulary.
* **Rule 11** — any form writing money, service state or legal notices shows a
  consequence-preview box **before** its commit button.

**None of these has been checked against the running app**, and hard-won law 1
says a document claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee. Auditing the deployed
screens against the twenty rules is real work with a real defect yield, and it is
independent of the OQ — it can start whether or not Work is in scope.

**Lanes building right now:** none touches Work, Workflows or Assets tabs; the
bundle is additive and no in-flight lane needs to be stopped.

That divergence is a cost the PO accepted knowingly in order to work from the new

### THE ACCEPTANCE BAR, set by that last sentence

**Every item below ships all four parts of r11 step 2 or it is not done:**

This is written into the CR rather than assumed because **2b is the part that
goes missing**: R2's central failure was 66 stories with a finished engine and
no screen, every deferral honest and nothing adding them up. A new lookup list
with a table, a handler, a seeder and passing backend tests but no card on
SET-04 satisfies nothing here.

### The final list — 29 cards

| Plans & Rates | Charge codes · Tax jurisdictions · Reason codes · **Meter size classes** 🆕 |

accounting tab"*).

### What we already have, and what we do not

**Have — reusable, zero new work:**
* **Every endpoint.** `/lookups`, `/lookups/{list}`, `POST`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`,
  `/deactivate`. A new list needs **none**.
* **The stories.** US-TEN-009 (card grid), US-TEN-010 (view/search/add/edit),
  US-TEN-011 (delete/deactivate). A new list inherits all three and does not
  need its own CRUD story.
* **The rules.** BR-TEN-030 (code unique per tenant, immutable once used),
  BR-TEN-031 (framework is tenancy's, content belongs to the owning module),
  BR-TEN-034 (audit-lock), BR-TEN-036 (seeded defaults, tenant may extend).
* **The list view and its modals.** Add/Edit already open a `FormModal` with the
  `← Reference data` return. **The PO asked whether modals are needed: they
  exist and are right.** The row already renders Edit · Deactivate/Reactivate ·
  Delete with the locked-delete reason — exactly r10's three icons, so that is
  a text→icon conversion, not new behaviour.

**Do not have:** there is **no generic lookup table.** Each list is hosted in
its owning module's own table behind a duck-typed handler. So every new list
needs a table (B2), a handler, two registry rows, seed entries, a business rule
naming its vocabulary as ratified, and an S-ID.

### The service-scope field

**Nine cards CONFIRMED unscoped**, one CONFIRMED scoped (units of measure),
**eight unruled and unscoped by default** — tax jurisdictions, read methods,
asset types, asset lifecycle stages, certification types, and **meter types,
device types (BTM), meter size classes**, which were grouped with charge codes
as *likely* scoped and so never got a verdict of their own. See the decision log
for the rulings verbatim.

**Default is unscoped, by asymmetry:** switching a list ON later is one line;
switching it OFF after tenants have entered scoped data is a migration.

**The unfiltered UoM picker is DEF-184, not part of this CR.** A water service
can today be assigned `therm`. Same landing, different register — filing our own
gap as a change would convert it into the customer's requirement.

### ⚠ CORRECTION, 2026-08-16: it is ELEVEN new cards, not nine

The first pass through this CR said nine. It is **eleven**, and the one missed
matters because it looks finished from the outside.

**Premise & unit types has NO CARD TODAY.** `premises_types` is declared in
`LOOKUP_LISTS` — DEF-026 added it — but `apps.metering` never registered a
handler, and `lookup_cards()` skips any list whose handler is `None`. So the
list is seeded, reported and reachable through metering's own endpoint, and the
Reference-data grid has never shown it. It was counted here as an existing card
needing only a rename. It needs the whole four-part build.

The other addition is **Import mappings**, previously carried as a separate
item rather than a card.

Full count: 18 of our 19 cards map onto r10 (the 19th, Finance controls, moves
to the Accounting tab). 29 − 18 = **11 new**: areas & sub-areas · meter size
classes · **premise & unit types** · occupancy statuses · device types (BTM) ·
certification types · skills catalog · safety kits · work priorities & SLA ·
parts categories & locations · import mappings.

### Two further PO requirements, both acceptance criteria

> "Full Add, Edit, Update, view - all shoudl work; also for all these we will
> provide meaningful and relevant seed data at the time of tenant creation"

**1 · CRUD is functional FROM THE SCREEN.** The PO said this twice, the second
time to remove any doubt: **"full CRUD working - from Ui scren not just
backend"**. So the evidence for add / edit / update / view is r11 step **2d** —
someone signs in, opens the card, adds a row, edits it, deactivates it and
deletes one, and the result is quoted. A green backend test is not that
evidence; neither is a passing component test. The audit-lock (BR-TEN-034) and
the case-insensitive code rule (BR-TEN-030) must behave from the screen exactly
as they do for the lists already shipped — including the refusals, which is
where a screen most often turns out to be wired to nothing. A card that renders
rows but refuses a write is not done, and a write that works in a test but not
in a browser is not done either.

**2 · Seed at TENANT CREATION, not by a later script.** The entries ride the
existing provisioning path — `SEED_LIST_OWNERS` + the fixture + each module's
`seed_reference_list` — so a brand-new tenant has them on first sign-in. The
content is transcribed from r10's own sub-screens, never invented: r10 supplies
entries for seven of the nine new cards (areas 4, meter size classes 7,
occupancy 5 from the PO's screenshot, device types 6, certification types 6,
plus the four Work lists), which is what makes this buildable without guessing
at a vocabulary.

**One question this raises and a lane must not answer alone:** BR-TEN-067
narrows the sample-data toggle to six STRUCTURAL_REFERENCE_LISTS, *"because they
are vocabulary the schema requires"* — an account cannot exist without a status.
Are the new lists structural (always seeded, toggle cannot suppress them) or
sample content? Occupancy statuses and device types look like vocabulary rather
than samples, but that is a judgment with a live consequence — a tenant that
turns sample data off and then cannot resolve an occupancy status — so it goes
to the PO with a worked example rather than being decided in a seeder.

### 7 · Version — **`2.4.0`**, allocated 2026-08-17

**This section previously read "Not allocated. `package.json` still reads
`0.0.1`."** It is now allocated, and the process step it was blocking is the
one the PO named as the one usually skipped.

**The arithmetic**, on the scheme `13-change-process.md` §7 fixes —
`<release>.<change>.<fix>`, worked there as *"R2, fourteenth change, seventh
fix since → `2.14.7`"*:

* **release = 2.** Every open CR row states `Release: R2` (CR-002, CR-003,
  CR-004); CR-001 was the last R1 change.
* **change = 4.** CR ids are allocated globally and sequentially in this file —
  four raised: CR-001 implemented, CR-002 captured and shipping no code,
  CR-003 built, CR-004 landing. **CR-004 is the highest-numbered change to have
  landed code.** The scheme's own example maps "fourteenth change" onto CR-014
  under exactly this reading, so the component is monotonic and reads back to
  one register row without a lookup table. When a code-shipping CR-005 lands it
  goes to 5, whatever CR-002's fate.
* **fix = 0.** The defect register holds **186 rows, 132 of them `fixed`**
  (counted 2026-08-17, after the allocation — see the correction below) — and
  none of them counts here, because the fix component counts defects fixed **on
  top of** the change, and **`2.4.0` is the first build this product has ever
  stamped.** Nothing shipped as `2.3.x`, so there is no shipped build for a fix
  to sit on top of. Three rows were checked one at a time rather than counted in
  bulk:
  * **DEF-185** — `introduced_in` CR-004's own commit `4b02f48` and fixed inside
    the same unshipped work. A defect found and fixed before the change ships is
    part of the change, not a fix on it.
  * **DEF-184** (a water service measurable in therms) — the one that predates
    CR-004 entirely (`introduced_in` US-TEN-007). Its backend half landed in
    `60422d2` and **its screen half landed in `c4c997e` while this allocation was
    being written**, but **the register row still reads `open`**, and a version
    must not bump on a defect the register calls open. It rides `2.4.0`
    unstamped, like everything else built before today.
  * **DEF-186** (the scope refusal blames the wrong cause) — filed *after*
    CR-004's code, `introduced_in` "DEF-184 backend lane, same day". Still
    `open`. Same treatment as DEF-185: born and handled inside the unshipped
    window.

**2 · 4 · 0 = `2.4.0`.** The first defect fixed on top of the stamped `2.4.0`
makes it `2.4.1`.

⚠ **A correction about the register count, recorded rather than smoothed over.**
The arithmetic was worked against **185** defect rows and the commit that
stamped the version (`28cfb83`) says 185. The register reached **186** (DEF-186)
during the same session, and two more commits — `c4c997e` (DEF-184's screen) and
`f7c3196` (DEF-186) — landed between reading the registers and writing this row.
**Neither moves any component**, for the reasons above, so `2.4.0` stands. It is
written down because step 0 of the build process exists for exactly this — the
repo changes under you — and because "the figure I quoted was one behind" is the
kind of thing that is only ever cheap to say immediately.

**ONE SOURCE OF TRUTH: `07-frontend/package.json`'s `version` field.** Not a
new `VERSION` file at the repo root, and the reason is a fact about the build
rather than a preference: the two apps build from **separate docker contexts**
(`./07-frontend` and `./06-backend`, `docker-compose.yml`), so no file above
either directory is readable at build time and a root `VERSION` would have to be
copied into both — **three committed copies instead of two**, hard-won law 5
pointing the wrong way. package.json is the one version field that already
exists, that npm and vite require anyway, and that the running app can read
with no build-config change.

**VISIBLE ON SCREEN** (§7 rule 2): `AppShell.tsx` imports that field and renders
`v2.4.0` at the foot of the sidebar, above the user block. **Unconditionally** —
the user block is optional and a version a signed-out or half-loaded frame
cannot show is missing from exactly the screenshot a defect report carries.
**It is a derivation, not a copy:** there is no version literal in the
component, its CSS or its tests; the tests assert against `pkg.version`, so the
only way to make them red is to stop rendering the version. Proved red on
2026-08-17 by deleting the element — three of four assertions failed with
`expected … to contain '>v2.4.0<'`, and the fourth was **strengthened because it
stayed green**, which is the check that could not distinguish pass from fail.
Confirmed in the shipped bundle: `2.4.0` appears once in `dist/assets/*.js`, and
no other package.json content survived tree-shaking.

**⚠ TWO THINGS OWED, and both are machine-checks §7 rule 4 demands that
`10-scripts/gates/` does not have.** Named here rather than assumed away
(law 1), because §7 rule 4's whole argument is that *"a step that depends on
someone remembering is a step that is 'many times not followed correctly'"*:

1. **No gate refuses a CR marked done with no version.** That is the exact
   machine §7 rule 4 calls "the only durable answer". It does not exist. This
   row is compliant because a human wrote the number in, which is the failure
   mode the rule predicts.
2. **`06-backend/pyproject.toml` is the ONE derived copy and nothing pins it.**
   It now reads `2.4.0` with the reasoning in a comment, but Python packaging
   cannot read a version out of a JSON file in a sibling build context and
   setuptools' `dynamic` can only read inside its own project directory — so
   **nothing fails today if the two literals disagree.** A gate asserting
   `pyproject.version == package.json.version` closes it in a few lines. Until
   it exists, moving one line means moving the other in the same commit.

Also owed, and smaller: §7 rule 4's second half — **a version bump with no
CHANGELOG entry must fail.** The product changelog is `CHANGELOG.md` at the
repo root (not `04-docs/CHANGELOG.md`, which serves a different reader); its
`[Unreleased]` section has no `2.4.0` heading and this lane did not add one.

### Rollback

Per task. The five new lists revert as a migration each; the layout, renames,
move and placeholders revert with the commit. **The version allocation reverts
on its own**: `package.json` and `pyproject.toml` go back to `0.0.1` / `0.1.0`,
the sidebar element and its four assertions come out, and nothing else in the
repo depends on the number — which is the point of having exactly one source.

**Status: DONE. Version 2.4.0.**

The walkthrough was re-run against a live stack — Postgres, Django, a built SPA

## CR-005 · SET-08 Numbering: every system-generated number gets a defined format

**Raised:** 2026-08-16, Product Owner, with four r10 SET-08 screenshots and a
written requirement.
**Release:** R2. The Work conflict below was RULED on 2026-08-16 (*"it should
work standalone in settings"*) and the three Work rows ship as formats.
**Status:** ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-17 — version `2.5.0`.** ⚠ **This header read
*"BUILT … Awaiting human review"* until 2026-08-18 while its own closure record
900 lines below said CLOSED** — the top/bottom drift this file already warns
about at CR-006's header, third occurrence. The closure is real and is the
walkthrough: **`15 passed (11.4m)`** in Chromium against a live stack, with
requirement 8 — the Executive seeing the table read-only, every control visible
and disabled, each carrying *"Your role can view this, but not change it."* —
the one that had kept it open. **It MEETS the 2026-08-18 browser closure bar
(§8), measured retroactively in the CR-011 audit.** The three open questions
below (OQ-250, OQ-252, OQ-258) are recorded against it and are not closure
blockers.
**Supersedes:** extends BR-TEN-035 with clauses (a)–(e); reverses nothing.
**Rollback:** the screen and the endpoints revert cleanly. **The DATA does not:**
once a series has restarted, or once a number has been issued from a new format,
those numbers are on immutable rows (hard rule 4) and cannot be re-minted —
dropping `restart_period`/`period_counted` would leave a `never` series willing
to issue a year of numbers again. Reverting is safe only before the first
restart boundary.

### What the PO asked for, verbatim

> "Next CR - Requirements — SET-08 · Settings → Configure → Numbering
> **Purpose** Central place to define the ID format for every system-generated
> number (accounts, premises, bills, payments, work orders, etc.). System of
> record — formats must be predictable, auditable, and never break existing
> numbers.
> **Scope — entities that get a format (grouped)**
> 1. Customers & Premises: Account #, Premises #, Unit #, Service request #
> 2. Billing & Payments: Bill #, Payment/receipt #, Adjustment #, Deposit #, Write-off #
> 3. Work: Work order #, Service template #, Dispatch batch #
> 4. Assets & Reads: Asset/meter tag #, Read batch #, Route #, Cycle #
> **Format definition (per entity)**
> * A format = optional prefix + optional date tokens + exactly one zero-padded counter
> * Supported tokens: `{YYYY}` `{YY}` `{MM}` and counter `{0000…}` (pad length 4–8)
> * Ready-made options per entity in a dropdown, e.g. Account: `AC-{YYYY}-{00000}`, `ACCT-{00000}`, plain `{00000}` (no prefix — plain sequential number), plus Custom (free-form pattern input, validated: max 1 counter, only allowed tokens, ≤ 24 chars)
> * Plain-number option is mandatory in every category (user rule): just `{00000}` with no prefix
> **Counter behavior**
> * Each entity row shows: current format, Next counter (editable numeric field), live Preview ("Next: AC-2026-01248"), and a reset icon
> * Counter reset: allowed only forward (can't set lower than current — prevents duplicate IDs); confirmation required, audit-logged
> * Date-token formats roll the counter per period option: "Restart counter each year/month — Yes/No" per entity
> * Changes apply to numbers issued from now on; already-issued numbers are never renumbered (immutable, stated on screen)
> **Validation rules**
> * Exactly one counter token required; duplicate prefixes across entities → warning (not blocking)
> * Preview updates live as format/counter changes
> * Uniqueness guaranteed per entity per tenant
> **Right rail — "How they appear together"** Live sample showing formats in
> context: bill header (Account, Bill, Payment, Receipt), work order card (WO,
> Asset, Premises), finance trail — re-renders as formats change so the admin
> sees the downstream effect before saving.
> **Actions**
> * Save (primary, bottom-left) — persists all rows in one transaction, toast + audit log entry (who, when, old → new format per entity)
> * Per-row reset counter (icon, confirm dialog)
> * Every change audit-logged with before/after
> **Permissions**
> * Owner + Admin only; read-only for other roles (controls disabled, tooltip "Owner/Admin only")
> **UX rules (per system conventions)**
> * Table layout: Entity | Format (searchable dropdown) | Next counter (right-aligned, tabular numerals) | Preview | Reset
> * Section kickers per group (CUSTOMERS & PREMISES, BILLING & PAYMENTS, WORK, ASSETS & READS)
> * Description text at 2/3 width; icons for actions with tooltips; 44px min hit targets
> * Numbers in `tnum`; preview in bold
> **Edge cases**
> * Counter overflow (counter exceeds pad length) → keep issuing, widen number, surface a warning banner
> * Format change mid-year with `{YYYY}`: old numbers keep old format; no gap or renumber
> * Import flows must respect these formats when generating IDs; imported records with their own IDs keep them (never overwritten); we need final confirmation it working on screen; you will find the design in R10 prototype;"

### First-pass observations — capture only, NOT an analysis

**This is not a greenfield screen.** Numbering EXISTS: `BR-TEN-035` is
CONFIRMED and already states "literal prefix + `{YYYY}/{YY}/{MM}/{DD}` + one
zero-padded sequence token; allocation inside the issuing transaction from a
per-tenant per-series monotonic counter" — which is this CR's format grammar
almost word for word. `models.NumberSeries`, `selectors.number_series_overview`
and `SettingsNumberingTab.tsx` are built. So a large part of this is EXTENDING a
working screen, not building one, and the analysis must start by measuring what
already works rather than by reading r10.

**FIVE series are seeded today** — `ACCOUNT` `AC-{YYYY}-{00000}` · `BILL`
`BL-{YY}{MM}-{000000}` · `PAYMENT` `PY-{YY}{MM}{DD}-{0000}` · `ADJUSTMENT`
`ADJ-{000}` · `ASSET` `AST-{00000}`. **The CR names sixteen entities.** A
previously-reported exception says the `DEP-/RCT-/EXP-` formats were "unstated
→ not seeded (reported)"; this CR states them, which closes that gap.

**⚠ THE WORK GROUP CONFLICTS WITH A RULING GIVEN HOURS EARLIER, and this lane
will not resolve it.** Scope group 3 is *Work order # · Service template # ·
Dispatch batch #*, and r10's SET-08 also draws *Work order #* and a WORK ORDER
CARD in the right rail. But on the same day the PO ruled on OQ-249: *"we will
build as version 2 of the product ... it is not part of R4 ; it will be R5 ; you
dont need to do anything right now"*. **A number series for a work order is a
piece of the Work module.** Three readings, all plausible, none ours to pick:
(a) the numbering ROWS ship now and the entities they number arrive in R5 —
harmless, since a series that issues nothing costs nothing; (b) the Work group
waits for R5 with everything else; (c) this CR post-dates that ruling and
narrows it. **PUT TO THE PO BEFORE ANY WORK-GROUP ROW IS BUILT.**

**Two more that need the same treatment before sizing:** *Service request #* and
*Dispatch batch #* name entities no module owns — the same shape as the Work
question. And **"we need final confirmation it working on screen"** repeats the
acceptance bar from CR-004, which CR-004 met only after a browser walkthrough
found five screens returning HTTP 500 (DEF-187). Plan the walkthrough into this
CR from the start rather than at the end.

### WHAT WAS BUILT — 2026-08-17, version `2.5.0`

**THE FIRST-PASS OBSERVATION WAS RIGHT AND DID NOT GO FAR ENOUGH.** Measuring
before building found the screen, the model, the selector, the kernel and five
seeded series — and it also found a **live defect the CR would otherwise have
walked past**: `SERIES_DEFAULTS` was a hand-typed literal with FIVE entries while
`core.numbering.KNOWN_SERIES` held NINE. The four in the gap had no row on any
tenant, so **every manual journal entry ever posted has no number** (BR-LED-021
(i) predicted exactly this and named the one-line fix), deposit batches, receipts
and accounting exports were in the same state, and metering had been asking for
`premises`/`unit`/`read_batch` since it was built and getting
`numbering_series_missing` back. The fix is structural rather than one line:
**`core.numbering.SERIES_CATALOG` is now the single source of both the ready-made
options the screen offers and the format each tenant is seeded with**, so a
series cannot be known-and-unseeded and a tenant cannot hold a format its own
dropdown does not offer.

**Backend** — `core/numbering.py` (the catalog; ≤24 chars; pad ≤8;
`period_key`/`validate_restart_period`/`literal_prefix`/`will_overflow`; the sink
signature gains the issue date) · `apps/tenancy` (derived `SERIES_DEFAULTS`;
seeding wired into the `manage.py seed_demo --tenant <sub>` repair door so
tenants that already exist can be fixed; `save_number_series_bulk` = one
transaction, one audit row keyed by entity; the allocator restarts per period)
· migration `tenancy/0012` (`restart_period` + `period_counted`, CHECK on the
three values, every existing row at `never`).

**Screen** — `SettingsNumberingTab.tsx`, rebuilt as r10 SET-08 draws it: Entity |
Format | Next counter | Restart | Preview | Reset, section kickers per group, the
sticky *"How they appear together"* rail re-rendering from the drafts, Save at
bottom-left saving the whole table in one call, the reset icon confirming before
it moves a counter, the duplicate-prefix and overflow warnings (neither blocks),
and the immutability sentence ON the screen. 64 new i18n keys × 11 locales.

**Tests** — `tests/test_cr005_numbering_set08.py` (24) + the tab's 20; **eleven
guards broken FIRST and quoted** (law 7). **Two of the eleven would not go red
and both were fixed rather than accepted:** the one-transaction break was a no-op
nested `atomic`, and the permission test stayed green with the ENDPOINT's gate
removed because the service's `@require_role` refused underneath — the permission
class is asserted directly now, and both gates stay.

**A real bug fell out of the first green run**, which is the argument for writing
the worked figure into the test: turning restart ON reset the counter on the very
NEXT number, discarding an admin's 18,411. A first allocation now ADOPTS its
period without resetting; the restart begins at the next boundary.

### THE ENTITY LIST IS THE UNION OF TWO PO ARTEFACTS, NOT A CHOICE BETWEEN THEM

**CR-005 names sixteen entities. r10's SET-08 draws fourteen. They are not the
same fourteen.** CR-only: Unit · Write-off · Service template · Dispatch batch ·
Read batch · Route · Cycle. r10-only: Credit memo · Journal · Collections notice
· Import run. **Twenty-two ship** (those plus the ten both name, plus
`export_batch`, which `KNOWN_SERIES` has carried since BE-06 and neither source
mentions) — because picking between two artefacts the PO produced on one day is
not a lane's call, and because the PO's own economics for the Work rows applies
to all of them: a series that issues nothing costs nothing. **Trimming is the
PO's call — OQ-251.**

### THREE QUESTIONS RAISED RATHER THAN GUESSED

* **OQ-250 — the pad minimum.** The CR says *"pad length 4–8"*; the shipped
  `ADJ-{000}` and nine of r10's own options are below four. **≤8 is enforced; the
  minimum is not**, because enforcing it would make a row nobody touched
  unsaveable. `ADJ-{000}` at 1,000 renders **ADJ-1000** — short pads are not
  unsafe, only untidy.
* **OQ-251 — the entity list** (above).
* **OQ-252 — restart without a date token is REFUSED**, and so is a backdated
  issuance under a restart. Both prevent handing out a number a customer already
  has, on a row nobody may correct.

### THREE THINGS THE PO ASKED FOR THAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM

1. **"we need final confirmation it working on screen".** The screen is proved by
   render tests and typecheck, **not yet by a browser walkthrough** against a
   running server — the acceptance bar CR-004 met only after one found five
   screens returning HTTP 500 (DEF-187). That walkthrough is owed before this CR
   is closed.
2. **"Import flows must respect these formats … imported records with their own
   IDs keep them".** Import paths are NOT wired to this screen by this change.
   The formats are defined and standalone, per the ruling that a Settings screen
   defines a thing and the wiring is later work — but this specific sentence is
   an import-lane obligation and is recorded here so it is not assumed done.
3. **The format picker is a NATIVE select**, as r10 draws it; the CR's prose says
   *"searchable dropdown"*. With at most seven options per entity, a filter box
   would be furniture. Reported, not resolved.

> Step 3 — Review members & meters: summary counts (X premises, Y units, Z meters). Meter-level list with deselect allowed per meter (user rule: reader may exclude specific meters, e.g. inaccessible sub-meters). Excluded meters remain on the premise but off the route.
> Step 4 — Review & confirm: full summary card (basics, member counts, exclusions, cycle if pre-assigned) → Save as draft / Activate. Audit-logged.
> **SET-07 · Add/Edit Cycle — 4-step wizard (same shell)**
> Identical pattern but the members are routes instead of premises:
> 1. Basics: name, cycle ID, frequency (Monthly/Bi-monthly/Quarterly), read window (day-of-month range), bill date (offset from read close, e.g. read close +3 days), due date (bill date +21 days), late fee trigger date.
> 2. Select routes: picker of active routes with type/members/meters; a route can belong to only one cycle per service — conflict badge + confirm-move.
> 3. Review coverage: accounts/premises/meters rolled up per route; flag any active account NOT covered by any cycle ("47 accounts unscheduled").
> 4. Review & confirm → Draft/Activate; timeline strip preview of the cycle month (read window → exception review → bill run → due → late).
> **Shared rules**
> * Wizards are full-page workflows with stepper header (numbered, clickable back, forward only via Continue), Cancel returns to SET-05 with confirm-if-dirty
> * Draft state visible in tables with "Draft" pill; drafts don't affect Reads/Billing
> * Edit uses the same wizard pre-filled; changes to an active route/cycle take effect next read window, stated inline
> * All CRUD audit-logged (who, when, before/after member counts)
> * Permissions: Owner/Admin; read-only otherwise
> * Data integrity: deleting is not allowed once a route has reads history — deactivate only
> **Downstream links**
> * Reads module groups by route and shows cycle read windows
> * Billing "Run bills" preselects by cycle
> * Dispatch can filter work orders by route/area; I will give you few more scrrenshots. you can find them from R10"

### First-pass observations — capture only, NOT an analysis

**Again not greenfield.** `apps/metering/models.py` already has `Cycle`, `Route`
AND `RouteMembership`; the frontend has `RoutesCyclesPage.tsx` and
`SettingsRoutesCyclesTab.tsx`. So the data model for route membership exists and
the analysis must begin by measuring it against this requirement — CR-004 taught
that lesson three times over (pagination, page sizes and "+ Add entry" were all
reported as gaps and all already built), and CR-005 carries the same warning.

**THREE DEPENDENCIES, and two are on change requests that are not finished.**
* *"route ID (from Numbering format, editable)"* → **CR-005**, which is captured
  and unanalysed. A route ID drawn from a numbering series cannot be built
  before the series exists.
* *"area + sub-area (from reference data)"* → **CR-004's `areas` list**, which
  shipped hours ago. Note the requirement says **area AND SUB-area**: the seeded
  vocabulary is flat (NORTH, DTWN, EAST, IND) and r10's own card text says
  *"3 sub-areas"*. **The hierarchy was deliberately NOT built** — recorded in
  the model docstring as a shape nothing had specified. This requirement is the
  specification, so that gap is now live work rather than a deferred one.
* *"Dispatch can filter work orders by route/area"* → **Work, which the PO ruled
  R5 the same day.** Same conflict CR-005 carries. It reads as a forward
  statement rather than a request to build dispatch now, but it must not be
  assumed.

**One requirement is a money-adjacent rule and must not be inferred:** cycle
Basics carries *bill date (offset from read close)*, *due date (bill date +21
days)* and a **late fee trigger date**. Late fees are B4/B5 ❄️ FROZEN territory
(BR-BIL-001/002 govern the late percentage, minimum and grace). A date that
TRIGGERS a late fee is a billing-calendar input, and whether this screen may set
it — or merely displays what the frozen rules already decide — needs answering
before the field is drawn. Do not build a control that appears to set a frozen
figure.

**Two more to resolve before sizing:** *"a route can belong to only one cycle per
service"* and *"deleting is not allowed once a route has reads history"* are
both business rules that may or may not already exist in the metering register —
check before minting new BR-IDs. And *"47 accounts unscheduled"* on SET-07 step 3
is a real coverage query, not a label.

### Next step

Step 1 CLASSIFY and step 3 IMPACT against the SHIPPED `Route`/`Cycle`/
`RouteMembership` tables. Nothing is built until the late-fee-trigger question
and the CR-005 ordering are answered.

### CR-006 addendum — the four SET-07 screenshots (received 2026-08-16)

The promised screenshots arrived: SET-07.1 Details · 07.2 Select routes ·
07.3 Schedule · 07.4 Review & confirm. **They contradict the written
requirement in one place and settle a worry in another.**

**THE CONTRADICTION — step 1 is three fields, not nine.** The written
requirement puts frequency, read window, bill date, due date AND the late-fee
trigger all in *"1. Basics"*. r10's SET-07.1 draws exactly **Cycle code · Name ·
Frequency**, and every date lives in a separate **step 3 · Schedule**. The
design is the better shape — a step that asks nine questions is not a step — and
per the standing ruling that r10 is the default reference, **r10 wins and the
written requirement's step 1 is stale.** Recorded rather than silently followed.

**THE WORRY, PARTLY SETTLED AND PARTLY SHARPENED.** The capture above flagged
the late-fee trigger as possible ❄️ frozen-money territory. SET-07.3 shows it is
a **DATE OFFSET, not an amount**: *Late / penalty date = "Due + 5 days"*, with
the constraint *"Dates must land in order: read → bill → due → late"* and a
worked preview — *"Read 1–3 · exceptions cleared by 4th · bills out 5th · due
26th · late fee 31st"*. An offset is not a rate, so B4's percentage and minimum
are untouched.

**But it collides with two fields that already exist**, and this is the part to
resolve before anything is drawn: `late_grace_days` (BR-BIL-008) and
`late_grace_mode` (BR-BIL-002, calendar vs business) are **already configurable
today on the Billing defaults rule page**. So after this ships a tenant could
set *grace = 10 days* there and *"Due + 5 days"* here, and **nothing says which
one charges the fee.** Three readings and the PO must pick: (a) the cycle field
REPLACES the grace setting for accounts on that cycle; (b) it DISPLAYS the grace
setting resolved onto this cycle's calendar and is read-only; (c) they are
different things and both apply, in which case the interaction must be written
down before either is trusted. **Do not build the control until this is
answered** — two screens that each appear to set when a late fee starts is worse
than one screen that does.

**Two smaller facts worth capturing while they are visible.** SET-07.4 states
*"First run Oct 1, 2026"* — a cycle has a first-run date the written requirement
never mentions, and it is the thing that decides when the schedule takes effect.
And its footer reads *"Accounts on these routes bill on this cycle from the first
run — nothing already issued changes"*, which is the same immutability promise
SET-08 makes about numbers and hard rule 4 makes about issued invoices. Both
belong in the acceptance criteria.
