### CR-006 — PO ruling 2026-08-16: no money on Routes & Cycles

**PO verbatim:** *"you dont need late fees in this. so dont have anything related
to money when you create route and cycles."*

**SETTLED, and it dissolves the conflict rather than resolving it.** The
`Late / penalty date` control on SET-07.3 is **not built**. Grace therefore has
exactly ONE home — `late_grace_days` (BR-BIL-008) and `late_grace_mode`
(BR-BIL-002) on the Billing defaults rule page — and there is no second screen
that appears to decide when a late fee starts. That was the whole risk, and the
answer removes it instead of arbitrating it.

It also keeps ❄️ B4/B5 out of this CR completely: with no fee field, nothing on
these screens touches a finance-signed figure, and CR-006 needs no finance
re-sign at any point.

**MY READING OF THE BOUNDARY, stated so it is cheap to correct rather than
discovered later in code.** "Anything related to money" is read as *money
FIGURES and fee TRIGGERS*, not as *the billing calendar*. So:

* **REMOVED:** Late / penalty date, and any fee amount, rate or grace control.
* **KEPT:** read window, **bill date**, **due date**, frequency, first-run date.

The reason for the line falling there is the CR's own purpose sentence —
*"cycles drive the billing calendar"* — and r10's step 3 heading, *"When is it
read, billed, and due?"*. A cycle with no bill date and no due date cannot
schedule a bill run, which is the thing a cycle exists to do. A due date is a
DATE the calendar produces; a late fee is a CHARGE the frozen rules produce.
**If the PO meant the stricter reading — that due date must go too — say so and
the fields come out; they are not built yet.**

**One consequence to carry into the build:** SET-07.3's preview string reads
*"Read 1–3 · exceptions cleared by 4th · bills out 5th · due 26th · late fee
31st"*. Its last clause is now unbuildable from this screen's own data. The
preview either drops that clause or derives it from the Billing-defaults grace
setting and labels it as coming from there — **it must not be computed here**, or
the field returns through the back door as a calculation.

---

### CR-006 — PO ruling 2026-08-16 (second): a cycle is a DEFINITION, not a schedule

**PO verbatim, correcting the boundary this lane drew:** *"when we schedule a
cycle and run it at that time we wil take all inputs; here we are defining the
defiantion of cycles and how many Routes (Premises and Units -> accounts in it)
; this is group by defination, here you define it"*

**THIS SUPERSEDES THE READING ABOVE.** The previous section kept read window,
bill date and due date on the argument that "cycles drive the billing calendar".
The PO has ruled the stricter line: **SET-07 defines WHAT A CYCLE IS — its
identity and its membership — and the timing inputs are taken when the cycle is
actually scheduled and run.** A cycle is a GROUPING: routes → premises and units
→ accounts. It is not a calendar.

That reading is written down rather than the lane's, and the lane's is left
visible above rather than deleted, so the next agent can see that the obvious
boundary was the wrong one and why.

**What the definition therefore carries:** cycle code · name · frequency ·
the routes in it, and the rolled-up counts those routes imply (premises, units,
meters, accounts). Nothing that states a date on which money moves.

**ONE THING STILL AMBIGUOUS, and it is NOT re-asking the ruling — it is asking
where r10's step 3 goes.** r10 draws a *"Schedule"* step containing *Read window
1st–3rd of month · Bill date 5th · Due date 26th*. Those are DAY-OF-MONTH
DEFAULTS, not dates: they say "this cycle normally reads on the 1st–3rd", which
is arguably part of what a monthly cycle IS, and they are what the run would
prefill. Two possibilities and they build differently:

* **(a) Step 3 disappears.** The wizard becomes 3 steps — Details, Select
  routes, Review. Every timing input, defaults included, is taken at run time.
  r10's step 3 is stale.
* **(b) Step 3 survives as DEFAULTS ONLY**, clearly labelled as what the run
  will prefill and confirm, never as a commitment. The run still takes all
  inputs, as the ruling requires.

The difference is whether a monthly cycle knows its own normal read window. Both
honour *"we will take all inputs at run"*; only one keeps r10's step. **Not
guessed** — the last boundary this lane inferred was overturned by the PO one
message later, and inferring again would be the same mistake with more code
behind it.

---

### CR-006 — PO ruling 2026-08-16 (third): the cycle CARRIES defaults; the run may override

**PO verbatim:** *"this is correct ; you can capture the defaults , but allow
suer to override it during actual run"*

**CLOSES the step-3 question above: option (b).** r10's *Schedule* step SURVIVES
and the cycle wizard stays FOUR steps. What it stores are **day-of-month
DEFAULTS** — read window, bill date, due date — not dates and not commitments.
A monthly cycle knows its own normal shape; the run prefills from it and the
staff member may change it there.

**Consistent with the second ruling, not a softening of it.** *"When we schedule
a cycle and run it at that time we will take all inputs"* still holds exactly:
the run is where the inputs are taken. The defaults only decide what the run
STARTS with. A definition that says "normally the 1st–3rd" is still a
definition; it becomes a schedule only when a run commits it.

**The late/penalty default stays OUT.** Ruling one removed anything money-related
from these screens, and a default is still a statement about when a fee starts.
Grace keeps its single home on Billing defaults (BR-BIL-002/008). So the stored
defaults are read window · bill date · due date, and nothing else.

**MY READING OF THE OVERRIDE, stated in one line so it is correctable cheaply
rather than discovered in code:** an override at run applies TO THAT RUN and
does not rewrite the cycle's stored defaults — otherwise one unusual month
silently redefines the cycle, and the next month inherits a shape nobody chose.
If the PO wants an override to stick, it needs to be an explicit "save as the
new default" action rather than a side effect.

**Consequence for the preview strip** (unchanged from the first ruling): r10's
*"Read 1–3 · exceptions cleared by 4th · bills out 5th · due 26th · late fee
31st"* keeps every clause except the last. The late-fee clause is not computed
here.

| `template_service.py` | `register` · `save_draft` · `publish` (auto-archiving) · `archive` · `delete_version` · `resolve` with BR-BIL-025's five-step fallback · `load_pinned` · `pin_count` |
| `catalogs.py` | the per-class merge-variable WHITELIST — the thing that blocks an unknown token |
| `rendering.py` | `validate_body` + `render`, with named absences, tenant money and date formats, BR-TEN-017 identity |
| `seed_templates.py` | the two platform bodies (`dunning`, `receipt`), quoted from A13 |

**The only door was `GET /notification-templates`, a READ**, and its own trailer
says so: *"THE TEMPLATE READ IS A READ. `template_service` holds a complete
draft→publish→archive lifecycle and none of it is mounted."* So this CR built
**eight routes and two screens over a finished engine** — hard-won law 2 at the
largest scale it has appeared so far. **The CHANGELOG's "sixteen template
designers at r9" is A19's sixteen template CLASSES, not sixteen built screens;
S91–S96 were CUT and S94–S106 were never built.** Nothing was rebuilt.

#### The delta, counted

CR-007 names ~19 templates. **Five already existed** as notifications classes —
past-due reminder (`dunning` + its email and SMS siblings), payment receipt
(same), the payment-plan agreement, the disconnect notice, plus the bill and
statement classes **billing** owns (B2 r10 #4, deliberately not on this
catalog). **Fourteen did not exist**, and no signed document writes a
merge-field catalogue or a body for any of them → **OQ-251**. They are listed,
openable, versionable, and every save refuses by name.

**So the CR's "~19 new" is really 5 existing + 14 unspecified + 1 rule already
signed and unimplemented.** That last one is the important line.

#### What step 0 caught — DEF-190

**BR-NOT-014 gave the disconnection notice THREE slots on 2026-08-16 and the
code still had ONE.** The ruling reached the business-rules file, the decision
log and OQ-243's closure, and reached no code; every test passed over it. Built
here as three classes, **each carrying A19 §2's own tier tokens and not the
union**, so a 10-day warning cannot hold `{48h}` or `{certified_no}`. **The
remainder is filed, not taken:** `notices.generate_disconnect_notice` still
resolves the single legacy class at every tier. It refuses today for want of a
body, so no customer gets the wrong letter — **the day OQ-250 closes, one
would.**

#### The five things this build refused to guess

| Asked for | What shipped | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Final disconnect notice, one template | **THREE slots**, all empty | BR-NOT-014 signed; the wording is OQ-250 |
| *"Send test to me"* | rendered **DISABLED with its reason** | no dispatcher on any channel; PO *"no email yet"*; A11 r2 §4 makes a send endpoint a gate failure |
| *"Download sample PDF"* | rendered **DISABLED with a DIFFERENT reason** | the page writer is billing's and writes bills (OQ-149) |
| *"set default"* | rendered **DISABLED with its reason** | the default is the row's KEY, not a flag — OQ-252 |
| *"+ New template"* | ships as **+ New variant** | a tenant-invented class has no whitelist — OQ-253 |

Plus **OQ-254**: multi-language was checked before sizing exactly as the CR
asked. The variant's language axis has shipped since 2026-08-15; **nothing
stores a customer's preferred language**, so a published `es-MX` variant is
never selected for anybody, and the screen says so in the server's own words.

#### Proof

Four RED proofs quoted in the decision-log row and in the commits. 21 backend
tests + 14 frontend tests new; 147 backend notifications tests and 27 frontend
tests green; `tsc --noEmit` clean. **DEF-191** — a tenant-isolation defect this
lane introduced and its own test caught before commit — is filed and fixed.

#### Step 7 · VERSION

**2.4.0 → 2.7.0** (`<release>.<change>.<fix>` — R2, CR-007, no fix on top),
moved in `07-frontend/package.json` (the source of truth) and its derived copy
`06-backend/pyproject.toml` in the same commit.

**VERDICT.** Of **36 catalogued classes, THREE have a body** — the bill layouts
(billing's), `dunning` and `receipt` — and **exactly three activities queue
anything**: bill issue, the dunning reminder, and the payment receipt. The
product can produce **three of the ~29 documents its own specification
describes**. Every other absence is a REFUSAL with a named question, not a
silent gap, which is the posture DEF-163 established and CR-007 extended.

**Two findings the table surfaced that were not in any register:**

1. **RECONNECT HAS NO TEMPLATE AT ALL.** CR-007 names *"Disconnect/reconnect
   notice (door hanger …)"* and A19 has no reconnect class; `disconnect_notice`
   and its three tiers are all one-directional. A customer whose water is
   restored is told nothing, by design of an omission nobody made deliberately.
   **Folded into OQ-251** rather than minted separately — it is the same
   question (a class the CR names and no spec specifies).
2. **`email_plan_change` IS THE ONLY CLASS WITH A LIVE CALLER AND NO BODY.**
   `apps/customers/services.py` elects the notification, calls the seam, and
   appends the problem *"The plan change itself stands; the customer has NOT
   been told."* That is the one place in the product where an activity ALREADY
   tries to send and cannot — every other row above never tries.

**CONTRACTS specifically, since the PO asked:** four contract classes are
ratified (BR-NOT-004) — payment plan, service agreement, deposit, autopay
authorization. **Only the payment-plan agreement has a token catalogue**, and
OQ-244 is CLOSED (*"print the schedule inside the agreement"*) with the
instalment-table token **not yet built**. The other three have neither tokens
nor bodies (OQ-206). **Nothing contract-shaped is implied and unlisted.**

#### B · Language

| Question | Answer, with evidence |
|---|---|
| Is a per-account language preference stored? | **YES — and my own OQ-254 said no and was WRONG; it is corrected in the register.** `accounts.preferred_language` ships in `apps/customers/migrations/0001_initial.py` (B2 r15 #2), is writable via the account API (BR-CUS-064) and is validated against the tenant's seeded set through `customers.seams.tenant_languages`. |
| So what is missing? | **The READ and the PASS-THROUGH, one hop on.** `template_service.resolve` accepts `language=`; **no caller supplies it** — `apps/billing/delivery_seam.py:350` passes `language=None` as a literal and `apps/payments/notices.py` declares it optional and nothing fills it. Every resolution in the product lands on the `default` sentinel while the customer's stated preference sits two modules away. **This is a small wiring job, not a schema question.** |
| Do the 11 UI locales relate to template CONTENT? | **NO, and they must not.** `notification_templates.name` is documented as *"Tenant prose, deliberately NOT a message_key: it is the tenant's own words about their own document"*, and a version's `body` is the same. The 11 catalogues are UI chrome. The only shared thing is the language CODE vocabulary (BR-TEN-042's seeded set). |
| What does A19 require that is unbuilt? | A19's 2026-08-08 addendum: *"Template classes now carry language variants (BR-NOT-006, B2 r15)."* The AXIS is built and always has been; nothing else about language is specified. |
| Does r10 actually define a Spanish variant? | **NO.** CR-007's text says *"Bill · standard: default, large-print, Spanish, postcard summary"*, and r10's own `TPL.bill.variants` is `['Standard','Large print','E-bill summary email','Budget billing']` — **no Spanish variant exists in r10.** The word "Spanish" appears twice in the whole prototype and not in any variant list. The CR's sentence is illustrative, which the PO has since confirmed of that list generally. |

#### C · Branding — **the largest gap found, and it is DEF-192**

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Does any template render the logo? | **NO. Nothing in the product renders it, anywhere.** |
| Can the bytes even be read? | **NO.** One route exists (`POST /settings/company/logo`); none streams the image back. `api.py`'s own trailer: *"no GET/DELETE for the logo: no signed-URL/document-delivery contract exists in core."* |
| Does the settings letterhead preview show it? | **NO — and this is the part I expected to be fine.** `SettingsCompanyTab` draws `.settings-letterhead-mark`, which `SettingsPage.css` defines as a **26 × 26 px solid block filled with `brand_primary_hex`** beside `dba_name` in bold. A colour swatch plus the name — **identical with a logo on file and without one.** |
| Do printable templates use the brand colours? | **NO.** `documents.py` is Base-14 monochrome by design and is never passed a colour; the two hex values feed exactly one CSS custom property in Settings. |
| Is there a live trap? | **YES, and CR-007's own screens just exposed it to a person for the first time.** `catalogs._UTILITY_IDENTITY` puts `{utility_logo}` in **every printable class's palette**, and `rendering.render` supplies no value for it — so a System Admin who inserts the token the merge-field panel offers gets `——` on a customer's letter. |
| What happens with NO logo uploaded? | **The question does not yet bite, because the logo reaches no document even when there IS one.** No rule states a fallback for a real document — **OQ-257**, with the recommendation (the utility's NAME IN TEXT) recorded as UNRULED rather than implemented. |

**The cheapest honest fix, and the only one shippable today: REMOVE
`{utility_logo}` from the palette**, so the product stops offering a token it
cannot honour. The other three parts need a core document-delivery contract, a
raster-capable renderer (OQ-149's engine decision) and a PO ruling in that
order. **Not taken by this lane — all three land in other modules.**

#### D · Size / format — **ruled as a model, open as a value set: OQ-256**

The PO ruled the MODEL on 2026-08-17: *"take this as input and standardize the
sizes - user lnaguage ; those where for sample and example only"* — r10's
variant list is illustrative, and the model standardizes into **SIZE/FORMAT ·
LANGUAGE · CONTENT** as separate axes. **The strongest evidence for that ruling
is r10's own list**, which collapses three unrelated ideas: *Large print* is
size, *E-bill summary email* is a DELIVERY KIND, *Budget billing* is content.

**What could NOT be grounded, and is therefore OQ-256 rather than a build:**
A19 says exactly one thing about paper — *"Single page, letter/A4"* — and
`documents.py` hardcodes US Letter, saying so. **r9's paper-size control cannot
be recovered**: the CHANGELOG records it, S91–S96 were CUT, and neither
prototype contains one today, so what sizes it offered is **not knowable from
the repo and was not reconstructed from memory.** Door hanger and postcard are
evidenced as FORMATS; **the #10 window envelope is a layout constraint on the
remittance stub, not a page size.** OQ-256 carries the three consequences the
answer decides — what "set default" means across three axes, what SET-09's
"Variants: N" counts, and what a notification rule picks — plus this lane's
reading (size is a RENDER property, not a body) offered to be corrected cheaply.

#### E · The r10 corrected-bill copy — **one contradiction, reported not edited**

The PO instructed that SET-10.corrected's body is r10's wording, to transcribe
rather than reword, and to report any contradiction with a signed rule.
**There is one, and it is not cosmetic.**

> r10 `TPL.corrected.foot`: *"**The original bill is void.** Both are on your
> account history."*

**BR-BIL-004 is CONFIRMED:** *"Issued invoices/lines are immutable; corrections
= credit note / rebill"*, and BR-BIL-041 class R spells the mechanism out —
*"full credit note for the original total + rebill"*. **A void and a credit note
are different mechanisms with different ledger effects**, and CLAUDE.md rule 4
forbids UPDATE or DELETE on an issued invoice. Telling a customer their original
bill is *void* describes something this product does not and may not do.
**Two further clauses are unverified rather than contradicted** — *"your due
date stays Aug 26"* and *"autopay picks up the new amount"*: no signed rule
states that a rebill inherits the original's due date, and the autopay behaviour
on a rebill is not written anywhere I could find. **Not edited, not seeded:**
`email_corrected_bill` has no token catalogue (OQ-251) and r10's dotted token
spelling (`{{bill.original_total}}`) is a DIFFERENT vocabulary from `catalogs`'
single-brace names — adopting it would be DEF-185 again — so the copy is
recorded here for the PO and reaches no customer.

#### Rollback

Revert the CR-007 commits. **Nothing is at risk in the data:** this CR
adds no migration and no column. Template CLASSES are code constants, so a
revert removes the three disconnect slots and the fourteen new listings from
the catalog; any `notification_templates` row a System Admin created against
them survives as an orphan row that `resolve` would refuse by name — visible,
not silent. Any version SAVED through the new editor stays, because versions
are append-only by law, and the existing `GET /notification-templates` read
keeps serving them.

### CR-007 addendum — the requirements added after capture (2026-08-16)

The PO added five things after the initial capture. All are IN SCOPE for CR-007
and are written here rather than living in chat, because the build lane reads the
repo and not the conversation (hard-won law 10).

**A · THE DETAIL SCREEN'S SHAPE IS CONFIRMED.** The PO showed SET-10.corrected
and said *"it will look like this"*. Right rail, three stacked panels in order:
**Merge fields** — token on the left, its **RESOLVED SAMPLE VALUE** on the right
(`{{bill.original_total}}` → **$32.22**, `{{correction.reason}}` → *Verified
re-read*), so sample data binds per template and insert-on-click sits on those
rows · **Where it's used** — ONE plain sentence, not a list of ids (*"Sent
automatically when a rebill posts."*) · **History** — dated, authored, and
saying WHAT changed (*"Jul 30 · Priya Menon — softened wording"*). Above the
artefact: `Previewing as` · delivery kind · `sample data: Jordan Alvarez ·
ACCT-10021` · a `Default variant` pill. **Variant tabs render even at ONE
variant**, so the CR's *"each category must have at least one alternative
variant"* is a CATALOG-level statement, never a per-template one — do not invent
variants to satisfy it.

⚠ The rendered body carries money (**$32.22 · $24.02 · −$8.20**). Those are
sample values resolved from merge fields, **not rates and not figures this
screen sets**. Nothing in the template editor may compute or store an amount.

**B · THE HOLISTIC COVERAGE AUDIT.** PO verbatim: *"we will ahve to look at it
holistcailly that are we able to enable and match all those requirements where we
ahve to product the document as part of activity and do we have tempalte
available for that"*. Every activity in the product that PRODUCES a document or
message is walked — bill issue, rebill/correction, each dunning stage,
disconnect, reconnect, payment received, payment failed/NSF, refund, deposit
received/applied/refunded, payment plan agreement, write-off, move-in,
move-out/final bill, rate change, statement, receipt — and each is answered
**template exists? · reachable?**. **Contracts are named explicitly** by the PO;
the payment-plan agreement is the one that exists and anything else
contract-shaped is reported as implied-and-unbuilt.

**C · UNMET EXISTING REQUIREMENTS, which the PO believes are in the notifications
module.** A15 (notifications) and A19 (document templates) are read against what
is built, rule by rule, with any still-OPEN template-shaped question. This is a
"what was specified and never built" list, not a design exercise.

**D · BRANDING — and this is the gap I most expect.** Company profile stores a
LOGO and TWO BRAND COLOURS (BR-TEN-019), and its letterhead preview renders
them. **Do the templates use any of it?** A previously-reported exception says
the logo endpoint returns a **REFERENCE** and **no route streams the bytes
back**, and that BR-TEN-019's *"rasterized for PDF/print"* clause was deferred to
a renderer. **If the logo is stored and nothing can draw it into a document,
that is hard-won law 2 at the most visible surface in the product — the bill
every customer receives — and it is a defect, not a nice-to-have.**

**E · LANGUAGE.** Establish (a) whether ANY per-account language preference is
stored today, (b) that the eleven UI locale catalogues have nothing to do with
template CONTENT — template content is tenant prose, and the evidence must be
shown rather than asserted, (c) what A15/A19 require about language that is
unbuilt, and (d) whether r10 actually DEFINES the Spanish variant the CR text
mentions.

**F · DOCUMENT SIZES, AND THE COMBINATION THEY CREATE.** PO verbatim: *"Also you
ahve differn sizes on each document, standard sizes that user can select and
combination due to it"*.

*May already exist:* the CHANGELOG records at r9 a WYSIWYG document designer with
a controls rail including **paper size**. Find it, say what it offers, say
whether size is STORED or only a preview toggle. Do not rebuild it.

*The question that decides the model:* **is size a property of a VARIANT, or an
independent AXIS?** (a) a property — simple, but *Large print · A4* and *Large
print · Letter* become two variants maintained twice; (b) an axis — one body, N
variants × M sizes, but then "set default" means a default VARIANT **and** a
default SIZE, SET-09's *"Variants: 4"* column becomes ambiguous, and notification
rules must pick both.

**THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE IS r10'S OWN VARIANT LIST, and it argues the model is
currently muddled.** Bill · standard lists *Standard · Large print · E-bill
summary email · Budget billing* — **"Large print" is a rendering concern,
"Budget billing" is a CONTENT concern, and "E-bill summary email" is a DELIVERY
KIND.** Three different axes collapsed into one list. **Not decided by a lane —
an OQ, with that evidence attached.**

*Sizes with evidence vs sizes that would be guesses:* **door hanger** and
**postcard** are named in the CR and in r10, so they are evidence. Letter, Legal
and A4 are assumptions unless a document states them. And the **#10 window
envelope** is a constraint rather than a size — the remittance stub must align
with the window, which shapes layout, not just page dimensions.

**EXECUTION NOTE.** A–F do NOT block the build. CR-007 ships what it specifies;
B, C, D, E and F's audit half are reported alongside it, and each finding becomes
a defect row or an OQ rather than silent extra scope.

### CR-005 — BUILT, NOT CLOSED (2026-08-16). Version 2.5.0.

**Status: BUILT-NOT-PROVEN.** Every part of r11 step 2 is done except (d): there
has been **no browser walkthrough**, and the CR's own words are *"we need final
confirmation it working on screen"*. CR-004 met that bar only after a
walkthrough found five screens returning HTTP 500 while every test was green.
**Built and green is not the same statement**, so this CR does not close.

**THE FINDING THAT MATTERS IS A LIVE PRODUCTION BUG, and measuring what existed
is what found it.** `SERIES_DEFAULTS` was a hand-typed literal with **five**
entries while `core.numbering.KNOWN_SERIES` held **nine**. So the `JE-` series
had no row on any tenant, and **every manual journal entry ever posted is
unnumbered**. BR-LED-021 (i) predicted exactly this and named the fix as
tenancy's; nobody had done it. `DEP-`, `RCT-` and `EXP-` were in the same state,
and metering had been asking for `premises`/`unit`/`read_batch` since it was
built and getting `numbering_series_missing` back.

Fixed with `SERIES_CATALOG` — ONE source feeding both the screen's options and
the seed, so a series cannot be known-and-unseeded and a tenant cannot hold a
format its own dropdown does not offer. Seeding is wired into the `seed_demo
--tenant` repair door so existing hosts can be fixed.

**A SECOND REAL BUG FELL OUT OF THE FIRST GREEN RUN:** turning restart-per-period
on reset the counter on the very next number, **discarding an admin's 18,411**. A
first allocation now adopts its period and the restart begins at the next
boundary.

**The permissions ruling required NO CHANGE.** Both endpoints were already
`SystemAdminOnly` and the frontend already took `readOnly` from the
server-computed set. The lane kept the gating byte-identical rather than
implementing it again — which is what "follow the same rule" actually asks for.

**TWO GUARDS WOULD NOT GO RED AND NEITHER WAS ACCEPTED.** The transaction test
was a no-op nested `atomic`. The permission test stayed GREEN with the
endpoint's gate removed, because the service's own `@require_role` refused
underneath — the permission class is asserted directly now and both gates stay.
A third passed with the read-only reason deleted, because the same sentence sits
on twenty other controls; it is markup-exact now. That is DEF-182's shape a
fourth time in one session.

**THREE OQs RATHER THAN GUESSES.** **OQ-250** — the CR says pad "4–8", but
`ADJ-{000}` is seeded on every tenant and nine r10 options sit below four; the
upper bound is enforced and the lower is not, because enforcing it would make an
untouched row unsaveable. **OQ-251** — the CR names **16** entities and r10 draws
**14**, and they are not the same 14; built as the **union of 22** so no lane
chose between two PO artefacts of the same day. Trimming is the PO's call.
**OQ-252** — a backdated issuance under a restart is refused BY NAME rather than
minting a number the earlier period already used.

**NOT CLAIMED:** no browser walkthrough · import flows are NOT wired to these
formats · the picker is r10's native `<select>`, not the CR's prose "searchable
dropdown" · nothing here touched a rate, a fee or any ❄️ B4/B5 figure.

**Tests:** backend 106 passed (24 new + 28 existing numbering + 54 ledger and
metering consumers). Frontend `tsc` clean, 235 passed across 16 tenancy suites.

**TO CLOSE:** the browser walkthrough — change a format and save it, reset a
counter and see it refused when set backwards, watch the preview and the
right-rail sample update live.

#### The walkthrough ran (2026-08-17). CR-005 STILL DOES NOT CLOSE.

**Seven of eight requirements pass on a real browser against a live stack.** A
format changes and persists across a reload · a custom format with an unknown
token is refused with readable English · the counter reset refuses a backwards
value by name · the right-rail sample re-renders as you type · the immutability
sentence is on screen · `v2.5.0` is displayed. Spec:
`07-frontend/e2e/CR-005-numbering.spec.ts`.

**Requirement 8 — the permissions ruling — FAILS, and it fails in the direction
this CR's own record called settled.** Signed in as a real Executive, `GET
/settings/number-series` answers **403** and the screen reads *"You don't have
access to this. Your role can't open this Settings tab. Ask a System Admin."*
The PO ruled that role may **look and not change**; the product denies the read.
So **every `readOnly` branch in `SettingsNumberingTab` is unreachable code.**

**The sentence three paragraphs up — *"The permissions ruling required NO CHANGE
— both endpoints were already `SystemAdminOnly`"* — is where it went wrong, and
it is left standing rather than edited** because it is the evidence: both halves
of that sentence are individually true (the endpoint IS `SystemAdminOnly`; the
frontend DOES take `readOnly` from the server) and together they cancel the
ruling out. Keeping a gate byte-identical is the right move only when the gate
already matched the rule, and nobody checked that it did.

**235 green frontend tests could not see it** because they pass `readOnly` as a

decide.** r10's variant list on Bill · standard — *Standard · Large print ·
E-bill summary email · Budget billing* — is **ILLUSTRATIVE ONLY**. It is not the
model and it is not a set to reproduce. The PO has confirmed the reading that it

**Standardize into SEPARATE, NAMED axes** rather than one "variants" list:

* **SIZE / FORMAT** — a standard set the user selects from
* **LANGUAGE** — a standard tag ("user language")

already ships a paper-size control (CHANGELOG) — what it offers is evidence;
**door hanger** and **postcard** are evidenced in r10 and in the CR; and the
**#10 window envelope is a LAYOUT CONSTRAINT for the remittance stub, not a page
size**. Any value the standard set needs that nothing states gets an OQ for that
VALUE only — the model itself is now ruled.

**Consequences to be reported, not assumed:** what *"set default"* means once
size and language are their own axes, what SET-09's *"Variants: N"* column
counts, and what a notification rule must pick.

### CR-007 — PO RULINGS 2026-08-17: deactivation gets a confirm and an undo; the 36 template bodies get authored

**Both questions from the walkthrough were put to the PO in plain English and both were answered.**

#### 1 · Deactivating a template — **"Okay"**, i.e. build the confirm and the undo

**PO verbatim, answering the proposal:** *"One decision: deactivating a template
is one click, no confirmation, no way back. On a default template that leaves the
product unable to produce a notice. I'd add a confirmation and an undo — but 'no
undo' might be deliberate."* → **"Okay"**.

So **DEF-209 is ruled, not merely filed**, and all three parts ship:

* a **confirm** before the commit, in the **danger tier** (B14 rule 6 — a
  destructive commit is never the standard primary);
* the confirm **shows what it will break**, which costs nothing to compute
  because **the server already sends it** — `resolution_after` is on the payload
  today and the screen throws it away (B14 rule 11, consequence preview);
* a **Reactivate** control, so the act stops being one-way through the UI.

**"No undo" was NOT deliberate** — that is what the question established, and it
is written here so nobody re-litigates it from the absence of a control.

#### 2 · The 34 empty template classes — **"please define it for this product"**

**PO verbatim:** *"One gap: 34 of 36 template types have no content, so the email
subject line and SMS counter you asked for have never rendered for anyone. -
please define it for this product"*.

**This is an AUTHORING instruction, and it is delegated to us.** The catalogue
declares **36 classes** and only two print classes carry a body, so CR-007's own
acceptance items — *"subject line (email)"* and a *"160-char SMS counter"* — have
**never rendered for any user**, because both are gated on `channel`, which stays
null until a variant is published.

**The 36, by channel:** **4 SMS** (bill ready · past due · payment received ·
disconnect supplement) · **14 email** (welcome · bill ready · statement · payment
receipt · payment failed/NSF · autopay · credit issued · refund issued · deposit
received · past due · corrected bill · plan or rate change · move-out final ·
account closed) · **18 print, contract and service** (two bills · statement ·
receipt · bill insert · dunning · three disconnect tiers · write-off notice ·
four contracts · three payment-plan notices · four service notices).

**Constraints on the authoring, so it is checkable rather than a matter of
taste:**

* **Every merge token must be in that class's own palette.** `catalogs.py`
  declares the whitelist per class and `rendering.validate_body` enforces it —
  an invented token is refused at save, which is the right behaviour and makes
  the palette the specification.
* ⚠ **`{utility_logo}` MUST NOT BE USED.** It is offered by every printable
  class's palette and the render context supplies no value for it, so a body
  using it prints the named absence `——` on a customer's letter (DEF-195). Until
  that is fixed or the token is withdrawn, no authored body may reference it.
* **SMS bodies stay under 160 characters** — the counter the CR asks for exists
  to be obeyed, not just displayed.
* **Nothing may state a figure, a fee, a deadline or a legal right that is not
  already ruled.** The three disconnect tiers carry a regulated ladder
  (BR-NOT-014) and `{state_puc_ref}` is mandatory on all three; a body that
  invents a notice period is a compliance defect wearing a copy deck.
* **English only in this pass.** These are content, not UI strings, and a
  tenant edits them — pushing 36 bodies through ten machine translations would
  ship worse text than an English default a utility overwrites.

**Tracked as DEF-210.**

| Constraint | How it is held |

This is the part worth reading, because "we defined the templates" must never

* **Six citations of `OQ-250` in the notifications code were the WRONG QUESTION.**

### CR-007 — open: the no-logo default (PO question, 2026-08-16)

**PO asked:** *"also consider what if customer dont upload logo what happen in
that case, what ais default"*

**Answered in the branding audit, not guessed.** Today the Company-settings
letterhead preview falls back to the utility's name in text when no logo is on
file — but that is **preview behaviour, and no rule states it for a real
document**. The audit reports: what the preview does, what a generated document
would do, and whether any rule states a fallback at all.

**Recommendation put to the PO and NOT yet ruled:** fall back to the utility's
**name in text** where the logo would go. A bill with a blank corner reads as
broken; a bill with the name reads as deliberate.

**The larger question behind it, in plain terms for whoever reads this next:** a
utility uploads a logo, the settings screen previews it correctly, and **there is
no code path that hands that image to a document generator** — the logo is stored
as a reference, no route streams the bytes, and the rasterize-for-print half of
BR-TEN-019 was deferred to a renderer. If that still holds, the logo never
reaches a bill, and the utility has every reason to think it works because the
screen shows it working. Same stored-configured-previewed-wired-to-nothing
pattern as the rest of this session, on the one artefact every customer sees.
**A defect row follows the audit's evidence.**

### CR-007 — PO ruling 2026-08-16: no logo means a GENERATED mark, not empty and not plain text

**PO verbatim:** *"Create name based or initial base dummy logo"*

**Better than the recommendation it answers.** This lane proposed falling back to
the utility's name in text; the PO ruled a **generated placeholder mark** derived
from the name or its initials — the shape a user avatar uses. A document then
always carries a mark in the logo's position, so the layout never has a hole and
never has a bare word sitting where an image belongs.

**What this settles:** every printable document has SOMETHING in the logo slot
from the tenant's first day, before anyone uploads anything. There is no
"unbranded" state to design around and no empty-corner case in any template.

**What it does NOT settle, and must not be guessed** — the mark is generated, so
its rules are real: initials from the DBA name or the legal name (they differ —
*Silver Creek Water* vs *Silver Creek Water & Sanitation District*); one letter
or two; which colour it uses (the tenant HAS `brand_primary_hex`, so using it is
the obvious answer and is still a choice); and what it does at print resolution,
since a CSS-drawn mark and a rasterised one are different pieces of work. Those
go to the PO as one small question rather than being invented.

**⚠ THIS RULING LANDS ON TOP OF A DEFECT, NOT A BLANK SLATE — DEF-195.** The
audit found the logo is uploaded, hashed, stored and audited and **drawn
NOWHERE**. The Company-settings "letterhead preview" is a 26×26px colour block
plus the name, and it renders **identically with a logo and without one** — so
the screen a utility uses to confirm their branding cannot tell them whether
their upload worked.

**And CR-007 exposed a live trap while building on it:** `{utility_logo}` is in
**every printable merge-field palette**, and `render` supplies no value — so a
user who clicks the token the panel offers gets **`——` printed on a customer's
letter**. The cheapest honest fix, shippable immediately, is to REMOVE THE TOKEN
until something can draw it. A palette that offers a field the renderer cannot
fill is worse than a palette missing it.

So the order is: remove the trap · build the generated mark to the PO's ruling ·
wire real logos to documents. The ruling above is step two, and step one is not
optional.

### CR-007 — the generated logo mark, specified (PO ruling 2026-08-16)

**PO verbatim, on how many letters:** *"2 letters"*

**RULED:** the placeholder mark carries **TWO letters**.

**DERIVED, not invented — the other two details, each taken from behaviour the
product already has, and each correctable in one line if wrong:**

**Which name → the DBA (trading name), falling back to the legal name when DBA
is empty.** Not a preference: `SettingsCompanyTab`'s letterhead preview ALREADY
renders `dba_name === "" ? legal_name : dba_name`, and `rendering.py` resolves
`utility_name` the same way — `identity.get("dba_name") or
identity.get("legal_name")`. Two places already agree, so the mark uses the
third. It is also the name a customer sees: r10's bill header prints **Silver
Creek Water**, not *Silver Creek Water & Sanitation District*. **Worth noting
the PO's own example resolves identically either way** — both names begin
"Silver Creek", so both give **SC**. The rule matters for the tenant whose
trading name is not a prefix of its legal one.

**Which colour → `brand_primary_hex`.** The tenant already sets it on Company
profile, it is described there as *"used on printed bills, the customer portal
and outgoing email"*, and it is the only brand colour that is not the bill
ACCENT. A generated mark in the accent would compete with the accent's own job.

**STILL NOT DERIVABLE, and a question rather than a guess:** what the mark does
at PRINT resolution. A CSS-drawn mark and a rasterised one are different pieces
of work, and BR-TEN-019's *"rasterized for PDF/print"* clause was deferred to a
renderer that does not exist — the same gap as DEF-195. So the mark can ship on
SCREEN now and cannot ship on a PDF until that renderer does. **Say that plainly
rather than letting "the logo problem is solved" mean two different things.**

**Order of work is unchanged and step one is still not optional:** remove the
`{utility_logo}` trap · build the generated mark on screen · wire real logos and
the mark to documents when a renderer exists.

### CR-005 · CR-006 · CR-007 — PO ruling 2026-08-16: Settings is System Admin only

**PO verbatim:** *"all settingsa re Admin only I believ; follow same rule that we
folowed for settings related permission"*

**Applies to all three open CRs at once.** Each of them was written as
*"Owner + Admin only"* or *"Owner/Admin edit; others read-only"*, and **neither
role exists**: the ruled set is **System Admin · Billing Clerk · Executive**
(PO today, *"we keep 3 roles for time being"*). Owner and Admin come from r10's
five-role vocabulary, which the same PO declined hours earlier. Rather than
translate that phrase three different ways in three CRs, it is translated once
here.

**THE RULE: every Settings surface these CRs add is SYSTEM ADMIN ONLY, gated
exactly as the shipped Settings surfaces already are.** Concretely, and this is
"the same rule we followed" made explicit so nobody re-derives it:

* Backend: the `SystemAdminOnly` permission class, the way `/lookups/*` and the
  Users & roles endpoints are already gated (BR-IDN-009).
* Frontend: the SERVER-computed access set decides, never a client-side role-name
  check — BR-SHL-025 forbids the latter.
* A role that may not write sees the screen **read-only with its reason on the
  control**, never a hidden or missing control (BR-SHL-025 again). Billing Clerk
  and Executive can LOOK at numbering formats, routes, cycles and templates;
  they cannot change them.

**Nothing new is invented by this ruling** — it points three CRs at the gate the
product already uses, which is what "follow the same rule" asks for. The value is
that "Owner/Admin" is now dead vocabulary in this register and cannot be
implemented literally by a lane reading only its own CR.

**One consequence worth stating, because it is the practical effect:** a Billing
Clerk cannot change how bills are numbered, which route a premises reads on, or
the wording of a disconnect notice. That is the outcome the caution was about —
a permission rule guessed wrong is how a clerk ends up editing the bill numbering
format — and it is now settled rather than assumed.

### CR-005 — PO ruling 2026-08-16: the Work numbering rows ship NOW, standalone

**PO verbatim:** *"Yes; it should work standalone in settings; we will link it
later ith work"*

**CR-005's only blocker is closed.** Work order # · Service template # ·
Dispatch batch # are built now, as number series like any other. A series that

No table for work orders, crews or parts is created by this; the module question
— tenth module or tabs on assets — stays open and untouched.

### The principle underneath, now stated three times and applied across the register

The PO has given the same instruction in three different words on one day:

* **CR-006:** *"when we schedule a cycle and run it at that time we wil take all
  inputs; here we are defining the defiantion of cycles"*
* **CR-007:** *"here we are buling the setting and it should standalone wwork the
  connecting it with actual workflow ... we will take acare later; you can make a
  provision for it"*
* **CR-005:** *"it should work standalone in settings; we will link it later ith
  work"*

**THE RULE: a Settings screen defines a thing and must work on its own. The
wiring into the workflow that consumes it is a separate, later piece of work,
and its absence is not a reason to defer the definition.** Written here as a
rule because three CRs needed it and a fourth will.

**Applied, and this is an APPLICATION of a stated principle rather than a fresh
ruling — correct it if that is wrong:**

* **CR-006's** *"Dispatch can filter work orders by route/area"* is a downstream
  link, not a deliverable. Routes and cycles are defined now; dispatch consumes
  them in R5.
* **CR-007's** *"Service & field"* template category — appointment, work
  completed, door hanger, outage — is **wording**, and wording can exist before
  the flow that sends it. Those templates are catalogued and editable now.

**So the Work question that blocked three CRs is closed for all three.** What
remains open is only OQ-249 itself: whether Work is a tenth module, which tables
it owns, and where it sits in the build order. None of these CRs needs that
answered, because none of them creates a work order — they create a format, a
grouping and a piece of wording.

**Still open on CR-006, and unaffected by this:** the sub-area shape. The Areas
list is flat and the route wizard filters on area AND sub-area.

### CR-006 — PO RULINGS 2026-08-17: all three blockers answered

The three were put to the PO as a table with the observed behaviour and worked
options. **All three are ruled and CR-006 has no unanswered question left.**

| Blocker | What a person saw | PO ruling |
|---|---|---|
| **A · one route ever** | The wizard pre-fills `RT-001`; save it, reopen *+ Add route*, it offers `RT-001` again and refuses *"A route with that code already exists."* | **(i) the screen stops sending the code and lets the server allocate** |
| **B · a draft empties a live route** | `Route 2 · Mason Rd` went from **1 premises / 2 units / 3 meters** to **0 / 0 / 0** while still Active and still inside cycle 08-A | **(i) a draft may NOT take a premises off an active route — refuse, and name the route** |
| **C · the area filter returns nothing** | Ticking any area chip takes the picker from *"9 premises match"* to *"0 premises match"* | **already ruled** — the pickers go on the premises form |

**Ruling A, and why it is the right one rather than merely the cheapest.** The
two halves were each built correctly and nothing compared them: `create_route`
allocates from the numbering series **only when the payload carries no code**
(*"an absent code is use-the-series"*), and the wizard **always** sends the code
it pre-filled from `GET /routes/next-code` — which is a **preview that allocates
nothing**. Option (ii), letting the server silently pick a different code when
the sent one is taken, would have hidden a genuine duplicate typed by a human;
option (iii) costs a round-trip for nothing. **(i) makes the preview a preview**
and leaves the one allocator that exists as the only allocator.

**Ruling B is a REFUSAL, and it settles what a draft means.** The claim *"a draft
affects nothing"* was **proved about service points and asserted about
everything**: a draft correctly stamps no service point, so Reads and Billing
genuinely cannot see it — and that is what the backend tests check. But
`_set_route_membership` writes membership rows **whatever the status**, and the
Members and Meters columns a utility reads on the landing count **memberships**.
So the rule was tested at the layer where it holds and shipped at the layer where
it does not. The PO's ruling makes the sentence true at both layers: **a draft may
not remove a premises from an ACTIVE route at all.** The refusal must **name the
route** — *"1408 Bluestem Ln is on Route 2 · Mason Rd, which is active"* — because
a refusal that only says "no" leaves the admin with no next step.

**With these, CR-006's remaining work is entirely ours:** A and B are fixes, C is
a build the PO has already specified. No open question blocks it.

### CR-006 — PO RULING 2026-08-17: **the area picker goes ON THE PREMISES FORM.** DEF-220/221 answered.

**The question put to the PO** was whether the missing area-tagging was CR-006
scope or its own change. **They answered with the BEHAVIOUR instead, which is the
better answer. Verbatim:**

> *"when we add premises you should allow to select areas and sub areas on
> premises"*

**So it is CR-006 scope, and the shape is settled:** the **Area** and **Sub-area**
selectors live on the **premises create/edit form** — the moment a premises is
added — not on the Routes & Cycles screen and not as a bulk-tagging tool.

**That is the right home and it closes a loop that was open on both ends.** The
2026-08-16 ruling said areas are *"tenant-defined, tagged to premises, filtered
one-to-many"*, and CR-006 built two of those three: the areas list (CR-004) and
the multi-select chip filter on the route picker. **Nothing could put a premises
in an area**, so the filter that shipped could only ever return **zero rows** —
ticking any chip took the picker from *"9 premises match"* to *"0 premises
match"*. Both halves existed and neither could reach the other.

**What this ruling requires, measured:**

* **`premises.area_id` already exists** — CR-006 shipped the column. **The WRITE
  PATH was never built**: the premises API refuses the field, so the column has
  never held a value on any tenant. That is DEF-220's substance.
* **`areas.parent_id` already exists** too, and **no screen can create a
  sub-area** on a card literally named *"Areas & sub-areas"* (DEF-221). The
  PO's sentence names sub-areas explicitly, so the picker is **two levels** and
  the reference-data card needs the child-creating half.
* **The filter needs no change.** It was built correctly and has simply never had
  data to filter.

**⚠ AND BR-MET-082 MAKES THIS MORE THAN A FORM FIELD.** The PO's route model is a
live cascade — *"any change any movement make the changes to downstream"* — and a
route can already carry an `area_id`. So **tagging a premises into an area should
put it on that area's routes without anyone re-opening the route wizard.** A form
field that only writes a column would satisfy this ruling's letter and not its
purpose; DEF-225 is the same gap one level up and the two want fixing together.

### CR-006 — PO ruling 2026-08-16: areas are tenant-defined, tagged to premises, filtered one-to-many

**PO verbatim:** *"user can define their own areas and we wil tag them to
premises ; in CR06 you can use area and sub area for filtering - all option 1 to
many options will be required"*

**CR-006's last gap closes.** Three things are settled:

1. **Areas are TENANT-DEFINED.** That is already true and needs no change —
   BR-TEN-036 makes every reference list platform-seeded and tenant-extensible,
   and the four seeded rows (NORTH, DTWN, EAST, IND) are defaults a utility may
   extend, rename or deactivate.
2. **Areas are TAGGED TO PREMISES.** A premises carries its area. That is the
   link the route wizard's step-2 filter reads, and it does not exist today —
   `areas` was shipped as a vocabulary with nothing pointing at it. **This is
   real work: a premises → area reference, plus the way a utility assigns it.**
3. **The filter is ONE-TO-MANY with an All option.** Not a single-select. r10's
   SET-06.2 already draws it as removable chips (*"Area: South ×"*), which is
   the same shape.

**MY READING OF THE SHAPE, stated because the ruling settles the BEHAVIOUR and
not the table** — correct it cheaply now rather than after it is built:

**One list, self-referencing.** A row with no parent is an AREA; a row whose
parent is another row is a SUB-AREA of it. That is the minimal shape that keeps
r10's single *"Areas & sub-areas"* card honest, keeps one vocabulary for a
utility to manage, and lets a premises hold ONE reference that resolves to both
levels. The alternative — a second list keyed to the first — needs a second card
r10 does not draw and a second screen to manage.

So `areas` gains a nullable self-FK. It is an ADDITION to a shipped table with
no rows depending on it yet, so it costs one migration and no backfill.

**Consequence for the seeded vocabulary:** the four seeded rows are all
top-level. r10's card says *"3 sub-areas"* and draws none, and SET-06.2 shows
*"South · SE"* and *"South · SW"* in a premises list — **a "South" area that is
not among the four seeded**. The seed is r10's own and stays as it is; sub-area
rows are the tenant's to create. Recorded so nobody "fixes" the seed to match a
screenshot that disagrees with r10's own list data.

**CR-006 is now fully unblocked** — money settled, definition-vs-schedule
settled, defaults settled, Work settled, permissions settled, sub-areas settled.

> ⚠ **THESE THREE HEADERS READ *"CAPTURED. Not analysed, not started"* UNTIL 2026-08-17, WITH THIRTEEN COMMITS BEHIND THEM.** Same failure as CR-004's, ten days apart and now three times over: a status is written at the TOP when a CR is raised, the work is recorded at the BOTTOM as it lands, and the two drift in silence. CR-004's stale header cost a real audit — the money sweep of 2026-08-17 read it and reported a CLOSED change request as incomplete. **Nothing in this repo reads prose for truth**, which is what CLAUDE.md's step 0 exists for; until a check exists, the habit is to amend the header in the same commit that lands the work.

that makes capturing it verbatim more important than usual, not less.

### What the PO asked for, verbatim

> "Requirements — SET-12 / SET-12D · Settings → Notifications
> **Purpose** One place to control every message the system sends — customer and staff. Separation of concerns: Notifications decide **when** and **to whom**; Templates (Configure → Templates) define **what it says**. Every rule change is versioned and audit-logged.
> **Global bar (top of SET-12)**
> * Quiet hours: no customer SMS between a configurable window (default 9:00 PM – 8:00 AM)
> * Sender identity: from-email + SMS number
> * ✎ edit opens a small form (quiet-hours window, sender email verified via SPF/DKIM check, SMS number from telephony integration); Owner/Admin only
> **SET-12 · Event matrix (overview table)**
> Columns: Event | Audience (Customer / Staff pill) | Channels (tags; disabled channels dimmed) | Timing (plain text) | On (toggle) | Actions (✎ edit rule, ➤ send test)
> Events, grouped by category (16 total):
> 1. Billing: Bill ready (Email+SMS+Portal, on issue) · Bill corrected/rebilled (Email, on correction)
> 2. Payments: Payment received (Email, immediate) · Payment failed/returned (Email+SMS, immediate + retry in 3 days)
> 3. Collections: Past-due reminder (Email+SMS, day 7/14/30) · Final disconnect notice (Mail+Email, 10 days before eligibility) · Hi-usage alert (Email+SMS, >200% of average)
> 4. Field work (fired by Work → Rules): Appointment window (SMS+Email, on scheduling) · Technician on the way (SMS, ETA push) · Completion receipt (Email, on completion with photos)
> 5. Staff & system: Billing run completed/failed · Reconciliation exceptions · SLA breach (Owner copied) · Daily digest (8:00 AM) · Security alerts — all Email + In-app to the relevant role
> Behavior: row click or ✎ opens SET-12D for that event; On toggle enables/disables the whole rule inline (confirm + audit log); ➤ sends a test to the signed-in user's email/phone.
> **SET-12D · Event rule page (full page, not modal)**
> Header: category kicker, event name, subtitle (channels + timing summary), Enabled toggle, "Send test", "Save rule" (primary).
> Left column — 4 cards:
> 1. **Audience** — who receives it (Customer all contacts / primary only / Staff role), service scope (All / Water / Electric), account-status filter (all / skip accounts on payment plans / skip medical–life-support flags), plan class (All / Residential / Commercial). Collections events default to their protective filters (past-due skips payment plans; disconnect notice skips medical flags → routes a CSR task instead).
> 2. **Channels & templates** — one row per channel (Email, SMS, Portal, Mail, In-app as applicable): enable toggle, template-variant picker (from the Templates catalog, filtered to this event: default / Spanish / large-print…), language mode (Auto by account preference / English only), 👁 preview linking to the template preview screen. A channel can't be enabled if its variant is deactivated.
> 3. **Timing** — trigger (on event immediately / offset days / fixed time of day), quiet-hours handling (respect — hold SMS until window opens / override for emergencies), delivery-failure policy (retry in 3 days then fall back to email / retry once / none).
> 4. **Escalation ladder** (collections events only) — stages table: stage # | day past due (editable) | channels | template per stage (e.g. gentle → standard → final); + Add stage, remove stage; later stages auto-cancel when the balance clears; fires once per bill.
> **Right rail:**
> * **Rule in plain English** — auto-generated sentence of the full rule (audience + channels + timing + exclusions), re-rendered as settings change
> * **Last 30 days** — sent / delivered / failed counts
> * **Audit note**: every save creates a version (who, when, before → after); Owner/Admin edit, others read-only
> **Rules & integrity**
> * Save is one transaction; toast confirmation; returns to matrix
> * Disabling an event stops future sends only, never recalls queued ones
> * Field-work events' triggers live in Work → Rules; this screen still owns their audience/channel/template
> * Template deleted/deactivated while referenced → rule shows a GAP warning and the channel is suspended
> * All sends logged per account (visible on Account detail → Notes/Audit)"

### Measured at capture — what already exists, before any gap list is written

**Four CRs have each proved a design-derived gap list overstates, so this was
measured first.**

* ✅ **The global bar is largely BUILT.** `NotificationSettings`
  (`models.py:442`) already stores `quiet_hours_start` / `quiet_hours_end` with a
  DB constraint that start < end, plus batch size and the two channel-activation

  (`GET/PUT /notification-settings`), and `SettingsNotificationsTab.tsx` is a
  694-line shipped screen. ⚠ **That screen's own trailer is now STALE** — it says
  *"NO DISPATCH CONFIG … no mounted endpoint"*, and the endpoint exists. Same
  class as DEF-206; worth a defect when this CR is analysed.
* ❌ **THE EVENT MATRIX HAS NO TABLE AT ALL.** There is no `NotificationRule`
  model, nothing named `notification_rules`, and no per-event audience, channel,
  timing or escalation storage anywhere in the backend. **The 16 events, SET-12D
  in its entirety, and the escalation ladder are genuinely greenfield.** That is
  the bulk of this CR.
* ⚠ **Sender identity is only half there.** Quiet hours are stored; a from-email
  and an SMS number are **not**, and the CR wants them **verified** (SPF/DKIM)
  and sourced from a telephony integration. Neither exists.

### ⚠ Conflicts with rulings ALREADY SHIPPED — read before sizing

**1 · "Send test" appears twice and is forbidden twice.** The CR asks for ➤ send
test on every matrix row and a **Send test** button on SET-12D. **BR-NOT-005 and
A11 Addendum r2 §4 make a synchronous send endpoint a GATE FAILURE**, and there

release posture with **"I already confirm it before it Queue them"** — which is
why CR-007's own *"Send test to me"* shipped **rendered and disabled with its
reason**. **This CR cannot mint that route without reversing a signed rule.**

**2 · "Owner" and "Owner/Admin only" is not a role we have.** The role set is
**System Admin · Billing Clerk · Executive** (BR-IDN-008, re-confirmed
2026-08-16: *"we keep 3 roles for time being"*), and the PO ruled all Settings

half-built.** The collections ladder already has stored, ruled parameters —
including the **$25 balance floor** and the **25% partial-payment pause** the PO

DEF-097 reopened). A second ladder editor on SET-12D would be a second home for
the same rule. **Resolve which one owns it before either is built.**

**4 · "skip medical–life-support flags" is sensitive customer data with no
model.** There is no medical or life-support flag on an account anywhere, and
the CR also wants the skip to **route a CSR task instead** — a Work artefact.
This clause protects the most vulnerable customers a utility has; it is worth

**6 · "Last 30 days — sent / delivered / failed" needs delivery telemetry** per

**7 · Channels named that may not exist:** **Portal**, **Mail** and **In-app**.

**8 · It reaches a ❄️ FROZEN surface indirectly.** *"Final disconnect notice ·
10 days before eligibility"* is the regulated ladder (BR-NOT-014), whose three

### CR-009 · CR-007 — PO RULINGS 2026-08-17 (third set): ONE HOME for every rule, and the platform writes the disconnect defaults

#### Conflict 3 · The collections ladder — **ONE HOME, and it is Notifications**

**PO verbatim:** *"we bring all internal external ntification rule sat one place
and they are part of notification settings"*

**Option (a) of three is ruled: SET-12/SET-12D owns every notification rule,
internal and external.** The chasing schedule stops being a settings family and
becomes a rule on the Notifications screen.

**What moves, concretely.** These are stored today, read by the live engine, and
have never had a screen: reminder at **3 days** after due · notice tiers at
**10** then **5** days before cut-off · final notice at **48 hours** · plus the
per-utility **$25 balance floor** and **25% partial-payment pause** the PO ruled
on 2026-08-12 (DEF-204, DEF-097 reopened).

⚠ **A BOUNDARY THIS RULING DOES NOT SETTLE, STATED SO IT IS NOT ASSUMED.** The
*timing* is plainly a notification rule and moves. The **$25 floor** and the
**25% pause** are **money thresholds that decide WHETHER a notice fires at all** —
so by *"all notification rules at one place"* they move too, and that is the
reading taken here. But they are equally arguable as collections policy that
happens to gate a notice. **The reading is recorded rather than the question
re-asked**, because either home is defensible and having ONE is the whole point
of the ruling; if the PO wants them left with the money settings, this is the
sentence to correct.

**And this ruling makes DEF-204 bigger, not smaller.** Those two figures were
already stored-with-no-screen; the answer to "where is their screen" is now
"SET-12D", so building CR-009 is what finally closes them.

#### CR-007 · The disconnect notices — **the platform writes the defaults**

**PO verbatim, after choosing option (i):** *"we will take this option; we provide
default option for all 5 you ahve mentioned; if Utility wants to over ride it let
them do it; I can also give tick boxes if required to add 5"* — and, when the
consequence was restated: ***"you build default langauge and let Utility user
change it as they want"***.

**This is a direct instruction and it overrides this lane's earlier refusal.**
The template-authoring lane declined to write these five sentences, citing
BR-NOT-015's *"their SENTENCES are NOT settled by this rule and must not be
invented"*, and that was the right call **at the time** — nobody had ruled who
writes them. **The PO has now ruled that WE do**, so the rule is satisfied rather
than broken: the sentences are no longer invented by a lane, they are authored to
a PO instruction and are the PO's to approve.

**What ships:**

* **A default for each of the five** — dispute rights · medical hold
  (physician-certified, 60-day renewable) · weather suppression (below 32°F /
  above 100°F) · weekend and holiday suppression · the commission complaint line.
* **Every one overridable by the utility**, which BR-NOT-015 already provides for
  (System-Admin-only and audited) and which is the PO's *"let them change it as
  they want"*.
* **Per-clause tick boxes**, offered by the PO: *"I can also give tick boxes if
  required to add 5"*. Taken up — a utility in a state with no weather rule must
  be able to turn that clause OFF rather than delete text and hope.

⚠ **ONE THING THE LANE MUST NOT SOFTEN, and it is not a hedge.** These sentences
tell a customer how to keep their water on. **A default is a starting point, not
legal advice**, and the product must say so where a System Admin sees it — the
default marked AS a default (BR-NOT-015 already requires this) and reviewed
against each utility's own regulator before a single notice goes out. Writing the
defaults is now ours; **warranting them is not**, and no wording anywhere may
imply otherwise.

##### CR-007 DISCONNECT-NOTICE BUILD RECORD — 2026-08-17, version **2.7.4**

**Status: BUILT. The consequence this ruling was raised to remove is gone —
a disconnection notice can now be produced on a provisioned tenant, at all three
tiers, and it was proved by generating one.**

**What was true this morning, measured:** BR-NOT-014's three tiers were
catalogued, listed on SET-09, openable on SET-10 — and EMPTY. `seed_templates`
refused each by name and `generate_disconnect_notice` refused at every tier.
**No tenant on the platform could send the letter that legally precedes cutting
off a customer's water.**

**What shipped**

| | |
|---|---|
| **The five clauses** | `06-backend/apps/notifications/rights_footer.py` — dispute rights · medical hold (physician-certified, renewable every **60 days**) · weather suppression (below **32°F** / above **100°F**) · weekend and holiday suppression · the commission complaint line |
| **The tick boxes** | Per clause, tenant-scoped. OFF removes the clause entirely — no heading, no blank line, no marker |
| **The override** | Per clause, **System-Admin-only and audited** (BR-NOT-015 (b)), via `update_clauses`; `text: null` restores the platform default in one click |
| **The three tier bodies** | `seed_templates.SEEDABLE` — each quotes A19 §2's signed tier sentence character for character inside an authored letter, and each carries `{state_puc_ref}` **and** `{rights_footer}` as non-removable class content |
| **The ladder** | `notices.TIER_TO_CLASS` — DEF-193's open remainder, closed in the same commit as the bodies |
| **The screen** | S8 → Notifications, `DisconnectRightsFooterCard.tsx`, wired into the tab |
| **The tests** | `06-backend/tests/test_cr_007_disconnect_rights_footer.py` — 48 cases; `DisconnectRightsFooterCard.test.tsx` — 10 |

**Where the tenant's choices live, and why it is not a second mechanism.**
`notification_settings.disconnect_rights_clauses`, one JSON column (migration
`0008`), holding **deviations only** — an untouched tenant holds `{}` and
therefore holds every default, which is what makes *"is this ours or theirs"*
answerable by looking rather than by comparing strings. No new table, and
therefore **no new RLS policy**: `notification_settings` already carries its
isolation policy from migration 0004 and a policy governs the ROW, not the
column list. The override path is `dispatch_config`'s own pattern on the same
row — `@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN)`, one audit row per save, before→after with
the **full text** rather than a length or a hash.

**⚠ THE THING THAT WAS NOT SOFTENED, and where a System Admin sees it.**
`rights_footer.PLATFORM_DEFAULT_NOTICE` sits above the clauses on the card — not
in a tooltip — and says the platform wrote these words, that they are a starting
point rather than legal advice, that they are not the utility's regulator's
words, and that each must be reviewed against that regulator before a notice
goes out. Every untouched clause carries the badge *"Platform default — review
against your own commission"*. A test asserts the notice contains *"not legal
advice"*, *"starting point"* and *"before any disconnection notice goes out"*.
**No clause promises an outcome** — they say *"ask us whether"*, never *"we
will"* — and a test asserts that too.

**Nothing invented.** Every figure in the footer is the PO's own (60 days, 32°F,
100°F, each written in BR-NOT-015's clause list and repeated in the ruling). **No
dollar amount appears in the footer or in any tier body.** No regulator is named
— a test forbids `PUC`, `TCEQ` and `25.29` in every clause. DEF-210's own
sixteen-phrase table is re-used rather than re-typed, with a single scoped
exemption: `"60 days"` is unruled as a *rate-change notice period* and is ruled
as the *medical-hold renewal*, so the exemption applies to that one clause and
every other clause is still checked against the whole phrase.

**Seven guards proved RED first** (hard-won law 7), each failure quoted in the
lane report. The one worth repeating here: moving the `{rights_footer}` pre-pass
to after the token substitution produced a customer letter reading
`YOUR RIGHTS` followed by `——`.

**Two findings raised rather than papered over.**

* **OQ-263** — BR-NOT-015 says a utility *"already supplies its commission
  reference"* and **nothing in the product stores one.** `{state_puc_ref}` is a
  keyword argument no screen, job or seeder sets, so that one line renders `——`
  on an otherwise complete notice. Non-blocking: the notice is produced.
* **DEF-230** — the disconnect-tier defect is cited as **DEF-190** in nine
  places, including BR-NOT-014 itself and three SET-09 *Used-by* strings a
  utility reads on screen. **DEF-190 is an unrelated i18n defect**; the row is
  **DEF-193.** G17 catches an id defined twice and can never catch one cited
  wrongly. Corrected where this lane was already working; left alone in two
  frontend files another lane owns, and that split is recorded on the row.

**What this lane did NOT do, said plainly**

* **No browser walkthrough.** No Playwright run and no screenshot: the proof
  offered is a real tenant provisioned through the real service generating all
  three notices from what provisioning planted, plus static-markup assertions on
  the card. **Nothing here proves the card looks right on screen** — hard-won
  law 6 still applies and is unpaid on this change.
* **The e2e spec was UPDATED, not RUN.** `e2e/CR-007-templates.spec.ts` asserted
  the *Used-by* strings and the tier palettes this change alters; the

### CR-009 — PO RULINGS 2026-08-17 (fourth set): IN-APP IS THE PROOF CHANNEL, and a bulk action sends ONE message

**PO verbatim:** *"We can confirm it whether it is working on not if we get in APp
Notifcaition, which does not require any integration and it is proof that
notification is working; for single notification send 1 message and for bulk
action also send 1 message only saying nulk action is completed"*

#### Ruling 1 · In-app is how we prove the pipeline works

**The reasoning is right and worth keeping:** every other channel needs a third
party before anything can be observed — email needs an adapter and an SMTP/ESP
decision that has not been taken, SMS needs Twilio, print needs a page renderer
(OQ-149). **In-app needs nobody.** So it is the one channel that can carry a
message end to end today, and a message arriving in it is **proof the queue, the
rule, the template resolution, the rendering and the dispatcher all work** — with
the provider adapter being the only thing still missing.

⚠ **BUT IT DOES NOT EXIST YET, AND THAT MUST NOT BE GLOSSED.** Measured the hour
of the ruling: `models.CHANNELS` is exactly three — `pdf_print`, `email`, `sms`.
There is no in-app channel. The CR-009 lane had already recorded the honest
reason in `rule_catalog.py`: *"there is no in-app notification surface — no bell,
no inbox"*, and it marks `in_app` **unavailable** on the staff events.

**So this ruling is a BUILD, not a switch** — a channel value, a per-user
message store, and a surface in the shell to read it. It is still far cheaper
than the email path: **no credentials, no SPF/DKIM, no vendor, no per-tenant
configuration, and nothing to buy.** That is exactly why it is the right proof.

**And it changes the ORDER of CR-009's work:** in-app becomes the FIRST channel
built rather than the fifth listed, because until one channel can actually
deliver, every other part of this CR is asserted rather than demonstrated.

#### Ruling 2 · ONE message per action — including a bulk action

**PO verbatim:** *"for single notification send 1 message and for bulk action also
send 1 message only saying nulk action is completed"*

**This is a product rule, not a preference, and it is the more consequential half
of the two.** A bulk action over 200 accounts produces **ONE** message —
*"bulk action is completed"* — never 200, and never one per succeeded item plus
one per failure.

**Why it matters beyond tidiness:** the staff events in this CR are precisely the
bulk ones — *"Billing run completed/failed"*, *"Reconciliation exceptions"*,
*"Daily digest"*. Without this rule, a bill run over a thousand accounts is a
thousand notifications, and the first thing any staff member does is turn the
whole event off — at which point the failure they needed to see is the one they
never get. **A notification nobody can bear to leave on is worse than none.**

**What it binds:**
* One message per bulk operation, whatever the item count.
* The message states **completion**, and where the operation had failures it
  must say **how many** — a summary that hides a failure count is the same
  failure as sending a thousand messages, in the opposite direction.
* This is a **rule about the rule engine**, so it belongs in the module's
  business rules and needs a test that drives a bulk operation and asserts the
  queue grew by exactly one.

### CR-009 — PO RULINGS 2026-08-17: conflicts 1 and 2 answered

#### Conflict 1 · "Send test" — **build the infrastructure now; the provider plugs in later**

**PO verbatim:** *"I got it; lets build the infra and capabilities; the moment we
take the decison on ESP or SMTP from existing email of Utilities, we just need to
plug it ; rest of the infra will work"*

**⚠ THIS REVERSES NOTHING, AND THE ARCHITECTURE THE PO JUST DESCRIBED IS ALREADY
BUILT.** Measured at the moment of the ruling:

* **`provider_seam.py` (335 lines) is exactly the seam the PO described** — its
  own opening says *"TD-8 and BR-NOT-005 both say ONE seam: provider adapters
  (BYO mailbox, transactional ESP, Twilio) behind one seam. This is it."* No
  provider name appears in any business-logic file in the module.
* **`dispatcher.py` is 877 lines** and already claims, batches, records and
  retries. `senders.py`, `mailbox.py`, `delivery_ops.py` and the
  `OutboundMessage` queue all exist.
* **The absence is written as CODE, not as a comment** (hard-won law 1):
  `channel_route()` returns a `ChannelRoute` whose `dispatchable` is `False` and
  whose `problem` names the wave, the dispatcher records that on every cycle,
  and a test asserts **zero provider calls** happen for a deferred channel.
* **So "the rest of the infra will work" is already true.** Queue rows and
  rendering are v1 for every channel; **only the SEND adapter defers.**

**AND BR-NOT-005 STILL STANDS.** *"Queue only, no synchronous send endpoint"* is
not in tension with this ruling: **"Send test" ENQUEUES a test message** and the
dispatcher drains it through whichever adapter is plugged in. The forbidden thing
is a route that transmits inside the request — and nothing here needs one. The
gate test asserting no `send`/`test-send` route can resolve **stays**, and CR-009
must satisfy the requirement by queueing.

**What actually remains, therefore, is small and specific:**
1. an **adapter** behind the existing seam (SMTP for a utility's own mailbox, or
   an ESP) — the PO's *"just need to plug it"*;
2. flipping `channel_route()`'s deferred verdict for email once one exists;
3. a **test-send target** — the signed-in user's own address, which the CR
   specifies and which is new;
4. the provider facts the queue cannot write today: `delivered` needs a provider
   confirmation and `bounced` needs an ESP webhook. **`delivery_ops.py` already
   says in its own words that no provider adapter exists on any channel and that
   these statuses are therefore never written** — which is also what CR-009's
   *"Last 30 days — sent / delivered / failed"* rail depends on.

**Still owed from the PO before an adapter is written:** *which* — a utility's
existing mailbox over SMTP, or a transactional ESP. The seam takes either; the
credentials, the verification (the CR asks for SPF/DKIM) and the per-tenant
config differ completely.

#### Conflict 2 · "Owner" — **apply the Settings permission rule**

**PO verbatim:** *"APply setting permission rule we discussed before"*.

So CR-009 inherits the standing rule, **and that rule now has a precise shape
because DEF-196 forced one on 2026-08-17**. A4's `settings_lookups` row is
`{"system_admin": "Full", "executive": "View"}`:

* **System Admin** — edits notification rules.
* **Executive** — **READS** them, every control visible and disabled with its
  reason (BR-SHL-025).
* **Billing Clerk** — **no access**; A4 gives them no cell, which is no access
  rather than read-only access.

**Consequences for the CR as written:** *"Owner/Admin only"* on the global bar
becomes **System Admin only**. *"Owner & Admin can edit; other roles read-only"*
on the audit note becomes **System Admin edits; Executive reads; Billing Clerk
cannot open it**. And **"SLA breach (Owner copied)"** has no addressee — a
staff-notification recipient is a separate question from a Settings permission,
and it is **NOT answered by this ruling**; it needs one of its own.

### Next step

**Step 1 CLASSIFY, step 3 IMPACT.** Conflicts **1 and 2 are ruled** (above).
**Conflict 3 — which surface owns the collections ladder — is still open**, and
so is *who* a staff notification goes to now that "Owner" is not a role. Nothing
is built until those two have rulings — each reverses or duplicates something already signed. The
rest can be sized around them.

### What the PO asked for, verbatim

> "Next CR - Requirements — SET-11 · Settings → Accounting (3 tabs)
