Scope is revenue-only: bills, payments, taxes held, deposits, write-offs. No cost-of-service (power/water purchases, O&M) — that stays in the accounting system.
> **Tab 1 — Chart of accounts (SET-11.coa)**
> Header actions: ↑ Import CSV · ⇅ Sync from QuickBooks · + Add local account (primary)
> Table columns: Code | Name | Type (Asset/Liability/Income/Expense) | Source (🔒 Synced vs Local pill) | Used by (count of mappings/schedules/authorities referencing it) | Status (Active pill) | Actions
> Key rules:
> * Synced accounts are read-only — edited only in QuickBooks; Actions column literally reads "Read-only"
> * Local accounts (created here for gaps, e.g. "2200-04 Fees payable — PUC") get ✎ edit and ✕ deactivate
> * An account with Used-by > 0 cannot be deactivated — warning lists what references it
> * Toolbar: search by code/name, type filter chips (All/Income/Liability/Expense/Asset), column selector; standard sort + pagination footer (rows 50/100/200/500/1000)
> * Sync: shows last-sync timestamp; sync pulls adds/renames/deactivations from QuickBooks; conflicts (a local code colliding with a synced code) surfaced for resolution
> * Import CSV: ETL-style flow (upload → map columns code/name/type → validate → load) with dedupe on code
> **Tab 2 — GL mapping (SET-11.map)**
> Where every money event posts. Four sections, each a table with searchable account dropdowns + per-row edit/clear icon actions:
> 1. Service revenue: each service (Electric, Water…) usage/base charges → income account
> 2. Tax authorities: each authority (State, City, County, PUC fee) → liability account
> 3. Payments & deposits: each tender (Card/ACH-Stripe, Check-lockbox, Cash-counter, IVR) → cash/clearing account + settlement note; plus Unapplied cash and Customer deposits held accounts. Rule: a payment always posts somewhere the moment it's taken — unmatched money goes to unapplied cash
> 4. Charge codes → income: late fee, NSF, connection fee, reconnect, after-hours call → income accounts; unmapped charge shows a GAP banner and cannot be added to bills
> "Save mapping" persists atomically; every mapping change audit-logged.
> **Tab 3 — Finance controls (SET-11.controls)**
> Cards:
> * Fiscal calendar: FY start month (e.g. October municipal FY), period length (calendar month / 4-4-5), shows current open period + closed-through, who may reopen a closed period (Owner only / Owner+Finance admin / no one)
> * Posting policy: journals to QuickBooks summary (one per bill run/deposit day) vs detail (per bill/payment); revenue recognition accrual (on bill issue) vs cash (on payment); rounding-difference account
> * Scope card: static statement of revenue-only scope; only expense ever posted is bad debt on write-off
> * Existing controls: approval thresholds for adjustments/write-offs, period-close checklist requirements
> **Cross-cutting**
> * Permissions: Owner + Finance admin edit; others read-only
> * Everything audit-logged (who, when, before → after)
> * Downstream: Finance → Ledger/Journals use these mappings; Billing blocks a run if any active plan references an unmapped charge/tax; period close (FIN-03) enforces the fiscal calendar"

### THE MONEY SURFACES — read before sizing

**This is the first CR since CR-004 that puts money figures on a settings
screen**, and three of them need answering before anything is drawn:

1. **Approval thresholds.** r10's Finance controls draws **write-off approval at
   $5,000**, **second approver above $25,000**, **adjustment approval above
   $500**, and a **bank match tolerance of $0.05**. Are these ❄️ B4/B5-signed
   figures, tenant-configurable policy, or unruled? A control that appears to set
   a finance-signed figure is exactly what CR-006's late-fee question was about,
   and that one was resolved by REMOVING the control.
2. **Revenue recognition — accrual on bill issue vs cash on payment.** This is
   not a preference; it changes WHEN revenue hits the books, which is the
   ledger's core contract. B4/B5 territory almost certainly.
3. **A rounding-difference account.** CLAUDE.md hard rule 2 says round only at
   finalization/display, per B4. Where a rounding difference POSTS is a ledger
   rule, not a settings choice.

**None of these is ours to decide.** Put all three to the PO with worked figures
before the tab is built.

### CR-008 — PO RULINGS 2026-08-17 (second set): the GL MAPPING ARCHITECTURE, and a conflict this lane raised WRONGLY

#### ⚠ CORRECTION FIRST: the "AP conflict" was not a conflict, and this lane was wrong to raise it

This lane told the PO that their list — *"GL codes to AP { Expenses, discounts,
credits }"* — **reversed BR-LED-028**, quoting *"full accounts payable … was put
to the Product Owner and DECLINED"*.

**The PO clarified, verbatim:** *"When I say account apyable - I mean we become
system of record for account payable; we keep the records in system accept all
entries but dont do processing of it; that way uility can keep everything at one
place and when require pass the details to ERP or accouting system ; we will
alow allow them to tally the details"*

**That is what BR-LED-028 ALREADY SAYS, in its own opening words:** *"the product
is the system of record for AP and AR both and **PROCESSES NEITHER** — no
approval workflow, no payment run, no vendor master, no supplier ageing or
dunning, no cheque printing or remittance advice, no paying anything."* What was
declined was **option (c), full AP PROCESSING** — not AP record-keeping.

**So the PO's position and the signed rule agree exactly, and there is no
reversal to make.** The lane read the second half of a sentence and quoted it as
though it were the whole. **Recorded rather than quietly dropped**, because the
next reader will otherwise find "the PO reversed BR-LED-028" written somewhere
and act on it: **nothing was reversed.**

**What follows for CR-008:** cost/expense GL codes ARE in scope, because the
product records them — the chart already carries **eight 5xxx cost accounts**,
served marked `finance_signed: false` pending a finance re-sign. Recording an
expense against one is inside the rule. Paying it is not, and still must not be
built.

#### The architecture, agreed — ONE EDITOR, storage stays put

The PO put the model and asked for advice; the advice was given and **accepted in
full: *"Im okay with this ; I agree"***.

* **The SCREEN is one** — Settings → Accounting is the only place a GL code is
  edited. *"editing and chaigng will be done in setting only"*.
* **The STORAGE does not move.** A charge's account stays on the charge, a tax
  authority's on the tax. One mapping table would force every bill into an extra
  lookup and lose the property that makes it safe — **the account travels with
  the item it belongs to.** So this is a rule about the door, not a migration.
* **Everywhere else DISPLAYS and links back** — *"we will display it every place
  where it make sense"*.

#### Payments vs deposits — settled, and the PO agreed

* **Charges CANNOT cover payments.** A charge says where the REVENUE lands; a
  payment is the CASH side, moving money into a bank or clearing account. Two
  different accounts, and the charge says nothing about the second.
* **Deposits are already handled** by the ruled `deposit_liability` designation
  (seeded 2300) — a deposit is the customer's money, never income, so it needs no
  per-item mapping.
* **Tenders are the one real gap.** `PaymentMethod` holds code · name · is_system
  · active and **no GL column at all**, so a utility taking card, cheque, cash and
  IVR has nowhere to say that card lands in a merchant clearing account and
  cheques in the bank.

#### The three things to build — PO: *"Im good with all"*

1. **Add the tender → cash/clearing account column.** Genuine gap, small.
2. **Make Accounting the only editor.** Charges, taxes, plan services and
   adjustment reasons go READ-ONLY with a link to it.
3. ⚠ **Validate the account WHEN IT IS PICKED, not only when a bill runs.**
   Measured: four of the five GL links are bare `UUIDField`s marked *"DEFERRED FK
   → ledger_accounts"* with **no referential integrity**, and only
   `tenant_services.revenue_account` is a real foreign key. Billing does check at
   issue — it asks rating for the account and the ledger whether it is live — but
   **that is late**: a mapping can look correct on screen for weeks and fail on
   the day a bill runs, which is when a utility can least afford it.

### CR-008 — PO RULINGS 2026-08-17. All nine answered. **CR-008 IS UNBLOCKED.**

The PO was given nine decisions in plain English with worked figures and ruled
on every one in a single reply. **Verbatim, numbered as they were asked:**

> *"1. Accrual or cash — and there's a catch. - **take it off** 2 - **decide for
> me**; 3 **we only need file no live integration** 4. **System admin** ; 5
> **system admin** 6 **keep it for time being as it is** 7. **Okay. We can take
> it as threshold from user** 8. **Keep as it is don't post it yet we can handle
> it later** 9 **make it separate**"*

| # | Question | Ruling | What it means for the build |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Accrual vs cash — the control exists and nothing reads it | **TAKE IT OFF** | **Remove** `accounting_method` from the Regional screen. Do **not** draw a second one on SET-11. The column stays in the database (removing it is a migration with no caller); the CONTROL goes, because a switch that does nothing is worse than an absent one |
| 2 | The write-off threshold name collision ($5 capped $50 vs r10's $5,000) | **DELEGATED — "decide for me"** | Decided below, and recorded as a lane decision rather than a PO ruling |
| 3 | QuickBooks: file export or live sync? | **FILE ONLY, NO LIVE INTEGRATION** | ⚠ **The single biggest scope cut in this CR.** "⇅ Sync from QuickBooks", its OAuth connection, its conflict resolution and its last-sync timestamp are **OUT**. The existing export (`apps/ledger/exports.py`, CSV/IIF/QBO) is what ships. The "Synced vs Local" pill and the read-only-because-synced rule go with it — **every account is Local now**, so every account is editable |
| 4 | Who may open the Accounting screen | **SYSTEM ADMIN** | Follows the standing Settings rule. r10's "Owner + Finance admin" is not built and no role is invented |
| 5 | Who may reopen a closed period | **SYSTEM ADMIN** | Matches what the code already does (`apps/ledger/close.py:98`). The three-way chooser r10 draws is **not built** — a picker whose only legal value is the current one is decoration |
| 6 | "Lock periods once closed", the switch that does nothing | **KEEP IT FOR THE TIME BEING AS IT IS** | Explicitly ruled to stay as-is. It is now a **known, ruled** no-op rather than an unnoticed one — recorded so the next lane does not "fix" it |
| 7 | Bank matching to 5 cents | **"We can take it as threshold from user"** | **Build it as a user-set tolerance**, alongside the date tolerance that already exists. ⚠ This is a REAL BEHAVIOUR CHANGE on money — today the amount match is exact to the penny — so it wants a review-ledger row and its default must be **$0.00**, which is today's behaviour |
| 8 | The rounding-difference account | **"Keep as it is don't post it yet, we can handle it later"** | **Do not build the control and do not post rounding differences.** Deferred by ruling, not forgotten |
| 9 | Adjustment reasons → GL, the fifth mapping section | **MAKE IT SEPARATE** | Build it as its own section on Tab 2, so a "billing error" credit and a "goodwill" credit can post to different accounts. `reason_codes` gains the `default_gl_account_id` column US-TEN-010 §5 already specified |

#### Ruling 2, decided by this lane under the PO's *"decide for me"*

**The collision, restated in one line:** `write_off_threshold_amount` already
exists meaning **$5.00, capped at $50** — the balance below which a tiny residue
on a final bill is written off automatically (BR-BIL-013). r10 draws **$5,000
write-off approval / $25,000 second approver** on the same card, meaning
something else entirely.

**Decision, three parts:**

1. **The existing field keeps its key and gets an unambiguous label.** On screen
   it reads *"Automatically write off small balances on a final bill"* with its
   $0–$50 range visible. A label change costs nothing; renaming a stored key is
   a migration for no gain.
2. **The manual approval threshold ships**, separately labelled *"Write-offs
   above this amount need an approver"*.
3. ⚠ **AND ITS DEFAULT IS `$0.00`, NOT `$5,000` — this is the part that matters.**
   Today **every manual write-off of any size requires an approval**
   (`apps/payments/writeoffs.py` has no threshold at all). Shipping r10's $5,000
   as the default would mean **every write-off under $5,000 silently stops
   needing approval** the moment this CR lands. That is a LOOSENING of a money
   control arriving as a settings default, which is precisely how hard-won law 3
   ("defaults fail closed") gets broken. `$0.00` preserves today's behaviour
   exactly; a utility that wants the convenience opts into it and is seen doing
   it.

**What would falsify this call:** if the PO says the intent was that small
write-offs should not need approval, part 3 is wrong and the default becomes
$5,000. It is stated here so that can be checked rather than assumed.

#### What these rulings REMOVE from CR-008

Worth stating plainly, because four CRs have now shown a design-derived scope
list overstates: **the QuickBooks sync, the Synced/Local distinction, the
sync-conflict resolution, the period-reopen role chooser, the accrual/cash
control and the rounding-difference account are all OUT.** What remains is the
chart of accounts (**already built** — a move from Finance to Settings plus the
CSV import), the GL mapping tab with **five** sections instead of four, and a
fiscal-calendar tab that mostly points at controls that already exist.

**No open question blocks CR-008 any longer.**

### CR-008 — SECOND SET, BUILT 2026-08-17. **Build `2.8.0`.** What shipped, what did not, and why.

The three things the PO said *"Im good with all"* to. Two are done end to end; the
third is done on the half that was ruled and **openly not done on the half that
moves money**, with the reason measured rather than asserted.

| # | The thing | State | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The tender → cash/clearing account column | **BUILT** (storage · validation · screen · audit) — **posting NOT wired, deliberately** | `payment_methods.clearing_gl_account_id` (tenancy 0015) · SET-11 GL mapping §3 |
| 2 | Settings → Accounting is the ONLY editor of a GL code | **BUILT** | §1 services · §2 taxes · §3 tenders · §4 charges (new) · §5 reasons; S12/S13 and the plan wizard display + link |
| 3 | Validate the account WHEN IT IS PICKED | **BUILT** | `rating._validated_gl_account` · `tenancy.GlPointerLookupMixin` |

#### ⚠ Ruling 1's second half is NOT built, and this is the sentence to read

`post_payment_cleared` debits **undeposited funds** for every tender (PO ruling
2026-08-11, OQ-143: *"until bank record and reconcilaition confirm it it is not
realised"*). `apps/payments/reconciliation.py:68` posts the other leg — *DR cash
/ CR undeposited funds* — when the bank confirms it.

**If the receipt leg debited a per-tender clearing account while reconciliation
kept crediting undeposited funds, reconciliation would credit an account that
was never debited, and the trial balance would go out by the amount of every
card payment.** So the two legs must move in ONE change, both on the 🔒
ledger-posting path, on their own review. **OQ-264 stays OPEN carrying exactly
that half** — and `test_cr008_setting_a_tender_account_changes_NO_posting`
asserts ZERO readers of the column under `apps/payments`, so it goes RED the day
anyone starts, which is the arrival signal nothing else was watching for.

The screen says the same thing in a utility's own words: *"Setting this records
what you want; it does not move money yet. Every payment still lands in
undeposited funds until the bank confirms it, whichever way it was taken."*

#### The measurement that corrected the brief

The CR was sized on *"four of the five GL links are bare `UUIDField`s … with no
referential integrity"*. **Measured: two of those four already validated** —
`taxes.liability_gl_account_id` since 2026-08-11 (BR-BIL-069's lane) and
`reason_codes.default_gl_account_id` since that morning. The two that genuinely
did not are **`charges.gl_account_id`** and **`plan_services.gl_account_id`**.
Recorded because the next reader would otherwise re-do work that exists.

#### Two things that would have gone wrong quietly, and did not

**(a) One editor needs the one to exist first.** Making S12 read-only without
adding a charge → account editor to §4 would have left a late fee with **no
editor anywhere**, and BR-BIL-010 refuses the WHOLE bill at issue when a fee
line cannot resolve an account. Both halves landed in one change.

**(b) A read-only field must OMIT its column, never send `null`.** Both rating
forms posted the pointer on every save. Left sending `null`, a rename would have
**cleared the mapping** — proved by clicking: renaming *Connection fee* now
sends a PATCH with no `gl_account_id` key at all and the 4200 mapping survives.

#### What the browser walkthrough found that no gate could

The tab still told a utility *"you can also set this on Plans and Rates … both
places change the same account."* True in the morning, false by the afternoon.
Corrected in eleven languages; the test that asserted it is **inverted**, not
deleted. Hard-won law 6, exactly as written.

#### Filed

**DEF-231** — a FOURTH screen still claimed the chart of accounts *"arrives with
the Finance module"*. DEF-206 named three and was closed on three. The claim
lives in an **i18n key**, so one grep finds every screen making it; closing such
a defect per-file is closing it per-place-somebody-looked.

#### Rollback

Three commits, each independently revertable, and **nothing to undo in data**:
the migration only ADDS a nullable column, every existing row is NULL, and NULL
is byte-for-byte today's behaviour for every tender. Reverting the frontend
restores the pickers on S12/S13; reverting `_validated_gl_account` restores the
looser write. No data is migrated, moved or rewritten by any of it.

### CR-006 — BUILT, NOT CLOSED (2026-08-17). Change 6, shipped in build 2.7.1.

> **⚠ ITS CHANGE NUMBER IS 6 AND THE BUILD IT SHIPPED IN IS `2.7.1`, and the gap
> between those two sentences is a real problem with the scheme, not a slip.**
> CR-007 landed first at `2.7.0`. Setting this merge to `2.6.0` would move the
> version a user sees **backwards**, and would leave two different builds able to
> carry the same number — which defeats the one thing step 7 exists for, in
> CLAUDE.md's own words: *"when two production defects were reported, neither the
> PO nor the product could say which build they were looking at."* So the merge
> kept the version **monotonic**: `2.7.1` = 2.7.0 plus the four defect fixes
> landed since (DEF-197, DEF-199, DEF-207, DEF-208). Monotonic won because it is
> the property the scheme was invented to provide, and **CR attribution is
> already recorded here in the register — a better home for it than three
> digits.** Raised as **OQ-258** rather than settled: the scheme cannot be both
> "the middle number IS the CR" and monotonic, and today it had to pick.

> **ID NOTE (merge, 2026-08-17):** this lane minted `DEF-193/194/195` while CR-007's lane minted the same three numbers in its own worktree. Per the rule already adopted this session — **the earlier-committed row keeps its id** — CR-006's became **DEF-213 (pre-existing tenancy failures) · DEF-214 (the empty-state check that could not fail) · DEF-215 (the 201 English strings)**. A worktree branches the FILES and not the ID SPACE.

**Status: BUILT-NOT-PROVEN.** Every part of r11 step 2 is done except (d):
**there has been no browser walkthrough.** CR-005 sits at exactly this bar for
exactly this reason, and CR-004 met it only after a walkthrough found five
screens answering HTTP 500 with the whole suite green. **Built and green is not

footer, empty states with their action, Draft pills, the deactivation warning
naming the cycle and the premises count) · SET-06 route wizard (basics with the
series-filled code, type, service, area, notes → premises picker with
multi-select area chips, *"Select all N"* and the move badge → meter review with
per-meter deselect → review with the move consequence and Draft/Activate) ·
SET-07 cycle wizard (basics → route picker with the conflict badge → the
day-of-month DEFAULTS with a preview → review with the coverage flag, the
first-run date and Draft/Activate).

#### The five rulings, and where each one landed

1. **NO MONEY.** The `Late / penalty date` control is **not built**. No fee,
   rate, amount or currency field exists on either screen — asserted
   structurally, so adding one goes RED. The preview strip keeps every clause
   except the last, and the last is **not derived from Billing defaults
   either**: a fee date rendered here reads as this screen's field however it
   was sourced. **CR-006 needs no finance re-sign at any point.**
2. **A cycle is a DEFINITION.** Its lede says so to the user: *"A cycle is a
   group of routes… you define the group here; the timing is confirmed when you
   actually run it."*
3. **It carries day-of-month DEFAULTS.** Four integers 1–31, not dates. The
   legacy DATE columns are left in place, unwritten by this screen, because
   `read_schedules` and the billing seams read them.
4. **System Admin only**, gated exactly as `/lookups/*` is — **both** gates,
   because CR-005 proved a permission test stays green with one removed.
   Everyone else read-only **with the reason on the control**.
5. **Areas** gained the self-FK, premises gained the area reference, and the
   filter is multi-select with All — including premises with **no** area,
   because a filter that hid untagged premises would hide exactly the rows a
   utility is trying to tag.

#### Two findings worth the record

**The old refusal made the requirement unbuildable.** `_set_route_membership`
raised `unit_on_another_route`, so *"selecting moves them, with confirm"* could
never be reached — the badge could only ever be followed by an error. Two
existing tests asserted that refusal and were **AMENDED, not deleted**: the
invariant (one route per unit per service) survives; only the mechanism changed.

**The reads-history guard could not be built the obvious way.** Reads reach a
route through service points, and removing a route's members UNSTAMPS its
service points — so an emptied route would report zero history and become
deletable, which is the exact hole BR-MET-079 exists to close. It hunts through
`read_import_batches.route_id`, which no membership edit clears.

#### Guards proved RED first — twelve, and two of them taught something

Removing the reads-history guard does **not** silently permit the delete: it
produces a raw `ProtectedError`, an HTTP 500 where the rule wanted a sentence.
And the **empty-state check stayed GREEN** when its button was deleted, because
the page header carries the same `+ Add route` label — **DEF-182's shape a
sixth time**, filed as **DEF-214** and fixed by scoping the assertion inside the
`settings-empty` cell.

#### Tests

Backend **26 new** + the metering/tenancy selection at **650 passed**. Sixteen
failures in that run are **PRE-EXISTING** — `test_us_ten_002_seeding` (3) and
`test_us_ten_020_sweep` (13) fail identically on base commit `a76398d`, verified
in a throwaway worktree rather than assumed, and filed as **DEF-213** rather
than silently absorbed. Frontend `tsc --noEmit` clean; **79 passed** across the
three suites the new row types touch.

#### NOT CLAIMED

**No browser walkthrough** · the reader/tech assignee on SET-06 step 1 is not
wired (`routes.assigned_to` exists; no user picker exists on this surface) ·
walk order is stored and is not editable here · Reads and Billing are not
re-pointed at the new fields — a bill run still scopes by `service_points.
cycle_id`, which is what membership stamps, so the wiring is unchanged rather
than extended · *"Dispatch can filter work orders by route/area"* is a
downstream link and Work is R5 · nothing here touched a rate, a fee or any
❄️ B4/B5 figure.

### CR-006 — THE BROWSER WALKTHROUGH, AND THE VERDICT: **IT DOES NOT CLOSE** (2026-08-17)

**PO instruction:** *"CR-006 — nothing but a walkthrough - complete it"*.
**PO's standing acceptance bar:** *"full CRUD working - from Ui scren not just
backend"* and *"we need final confirmation it working on screen"*.

**Done.** Chromium against the real stack — Postgres, Django and the BUILT SPA
on one origin (`08-qa/01-e2e/stack/boot_stack.sh`, database `sbh_e2e_cr006`,
ports 8041/8141), signed in through the S3 form as the seeded System Admin.
**21 tests · 343 browser assertions, green end to end — and green again on a
re-run over its own leftovers.** The walkthrough is committed as
`07-frontend/e2e/CR-006-routes-cycles.spec.ts`, every assertion in it is on
RENDERED TEXT a person reads, and the only API calls in the file create the
Executive test user and are fenced into one labelled function, because
`/change-password` is not built (DEF-200).

⚠ **HOW MANY TIMES IT WAS RUN, EXACTLY — written out because "run twice, once
without resetting the database" was the instruction, and because a run count is
the easiest thing in a QA report to round up.** Four runs against a live stack:

| run | database | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | reset before the run | 18 passed · 3 failed — all three failures were bugs in the SPEC, not the product (two step titles that a table also repeats in a visually-hidden `<caption>`, so `getByText` matched two elements; and one whole-modal regex that passed on the dialog's own heading, reporting *"expected to fail, but passed"*) |
| 2 | reset before the run | **20 passed · 1 failed · 325 assertions** — the one failure being the third `<caption>` collision, now fixed |
| 3 | reset before the run | ✅ **21 passed · 0 failed · 343 assertions, in 13.3 minutes** |
| 4 | **NOT reset — run 3's routes, cycles and moved premises left in place** | ✅ **21 passed · 0 failed · 332 assertions, in 13.1 minutes** |

**Both of the last two runs are green, and RUN 4 IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS FOR
TRUST.** It drove the identical spec straight over run 3's leftovers — five QA
routes, a QA cycle, `Route 5` already moved off 08-B, `Route 2` already emptied
by run 3's draft — and every claim still held. So **nothing in this walkthrough
passes only on a pristine seed**, which was the thing worth proving: a
walkthrough that is green once and red the second time is one nobody runs again.

**The 11-assertion difference between the two green runs is the design working,
not drift.** DEF-218's test asks whether the code the wizard pre-fills is already
taken. On a fresh seed `RT-001` is free, so it creates a route with it and asks
again — the longer path. On run 4 `RT-001` already existed, so the same claim was
reached in one step. Every code either run creates carries a per-run stamp, and
no assertion anywhere depends on a counter starting at 1.

Every failure in runs 1 and 2 was in the SPEC rather than the product, and all
four are fixed. Everything below was seen on screen in both green runs.

#### What WORKS on screen — said plainly, because most of this CR does

* **SET-05 draws.** Both tables, with r10's columns, real counts, the Draft
  pill, icon row actions with tooltips, a pagination footer under each, and a
  search that narrows to one row.
* **The route wizard puts real premises on a route, and they are still there
  after a full page reload.** That is the thing the shipped screen could not do
  at all before this CR. Measured: a route created from the screen with two
  premises came back reading **2 premises · 3 units** after `page.goto` threw
  the whole SPA away, and re-opening the wizard showed both still ticked.
* **A meter can be left off, and the exclusion sticks.** Ticking one of three
  meters off took the count to **"2 of 3"**, the summary said **"2 (1 left
  off)"**, the landing showed 2 meters, and re-opening the edit brought the same
  meter back **unticked**.
* **A premises cannot sit on two routes for one service.** The badge names the
  old route, the consequence box says *"1 premises currently on QA-RT-F-… move
  here — No bills change; only who reads them."*, and after the save the old
  route reads `0 · 0` and the new one `1 · 1`.
* **The cycle wizard's four steps work and its defaults persist.** Frequency
  Quarterly, read window 1–3, bill day 5, due day 26 and a first run of
  1 Oct 2026 all survived a reload; an edit re-opened them and a changed due day
  persisted. The conflict badge fired on a route already on a cycle and the
  route moved.
* **Both delete guards refuse in English, not with a 500.** Confirming the
  delete of a route with reading history produced *"135 reads were collected on
  this route. Deactivate it instead — deleting it would lose the record of who
  read those meters."*, and the cycle guard produced *"Reads or bills already
  reference this cycle, so it can't be deleted."* Both rows were still there
  afterwards.
* **Deactivation warns properly:** *"Route Route 3 is in cycle 08-A — its next
  scheduled reads will skip 2 premises."*
* **RULING ONE HOLDS COMPLETELY.** Swept the landing and all eight wizard steps
  for any currency symbol, fee, rate, penalty, tariff or amount: **zero hits.**
* **RULING TWO HOLDS.** The lede a user reads says *"You define the group here;
  the timing is confirmed when you actually run it."* and nothing on the surface
  offers to run or schedule anything.
* **RULING THREE HOLDS.** Step 3 stores day-of-month boxes hinted *"Day of the
  month, 1–31"*, never date inputs, and its lede says the run may change them.
* **PERMISSIONS ARE RIGHT HERE — and this is worth stating because DEF-196 says
  they are wrong next door.** A real Executive user, created and signed in
  during the run, saw the whole surface **read-only**: both tables fully
  legible, and `+ Add route`, `+ Add cycle` and every ✎ **visible, disabled and
  carrying `Your role can view this, but not change it.`** That is BR-SHL-025
  honoured exactly. **CR-005's DEF-196 shape does NOT occur on this surface.**

#### Why it does not close — eight findings, three of them serious

**DEF-217 · A 500 ON THE CR'S OWN HEADLINE FEATURE.** Put a premises that has
meter reads on a route and press `Create route ✓`: `POST /routes` answers
**HTTP 500** and the screen says *"Something went wrong on our side. Nothing was
saved."* Editing the seeded `Route 1` does the same. The cause is one value:
the route's `last_completion` is a raw timestamp, it goes into the audit row's
JSON, and the database driver refuses it. **On the demo tenant exactly ONE of
the nine premises has been read (1408 Bluestem Ln, 135 reads) and it is the one
that cannot be put on a route — which is also why the bug is easy to miss here
and impossible to miss on a live utility, where every premises has been read.**
COUNTED, not estimated. The CR-006 build passed 26 new backend tests and a 650-case selection
because none of those fixtures has a single meter read on the premises it puts
on a route.

**DEF-218 · THE SCREEN CAN CREATE EXACTLY ONE ROUTE AND ONE CYCLE.** The code
box is pre-filled `RT-001` from the numbering format. Create that route, press
`+ Add route` again — it offers **`RT-001` again**, and saving is refused *"A
route with that code already exists."* The counter never advances, because the
server only takes a number from the series when the screen sends none, and the
screen always sends the one it pre-filled. Same for `CY-001`.

**DEF-219 · A DRAFT EMPTIES AN ACTIVE ROUTE.** `Route 2 · Mason Rd` — Active,
inside cycle 08-A — read **1 premises · 2 units, 3 meters**. A route built over
the same premises and saved with `Save draft ✓` took them: Route 2 then read
**0 · 0 and 0 meters** on the landing, still Active, still listed inside 08-A.
The CR's own rule is *"drafts don't affect Reads/Billing"* and the radio a user
picks says *"Draft — not used by Reads or Billing yet"*. Reads themselves still
run; what is wrong is that the screen now tells a utility an active route is
empty when it is not.

**DEF-220 / DEF-221 · THE AREAS RULING IS NOT DELIVERED ON ANY SCREEN.** PO
ruling 2026-08-16: *"user can define their own areas and we wil tag them to
premises ; in CR06 you can use area and sub area for filtering - all option 1 to
many options will be required."* The filter is built, and it is genuinely
multi-select with removable chips — **and it can only ever return zero rows.**
Every row of the picker shows `—` under `Area · sub`, and ticking any area chip
takes it from *"9 premises match your filters."* to *"0 premises match your
filters."* **No screen anywhere can tag a premises to an area** (the column
shipped, the write path did not: the add-premises wizard and the premises detail
page draw no such field, and the API refuses the field outright), and **no
screen can create a sub-area** — the card is literally named *"Areas &
sub-areas"* and its `+ Add entry` form offers Code, Name and Detail and nothing
else, so the second level exists only in the database.

**DEF-222 / DEF-223 / DEF-224 · three smaller ones.** Editing commits with a
button that says **"Create route ✓"** under a summary that says *"Ready to save
Route 1."* · four B14 rules measured broken in the browser (two table type sizes
— 14px on the landing, 13.5px in the wizards, where the rule is one size; three
button sizes where the rule allows two; two wizard list tables with no
pagination footer; and the cycle wizard's route picker with no toolbar at all
while the premises picker two steps away has search, chips and a filter) · and
the copy: the preview reads *"bills out the 5 · due the 26"* where r10 says
*"5th"* and *"26th"*, and no count has a plural form (*"1 routes selected"*).

#### THE VERDICT

**CR-006 does NOT close.** The screens are real and most of the change works, so
this is not CR-004's *five screens answering 500* — but the three lead findings
each break a promise the CR itself made:

1. **the feature does not work on a tenant with reading history** (DEF-217),
2. **it works exactly once** (DEF-218), and
3. **the "areas and sub-areas" the PO ruled for cannot be entered anywhere**
   (DEF-220/221), which makes the filter that was built unusable.

**WHAT REMAINS, in order.** Fix DEF-217 (one value in an audit payload) and
DEF-218 (which end of the numbering contract allocates), then re-run this spec —
those two are small and they are what stands between this CR and a working
screen. DEF-219 needs a RULING before a fix: does a draft hold a provisional
membership, or does the picker refuse to move a premises into a draft and say
so? DEF-220/221 are the real remaining SCOPE — a premises→area control and a
sub-area parent field are two new pieces of screen, and the PO should decide
whether they land inside CR-006 or as their own change. DEF-222/223/224 are copy
and convention and can travel with any of the above.

**Nothing in this walkthrough touched a rate, a fee or any ❄️ B4/B5 figure, and
CR-006 still needs no finance re-sign.**

**How this spec behaves after a fix, deliberately:** the eight findings are
pinned as `test.fail()` tests that state the RULE, so **the moment one is fixed
the run goes RED with "expected to fail but passed"** at that line, forcing the
annotation off and the defect row closed. A green run of the file means *the
screens work as described and the eight findings are still open* — it does not
mean the surface is right.

### CR-006 — THE AREA PICKER IS BUILT (2026-08-17). Blocker C closed; build 2.7.3.

**The ruling:** *"when we add premises you should allow to select areas and sub
areas on premises"*. This was the last of CR-006's three blockers — the wizard
one-route bug and the draft-empties-a-live-route bug landed earlier the same day.

**THE NUMBER THAT SAYS IT WORKS.** The area filter on the SET-06 route picker
could only ever return **zero rows**: ticking any chip took it from *"9 premises
match"* to *"0 premises match"*, on every tenant, because `premises.area_id` had
never held a value anywhere. It now returns rows. The acceptance test seeds three
premises, tags two into NORTH, ticks NORTH, and asserts **2** — not 0, not 3.

**What shipped, in three parts:**

1. **THE SCREEN (r11 step 2b).** An **Area** select and a **Sub-area** select on
   the premises form — the add wizard (S16 step 1) and the edit modal (S14) use
   the SAME component, so the two forms cannot drift. The premises detail shows
   the area (a fresh GET, so it proves the tag stuck) and the list gains an
   Area column, available rather than default.
2. **THE WRITE PATH.** `POST/PATCH /premises` accepts `area_code`. It used to
   answer `VAL-002 metering.unknown_field` — the measured refusal, quoted from
   the run at HEAD. Absent leaves the tag alone; an explicit empty clears it.
3. **SUB-AREA CREATION.** The *"Areas & sub-areas"* reference-data card gains a
   **Parent area** picker that sends `parent_code`, and a Parent column. The
   backend validation had existed since CR-006 and nothing could reach it. Two
   dropdowns in the route wizard have rendered `parent_name ? "A · B" : B` since
   then over data the product could not produce — **that dead branch is alive.**

**⚠ AND THE PART THAT IS NOT A FORM FIELD — BR-MET-083, new and CONFIRMED.**
BR-MET-082 says the route model is a live cascade, and `routes.area_id` had
existed since CR-006 without ever paying out. Now: **(a)** tagging a premises
into an area joins it to that area's ACTIVE routes, and **(b)** a unit added to
a premises already on a route joins that route. Four boundaries, each with a
test that says it must not happen — active routes only; a cascade never takes a
unit off another route (that is BR-MET-074's move and it is confirmed on
screen); a parent's route covers its sub-areas; re-tagging never removes.

**⚠ WHAT IS EXPLICITLY NOT DONE, so nobody reads this as DEF-225 closed.**
Membership is still a **stored** answer kept correct by two more write paths —
**not derived at run time**, which is what BR-MET-082 Amendment 1 asks for.
**DEF-225 stays OPEN** and its row says what remains: the derivation itself, the
preview-to-issue freeze the amendment's tension requires, a route whose
`area_id` CHANGES re-deriving its members, and **accounts, which still have no
path to a route or a cycle in any form** — so *"how many accounts does this run
cover"* remains unanswerable through the chain.

**Fixed alongside:** DEF-220, DEF-221, and DEF-227 (filed by this lane before
fixing it — `ensure_service_point` inherited ANY of a unit's routes rather than
the one for its own service, a coin-flip since BR-MET-074 made membership
per-service).

**Rollback:** revert `ad60b77` (backend + BR-MET-083), `23f91d0` (screens) and
`7d89a84` (types + catalogues). The column and the parent FK predate all three
and stay; reverting returns the product to "the filter returns zero rows",
which is where it was this morning. No migration, no data written that a
revert would strand — the cascade writes `route_memberships` rows, which the
route wizard already writes and already rewrites on every edit.

**Version 2.7.3.** `<fix>` and not `<change>`: the change digit tracks the most
recent CR to land code and CR-007 already took 7. CR-006's own build was 2.7.1.

**CR-006 still needs no finance re-sign** — nothing here touches a B4/B5 figure.

### CR-010 · THE CLOSURE RECORD — 2026-08-19 · version `2.22.0` · **CLOSED**

> **The version was assigned `2.20.0` and re-assigned to `2.22.0`, and the
> reason belongs in the record.** `2.20.0` was written into `package.json`,
> and a concurrent lane's write to the same line landed between that edit and
> the commit that should have carried it — so the file went 2.19.1 → 2.21.0
> and **`2.20.0` was never a build anybody can look at**. This is the SAME
> instant-expires mechanism recorded in §6 below, on a second file, found by
> the law-11 post-push check (`git show <tip>:07-frontend/package.json` did
> not contain the number this record claimed). The closing slice is `2.22.0`,
> it is stamped, and `2.20.0` is retired unused.

Written under `13-change-process.md` §8 and the section under it that the PO's
own challenge produced — *"why you are not closing it and every time keep
something open we are losing time"* — **a defect blocks its CR only if it is one
of THAT CR's OWN REQUIREMENTS not working.** Every claim below is measured
against the running `sbh_e2e` database and against Chromium on the booted stack;
nothing here is copied from a document, because copying a document is what
produced the number this CR opens with.

#### 1 · THE COUNT — item 0 answered, out of the product

The PO's *"we have increase this number check out seed data"* was aimed at
**"31 priced objects"**, a figure the CR-013 design took from r10's own fixture
line: *"6 plans · 7 rate schedules · 13 charge codes · 5 discounts · 6 taxes &
fees"*. That line describes a **drawing**. Here is the product, counted with
`select count(*)` on the seeded tenant (Brazos Bend Utilities, provisioned
2026-08-18 08:19 at fixture **V2.18.0.0**), beside what a tenant provisioned at
HEAD receives today (fixture **V2.19.0.0**, pinned by
`06-backend/tests/test_cr010_reference_list_inventory.py`):

| Priced object | r10's drawing | **LIVE, this tenant** | A tenant provisioned at HEAD |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plans | 6 | **5** | 5 |
| Rate schedules (`tariffs`) | 7 | **6** | 6 |
| Charge codes (`charges`) | 13 | **23** | 23 |
| Discounts | 5 | **0** | 0 |
| Tax RATES (`taxes`) | 6 | **2** | **5** |
| Tax JURISDICTIONS | — | **5** | **7** |
| **"Priced objects" on r10's own definition** (schedules + codes + discounts + taxes) | **31** | **31** | **34** |

**Three things in that table matter more than the total.**

#### 4 · WHAT BLOCKED, AND WHAT WAS FIXED

**One defect blocked, and the blocking sentence is written out as §8 requires:**

> **DEF-258 blocks because CR-010 item 7 says *"the NotificationSettings row is

It was invisible from every screen, because the rows materialise on first read —
so the API, the tab and every existing test saw a populated matrix whatever
provisioning did. **The database is what could tell them apart**, and it did:

```
notification_settings   min(created_at) = 2026-08-18 08:19:26   ← provisioning
notification_rules      min(created_at) = 2026-08-19 04:21:17   ← twenty hours later,
                                                                  when a lane opened S8
```

Twenty hours in which *"has this utility configured its notifications?"* answered
**zero rows**, which is indistinguishable from *"nobody has opened the screen"* —
the exact ambiguity item 7 removed for the dispatch row and left standing here.

**The fix:** `apps.notifications.rule_service.seed_rules()` is published and
called from `seed_notification_settings`, which provisioning already calls, so
the **15 rule rows and their 26 channel rows** are written in the same breath as
the dispatch row. `manage.py seed_demo --tenant <sub>` gains the matching repair
door, because a change to provisioning never reaches a tenant that already exists
(hard-won law 4). **Proved RED first, in a `git worktree` at HEAD so the shared
tree was never moved:** the new
`test_def258__the_set12_rule_rows_seed_at_provisioning_too` fails
`AssertionError: assert 0 == 15` against the code as it was, and passes after.
**Nothing about sending changes:** BR-NOT-005 and BR-NOT-013 stand.

#### 6 · WHAT THIS LANE FILED

* **DEF-289 · the register said `open` for four defects that were fixed a day
  earlier.** `git show f6c0120 --stat` lists ten files and none of them is
  `10-defect-log.csv`. **The cost is measured, not hypothetical:** this lane was
  handed *"DEF-256, DEF-257 open"* as its triage list and both had been shipped
  for a day. Its `escape_reason` is the useful part — **nothing joins a DEF-###
  in a commit message to that defect's row**, so the staleness is invisible to
  every gate and to the report the PO reads. The proposed check is a string join,
  not a judgment: fail any commit naming a DEF-### whose row still reads `open`
  with an empty `fixed_commit`.
* It was filed as DEF-284, **renumbered to DEF-289** because two other lanes
  reached for 284 within the same hour. Recorded because it is the same class of
  fault as the defect itself.

* **And one thing this lane did WRONG, recorded because the record is the
  point.** The closure commit `a0dde65` was assembled through a private
  `GIT_INDEX_FILE` precisely so it would carry no other lane's work — and it
  carried one anyway: `CHANGELOG.md` was checked for foreign hunks, found clean,
  and the CR-011 lane wrote its `## [2.21.0]` entry into the working copy in the
  minutes between that check and the commit. **Nothing is lost** — the entry is
  correct, it is theirs, and it is now safely in history — so it is recorded
  rather than reverted, exactly as `b0b7080` decided the same day for the same
  class. **The lesson is narrower than "read the hunks", which this lane did:**
  a file verified exclusive is only exclusive *at the instant it is verified*,
  and in a tree with six lanes that instant expires. For a file nobody else is
  expected to touch, build it from HEAD plus your own hunks anyway — the same
  treatment the shared files got — because the cost is one string replace and
  the alternative is publishing work its author has not finished.

#### 7 · THE ROLLBACK, STATED BEFORE SHIPPING

**Reversible, and cheaply.** The change is one call and its repair door: remove
the `rule_service.seed_rules()` call from `seed_notification_settings` and the
`seed_demo` block, and provisioning is exactly as it was. **No data has to be
undone** — the rule rows it writes are the same rows the first read would have
written, with the same values, so a tenant seeded under this change and a tenant
seeded before it are indistinguishable in content. **No migration, no money, no
figure moves.** That is the whole reason this was safe to land under a closure.

#### 8 · WHAT CR-010 STILL OWES THE PO — and why it is not a block

Two items are **waiting on the Product Owner, not on us**, and closing the CR
does not close them:

* **Item 1's nine short lists.** Nine of the twenty are shorter than a real
  water/electric/gas utility operates on. The drafted additions are written and
  are with the PO, because the sign-off rule of 2026-08-11 makes vocabulary
  theirs — *"each drafted list goes to the PO in plain English with its rows
  before it ships"*. A test that pinned a guess would make the guess look signed.
* **Item 4's template review** — which activities the PO expects that the 32
  classes do not cover. The 32 are on screen; the review is a conversation.

Both are agenda items with a named owner. Neither is a defect and neither is
this CR's own requirement failing, which is precisely the distinction the PO's
2026-08-19 challenge asked us to start making.

The standing sign-off rule (PO 2026-08-11) has two parts and **both are
required**: the rule and its worked number are put to the PO **in plain English
with a concrete figure — never as an ID to go and look up**, and the ruling is
then written into the ledger verbatim with the exact statements shown. **A
signature covers only what was shown.**

The list this message answers was written as **IDs** — "OQ-256 variant axes",
"OQ-262 three trigger-less events", "4180 + 8 cost rows". That is precisely the
form the standing instruction forbids, and the fault is the asker's, not the
PO's. So the answers are captured here in full, and each is marked with whether
it can be acted on:

| # | Item | PO's answer | Actionable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Tax jurisdiction rates | *"already answered"* | **VERIFY FIRST** — find the prior ruling and its five figures; if none exists, re-present with the figures |

| 3 | Account sub-type names | *"Confirmed"* | **YES** — the 12-row tree was shown on screen (audit Part 10.0) |

| 6 | OQ-262 three trigger-less events | *"okay-"* | **NO — no options were put.** The question is who owns three events with no trigger; "okay" selects nothing |

| 8 | Security policy row-at-provisioning | *"you decide"* | **YES** — explicit delegation |
| 9 | The 4 legal-wording template classes | *"already answer - provide default and allow user to change"* | **YES, and it REVERSES the current posture** — see below |

### Item 9 is the largest and it reverses a standing refusal

Four template classes ship deliberately EMPTY today, each holding a written

### CR-011 · THE RETROACTIVE CLOSURE AUDIT — every CR measured against the new bar (2026-08-18)

The PO's closure ruling (`13-change-process.md` §8) is a **standing rule, applied
backwards as well as forwards**. Applying it retroactively is the point: a bar
that only governs future CRs would leave the ones already marked finished
resting on the evidence the bar was written to reject.

**Measured, not asserted** — `07-frontend/e2e/` was listed and each spec counted,
and each CR's own record was read for a RUN, because a spec that exists and was
never run against a live stack is a file, not evidence.

| CR | Browser evidence in the repo | Run recorded? | Meets the bar |
|---|---|---|---|
| CR-001 | none | — | ❌ **unmet** (R1, closed 2026-08-11, predates the rule) |
| CR-002 | ships no code | n/a | **N/A** — nothing for a person to do on a screen |
| CR-003 | none | — | ❌ **unmet** — closed 2026-08-17 on gates + checklist only |
| CR-004 | `CR-004-reference-crud.spec.ts`, 454 lines / 2 tests | ✅ *"Proved by clicking, not by tests"* | ✅ **MET** |
| CR-005 | `CR-005-numbering.spec.ts`, 1019 lines / 17 tests | ✅ `15 passed (11.4m)` against a live stack | ✅ **MET** |
| CR-006 | `CR-006-routes-cycles.spec.ts`, 1792 lines / 29 tests | ✅ 4 runs, incl. run 4 **over its own leftovers** | ✅ **MET** — and it still does not close, on open defects |
| CR-007 | `CR-007-templates.spec.ts`, **1099 lines / 9 tests** | ❌ **no run recorded anywhere** | ⚠ **UNPROVEN — the spec exists and nothing says it ever ran** |
| CR-008 | none | — | ❌ **unmet** |
| CR-009 | none — the lane self-reported it | ❌ | ❌ **unmet**, and honestly declared at the time |
| CR-010 | `CR-010-seed-completeness.spec.ts`, 4 tests | ✅ **2026-08-19, `4 passed`, 88 browser assertions, run twice** | ✅ **MET** — and CLOSED; see its closure record |

#### The finding that matters most: CR-007

CR-007's status reads *"BUILT · awaiting human review"*, and the review was
described to the PO as **the only thing standing between it and closed**. That
was wrong, and this audit is what found it. A 1,099-line walkthrough was
authored and **no record in this repository says it was ever executed against a
booted stack.** Under the new bar CR-007 cannot close on a review alone,
regardless of what the review says.

**This is exactly the failure mode the bar exists for**, and it is CR-005's
lesson repeating: that CR also had its walkthrough written, then the run found
seven of eight requirements passing and one failing, and it did not close. A
spec is a claim. A run is evidence.

#### What each unmet CR owes

* **CR-003** — a walkthrough of the Settings tab strip and the Configure
  sub-tabs: click every moved tab, confirm each resolves and its old URL still
  works. Small; the CR is otherwise complete.
* **CR-007** — **RUN the spec that already exists**, then fix what it finds.
  Cheapest unmet item on this table, because the expensive half is written.
* **CR-008** — no spec exists. Chart of accounts, the GL map's five sections,
  the CSV import and the tender→cash column, performed by a person.
* **CR-009** — the two new S8 cards (Email sender, Send-time elections), named
  by its own lane as the debt.
* **CR-010** — per landing slice, not once at the end.
* **CR-001** — closed under the old bar and shipped in R1. **NOT reopened**:
  the rule is dated 2026-08-18 and a rule applied to a shipped R1 change would
  be re-litigating a closed release. Recorded here as unmet so the record is
  honest about WHY it is exempt, rather than silently meeting a bar it never
  faced.

#### The gate that would enforce this does not exist

Nothing in `10-scripts/gates/` reads a walkthrough result, and G23's own header
says why the general case is hard: *"nothing automated reads prose for truth."*
What IS mechanisable is narrower and worth building: **refuse a CR whose status
says CLOSED when no run record cites a spec file.** That is a string check over
two files, not a judgment. Owed, and named here rather than assumed.

### CR-011 item 9 · THE PO RULED ON BOTH FLAGGED CONTRACTS (2026-08-18) — one accepted, one OVERRULED

This session put the four legal-wording classes back as **2 authored / 1
placeholder / 1 held**. The PO answered both flagged ones in one message.

#### (a) ACH / autopay authorization — the placeholder proposal ACCEPTED

> *"Do it; put the details, I will handle it with user"*

**Ruled: build the labelled placeholder**, and **write down the details so the
PO can take them to the utility.** The second half is a deliverable, not a
courtesy — the PO is taking this to a real customer, so what the utility must
supply has to be stated in plain English on the screen and in the record, not
left as "paste your own".

**What ships:** the class carries a body that is visibly a PLACEHOLDER, refuses
to be used until the utility replaces it, and states WHY on its face — the
wording of a recurring-ACH authorization is prescribed by NACHA, a scheme this
repo does not hold, so a default drafted by inference is the one document in
this product where a plausible wrong answer creates real liability. **The
refusal is the feature.** What the utility must supply is enumerated for the PO
in the same slice.

#### (b) Payment-plan agreement — this session's "held" recommendation is OVERRULED

> *"create this dont leave it open ; once sample and defaults are available we
> can make changes later; but without default sample functionalities ill not
> work"*

**Ruled: create it.** The PO's reasoning is recorded because it is the general
principle and not a one-off: **a class held empty makes the FEATURE not work at
all**, and a default that is imperfect but present can be changed later, while
an absent one leaves a utility with nothing to demonstrate or edit. That
outranks this session's objection.

**The objection is NOT withdrawn, it is OVERRULED, and both halves are recorded
because the constraint is real and someone will meet it again:** `rendering.py`
cannot express a REPEATING BLOCK, so the instalment schedule table
(# · due date · amount · remaining) has no token. A body authored today can
state the plan's TOTAL, its down payment, the NUMBER of instalments and their
frequency — every one a scalar the renderer already handles — and **cannot print
the per-instalment rows.**

**So the deliverable is scoped honestly rather than silently under-delivered:**
the default body is authored from the scalars, and where the schedule belongs it
carries a NAMED, visible absence — the same posture every other unrenderable
figure in this product already takes — rather than quietly omitting the rows and
producing a document that reads complete and is not. **A signed agreement stating
a total with no due dates is the failure mode the original refusal was written
about.**

⚠ **CORRECTION, 2026-08-18 — THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE ORIGINALLY OFFERED "THE
SCHEDULE IS ATTACHED" AS AN ACCEPTABLE POSTURE, AND THAT IS THE OPTION THE PO
HAD ALREADY REJECTED.** The building lane found it and it is corrected here
rather than quietly edited, because this record is what the next agent builds
from. **OQ-244 was ANSWERED on 2026-08-16 → BR-NOT-016 CONFIRMED**, PO verbatim:
*"a Print the schedule inside the agreement"* — with the reason written into the
rule: *"an attachment can be separated from the document it belongs to, and a
customer who signed a total without dates agreed to a number rather than to a
schedule."* This session read OQ-244 as still open on *"should this class exist
at all"* and it was open on nothing of the kind. **The schedule prints INSIDE
the agreement, through a merge token for the table, and an attachment is not on
the table.**

**What that changes in practice, and it is stronger than what was proposed:**
`{schedule_table}` is a RULED token, it sits in the palette, and it is MANDATORY
CLASS CONTENT — a utility may rewrite every word around it and cannot save a
version without it. Nothing builds the repeating block yet, so it renders `——`,
the same named absence every unsupplied token renders, under a clause reading
**"Do not sign this agreement if the schedule above is blank or shows ——."**

**OQ-244 still does NOT close.** It changes from *"print it inside or attach
it"* — answered — to *"how does the renderer print a repeating block"*, which is
a follow-on capability with a real body waiting on it rather than a question
blocking one.

**Both are BR-NOT-002 effective-dated contracts**, so a draft still needs an
`effective_from` a human chooses; provisioning-day is not that date. That
constraint is untouched by this ruling and applies to both.

### CR-011 · THE CLOSURE RECORD — 2026-08-19 · version `2.21.0` · **CLOSED**

**What this CR required, restated because it is not the usual shape.** CR-011
shipped no screen. Its requirement IS **the ten decisions being recorded and
implemented**, so the closure test is applied decision by decision: *was it
written down where the next agent will find it, and — where it produced
something a person should be able to see or do — does that happen on the
screen?* Nothing here is closed on prose claiming it was done.

**The walkthrough**, on the PO's bar of 2026-08-18 (§8): a person signed in at
`http://127.0.0.1:8080/brazosbend/signin` as `dana@brazosbendutilities.com`
against the booted stack (PostgreSQL 16 + Django + the BUILT SPA) and drove
`07-frontend/e2e/CR-011-decisions.spec.ts`.

| run | result |
|---|---|
| 1 (first ever, before any fix) | 3 passed · **2 failed** — decision 7 red on `locator('#email') … element(s) not found`; decision 1 red on a selector, not on the product |
| 2 (after the two fixes + SPA rebuild) | ✅ **5 passed** |
| 3 — **straight over run 2's leftovers, no reset** | ✅ **5 passed** |

Run 3 is the one that matters for trust: decision 7's case CHANGES a seeded
user's email and puts it back, so a second pass straight over its own residue is
what proves nothing here passes only on a pristine seed.

#### The ten decisions, decision by decision

#### What blocked, stated as the rule requires

Under `13-change-process.md` §"a defect is not a CR blocker", a defect blocks
only if it is **that CR's own requirement not working**. CR-011's requirement is
the ten decisions being recorded and implemented, so an unimplemented decision
genuinely blocks and a bug in a surface a decision merely touches does not. Two
blocked:

* **Decision 7 blocked because CR-011 decision 7 says the utility may later
  change email as well as name, and changing an email did not happen** — the
  Edit-user modal rendered no email field and its PATCH carried none. Fixed
  (DEF-290); proved on screen by changing an address and reading it back.
* **Decision 8 blocked because CR-011 decision 8 delegates the security-policy
  row-at-provisioning question to us to decide, and no decision existed** — not
  a ruling, not an OQ, not a line of code. A delegation nobody exercised is the
  decision not being made. Decided, recorded with its reasoning and its figures,
  implemented, tested RED-first, and repaired on the live tenant.

Items 4 and 6 were the third and fourth blocking claims and they are the same
sentence in a different key: **CR-011's stated requirement for those two is that
they go back to the PO with concrete figures and named options, and no such
packet existed.** It exists now. (Obtaining the PO's *answer* is not this CR's
to deliver — a CR that closed only when the PO replied could never be closed by
us at all.)

#### Open defects against these surfaces, and why none of them blocks

* **DEF-291** — the Taxes & fees screen states a rate as the stored fraction,
  *"0.062500 of the taxable amount"*, where the ruled table says 6.25%. **Does
  not block:** decision 1's requirement is that the five figures be ruled and
  seeded, and they are; how the rate is *presented* is an adjacent surface the
  decision merely touches. Pinned RED-on-fix by the walkthrough, so the day the
  screen speaks percent the assertion goes red at the line and this row closes.
* **DEF-292** — a tax's customer-class exemption and premises-geography scope
  can be stored, seeded and enforced and appear on **no screen**, so the ruled
  City Franchise Fee can never be given a city and reaches nobody. **Does not
  block:** the five ruled rows seed with their conditions and the engine fails
  closed, which is the safe direction; a missing editor is a gap CR-011's text
  never asked for — a new change, not this one. Named here because "seeded and
  working" must not be said of that row until it has a box to type a city in.
* **DEF-293** — CR-008's status paragraph says the finance re-sign is
  outstanding; it was signed the same day. **Does not block:** it is a stale
  header on another CR, found by CR-011's item-2 verification and stamped in
  place in this commit rather than silently rewritten. Restating that header is
  CR-008's owner's act.
* **DEF-195** (pre-existing, open) — a utility's logo and brand colours are
  drawn nowhere, and the generated two-letter mark OQ-257 was ruled into on
  2026-08-16 is not built. **Does not block:** decision 5 was VERIFY-FIRST and
  the verification is complete — the question was already answered, and building
  the mark is CR-007's order of work.

#### Three things this closure did that were not asked for, recorded so they are not lost

1. **The defect register held a duplicate `DEF-284`** — two lanes allocated the
   same id within an hour and both committed it. The later row (the CR-010
   closing lane's) is renumbered to **DEF-289**, which was free, and G17's
   duplicate-id gate stops reporting it. Nothing else in that row moved; that
   lane has since recorded the collision from its own side.
2. **`12-governance/01-open-questions.md` still holds three duplicate ids** —
   OQ-253, OQ-254 and OQ-255 are each defined twice, in HEAD, before this lane
   touched the file. **Deliberately not fixed here:** three renumbers in a
   register another lane is actively editing is the DEF-165 hazard, and G17 was
   already failing on them.
3. **This lane's own `## [2.21.0]` CHANGELOG entry and its two version literals
   were swept into commit `a0dde65` by the CR-010 lane**, in the minutes between
   that lane verifying `CHANGELOG.md` was clean and committing it. That lane
   found it, recorded it against itself in its own closure record above, and
   nothing was lost. **One consequence is worth stating because change-process §7
   depends on it: `07-frontend/package.json` never held `2.20.0` in any commit**
   — `git log -S` finds no such change — so CR-010's recorded version names a
   slice that exists in the register and not in a build. Both literals read
   `2.21.0` from here.
4. **A 15-line paragraph of that same CR-010 record was clobbered by this lane
   in the opposite direction** — read, transformed and written back across a
   window in which its author appended to the file — and was **restored from HEAD
   byte-for-byte before this commit**, verified by re-reading the diff until
   every remaining deletion was one this lane authored. Recorded rather than
   quietly repaired: it is the fourth mechanism in CLAUDE.md law 11 arriving in a
   markdown register instead of a source file, and the check that caught it was
   reading the hunks, not the file count.

#### Two things this closure did that were not asked for, recorded so they are not lost

1. **The five dark DSH-01 seams were never parked, and G20 has been RED on
   CR-012's own file since 2026-08-18.** `pending_approval_count`,
   `disconnect_eligible_count`, `open_close_period`, `monthly_revenue_target`
   and `current_subscription` are declared in `dashboard_seams.py` and published
   by nobody. Each is now a row in `seam_known_gaps.txt` with the reason its
   absence is honest — the disconnect one is the sharpest: **a wrong count there
   proposes disconnecting a household**, so the panel contributes no row at all
   rather than an approximation. Parking is not how a finding is closed; the row
   writes down the price. G20 goes from FAIL to PASS.
2. **Three dashboard catalogue keys were dead in all eleven catalogues** —
   `dashboard.aging.wouldTotal`, `dashboard.serviceMix.unattributed` and
   `dashboard.todo.explainer`, left by DEF-282's fix and reachable from no call
   site. Deleted. `dashboard.cycle.closesIn` and `dashboard.serviceMix.remainder`
   still read as findings in G18 and are NOT a defect: the gate cannot see
   i18next's `_one`/`_other` plural suffixes, so it reports the base key missing
   and both suffixed forms dead. That is a gate blind spot, it predates this
   slice, and it is stated here rather than silenced.
3. **This lane's own catalogue edits were swept into another lane's commit**
   (`3e51e11`) in the minutes between writing them and committing them — the
   eleven `dashboard.serviceMix.empty` strings landed under a commit about a
   different defect. **Nothing was lost and the published content is correct**,
   so it is recorded rather than repaired: it is CLAUDE.md law 11's fifth
   mechanism seen from the PUBLISHING side, and both checks the law prescribes
   pass on it — the file count was right and the author's own change was present.
   The practical rule underneath it is the one the law already states: commit
   small and commit often.
4. **The regenerated journey index is deliberately NOT in this commit.** G12
   reports it stale, and re-running the generator produced a 60-line diff that is
   entirely about **US-PAY-025 becoming built** — another lane's work. Committing
   a generated file that states someone else's progress is the same class of
   mistake as DEF-168. It was stale before this slice and is left to its owner.

#### The rollback, stated before shipping

**Reversible in full, and no data is destroyed by reversing it.** The frontend
half is one field: removing the Email control and the `email` key from the PATCH
returns the modal to what it was, and no stored address is touched. The backend
half is one `get_or_create`: removing the provisioning call and the seam leaves
`security_policy_values` serving the same six figures from an unsaved instance
exactly as it did before, and the rows already written are read identically by
that same function — **there is no state in which a written row and the old
fallback disagree**, which is what the second test exists to guarantee. The
governance half (the decision batch, the OQ amendments, the defect rows) is
record and reverses by reverting the commit.

**Service mix · MTD (`.mix-row`) — THE HEART OF THIS CR.**
```
<div class="mix-row"><span class="lbl">Electric</span><span class="bar"><span style="width:70%"></span></span><span class="val">$238k</span></div>
…
<div class="mix-row"><span class="lbl">Trash</span><span class="bar"><span style="width:0%"></span></span><span class="val">—</span></div>
```
⚠ **THIS PARAGRAPH IS SUPERSEDED BY THE PO'S REQUIREMENTS OF THE SAME DAY —
READ BOTH, BECAUSE THE DRAWING AND THE RULE DISAGREE AND THE RULE WINS.**

*What r10's file computes* (kept, because the next agent will decode it exactly
as this lane did and "correct" the build back): 238 + 76 + 28 = **342**;
238/342 = **69.6% → 70%**, 76/342 = **22.2% → 22%**, 28/342 = **8.2% → 8%**.
Those are the three widths in the markup and they sum to 100, so **r10's own
bars are a share of the TOTAL**.

*What the PO ruled*, verbatim: **"Bars proportional to the largest service, not
the total."** That makes Electric **100%**, Water **32%** (76/238) and Sewer
**12%** (28/238) — different widths from the ones drawn in the file.

**THE PO'S REQUIREMENT GOVERNS.** r10 is the reference for layout, copy, flows
and states (PO ruling 2026-08-16); it is not a signed statement of arithmetic,
and where the requirement writer and the drawing disagree the writer is the
authority. Recorded here rather than silently followed so that nobody
re-derives 70/22/8 from the file in three weeks and files a defect against a
correct build.
**AND A SERVICE WITH NO REVENUE IS DRAWN, NOT OMITTED**: `width:0%` with `—` as
its value. That is the *"build all services"* instruction in one line of markup,
and it is the difference between *"this utility does not sell trash"* and
*"trash billed nothing this month"*.
**Values are ABBREVIATED** — `$238k`, not `$238,000`.

The PO supplied a full spec after the screenshot. Recorded word for word, because
a paraphrase of a design constraint is how the next agent builds the wrong thing.

> "Screen DSH-01, default landing route, renders inside the app shell's scrolling
> .view (padding 28/32/64).
>
> Tokens (from styles.css, don't invent): bg #f3f2f2, surface #eae9e9, ink
> #201e1d, accent #ec3013, divider = 40% ink. Archivo, headings 800. Radius 0
> everywhere, no shadows, no gradients. Structure comes from 1–2px rules, not
> cards. Numerals tabular.
>
> Layout — page-head → KPI band (5 cells, auto-fit minmax(180px,1fr), 2px rules
> top/bottom, 1px between) → 2fr 1fr grid: Recent activity | Service mix (this
> one gets the accent top-border) → 2fr 1fr grid: AR aging | To do.
>
> Components — .kpi (10px uppercase label / 30px value / 12px delta, .up in
> accent-700); .panel (surface bg, 2px divider top-border, h3 + accent "see"
> link); .act-row (60px 1fr auto: time / description with bolded entity /
> tabular amount); .pill in ok/warn/past/draft; .mix-row (label, 6px accent-fill
> track, right value); aging table with right-aligned Accounts/Amount/% columns.
>
> Data — one GET /api/dashboard?tenantId&asOf returning greeting, kpis[],
> activity[], serviceMix[], arAging[], todos[]. Money and counts arrive
> pre-formatted as strings — no client-side currency math. Per-section
> loading/empty/error states; one section failing must not blank the page.
>
> Interactions — Import reads opens the reads-import workflow; Run billing →
> Billing; panel links → audit log / Reports / Finance; To-do rows navigate via
> link.module. KPI cells are display-only in v1.
>
> The spec file also has the responsive breakpoints (1440/1200/1024) and 7
> acceptance criteria. Want me to add the sidebar/top-bar shell spec too, since
> the dashboard can't render standalone without it?"

#### TOKENS VERIFIED AGAINST THE REPO, not taken on trust

Every value the PO named is already declared in
`07-frontend/src/styles/tokens.css` and matches to the character: `--color-bg
#f3f2f2` · `--color-surface #eae9e9` · `--color-text #201e1d` · `--color-accent
#ec3013` · `--color-divider color-mix(in srgb, #201e1d 40%, transparent)` ·
`--font-heading "Archivo"` with `--font-heading-weight 800` · and all three
radius tokens at `0px`. **So the whole screen is buildable without one hardcoded
hex**, which is what *"don't invent"* asks for and what makes it checkable later.

#### THE SHELL QUESTION — ANSWERED: NO, and here is why

**The shell is already built and RATIFIED; a second spec for it would be a
second source of truth for a signed rule.** `components/AppShell.tsx` is 883
lines with its own stylesheet and test file, and **BR-SHL-001** governs it —
*"Sidebar 240/64px + toggle; canonical item order AMENDED TWICE. CURRENT ORDER
(PO ruling 2026-08-16): Dashboard · Plans & Rates · Premises · …"*. The dashboard
already renders inside that shell's `.view` today, which is why this CR is a fix
to a screen and not a new page.

**What WOULD be worth having instead**, if the PO's spec file holds it: the
**responsive breakpoints (1440/1200/1024) and the seven acceptance criteria**,
which this repo does NOT have for this screen and which decide when the build is
done. Those are asked for; the shell spec is declined with its reason.

#### ONE THING THE SPEC CHANGES ABOUT THE EXISTING BUILD

*"Money and counts arrive pre-formatted as strings — no client-side currency
math."* Today `DashboardPage.tsx` calls a `money()` helper on the payload. That
is a real change of contract and it is the RIGHT direction — hard rule 2 keeps
rounding on the server, and a client that formats money is a client that can
round it differently from the bill. The endpoint shape also moves: the PO names
`GET /api/dashboard?tenantId&asOf`, where the built route is
`GET /dashboard/summary` (A11's own S7 row, US-REP-019). **Which one wins is a
contract decision, not a preference — A11 is a signed interface**, so it is
raised rather than silently re-pointed.

### CR-012 · THE FULL DSH-01 REQUIREMENTS, verbatim (2026-08-18)

The PO's complete requirement, recorded word for word. **It supersedes two things
this lane had derived from r10's file** — see the two ⚠ notes after it.

> "Requirements — DSH-01 · Dashboard (Home)
> **Purpose** Give the operator a single morning view of where money and work stand
> before the day's actions: what is owed, what is unbilled, what failed, what is due
> this cycle, and what needs a decision today. The dashboard originates no data —
> every figure is a rollup owned by another module, and every element is a doorway
> into that module. Landing page after sign-in and after onboarding completion.
> **Region 1 · Greeting & cycle status** — "Good morning, {first name}" + `{weekday} ·
> {month day} · Cycle {code} closes in {n} days`. Named cycle is the next-closing
> active cycle from SET-07 (tie broken by account count). On close day: "closes
> today"; after close before the run: "closed — bill run pending"; no cycle
> configured: link to Settings → Routes & Cycles. Actions: Import reads (secondary,
> opens reads-import workflow), Run billing → (primary, opens Billing). Both hidden
> for read-only roles.
> **Region 2 · KPI band** (five, fixed order)
> * AR outstanding — open balances across active accounts, now · MoM change
> * Unbilled reads — validated reads not yet consumed by a bill run · routes pending
> * Failed payments — failed/returned attempts this cycle · eligible for auto-retry
> * MTD revenue — billed amount posted MTD · against forecast
> * Active connections — active service connections · against plan limit
> Tenant-scoped, respecting area/sub-area restrictions. Deltas shown in accent when
> the movement is the unfavourable one. Over plan limit is a commercial signal, shown
> plainly — upgrade prompts live in Settings → Subscription. KPI cells do not
> navigate in v1.
> **Region 3 · Recent activity** — last 24h, max 6 rows, newest first: bill runs,
> payments, read imports, adjustments, dunning, new accounts. Time / event with
> entity / amount (`—` where none). Status pill only where the event has a flaggable
> outcome. Sourced from the audit log filtered to operator-relevant types; events the
> role can't see in their own module are excluded. "View all →" opens the audit log
> unfiltered.
> **Region 4 · Service mix · MTD** — billed revenue split across Electric, Water,
> Sewer, Trash, Gas. All five always listed (unsold services show an empty bar and

> **Shared rules** — fetch on load, refetch on focus when older than 60s, no polling;
