#### Group 5's notification queues — BUILT, 40 → 43 of 52

The first cohorts in this CR whose **counts are the fixture**: **340** accounts,
**680** queued rows, a **2,000**-row drop draining at batch size **500** (= four
hand-offs, which is what makes T7-17's *"changes the size after the 2nd
hand-off"* observable at all). A queue journey over a dozen rows asserts nothing
about batching, passes, and is DEF-108 with arithmetic instead of an empty table.

**⚠ `held` IS NOT QUIET HOURS, AND READING IT THAT WAY WOULD HAVE SEEDED THE
OPPOSITE WORLD.** `outbound_messages.held` is BR-PAY-018's **paper
suppression** — the account's address is known bad — and a held row is skipped
by every cycle until an ADDRESS VERIFICATION releases it. Quiet hours leave the
row `queued` and unheld; `dispatcher._within_send_window` simply declines while
the tenant's local clock is outside 08:00–21:00. The journeys' phrase
*"queued-and-held"* is prose for the second. A fixture that set the column would
have seeded 680 permanently-suppressed rows, and **T7-16 — whose whole subject
is moving the window and watching them go — would have been permanently false
while every count still looked right.** The seeder asserts `held == 0` for that
reason.

**Half the 680 carry no address, and the product is right about it.**
`customers.selectors.delivery_recipients_for_account` answers SMS
`recipient_not_resolvable` **always**, because the mobile-consent column
(`accounts.sms_reminders`) is PROPOSED-SCHEMA: *"nobody has asked this customer
whether they consent to texts"*. So 340 email rows are addressed and 340 SMS
rows carry a stated reason. The count both journeys assert is exact; inventing
phone numbers to "fix" the other half would be seeding consent nobody gave.

**DEF-577 (filed as DEF-572 — see the renumber note above), found by needing
340 units in one pass.** The `unit` number series
stood at **next_number 102** while units up to **U-00420** already existed, so
the 340-unit run walked the counter into the pre-existing block:
`IntegrityError: duplicate key value violates unique constraint
"uq_units_tenant_unit_no" … (unit_no)=(U-00102) already exists`. Some bulk path
creates units without allocating from the series, and every later creation
through S16 collides until an operator clicks through the failures one at a
time — *"Add unit" fails on any tenant that has ever imported or been
sample-seeded*. Not this lane's to fix; the cohort advances the counter through
`tenancy.services.save_number_series`, the S63 act, which is **forward-only by
rule** (BR-TEN-035). The durable fix named in the row: a guard that fails when
any series' `next_number` is at or below the highest value in its own table —
one cheap query, and a counter and the rows it numbers are two sources for one
fact that nothing in this repo compares.

**Coverage after this commit: 43 of 52.** What is left is **J24 (1,124
accounts)** and **T5-05 (1,240 invoices)** — not reached, and not blocked:
both are the same shape as the 340-account cohort just built, an order of
magnitude larger, and the honest statement is that this round ran out of room
rather than out of a way.

## CR-015 · The dashboard needs a period filter, because a calendar month is the wrong window for cycle-shaped work

| | |
|---|---|
| **Arrived** | 2026-08-19, working chat session, from the Product Owner |
| **Classification** | **CHANGE.** The period filter is not drawn in r10's DSH-01 and is not named in CR-012's requirement, so it is a new capability rather than CR-012 not working. |
| **Urgency** | Raised as a correction to a defect diagnosis, not flagged urgent. |
| **Status** | 🟢 **BUILT 2026-08-19 · version `2.25.0`** — see the closure record at the end of this section. |

### The request, verbatim

> "If we allow this then there is now way user can see previous values and they will be
> confuse what is dashbaord is saying - so we will ahve to allow period filter on
> dashbaord - so user can select the filter ; default filter can be last cycle or last 30
> days and let user to change the peiod"

### ⚠ THIS CORRECTS A WRONG DIAGNOSIS OF MINE, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE POINT

DEF-298 was filed hours earlier saying the demo tenant's dashboard is empty **because the
seed bills July and the dashboard defaults to the current month**, and that *"the fix
belongs in the seed, not the dashboard"* — explicitly recording that neither component had
a bug. **That was wrong, and the case that shows it uses no demo data at all:**

> A real utility, on the **3rd of any month**. Bills went out on the 25th. The dashboard
> shows the calendar month, so it shows **almost nothing** — for the first week of every
> month, forever. Revenue near zero, service mix nearly empty. Nothing is broken and the
> operator cannot tell why the screen looks dead.

The seed did not cause that; **the seed exposed it.** A calendar-month window on a screen
that reports cycle-shaped work is a product flaw, and fixing the fixture would have HIDDEN
it — making the demo look right while leaving every real tenant the same dead screen every
month. DEF-298's `escape_reason` is corrected in the register rather than left standing.

**The same fact had already been established in this repo and not applied here.** The
forecast analysis of 2026-08-18 recorded: *"billing is LUMPY, not daily — pro-rating by DAY
is wrong for any utility that does not bill daily, which is all of them."* That was applied
to the forecast sub-line and not to the period underneath it.

### THE DEFAULT — the two options the PO offered are not equivalent

The PO offered *"last cycle or last 30 days"*. Recommended: **last completed cycle, falling
back to last 30 days only when no cycle is configured.**

* **Last completed cycle** is the utility's OWN unit — what Finance closes against, what a
  bill run produces, and what an operator means by *"how did we do"*. It is also **stable**:
  it does not slide under the reader between two glances.
* **Last 30 days** is a rolling window that agrees with nothing else in the product. Two
  people looking an hour apart see different figures, and the dashboard can disagree with
  Finance while both are correct.
* The fallback also gives the cycle-status line's fourth state (`not_configured`) something
  honest to say on a brand-new tenant.

### TWO THINGS THIS DRAGS WITH IT, both stated before the build

1. **THE CONSISTENCY RULE GETS HARDER AND THE PERIOD MUST BE ON SCREEN.** The PO's rule is
   *"a KPI must agree with its owning module for the same as-of moment"*. Once a user may
   pick an arbitrary window, the dashboard can differ from Finance **because they are
   looking at different periods** — both correct, and it reads as a bug. So the selected
   period is stated prominently, not buried in a filter control.
2. **DEF-299 STOPS BEING COSMETIC AND SHOULD BE FIXED FIRST.** The dashboard labels itself
   `as_of 2026-08-31` when today is the 19th. With a user-selected period that ambiguity
   worsens, and it also breaks the server-side cache the PO authorised on 2026-08-19 —
   cache age computed against a future timestamp. Sequence: DEF-299, then this.

### RELATIONSHIP TO CR-012 — the PO's call, and recorded as open

CR-012 has three lanes' worth of proven work and is mid-close. This CR is its successor
rather than part of it, **unless the PO rules that CR-012 should be held open until the
filter ships.** That question is put to them; it is not decided here. Noted with it: holding
a CR open for a capability its own requirement never named is the pattern the PO corrected
on 2026-08-19 (*"why you are not closing it and every time keep something open"*).

---

### CR-015 · CLOSURE RECORD — BUILT 2026-08-19, version `2.25.0`

**Built in the ruled order: DEF-299 first, then the filter.** The order was a
ruling and not a preference, and it paid: the cache-age line built in step 3
states its figure against `as_of`, which was meaningless while `as_of` was a date
that had not happened.

#### 1 · DEF-299 — FIXED, and proved against the running product first

Reproduced on the booted stack on 2026-08-19 BEFORE anything was written:

```
as_of 2026-08-31 period {'start': '2026-08-01', 'end': '2026-08-31'}
today 2026-08-19
```

`as_of` is now **the read moment clamped into the selected period** (BR-REP-036).
The same tenant, same day, after the fix:

| Window selected | `period` | `as_of` | `read_on` | Revenue in window |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| last cycle *(default)* | 2026-08-12 → 2026-08-19 | **2026-08-19** | 2026-08-19 | 0.00 |
| this accounting period | 2026-08-01 → 2026-08-31 | **2026-08-19** | 2026-08-19 | 0.00 |
| last accounting period | 2026-07-01 → 2026-07-31 | **2026-07-31** | 2026-08-19 | **4,648.22** |
| last 30 days | 2026-07-21 → 2026-08-19 | **2026-08-19** | 2026-08-19 | 289.40 |

Mid-period it is today; on a closed period it is the period end. **BR-TEN-043
survived**: pass `as_of` and no clock is consulted at all — a test BREAKS the
`tenant_today` seam and asserts a caller who passed one still gets a full answer.

#### 2 · THE FILTER — four windows, the ruled default, and the window ON SCREEN

`last completed cycle · last 30 days · this accounting period · last accounting
period`, defaulting to **the last completed cycle** and falling back to **the last
30 days** when no cycle is configured. The choice rides in the URL as
`?f.period=<id>` (BR-SHL-011), so a window is shareable and survives a reload.

⚠ **THE WINDOW IS STATED IN DATES ABOVE THE FIGURES**, which is CR-015's own
condition and not a styling choice. The bar reads, in the reader's own locale:

> **Showing Aug 12, 2026 – Aug 19, 2026**  ·  Figures as of Aug 19, 2026

An e2e case asserts the bar's bounding box sits ABOVE the KPI strip's, because
*"prominent"* that a reader has to open a dropdown to satisfy is not prominent.

**An option the server cannot compute is ABSENT from the menu with its reason**
(`no_completed_billing_cycle`, `fiscal_period_not_configured`) — never
present-and-broken.

#### 3 · THE SERVER-SIDE CACHE IS **NOT BUILT**, and this is the reason

CR-012 reported it not-done for two reasons. **One is now closed** — a cache
states its age against `as_of`, and `as_of` is now a real moment. **The other is
not, and it is infrastructure rather than dashboard:** this deployment configures
**no `CACHES` setting at all**, so Django falls back to a per-process
`LocMemCache`, and `docker-compose.yml` says in its own header that there is
deliberately *"No Redis, no Celery worker, no beat."* A per-worker cache gives two
clerks two different cache ages for the same figures — the PO's condition
(*"where cached, state cache age rather than disagree with Finance"*) failing in
the one way it was written to prevent. Reported, not half-built.

**What WAS built is that condition applied to the cache that EXISTS.** The
five-minute client `staleTime` is real caching and nothing stated its age. The
period bar now reads *"Read 4 minutes ago"*, measured from react-query's own
`dataUpdatedAt`, and says nothing under a minute — *"0 minutes ago"* reads as a
fault where silence reads as the truth. ⚠ **And the cache key now carries the
period**, or the five-minute window would have served the previous window's
figures under the new window's heading.

#### 4 · DEF-298's SEED HALF IS **NOT BUILT** — reported rather than reached

The PO ruled option (b): the filter **and** the seed. The filter is built. The
seed is not, and the constraint is real: `08-qa/01-e2e/stack/seed_e2e_fixture.py`
pins its dates deliberately — `ISSUED_AT = datetime(2026, 7, 1, …)`, *"so a
re-boot on a different day writes the identical bill"* — and that bill is read
BY NAME by `W3-money-render.spec.ts` against **GT-1, B5 ❄️ FROZEN**. Moving it
moves a golden fixture. Adding a second, current-month bill run belongs to the
billing/QA fixture lane and would move row counts several specs assert. Left to
that lane, named here rather than attempted.

#### 5 · WHAT THE BROWSER WALK COVERED

Six cases in Chromium against the booted stack, `npm run build` run first: the
as-of moment against the browser's own clock · the window spelled out in dates
and positioned above the KPI strip · the ruled default · changing the window
moving the dates, the URL and surviving a reload · a hand-edited
`?f.period=last_fortnight` falling back instead of 500ing · the page header's
date NOT following the picker.

⚠ **RUN 1 FOUND A RED THAT WAS THE TEST'S OWN FAULT, and it is recorded rather
than quietly fixed.** *"the bar must state BOTH ends of the window; it reads
'Showing Aug 12, 2026 – Aug 19, 2026'"* — the screen was right and the spec's
date parser assumed `12 Aug 2026` against an en-US browser. A check whose output
cannot distinguish pass from fail is worse than no check (DEF-174's lesson), so
the parser now reads both orders and says in its own comment why.

#### 6 · WHAT THIS CHANGED THAT WAS ALREADY SIGNED

* **`dashboard_summary()` "takes NO arguments"** — the epic's own §US-REP-019 and
  the module's exception (2) both said a period picker on the landing screen
  *"would be a control that changes a number nobody asked to change."* The PO
  reversed it. Both texts are amended in place with the old wording kept, because
  the next agent will otherwise correct the build back to them.
* **`fiscal_period_not_configured` no longer blanks every money figure.** It now
  withdraws the two ACCOUNTING options. BR-TEN-022's reasoning is untouched and
  its premise is gone: the screen states its window, so it is no longer headed
  *"this period"* over something that is not one. An existing test asserting a
  page of nulls for that tenant is **inverted and kept**, not deleted.
* **The cycle read moved behind a failure boundary.** The first build called
  `seams.cycles_list()` bare in the page body and `test_cr012_tc15` went red with
  `RuntimeError: cycles_list is on fire` — a metering outage blanking the whole
  landing screen. CR-012's own test found it.

#### 7 · VERSION — `2.25.0`, and a collision worth recording

Both literals moved in one commit. ⚠ **Two lanes bumped the version on the same
day and the working tree held `2.24.1` while origin held `2.24.0`** — CR-016's
copy sweep took `2.24.0` and its Part E lane had `2.24.1` in flight. CR-015 takes
the next CHANGE, `2.25.0`, rather than contending for a number already spoken for.
This is DEF-296's shape one day on, and it argues that the version bump wants the
same treatment the defect register got: a tool that allocates against the remote
tip rather than a literal every lane edits by hand.

#### 8 · GATES — what this lane moved, and the two rows it did not

`run_gates` reads **19 PASS / 10 FAIL**, and every one of the ten was failing
before this lane started. Two deserve naming rather than a blanket "pre-existing":

* **G15 (i18n parity) is unmoved, and that was deliberate work.** The first
  version of the picker label used a `{{label}} · {{code}}` template — no
  translatable word, so all eleven catalogues held the identical string and G15
  counted one more value *"left in English"* in every one of them. It is now a
  whole sentence per language (*"Letzter abgeschlossener Zyklus ({{code}})"*),
  which is better copy and leaves the gate's count **exactly where it was**:
  de 450 → 450, ja 388 → 388, and so on for all ten.
* **G18 gains one instance of a KNOWN BLIND SPOT and it is not a new defect.**
  The gate cannot see i18next's `_one`/`_other` plural suffixes, so it reports
  `dashboard.period.age` as *"used in code, defined in no catalogue"* and both
  suffixed forms as dead. CR-012's closure recorded the identical finding for
  `dashboard.cycle.closesIn` and `dashboard.serviceMix.remainder`. The
  alternative — hand-rolling the plural in TSX — is wrong for every language
  with more than two plural forms, so the gate's limitation is stated rather
  than designed around.

**G27 (translation keys) is GREEN**, which is the gate that matters here: ten new
keys, all eleven catalogues, no `t("key")` without an entry. Golden **33 PASS /
0 FAIL**. `tsc --noEmit` clean, `vitest` 30 passed on the dashboard suite,
backend 98 passed across the three dashboard suites.

#### 9 · ONE QUESTION MINTED — OQ-268

The completed-cycle derivation is put to the PO as **OQ-268**, in a person's
words with the worked cycle, rather than left as a caveat inside a business-rule
row: *when you say "how did the last cycle do", do you mean the days the meters
were read, or the span ending with the bill going out?* It blocks nothing — the
window is stated in dates on screen either way — and a different answer moves the
default window by a few days and changes no rule.

## CR-016 · The UI is not verified by anything — styling conformance, and internal engineering prose on customer screens

| | |
|---|---|
| **Arrived** | 2026-08-19, from the Product Owner, with two screenshots of the DEPLOYED build at **v2.22.0** |
| **Classification** | **DEFECT-LED CHANGE.** The individual faults are defects and are filed as such. What the PO asked for is structural: *"lets handle it structurally"*. So this CR owns the SYSTEM that prevents the class, not the individual fixes. |
| **Urgency** | Reported from a live deployment a utility user can see. |

### The request, verbatim

> "We have deployed new version; I think Css and style for drop downs are not working;
> look at this screen from actual application"

> "in template view there is noting"

> "UI is very important, we need to be sure all UI works correctly"

> "How many styling, CSS issues are there, can you compare it with r10"

> "Youa re also adding internal content and BR codes on screen, that is not required; it
> is application also available to Utility suer why they ned all these details - those are
> for internal use"

> "Create a CR for this CS, STyling issues and internal content leak - lets handle it
> structurally"

### PART A · WHAT WAS FOUND, measured rather than estimated

**A1 · Every dropdown in the product rendered as an operating-system widget.** `.input`
sets a background, a border and a radius; a native `<select>` **ignores most of it**,
because the browser keeps painting its own control — the grey gradient body and the
platform arrow — ON TOP of the background the rule sets. There was a `textarea.input` rule
and **no `select.input` rule at all**. The design system styled two of the three form
controls and nobody noticed the third.

> **Why it survived so long, and this is the whole point of the CR:** *a select still looks
> like a select.* It is not broken, it is **foreign** — and foreign reads as fine in a
> screenshot and wrong on a screen. No test can tell the difference, because both render.

**A2 · 46 form controls across the feature screens carry no `className` at all**, so the
design system's control class never reaches them. They are native everywhere.

**A3 · Two components put a label on the wrong line.** A `<label>` is `display: inline`, so
one that WRAPS its control puts its text on the control's last baseline — on a twelve-row
textarea that drops the word *"Body"* to the bottom-left corner, level with the box's
bottom edge. That is the second screenshot.

**A4 · 16 catalogue strings and 2 JSX lines render internal references to utility users** —
`BR-`, `US-` and `OQ-` ids. Live examples:

> *"Rules BR-BIL-053 · BR-BIL-055 — returned by the calculation, not stored"*
> *"Rule BR-BIL-015 · column bill_run_decisions.case"*
> *"Story US-BIL-002 · GET /billing/runs/{id}/findings"*

A database column name and an HTTP route on a customer's screen. The PO's objection is
correct and is not cosmetic: it tells a utility about our internals, and it tells them
nothing they can act on.

**A5 · The full r10 comparison is NOT yet counted.** The PO asked *how many* styling issues
there are. Three classes are known; the total is not, and an estimate would be worse than
an admission. A token-by-token diff of r10's own `<style>` block against `tokens.css`, plus
a computed-style measurement in a real browser, is in progress and belongs to this CR.

### PART B · WHY IT KEEPS HAPPENING — the structural finding

**CLAUDE.md hard-won law 6 already says it:** *"Diff the running app against
`05-prototype/`. **No gate looks at rendered output.** Nine defects were found this way and
by nothing else."*

**And law 2's DEF-244 shape — a class referenced by components and declared by no
stylesheet — has now recurred SIX times** (`btn-icon-sm`, `--table-font-size`, seven
settings classes, `.settings-subhead`, `.btn-sm`, and DEF-248's swallowed rule). Tonight's
two reports are the **seventh and eighth**, and both were found by the PO looking at a
deployed screen.

**B14 is twenty binding UI rules and its own status table records most of them as RATIFIED
AND UNENFORCED**, for exactly this reason. The rules exist; nothing measures them.

> **The structural gap in one sentence: tsc, eslint and vitest all pass on a screen that
> renders as an OS widget in a designed page, because every one of them reads SOURCE and
> none of them reads PIXELS.**

### PART C · WHAT THIS CR DELIVERS

1. **A rendered-output gate** that loads real screens in a real browser and asserts
   **computed style** — no select with `appearance` other than `none`; controls at the
   design system's height, border and background; no label `display: inline` while wrapping
   a control; one table font size (B14 rule 20); two button sizes (B14 rule 5). **Proved
   RED before being trusted green**, per hard-won law 7.
2. **The r10 token diff**, as a table with a count — the PO's actual question answered.
3. **The internal-reference sweep** — 18 known sites rewritten as customer-facing copy,
   with the provenance moved to where support can still reach it, plus a check that fails
   when an id-shaped string enters a catalogue value.
4. **The fixes already landed** (`f21ca56`, restored by `b974922`) folded in.

### PART D · ⚠ ONE FINDING FROM THE FIX ITSELF, and it is a process finding

**The dropdown fix was reverted forty minutes after it landed, by a lane committing its
own STALE COPY of the same file.** Nothing was lost and no lane did anything unusual: it
pathspec-committed a file whose working-tree copy predated the fix, which is mechanism two
of law 11 and the **seventh** occurrence recorded here.

**What the law does not yet say loudly enough:** the danger is not only committing ANOTHER
lane's in-flight work — it is committing **your own stale copy** of a file someone else has
already pushed. That reads as an ordinary commit of your own change, and it silently
reverts theirs. **Both checks law 11 prescribes pass on it**: the file count is right and
the author's own change IS present. It was found by diffing the working tree against origin
while answering an unrelated question.

That belongs in law 11 and is proposed as part of this CR's write-back.

---

### PART E · THE SCREEN-BY-SCREEN AUDIT (2026-08-19)

> **⚠ THE PO ASKED FOR THIS AS "CR14".** Verbatim: *"So systematica analysis capture
> screen by screen details, document it in CR14 and then fix it very it"*, and
> *"you ahve to look at all screen in settings now each and every screen"*.
> **CR-014 is the journey-fixtures CR and is unrelated**; the UI CR is this one, CR-016.
> The number the PO used is recorded here so the reference is traceable rather than
> silently corrected.

**Method, because the method is what makes the numbers trustworthy.** Every one of the
thirteen Settings surfaces was loaded in a real browser against the running stack, and
the measurement is taken from the **rendered DOM** — every visible text node, the
**computed** `appearance` of every control, the computed `display` of every `<label>`
that wraps its control, and `scrollWidth` against `clientWidth` on every leaf element.
Not one number here is read from source.

**The frontend was REBUILT and the backend RESTARTED before each measurement.** This is
not ceremony: `boot_stack.sh` serves `dist/`, and `runserver` runs `--noreload`, so
measuring either without restarting reports a fixed defect as still broken — and, worse,
would have reported the fixes from `f21ca56`/`b974922`/`3e51e11` as failures.

#### E1 · The table

*"Internal strings" counts strings rendered to the user that contain a rule or story id,
a register id, a module path or `.py` filename, an HTTP route, a database column name, a
PO ruling or dated quote, or the phrase "hard-won law". Before → after this CR's sweep.*

#### E2 · What the 52 actually were, and where they came from

**Only 3 of the 52 came from the eleven i18n catalogues. 41 came from the SERVER**, as

Every finding was classified **(a) delete** — internal, no customer value; **(b) rewrite**

Filling this in now means email works the moment it is switched on."* |
> | *"stored and editable; the lockbox import does not queue receipts yet (US-PAY-025's lockbox half), so this election is consulted by nothing today"* | *"Your choice is saved, but nothing reads it yet — importing a lockbox file does not send receipts today."* |
> | *"⚠ A PLACEHOLDER EXISTS FOR THIS CLASS … PO, 2026-08-18: *'Do it; put the details, I will handle it with user'* … (`catalogs.CONTRACT_INPUT_REQUIREMENTS`)"* | *"This is a placeholder, not finished wording, and the product will not print it until you replace it. … The placeholder lists, in plain English, the eight things they need to settle."* |
>
> **Same claim, same honesty, nothing about us.** Not one absence stopped being stated.

#### E4 · The findings that are NOT copy, and are not duplicates of DEF-308..313

The parallel conformance lane measured the styling classes tonight (26 native selects,
six table font sizes, five button sizes, `.kicker`, fifteen undeclared custom properties).
A **content** walk of the same screens found four more, each filed:

| Defect | Finding | Why it is separate |
|---|---|---|
| **DEF-314** | The **bill-layout chooser renders as one paragraph of flowing text**. All **ten** `bil-*` classes are declared by no stylesheet, so the five layout cards are inline `<span>`s: `"StandardUS Letter"`, `"CompactUS Letter"`, `"Amount due firstUS Letter"`, with the "Use this one" buttons sitting mid-sentence. | DEF-308 counted this failure MODE but scoped it to `.kicker`. A per-component sweep of every `className` referenced by a Settings screen against every class declared in any `.css` found **43 undeclared classes across 17 components**. |
| **DEF-315** | **Label and value collide into one word** on Notifications — `"BouncedNot reported"`, `"Waiting93"`, `"EmailOff"`, `"Messages per hand-off500"`. `kpi-list` / `kpi-label` / `kpi-value` are undeclared. | ⚠ `"Waiting93"` **passes** a `toContain("Waiting")` assertion. The text is all there, merely joined — which is exactly why no test objected. |
| **DEF-316** | **The PO's blank-screen screenshot, reproduced.** `main.view` is a fixed-height inner scroller (844px) and the three Notifications columns are 8312px, ~3000px and ~1400px, so scrolling to read one leaves the others blank. | ⚠ **Invisible to screenshots.** Playwright's `fullPage: true` captures 900px here, because the DOCUMENT never scrolls — so every screenshot of this screen ever taken looked fine. Found only by setting `scrollTop = scrollHeight` on the scroller. |
| **DEF-317** | **Raw snake_case enum codes as template names**: `plan_notice_void`, `sms_bill_ready`, `service_door_hanger`, `staff_bulk_summary` and eight more. | Not a raw translation KEY, so G27 cannot see it; not a catalogue VALUE, so G28 cannot either. The register already holds a human name for every one. |

#### E5 · ⚠ TWO RAW TRANSLATION KEYS WERE STILL RENDERING — ONE DAY AFTER G27 LANDED (DEF-318)

Settings → Notifications printed the literal strings
`notifications.tones.class.disconnect_notice_10_day` and
`…_48_hour` in its notice-tones table.

**This is precisely the blind spot G27's own docstring declares and defends.** The call is
``t(`notifications.tones.class.${row.template_class}`)`` — a **template literal**, and G27
checks LITERAL keys only, because resolving a dynamic key needs the app running. G15
cannot see it either: the three keys were missing from **all eleven** catalogues, which is
perfect parity.

The cause is a **correct** server fix: BR-NOT-014 split `disconnect_notice` into three
tier classes on 2026-08-17, `notice_tones` was amended to report `TIER_TO_CLASS`, and the
catalogues were never extended. All three labels are added here, in all eleven languages.

**The structural fix, and it closes the declared blind spot without making G27 guess:** a
dynamic `t()` call must pass a `defaultValue`. G27's docstring already observes that most
such call sites do; this one did not, and that is the single thing that would have turned
a raw key into a readable fallback.

#### E6 · G28 — the sibling check, proved RED first

`10-scripts/gates/g28_internal_references.py`, registered in `run_gates.py`.

* **G27 asks** *"does this key resolve?"* · **G28 asks** *"should a utility be READING what
  it resolves to?"*
* It scans **all eleven catalogue values** plus the **named backend fields rendered
  verbatim** (five modules), reading the Python with `ast` so a docstring is never
  mistaken for a screen — which matters, because "move it into the comment" is the remedy
  it recommends.
* It fails on: rule/story ids · register ids · module paths and `.py` filenames · HTTP
  routes · database column names · PO rulings and dated quotes · `hard-won law`.
* **PROVED RED (hard-won law 7): 219 violations, exit 1**, run against the tip that
  carried them — a real pre-fix state, not a planted string. **Green at 0** after the
  sweep. **No baseline was needed**, so the ratchet file is empty and every violation is
  actually fixed.
* **Three false-positive concessions are documented in the gate**, each a real string it
  had to let through: a bare date is a format example and not a PO quote (*"for example
  2026-08-22"*); **"US Letter" is a paper size**, not a story id; and comments and
  docstrings are not screens.
* **`br_ref` is deliberately NOT checked.** It is a machine field and is *supposed* to
  hold `"BR-BIL-026 · OQ-149"`. The fix was to stop RENDERING it, not to empty it.

#### E7 · ⚠ G27 ITSELF WAS NEVER WIRED INTO `run_gates.py`

It was written on 2026-08-19 for DEF-307, proved RED, proved green over 126 components —
and left as a standalone script **no runner called**. That is **hard-won law 2 ("built is
not wired"), committed by the lane that was fixing a law-2 defect**, and it survived
because a gate's own green output looks identical whether anything runs it or not. Both
gates are registered now.

#### E8 · What was fixed, what was not

**Fixed:** all 52 strings on the Settings screens, and all 219 across the product; the two
raw keys; the eleven dead `gapRule` catalogue entries in eleven languages; the `br_ref` and
`ruleRef` provenance moved to `data-` attributes; three tests **inverted rather than
deleted** — including `test_cr_009_c12_sender_config`, which had *asserted* `"no SMTP
adapter is built"` and so had made the internal sentence a **requirement**.

**Not fixed here, and why:** DEF-314 through DEF-317 are **layout and rendering** defects
whose remedy is CSS, and the r10 conformance lane owns that surface tonight (DEF-308..313,
`e2e/CR-016-ui-conformance.spec.ts`, `ui-conformance-baseline.json`). Fixing 43 undeclared
classes from this lane, in the same files, on the same night, is mechanism two of law 11
waiting to happen. They are filed with their measurements so that lane can absorb them.

**The one check worth adding next**, and it needs no browser: **collect every `className`
referenced in `src/**/*.tsx`, collect every class declared in `src/**/*.css`, and fail on
the difference.** It is pure source analysis, and it would have caught DEF-244, DEF-305,
DEF-308, DEF-314 and DEF-315 — all six prior recurrences and both of tonight's.

#### E9 · ⚠ ADDENDUM — SEVEN TESTS HAD MADE THE INTERNAL COPY A REQUIREMENT, AND ONE OF THEM FOUND A STRING G28 MISSED

Part E above reported three tests inverted. Running the **full** suites found eight
more, and the total is **eleven** — seven backend, four frontend. That number is the
single most useful thing in this CR, because it explains the survival of the whole
class: **these strings were not merely unchecked, they were protected.**

| Test | What it asserted | The argument it made for asserting it |
|---|---|---|
| `test_cr_007__the_service_and_field_category_ships_with_its_four_templates` | `"R5" in row["used_by"] and "OQ-249" in row["used_by"]` | *"the Used-by column says R5 in the server's own words rather than implying a flow that exists"* |
| `test_cr_009_notification_rules` (×2) | `"IN-APP DELIVERS TODAY"`, `"no provider adapter exists"` | the release posture must travel with the rules |
| `test_us_not_004_settings_api` (×5) | `"nothing leaves the building"`, `"BR-NOT-001"`, `"BR-NOT-014"`, `"OQ-244"`, `"OQ-206"` | a tenant must not read a toggle as "email will now go out"; the two absences are different problems with different fixes |
| `AccountActions.test.tsx` (×2) | `toContain("OQ-168")`, `toContain("OQ-169")` | *"that is the id a clerk should be able to quote. Citing a closed question would send them to a decision that has already been made."* |
| `AccountDetailPage.test.tsx` | `toContain("OQ-169")` | the reason names the blocker rather than saying "soon" |
| `PaymentsPage.test.tsx` | `toContain("OQ-154")` | the choice is disabled *with its reason*, not silently |

**Every one of those arguments is careful, and every one answers the wrong
question.** Getting the *right* id in front of a billing clerk is still putting an
id in front of a billing clerk. The clearest case is the print-bill reason, which
asserted `"no route serves it yet"` on the reasoning that *"saying 'not built'
would be the easy lie and would send someone to write a second renderer"* — where
the "someone" is an **engineer**, and the sentence is read by a **clerk**, to whom
the two phrasings are the same words.

**All seven are INVERTED, not deleted.** Each keeps the claim that mattered — the
reason names a pending *decision* rather than saying "soon"; the release posture
still travels; a disabled control still explains itself — and each gained a
negative assertion (`not.toContain("OQ-")`, `assert "BR-NOT-" not in reason`) so
the internal form cannot return. The provenance each was protecting is written
into the comment directly above it.

#### E10 · ⚠ AND G28 HAD A MISS, FOUND BY A TEST RATHER THAN BY THE GATE

Fixing the fourth assertion meant reading `settings_api.NO_DISPATCHER_REASON`, and
it turned out to continue:

> *"…and nothing leaves the building **(US-NOT-002 and US-NOT-003 are R3 by PO
> ruling)**. These switches record whether this utility WOULD make provider calls…"*

Two story ids and a ruling, served to a Settings screen — and **G28 passed on it**,
because G28 checks an **explicit list of fields** and nobody had named that one.

**The miss is written into the gate rather than quietly patched**, because the
tradeoff is the point and the next person to edit that list needs it:

> An explicit list only checks what somebody remembered to name. A heuristic sweep
> over every backend string literal would fire on error codes, log lines and test
> fixtures until someone switched it off — which is how G26's and G27's first
> drafts nearly died. **The list still wins, but it must be audited whenever a
> string in one of these modules changes**, and the gate now says so in its own
> comment.

**This is also, precisely, hard-won law 7 paying off in reverse.** The gate was
proved RED before being trusted — and it was still incomplete, because "proved RED
on 219 known violations" says nothing about a 220th nobody had found. A gate is
only ever as wide as its inputs.

#### E11 · Final state

| | |
|---|---|
| Engineering strings rendered on the thirteen Settings screens | **52 → 0**, measured in a browser |
| Internal references across all eleven catalogues + served backend prose | **219 → 0**, G28 |
| G28 baseline / ratchet entries | **0** — nothing was deferred |
| Tests inverted rather than deleted | **11** (7 backend, 4 frontend) |
| Frontend suite after | **96 files · 1475 tests · all passing**, `tsc` clean |

#### E12 · The fixes that had already landed, VERIFIED ON SCREEN rather than taken on trust

Three fixes landed on this branch before this audit and none of them had been
measured in a browser afterwards. The final walk measures all three, and it
matters that it was done AFTER a rebuild: `boot_stack` serves `dist/`, so the
bundle being served when this audit started predated two of them.

| Fix | What it claimed | Measured on the final build |
|---|---|---|
| `f21ca56` / `b974922` — `select.input { appearance: none }` | dropdowns stop being OS widgets | **0 of 63 selects** on the Settings screens render as an OS widget, down from **4**. ⚠ It is `cf0423f` that made this true, not the original fix: DEF-309 found the rule was scoped to `.fin-page` and `.met-panel` and reached **none** of the Settings screens, and re-scoped it to `main.view`. |
| `f21ca56` — the `:has()` rule for a label wrapping its control | labels stop sitting on the control's last baseline | **0 inline wrapping labels**, down from **5** on Settings → Notifications. |
| `3e51e11` — G27 | no component asks for a key no catalogue defines | **127 components scanned, all clean.** ⚠ And **two raw keys were still rendering anyway** (E5, DEF-318), in G27's own declared blind spot. |

**The general point, which is CR-016's Part B in one line:** every one of these was
reported as done on the strength of reading the CSS or the gate's own output.
Two of the three were wrong on screen, and the only thing that found either was
loading the page in a browser and reading computed style. **`cf0423f`'s author
put it best — *"I verified it by reading the CSS, which is exactly the mistake
this repo keeps paying for."***

## CR-017 · A new tenant watches a blank wait while the product builds their utility

| | |
|---|---|
| **Arrived** | 2026-08-19, from the Product Owner, with a screenshot of signup **step 5 of 5** on the deployed build |
| **Classification** | **CHANGE** — a new screen. Nothing is broken; the product does substantial work and says nothing while doing it. |
| **Screen** | New. Sits between signup step 5 (*Create your login*) and the checklist. |

### The request, verbatim

> "New CR - after this step at the time of new tenant creation you need new screen
> showcaing data migration is going on so that User wil know whats going on in the
> background - add new screen after this"

### WHAT HAPPENS TODAY

`SignupWizard.tsx:437` — the moment step 5 succeeds it calls
`navigate(tenantPathFrom(result.subdomain, CHECKLIST_SEGMENT))`. **There is no screen
between the two.** The user presses a button and waits on whatever the browser shows for a
pending request, then lands on a checklist with a fully-built utility behind it and no
account of where it came from.

**And provisioning is not a small job.** `apps/tenancy/services.provision_tenant` builds,
for every new tenant:

* **twenty reference lists** — units of measure (26 rows), charge codes (23), asset types
  (12), account sub-types (12), meter size classes (9), payment methods (7), premises
  types (6), device types (6), certification types (6), tax jurisdictions (7), account
  statuses (5), unit types (5), reason codes (5), meter types (5), read methods (5), asset
  lifecycle stages (5), occupancy statuses (5), account types (4), areas (4)
* a **chart of accounts** — 33 GL accounts with their mappings
* the **notification rule matrix** — 15 rules and 26 channel rows
* **number series** for accounts, premises, units, bills, payments, receipts and more
* **tax jurisdictions and rates**, a **security policy row**, **company defaults**, a
  **holiday calendar**, and the **document template catalogue**

The PO calls this *"data migration"*. It is provisioning — but their framing is the
correct one from the user's side: **from where the customer sits, something substantial is
being built and they cannot see it.**

### WHY THIS IS WORTH A SCREEN AND NOT A SPINNER

A spinner says *wait*. What the PO asked for is that the user **know what is going on** —
and that difference is the whole CR. The customer has just typed their utility's name,
their billing shape and their plan; the product is turning those answers into two hundred
rows of configuration they will spend the next month editing. **Naming the work as it
happens is the product's first chance to tell them what it just built for them.**

It is also the first screen after signup that a real customer will ever see, which makes
it the product's first impression rather than an implementation detail.

### WHAT NEEDS DECIDING BEFORE IT IS BUILT — put to the PO, not assumed

1. **Is provisioning synchronous today, and must it become asynchronous?** If the work
   happens inside the step-5 request, a progress screen can only report *after* the fact —
   the honest version would be a completion summary, not progress. **Real progress needs
   the work moved to a job and a status endpoint to poll**, which is a backend change, not
   a screen. This is the question that decides the size of the CR and it is answered by
   measurement, not by preference.
2. **What does it say?** Named steps as they complete (*"Reference lists · 20 lists,
   187 rows"*, *"Chart of accounts · 33 accounts"*) or a single sentence with a bar? The
   PO's words — *"showcasing"*, *"know whats going on"* — read as the former.
3. **What happens if a step fails?** Provisioning is idempotent on the subdomain, so a
   retry is safe. The screen must say which step failed and offer that retry rather than
   stranding a half-built tenant behind a spinner.
4. **Is it skippable?** A returning operator provisioning a second tenant may not want to
   watch. A *"take me there"* link that does not cancel the work is the usual answer.

### RELATIONSHIP TO WORK ALREADY IN FLIGHT

Not blocked by, and does not block, CR-015 or CR-016. It touches the signup wizard and the
tenancy provisioning path — territory none of the three running lanes holds.

**One dependency worth stating:** CR-010 established what provisioning seeds and
`12-governance/16-seed-failure-modes.md` maps all 58 objects by how loudly each fails
(**28 LOUD · 17 STATED · 13 SILENT**). **That map is the content of this screen** — the
thirteen SILENT objects are exactly the ones a user would never otherwise learn had been
built, or had failed to be.

### ⛔ CR-017 · PART 2 — SIGNUP ITSELF IS BROKEN ON THE DEPLOYED BUILD (2026-08-19)

The PO attempted the very signup this CR was written about, and it did not work. Their
words:

> "It did not create the tenant just told me to download the report and unable to download
> the report also not even a user is created"

**Four symptoms, and each is worse than the one before:**

| | What happened |
|---|---|
| 1 | **No tenant was created** |
| 2 | **No user was created either** — so nothing partial was left behind, which is at least consistent |
| 3 | The browser **offered a file download** instead of showing a screen |
| 4 | **The download itself failed** |

**This outranks the progress screen this CR was opened for.** A screen that narrates
provisioning is worth nothing if provisioning never runs. Part 1 stands; it is now the
second half of this CR.

#### WHAT THE CODE SAYS, and what it does not explain

The wizard's commit path is single-flight and its failure handling is ordinary: on error
`commitSignup` returns `{ ok: false, reason }` and the frame renders that reason
(`SignupWizard.tsx:310-316`). **On no path does this product offer a download.** So symptom
3 is not the application choosing to hand over a file — **it is the browser deciding it
cannot render what the server returned.**

That narrows the cause to a small set, and each leaves different evidence:

* **The SPA never took the click.** If the JavaScript failed to load or threw before
  hydration, the form posts natively, the API answers `application/json`, and Chrome offers
  to save it. This matches every symptom including the failed download, and it would also
  mean **the whole application is down for that browser**, not just signup.
* **The API returned an error the SPA could not parse** — a 500 rendering an HTML error
  page, or a proxy-level response with a `Content-Disposition` header. Same visible result.
* **A deployment mismatch** — a rebuilt frontend served against a backend that has not
  migrated, so the commit 500s. Tonight's builds moved `2.21.0 → 2.23.0` and the two
  version literals were **unequal at one point** (DEF-296), so a half-deployed pair is a
  live possibility and not a hypothetical.

#### ⚠ WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT IN ONE MINUTE, and cannot be got from this session

This is a **deployed-environment** failure and the repository cannot reproduce it. The
local stack runs a different build against a different database. **The single most useful
piece of evidence is the network response for the failed request** — its status code and
the first line of its body — or the file the browser tried to download, whose CONTENT is
the server's actual answer. Either one distinguishes all three causes above immediately.

Recorded here rather than guessed at, because **a wrong diagnosis of a front-door failure
costs more than an hour of waiting for the evidence**: the fix for "the SPA never loaded"
and the fix for "the backend 500s" have nothing in common, and shipping the wrong one to a
production signup page would be the third deploy today.

#### SEVERITY, stated plainly

**Signup is the front door.** No tenant, no user, and a browser handing the customer a file
they cannot open is the worst first impression this product can make, and it is happening
on the deployed build the PO is showing people. **This is filed as CRITICAL and it precedes
every other item in this CR and in CR-015 and CR-016.**

#### ⚡ CR-017 PART 2 — REPRODUCED AGAINST THE CODE, AND THE CODE IS FINE (2026-08-19)

**Signup was driven end-to-end on the local stack, at HEAD, over HTTP — the same endpoint
the browser posts to. It succeeded.**

```
POST /api/tenants   →   HTTP 201   content-type: application/json
{"name":"Probe Utility","subdomain":"probe26899","created":true,
 "owner_user_id":"01a01910-664c-7b07-8e93-5fe696c21d0d",
 "reference_seed":{"version":"V2.19.0.0","seeded":{"uoms":26,"charge_codes":23,
   "tax_jurisdictions":9,"asset_types":12,"account_subtypes":12,"meter_size_classes":9,
   … 20 lists …},"skipped":[]}}
```

**A tenant was created. An owner user was created. Twenty reference lists seeded, nothing
skipped.** All four of the PO's symptoms are absent here.

**So the defect is NOT in the code on this branch. It is in the deployed environment**, and
that narrows the remaining causes to two, both testable on the host in one command each:

1. **UNAPPLIED MIGRATIONS — the leading candidate.** This database has **9 `rating`
   migrations applied**. Three of them landed TODAY, and `rating/0007_tax_conditions` adds
   three columns to `taxes` — `applies_to_customer_classes`, `premises_scope_kind`,
   `premises_scope_value` — a table provisioning writes through its `tax_jurisdictions`
   branch. A deployed backend carrying today's code against a database that has not run
   0007 raises on a missing column, the request 500s, and **no tenant and no user are
   created**, which is exactly the reported shape.
   **Test: `python manage.py showmigrations rating` on the host.** If 0007/0008/0009 are
   unapplied, the fix is a migrate, not a code change.
2. **A HALF-DEPLOYED PAIR.** The PO's screenshots show **v2.22.0**; the branch is now
   **2.23.0**, and the two version literals were *unequal* at one point today (DEF-296 —
   `package.json` 2.22.0 against `pyproject.toml` 2.21.0). A frontend and backend from
   different builds produce this class of failure.
   **Test: the version the deployed backend reports against the one the SPA shows.**

**Why the browser offered a download, explained:** nothing in this product serves a file
from signup. A 500 rendering Django's HTML error page, or a proxy response the SPA cannot
parse, is content the browser will offer to save rather than render. That is consistent
with both causes above and with neither being a front-end bug.

**⚠ WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE.** A green local run says the code is capable of succeeding;
it says nothing about the host. The two tests above are what close it, and they take a
minute each. Recorded rather than acted on, because the remedy for an unapplied migration
and the remedy for a mismatched deploy are different, and shipping the wrong one to a live
signup page would be the third deploy of the day.

#### ✅ CR-017 PART 2 — SETTLED 2026-08-19. THE API WAS NEVER RUNNING.

The evidence this section said would "settle it in one minute" arrived as the PO's own
deploy log. **Neither of the two candidates above was right, and the truth is simpler and
worse than both.**

**`06-backend/docker-entrypoint.sh` runs `migrate` BEFORE it starts the server:**

| line | statement |
|---|---|
| 12 | `set -eu` |
| **54** | **`python manage.py migrate --noinput`** ← fails here |
| 98 | `exec gunicorn config.wsgi:application …` ← **never reached** |

and `docker-compose.yml` gives the backend `restart: unless-stopped`. So the loop is:

> migrate raises → `set -e` exits the script → the container exits → the restart policy
> brings it back → migrate runs again from the top → dies one migration later.

**Gunicorn never binds. There is no API at all.** That is why the deploy log reads as one
incoherent traceback: it is FOUR failures from FOUR restarts, interleaved —
`notifications.0012` (policy exists), `payments.0001` (table `payments` exists),
`payments.0004` (`bank_accounts` exists), `payments.0007` (`payment_plans` exists).

#### Every one of the PO's four symptoms, explained by that single fact

| # | Symptom | Explanation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | No tenant created | the request never reached Django |
| 2 | No user created either | same — nothing partial, because nothing ran |
| 3 | The browser offered a file | the proxy answered 502/504 with an error body the browser would not render |
| 4 | The download failed | that body was a proxy error page, not a file |

**Symptom 2 was the clue all along and was read as reassurance.** "Nothing partial was left
behind, which is at least consistent" is consistent with a rolled-back transaction — and
equally consistent with **no transaction ever being opened**. The second reading was never
tested.

#### Why the two candidates were wrong, and why it matters

* **Candidate 1, unapplied migrations, was DIRECTIONALLY right and MECHANICALLY wrong.** It
  predicted "the backend runs and 500s on a missing column". The backend does not run.
  **Its prescribed fix — "the fix is a migrate, not a code change" — would not have worked**,
  because migrate is already running automatically on every boot and is what is failing.
  Telling the PO to run migrate would have produced the same log again.
* **Candidate 2, a half-deployed pair, is not in play**: a version mismatch needs two
  running halves.

**The lesson for the record:** the local reproduction (HTTP 201, tenant created, 20 lists
seeded) proved the code path works and was *correctly* labelled "this does not prove
anything about the host". What no one asked was the simpler question one level down —
**is the host serving the application at all?** Every hypothesis assumed a running server
answering badly, and the answer was that nothing was answering.

#### THE ROOT CAUSE, and it is not one defect

**DEF-333** — all 24 RLS policy files use a bare `CREATE POLICY` with no guard (94
policies). Any re-run against a database that holds the policy is a hard failure. Proved
by construction to be invisible to CI: every RLS migration is only ever run **once against
an empty database**, and from empty a bare `CREATE POLICY` always succeeds.

**And a second, larger condition DEF-333 does not fix:** three of the four failures are
duplicate **tables**, not policies. That database's schema is **ahead of its
`django_migrations` history** — the objects exist and Django has no record of making them.
`10-scripts/diagnose_migration_drift.py` (2026-08-19) is the read-only tool that classifies
every unapplied migration as MISSING / SAFE-TO-FAKE / ⚠ MISMATCH and prints the exact
repair, because `--fake` is right for some and buries a real schema gap for others.

#### ⚠ WHAT IS STILL NOT FIXED, and is the honest remainder of Part 2

**A failed migration takes the entire product down, silently, with no API at all** — and
that is a deploy-shape decision, not a defect to be patched under this CR. Migrating before
serving is *correct*; a restart loop that hides the reason behind repeated tracebacks and
leaves no health signal is not. Options — refuse to restart on a migration failure and fail
loudly; or separate migrate into its own one-shot step so the server's failure to start is
visible as itself. **Raised, not chosen.**

### CR-016 · ADDENDUM — EVERY SCREEN CARRIES ITS ID, VISIBLE (PO, 2026-08-19)

> "Cr16 - I want you to give sreen Id to each and Every screen and for time bing also
> display that as a tag - right bottom for every UI screen so that we know which scren has
> a problem - enrure engineer the screen IDs"

**This is how r10 already works.** Every screenshot the PO has sent from the prototype
carries its id in the bottom-right — `PLN-01`, `RAT-01`, `CHG-01`, `PLN-01.charges`,
`DSH-01`. The app does not do it, and the cost has been paid repeatedly today: every UI
defect this evening was reported as *"this screen"* plus a photograph, and matching that to
a component took a grep each time.

**IT ALSO CLOSES A DEFECT THAT HAS BEEN OPEN SINCE THE FIRST DEPLOYMENT.** DEF-137 reads:
*"S113 has no owning story, and screens do not carry their own id in the frontend — so no
gate can [check screen coverage]"*. A visible id is the user-facing half; the machine-
readable half is what lets a gate assert that every screen in A1 has exactly one component
and every component names a screen in A1.

**A1 is the vocabulary and it is not to be renumbered** — canonical range S1–S114, with
S49–S60 provisional and S61–S90 reserved. The ids are ALLOCATED there, not invented in the
frontend. Where a screen has no A1 id, that is a finding to report, not a licence to mint
one: CLAUDE.md's law 8 says *"every screen needs a story"*, and a screen with no id is a
screen with no story.

**"For the time being"** is the PO's own framing — the tag is a diagnostic affordance, so
it should be trivially removable behind one switch rather than woven through 100+
components.

#### ⚠ CR-016 SCREEN IDS — TWO VOCABULARIES, AND THEY DO NOT RECONCILE (open, needs the PO)

The PO asked *"How are you generating Screen IDs?"* and the honest answer is **they are not
generated, they are looked up** — which is right, and which surfaced a fork that must not
be resolved by a lane picking one.

| | Vocabulary | Where it lives | Who speaks it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A1** | `S1` … `S114` — 87 distinct ids today | `04-docs/01-spec/01-screen-inventory.md`, a table row per screen carrying purpose, entry, exits and access | every defect row · every story id · every ticket · `g25_screen_coverage.py` |
| **r10** | `PLN-01`, `RAT-01`, `DSH-01`, `CHG-01`, `PLN-01.charges` — module-prefixed, with sub-ids for tabs | `05-prototype/r10-2026-08-16/SMARTBillHub.dc.html`, rendered as a badge bottom-right | **the PO**, who sees it on every prototype screenshot |

**These are not two names for one thing, and no mapping table exists in the repo.**
CLAUDE.md records why: A1 was extracted from **r9**, and *"where A1's screen description
contradicts r10, r10 is right and the spec is stale — file it, don't follow it."*
**Re-extraction has not happened.** So a screen may have an A1 row, an r10 badge, both, or
neither.

**RECOMMENDATION — show A1's `S-id` as primary, and append r10's when it exists:
`S7 · DSH-01`.** A1 is what a defect row, a story and the coverage gate can all resolve;
r10 is what the reader has in front of them. One tag answering *"which screen is broken"*
in whichever vocabulary they hold. **Not** a third invented scheme.

**BUILT SO THE RULING IS A ONE-LINE CHANGE, not a re-tag of 87 screens.** The mapping is a
table that can hold both (`{ route, a1, r10 }`) rather than a single string, because a
one-string design forces the choice that is the PO's to make.

**AND THE MOST VALUABLE OUTPUT IS THE THIRD COUNT.** Not *how many screens have an id* but
**how many have NEITHER** — that is the set of screens shipped with no story, which is
CLAUDE.md law 8, and **DEF-137 (S113 has no owning story) is one known instance of it.**
The lane reports all three counts.

## CR-016 · PART F — the design-system half, closed (2026-08-19, shipped 2.25.1)

> Lettered **F** because the content lane's screen-by-screen audit already holds PART E
> in this CR. The two halves ran in parallel: PART E is the prose on the screens, this
> is the CSS underneath it.

PART C item 1 asked for the rendered-output gate; it landed on 2026-08-19 and CR-016's own
capture said *"The full r10 comparison is NOT yet counted… an estimate would be worse than an
admission."* **This is the count, and then the remediation.** The PO's question — *"How many
styling, CSS issues are there, can you compare it with r10"* — is answered with numbers taken
in a browser, twice, with `npm run build` run first each time.

### THE ANSWER TO "HOW MANY", and the same numbers after the fix

| What was measured | How many | Now |
|---|---|---|
| r10 design-system classes declared by **no** app stylesheet | **36** of 51 | 2 declared · 19 mapped to an app class · 15 unreferenced |
| `.kicker` elements rendering wrong (15px body ink instead of 11px accent) | **10** on 6 screens, from **26 files** asking for a class **nobody declared** | **0** |
| Distinct table font sizes (B14 rule 20 says one) | **6** — 10/11/12/13/13.5/14px | body **1** · header **1** |
| Screens rendering more than one table size at once | **10** | **0** |
| Distinct button font sizes (B14 rule 5 says two) | **5** — one of them 13.3333px, the browser's own default on a button no rule reached | **2** |
| Distinct form-control heights (r10 gives one) | **4** — 27/33/36/38px | **1** |
| CSS custom properties used and **declared nowhere** | **15**, of which **11 had no fallback**, so the whole declaration was invalid and did nothing | **0** |
| `<select>` still rendering as an OS widget | 26 | **0** |
| Controls not matching a live `.input` | 3 | **0** |

⚠ **THE LAST TWO WERE ALREADY FIXED AND THE REGISTER STILL CLAIMED THEM.** `cf0423f` took
`nativeSelects` 26 → 0 and `foreignControls` 3 → 0 and did not lower
`ui-conformance-baseline.json`. That is red by the register's own rule — *"a register that
keeps claiming debt it has paid off is how a gate stops being a gate"* (DEF-077) — and it was
found only because this lane re-ran the gate instead of trusting the recorded numbers. **Two
commits apart, the ratchet had already stopped ratcheting.**

### THE ONE PLACE THE GATE ITSELF WAS WRONG

`screensWithMoreThanOneTableSize` pooled `<td>` and `<th>` into one set, so it counted a
screen as broken **for having a table header at all**. r10 fails that metric — `.table` is
13.5px and `.table th` is 11px in the same block — and separating header from body
product-wide would have driven the number **up from 10 to 18 while the product got better**.
Split per role (`thead` is the boundary) it is a finer check, not a weaker one, and DEF-310's
own stated closure — *"the set becomes ['13.5px']"* — is now literally the body half's target
and is met. Proved RED first by breaking the BUILT bundle, never the shared source.

### WHAT IS STILL OPEN ON CR-016

1. **DEF-308 … DEF-313 still read `status: open`** in `12-governance/10-defect-log.csv`. Each
   is fixed and each has its evidence in the register and the decision log;
   `10-scripts/file_defect.py` appends only and deliberately refuses to edit a row, so closing
   six single fields in a 310-row CRLF register that six lanes write is a separate operation.
2. **OQ-267** — the table header ships at 12px where r10 draws 11px, because our sortable
   headers contain a real `<button>` and B14 rule 5 allows only two button sizes. Worked
   figure: 11px ⇒ 3 button sizes, 12px ⇒ 2. The PO chooses: keep the 1px, or change
   `DataTable`'s sort affordance to r10's clickable `<th>` and take 11px back.
3. **B14 rules 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9–17, 19 are still RATIFIED AND UNENFORCED.** Rules 2, 5, 8 and
   20 are now enforced in the paint; the other fifteen are not, and B14's status table says so.
4. **`inlineWrappingLabels: 0` is a floor.** The walk opens no modal, wizard or panel.

## CR-018 · Move the frontend from hand-written CSS to Tailwind

| | |
|---|---|
| **Arrived** | 2026-08-19, from the Product Owner, with a Tailwind stylesheet attached |
| **Requester's words, VERBATIM** | *"Instead of Plain CSS cant we use Tailwind?"* then, after the trade-offs were put to them: *"After 16 is closed - we will do tailwind CR - here is the file that I download from Claude design; raise next CR"* |
| **Classification** | **CHANGE** — not a defect. Nothing is broken; this replaces a working styling approach with a different one. |
| **Urgency** | **A thought, not urgent — and explicitly SEQUENCED.** The PO gave the order themselves: *"After 16 is closed"*. This CR does not start while CR-016 is open. |
| **Sizing** | **LARGE. Not a fast-path candidate** (change-process §5): it touches every screen in the product. |

### 1 · WHAT WAS PUT TO THE PO BEFORE THEY RULED, and what they decided anyway

They asked; the recommendation given was **"not now"**, with these figures:

| | |
|---|---|
| `className` sites to rewrite | **3,032** |
| Components | **127** |
| CSS to replace | **9,284 lines** across 40 stylesheets |
| Classes declared | **921** (804 before CR-016's remediation) |
| Design tokens | **76** |

Three reasons were given: two lanes were writing CSS at that moment; `r10` is the design authority and is plain CSS; and Tailwind's main benefit — making an undeclared class unwritable — had just been delivered by **G31** for a day's work instead of weeks.

**The PO accepted the sequencing and kept the change.** That is the ruling: the reasoning was about TIMING, and the PO answered on timing. Do not re-litigate it in this CR.

### 2 · WHAT THE ATTACHED FILE IS, measured rather than described

`smartbillhub-fixes.tailwind.css` — the Tailwind v4 translation of the plain-CSS file the PO sent for DEF-327.

**Its tokens are OUR tokens, checked value by value:**

| Token | File | Ours | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--color-bg` | `#f3f2f2` | `#f3f2f2` | ✅ |
| `--color-surface` | `#eae9e9` | `#eae9e9` | ✅ |
| `--color-accent` | `#ec3013` | `#ec3013` | ✅ |
| `--color-accent-700` | `#ae1800` | `#ae1800` | ✅ |
| `--color-divider` | `color-mix(in srgb, #201e1d 40%, transparent)` | identical | ✅ |
| `--font-heading` | `"Archivo", system-ui, sans-serif` | identical | ✅ |
| `--color-ink` | `#201e1d` | **we call it `--color-text`** | ⚠ one rename |

So the palette is right and one name differs. **That is a genuinely useful artefact** — it is a working `@theme` block for our real design system, which is the part of a Tailwind migration that is easy to get subtly wrong.

**Its class names are still not ours, and this time the CR says so up front.** `.chooser`, `.chooser-option`, `.co-*`, `.kv`, `.kv-k`, `.kv-v`, `.status-count` appear **0 times in our app and 0 times in r10**; only `.pill` is real r10 vocabulary (10 occurrences). The DEF-327 lane established this and adopted two of the patterns on other grounds. **A claim that these names align us with r10 is FALSE and was made in error during CR-016 — it is corrected here so this CR does not inherit it.**

### 3 · THE DECISION THIS CR MUST TAKE FIRST, before any code

The attached file offers two paths and says *"pick one, don't mix"*:

- **(A) Component classes** — `@layer components` keeps `.chooser`, `.kv`, `.pill err`, so existing markup keeps working. A drop-in.
- **(B) Raw utilities** — Tailwind-idiomatic; each component's equivalent utility string is in the comment above it.

⚠ **(A) IS NOT A TAILWIND MIGRATION.** It is our current architecture with Tailwind as the authoring syntax: the class names stay the contract between component and stylesheet, so **DEF-327's failure mode survives intact** — a component can still name a class no `@layer components` rule declares, and `tsc`, eslint and `toHaveClass()` will all still pass. Path (A) buys nothing the PO asked for.

**(B) is the migration.** It is also 3,032 rewrite sites. **This is the CR's central trade-off and it goes to the PO with a figure before anyone writes code.**

### 4 · WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT THAT THIS MUST NOT THROW AWAY

1. **The conformance harness** — `07-frontend/e2e/CR-016-ui-conformance.spec.ts` + `ui-conformance-baseline.json`, reading **computed style on 24 screens** against locked numbers. **This is what makes the migration safe**, and it is the strongest reason the PO's sequencing is right: CR-016 built the instrument. Computed style is computed style, so the harness works unchanged against Tailwind — every screen must hold every number, or the migration regressed it.
2. **B14's twenty ratified UI rules** — two button sizes, one table type size, radius 0, no shadows. The file already kills Tailwind's default rounding across all seven radius keys; that is B14 rule compliance and must be preserved.
3. **G31** — 0 undeclared classes and a ratchet at 0. Under path (B) it becomes meaningless (there are no bespoke classes left to declare) and must be **retired deliberately with a written reason**, not left passing vacuously. Under path (A) it stays load-bearing.
4. **G29 / screen ids, G28 / internal references** — unaffected, but re-run.

### 5 · OPEN QUESTIONS THIS CR MUST MINT, NOT ANSWER

- **Tailwind v4 or v3?** The file targets v4 (`@import` + `@theme`) and carries a v3 fallback config. v4 is a build-chain decision, not a styling one.
- **`text-pretty` and `has-checked:`** are v4-only; the file names the v3 substitutes. Moot if v4 is chosen.
- **The webfont.** `tokens.css:22` imports Archivo from Google Fonts. CLAUDE.md records that this font "was decided with the AppShell packet" and **was decided by nobody** — hard-won law 1. A migration that re-declares `--font-heading` should not silently re-ratify an undecided font.

### 6 · WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE

Every screen renders identically to its pre-migration self, proved by the conformance harness holding every baseline number, plus before/after screenshots of the same screens CR-016 photographed. **A spike on ONE screen first**, measured, before the other 126 — so the real cost per screen is a measured number and not this CR's estimate.

### 7 · STATUS

🟡 **PHASE 0 AND PHASE 1 BUILT AND ON THE BRANCH (2026-08-19, v2.29.4). PHASES 2–3 NOT STARTED.**

**The route is ruled: `"Route B"`** — styles in the markup, class names removed. Decision
log 2026-08-19, "CR-018 TAKES ROUTE B". Section 3 above is answered; do not re-open it.

**Phase 0 is the theme and the build chain, and it touches ZERO screens.** It was allowed
to start ahead of CR-016 closing for the reason the ruling states: it renders nothing, so
it cannot regress the build the PO is verifying in a browser. **Proved rather than
claimed — built twice at one commit in an isolated worktree with nothing changed but the
plugin line, the production CSS is byte-identical: `index-DSjCOfdd.css`, 125.25 kB,
`sha256 6ab0e6ad…85f123ed`.**

| Delivered | |
|---|---|
| build chain | `tailwindcss@4.3.3` + `@tailwindcss/vite@4.3.3`, plugin registered in `vite.config.ts`. **v4 confirmed** — its peer range `^5.2.0 \|\| ^6 \|\| ^7 \|\| ^8` is satisfied by our Vite 5.4.21, so no upgrade and no v3 fallback |
| theme | `07-frontend/src/styles/tailwind.css` — **all 76 tokens cross**: 63 under their own name, 6 as a derived alias with both names emitted, 7 by a proven-equal mapping with a written reason |
| B14 by construction | five namespaces cleared (`--color-*`, `--text-*`, `--radius-*`, `--shadow-*`, `--font-*`), so `text-lg` on a table cell and `text-base` on a button no longer exist. `rounded-full` deliberately NOT zeroed — the A12 service dots are circles |
| proof | `07-frontend/tailwind-specimen/` — rendered in a browser: **utilities 76/76 · variables 76/76 · neutralised defaults 17/17**, screenshotted. Proved RED on four sabotages first, and the red proof is what added the second check |
| drift guard | `src/styles/tailwindTheme.test.ts`, runs in `npm test`, proved RED on five sabotages |
| cost | **0 bytes** in the app bundle · **4.22 kB raw / 1.50 kB gzip** for the theme's own floor with zero utilities used — the baseline Phase 3 is judged against |
| raised, not decided | **OQ-272** the Archivo webfont (never chosen by anyone) · **OQ-273** four of the ten services have no colour · **OQ-274** six ad-hoc breakpoints, no ratified set |

**⚠ PHASE 0 WAS BUILT TWICE.** The first build was lost in full — eight files, zero
commits — when the shared working tree, ~170 commits behind origin for that entire run,
was brought up to date. It also poisoned three measurements that were taken from stale
files and would have shipped as fact. Both are recorded in the decision-log row §10.

**Phases 1–3 remain blocked by the PO's own sequencing on CR-016**, and by the closure bar
of 2026-08-18: a person performing the task in a browser. Section 4 of this CR still
stands unchanged — the CR-016 conformance harness is the instrument that makes the
migration safe, and G31 stays load-bearing until there are no bespoke classes left to
refuse, at which point it is retired deliberately with a written reason.

## CR-018 · PHASE 1 — THE SPIKE, AND ITS NUMBER (2026-08-19, v2.29.4)

**§6 above asks for exactly this: *"A spike on ONE screen first, measured, before
the other 126."* It is done. Decision log 2026-08-19, "CR-018 PHASE 1 — ONE SCREEN
MIGRATED, AND WHAT IT COST", carries the full working; this is the summary a
sizing conversation needs.**

**The screen: `features/rating/RateSchedulesTab.tsx`** — chosen to be
representative rather than easy. It has its own `<table>` twice, a card grid, a
search input, a pager, and the tab's one interpolated class name. Of the five
candidates measured it had the **highest proportion of shared classes (43%)**,
which is the risk this CR's own plan says lives in Phase 2.

| | |
|---|---|
| classes referenced | **23** |
| migrated to utilities | **13 (57%)**, all single-use |
| left as they were | **10 (43%)**, shared — Phase 2 by the ruling |
| CSS deleted | **87 lines** (`PlansRates.css` 509 → 423) |
| markup changed | **15 `className` sites** |
| wall clock | **2 h 10 min**, of which the screen itself was **~6 min** |
| visual difference | **NONE** — 0 differing computed values across 237 elements, byte-identical full-page PNG |
| CR-016 conformance | **every baseline number holds**, unchanged, 24 screens |
| gates | 24 PASS / 10 FAIL before **and** after — identical |
| bundle | 125,258 → **132,582** raw (+7,324; **6,388 of it the one-time floor**, 936 the screen) |

### THE SIZING, AND IT IS NOT THE PER-SCREEN NUMBER TIMES 126

**~30 min/screen of mechanical work → ≈63 h for the other 126, PLUS a Phase 2
for the 179 shared classes this spike could not touch from a single component.**

The 3,020 rewrite sites are the CHEAP part. The expensive part was four
decisions this CR did not know existed — and three of the four are now paid once
and written into the code:

1. **Preflight cannot be imported yet.** Measured: one import line moved **684
   computed property values on one screen** and dropped every `<h1>` in the
   product from **30px to 15px**, because `global.css` gives headings no
   font-size and the browser has always supplied it. Deferred to the last commit
   of Phase 3 — and **blocked on OQ-275**, because the product renders h1 at
   30px while the design tokens say 42px.
2. **Utilities must be imported UNLAYERED.** A cascade layer loses to unlayered
   CSS whatever the specificity, and 40 legacy stylesheets remain for all of
   Phases 1–3. Layered, the migrated card silently gains 12px of padding.
3. **G31 goes red at the START of the migration, not the end.** §4.3 above says
   it "becomes meaningless" and retires at the end of Phase 3. It went **0 → 25
   on component 1 of 127**. The ratchet was NOT lowered: migrated files are named
   in `src/styles/route-b-migrated.txt` and handed to
   `src/styles/routeBUtilities.test.ts`, which asks the stricter question by
   calling the real Tailwind compiler. **§4.3 of this CR is corrected by
   measurement.**
4. **`text-text/70` is not our colour.** Tailwind's opacity modifier emits
   `color-mix(in OKLAB, …)`; we write `in srgb` at **243 sites across 30
   stylesheets**. No pixel moved on this near-black ink, and it will on the
   accent reds — so every translucent colour is written long-hand. This is the
   biggest readability cost Route B pays here and it is permanent.

### RAISED, NOT DECIDED

* **OQ-275** — headings render at sizes no token declares (h1 30px vs `--text-h1`
  42px). **Blocks Preflight, and therefore blocks closing Phase 3.**
* **OQ-276** — 11/12/13px text has no token; Phases 2–3 will otherwise write
  **~287 arbitrary font sizes**, which is B14 rule 5's *"no inline font sizes"*
  relocated rather than enforced.
* **OQ-277** — G31's class-name reader now exists twice, in two languages, in two
  workflows that share no runtime.

### ALSO FIXED IN PASSING

**7,824 bytes of Phase 0's throwaway proof page were being shipped to
customers.** `tailwind-specimen/README.md` says it is "not shipped"; Tailwind
v4's source auto-detection walks the project directory, not `src/`, so 48 of the
first build's 148 rules came from `specimen.js`. `source(none)` + `@source "../"`.

### WHAT THE SPIKE DID **NOT** COVER — do not read the number as covering it

No media query or responsive variant (OQ-274 still open) · no `:hover`,
`:focus-visible`, `:disabled` or `::before` (all were in the shared set) · no
shared class at all · no `@keyframes`, `transition`, `z-index` or `position`
context · no dark mode or print sheet (the app has neither). And
**`svc-${card.service}` can never become a utility** — Tailwind generates only
what its scanner can see — so the six `.svc-*` rules must survive Phase 2, which
a test now asserts.

### ROLLBACK, STATED BEFORE SHIPPING (change process §8)

**Fully reversible, and cheaply.** Phase 1 is five files: revert the migration
commit and the screen returns to its own CSS; remove the `main.tsx` import line
and Tailwind leaves the bundle entirely, back to `index-DSjCOfdd.css` at 125.25
kB. Nothing in the database, no served string, no rule changed. The one thing
that does not revert is the knowledge — which is the deliverable.

### THE 77 MOVED ELEMENTS, WHICH IS THE WHOLE VISUAL DIFF

62 at 10px→11px (pills, kickers, meta) · 8 at 9px→11px (the sort arrow, below
r10's readability floor) · 5 at 12.5px→12px (a card description) · 1 at
42px→56px (the pricing hero, the one heading the ruling moves) · 1 at

### WHAT IS AND IS NOT ENFORCED — READ THIS BEFORE ASSUMING THE RULE BITES

**Enforced today:** the twelve steps are pinned on one line in
`tailwindTheme.test.ts`; `tokens.css` and the `@theme` block cannot drift token
by token; `text-xs/sm/base/md/display` must emit the RULED px through the real
Tailwind compiler; CR-016's register holds the rendered figures on 24 screens.

paragraph read: *"nothing stops a stylesheet writing `font-size: 17px` tomorrow.

* `npm run lint` now runs in `ci-frontend.yml`, where it had run nowhere at all

**What is still a convention and not a constraint:** the ROLE a token is used
for. `var(--text-h5)` on a control passes every check in the repo, and that is

* **DEF-339** — `npm run lint` was red on this branch and no workflow runs it.

### ROLLBACK, STATED BEFORE SHIPPING (change process §8)

**Trigger:** OQ-278 was ruled (decision log `6a13828`) and the tier it names had

signed rule reversed, no money, no data, no migration. **Version:** `2.29.6`,

in one commit, and visible on screen in the sidebar.

### WHAT SHIPPED

1. **Three metric tokens** — `--text-metric-sm` 22px, `--text-metric` 26px (the
   KPI role's app default), `--text-metric-lg` 32px, with two leadings. They
   carry a leading and **no weight and no tracking**, because every metric site
   already sets its own weight; `tailwindTheme.test.ts` asserts the absence.
2. **Eight of the fourteen off-scale literals became token references**, with
   **exactly two pixel movements**, both ruled: `.kpi .v` 30→26 (the dashboard
   and every KPI strip) and `.pay-today-amount` 40→32.
3. **The arbitrary-value escape hatch is closed** by a gate that actually runs.

### THE CENSUS WAS RE-DERIVED AND THE BRIEF'S FIGURE WAS WRONG

Ours is **14** (16px ×2 · 18px ×2 · 22px ×5 · 24px ×2 · 26px ×1 · 30px ×1 ·
40px ×1). There is **no 20px literal** anywhere in `07-frontend`. The lane brief
said 16 sites including a 20px; OQ-278's own registry row says fourteen and is
right. Read from the **pinned tip**, not from disk — the shared working tree had
reset to an Aug-18 snapshot 184 files behind the branch, and a census taken off
it would have been quietly wrong in the way Phase 0's first run was.

### PROVED BY CLICKING (closure bar, PO ruling 2026-08-18)

Booted stack — Postgres + Django + the BUILT bundle on one origin — signed in as
the seeded owner, bundle rebuilt between runs:

* **Census before/after: 25 screens, 11,089 elements each. The complete diff is
  217 rows and every one is the two ruled movements** (68 × 30→26 across 9
  screens, 3 × 40→32, plus their derived line-height and letter-spacing rows).
* **Four of six full-page screenshots are byte-identical** before and after;
  the two that differ are the dashboard and payments, which are the two intended
  changes.
* **CR-016's conformance register held every number on all 24 screens.**
* vitest 98 files / 1,510 tests green; `npm run lint` clean; `run_gates.py` — G34
  PASS, and the 10 pre-existing FAILs (G1, G8, G10, G12, G13, G15, G17, G18,
  G25, G26) are unchanged from the tip and belong to other lanes.

### RAISED, NOT DECIDED

* **OQ-279** — the six literals that are left. Every one is a ROLE the ruled
  scale has no name for, not a value it disagrees with: two controls/prose at
  `--text-h5`'s 16px, two 18px (one of them the sidebar wordmark, which r10 sets
  at exactly 18px), and two 24px TITLES between a metric name and a heading step.

### ROLLBACK, STATED BEFORE SHIPPING (change process §8)

**Fully reversible, and in two independent halves.** The tokens and the eight
re-points are CSS: revert those two commits and the dashboard returns to 30px and
payments to 40px. The gate and the lint rule are a third commit that touches no
rendered output at all — reverting it removes a check and changes nothing a user
sees. The one thing that does NOT revert cleanly is the `text-base`/`text-sm`
swap in `RateSchedulesTab.tsx`, and only in the sense that reverting it puts back
