## CR-018 · PHASE 3 — THE SHARED CLASSES, MEASURED ON THE BUTTON FAMILY (2026-08-20, v2.29.9)

**Phase 1 said what this phase had to answer, in its own words:** it *"could not
touch a single shared class"* and *"a Phase 2 for 179 shared classes remains
entirely unmeasured."* **Classification:** continuation of CR-018, not a new
change — no signed statement is reversed and no ❄️ FROZEN figure is touched.
Decision log 2026-08-20, "CR-018 PHASE 3 — THE SHARED CLASSES, AND THE QUESTION
ROUTE B DID NOT ANSWER", carries the working; the full measurement is
`12-governance/reports/2026-08-20-cr018-phase3-button-spike.md`.

### The question this phase was sent to answer

**For a class used by 82 components, does "styles in the markup" mean 82 copies of
the same utility string?** Three shapes were put: **(a)** repeat the utilities,
**(b)** extract a React component, **(c)** `@apply` in a component layer.

**(c) is Route A and the PO rejected it** — the class name stays the contract, so
DEF-327's failure mode survives. It was not chosen and is not smuggled in.

**(a) DOES NOT WORK, and that is a measurement, not an opinion.** Tailwind emits
one rule per utility and orders them itself, so `bg-transparent` (from `.btn`) and
`bg-accent` (from `.btn-primary`) in one class attribute is decided at BUILD time,
not by the order they are written. The first parity run printed **540 differing
properties**: a transparent primary button with body-coloured text.

**(b) is the answer.** One module owns the string; 250 call sites ask by meaning.

### Delivered

| | |
|---|---|
| the kit | `src/components/buttonKit.ts` — the strings, one copy, filled in named SLOTS |
| the components | `Button` · `ButtonLink` · `ButtonAnchor` · `ButtonSummary` — **five host elements, because the kit is applied to five** |
| checked | `src/components/buttonKit.test.ts` (every token through the real Tailwind compiler, in `npm test`) · `e2e/CR-018-phase3-button-parity.spec.ts` (legacy vs component, every computed property, rest/hover/active/disabled) · `e2e/CR-018-phase3-screens.spec.ts` (4 screens, every clickable, before/after) |
| migrated | **34 call sites in 8 files**, plus **18 in 9 more** forced by `GuardedButton`'s prop becoming a `variant` |
| proof | **16,768 + 11,875 computed-property comparisons, 0 differing.** PNGs differ by **53 pixels each — the sidebar version label this release bumped.** CR-016: 24 screens, every baseline number, PASS |
| raised, not decided | **DEF-342** four button sizes under one conforming font size · **DEF-343** the template chips' `active` styles nothing · **DEF-344** `.met-danger` duplicates the kit's `.btn-danger` · **OQ-280** the safety net does not reach a component API |

### ⚠ THE TWO THINGS A LANE STARTING PHASE 3 PROPER MUST READ FIRST

1. **Seven stylesheet rules style a button from its PARENT.** Route B has no
   parent selector, so the override must travel down. Missing this moved 1,416
   properties on 273 buttons with every gate green.
2. **A typo'd utility inside a component constant is invisible to BOTH G31 and
   `routeBUtilities.test.ts`** — proved by sabotage. Every extracted kit needs its
   own compiler check until OQ-280 is ruled.

### Sizing

**≈3 hours for the family**, ~2 of them one-time. **≈35–60 hours for the remaining
169 shared classes**, with the three big layout containers (`.met-panel` 41,
`.met-table` 30, `.kicker` 26) unexercised and structurally harder than a leaf
control.

### Status

🟡 **PHASE 3 SPIKE COMPLETE AND ON THE BRANCH. THE OTHER 169 SHARED CLASSES ARE
NOT STARTED.** The 28 button CSS rules are still declared and must be — 74 files
still name them — so the bundle grew (CSS 138.31 → 141.79 kB raw) and the shrink
arrives only when the last call site is migrated.

## CR-018 · PHASE 4a — THE BUTTON FAMILY'S 161 CALL SITES (2026-08-20, v2.29.22)

**Trigger:** the PO, *"start phase 4 of Cr18"*. **Classification:** continuation
of CR-018, not a new change.

### What Phase 4 was going to be, and why the order changed

The Phase 3 report sized *"the remaining 169 shared classes at 35–60 hours"* and
named the three biggest — `.met-panel` 41 components, `.met-table` 30, `.kicker`
26 — as *"unexercised and structurally harder than a leaf control"*. So Phase 4
opened by measuring `.met-panel`, and the measurement is the finding:

> **`.met-panel` IS NOT A CLASS, IT IS A STYLING SCOPE.** Its own rule is four
> declarations. But **`components/FormModal.css` carries EIGHT MORE RULES that
> style `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `label:has(> input)` and
> `input[type="date"]` AS ITS DESCENDANTS** — in a different stylesheet, across
> 46 components. Route B has no parent selector, so migrating it does not move 46
> class attributes; it moves eight rules down onto **every form control on those
> screens** (32 inputs, 15 selects, 38 labels, 155 headings by upper bound).

That is a different kind of work from a leaf control, and doing it first would
have spent the phase's budget on its hardest, least-understood item.

**So Phase 4a took the button family instead** — already de-risked by the Phase 3
spike, already parity-proved in a browser, and the only item that makes the
bundle shrink. The layout containers are Phase 4b with a real measurement behind
them.

### Delivered

| | |
|---|---|
| call sites migrated | **161 of 161** — 144 by codemod (`10-scripts/codemods/cr018_button_sites.py`, committed with the change), 17 by hand because each needed a judgement |
| CSS deleted | **six rules** — `.btn-primary`, `.btn-secondary`, `.btn-ghost`, `.btn-sm`, `.btn-danger`, `.btn-link`. `.btn` itself STAYS: three icon controls still use it as a base and the icon family is not in the kit yet |
| **bundle** | **CSS 141.94 → 140.69 kB raw · 21.44 → 21.29 gzip — DOWN FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS CR.** Every previous phase added. Target is still 125,258 |
| declared classes | 911 → **905** |
| component APIs | rating's `GuardedButton` takes a `variant` union instead of a class string — the change metering's took in Phase 3, for the same reason |
| retired | `e2e/CR-018-phase3-button-parity.spec.ts`, deliberately: it compared against CSS that no longer exists. Replaced by an anti-resurrection assertion in `buttonKit.test.ts`, RED-proved |
| defect found | **DEF-350** — six buttons on S73 wore a `btn-` variant with **no `.btn` base**, rendering as browser-default buttons. Found by the codemod REFUSING them |

### Three checks reported success over the thing they were pointed at

Worth recording together, because it is the same failure three times in one day
and it is the reason each was caught: **the proof was insisted on, not assumed.**

1. **G37's accessible-name check** searched a file for a string three elements

2. **The rule-15 browser spec** reported "641 row actions, all named" over five

3. **The anti-resurrection check** reported eleven declarations that were all

### Still open

**177 shared classes** by census (`>= 2 components`), the largest being
`.met-panel` 41, `.met-table` 30, `.kicker` 26, `.settings-refusal` 30. Phase 4b
is the layout containers and it now has a measured shape. **Route B ledger: 4
files of 130.**

### THE THREE THINGS ROUND 3 SHOULD READ FIRST

**1 · OQ-279 IS NOW THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, AND IT IS BIGGER THAN ITS OWN ROW
SAYS.** The row and G34's exact ratchet of 6 are about `font-size`. **`line-height`
has the identical shape and 23 live sites**, and no gate counts a single one of
them: `leading-[1.6]` is banned by G34 exactly as `text-[16px]` is, and 1.6, 1.7,
1.45 and 1.9 are reachable through no declared token. Measured:
`billing.css` 8 · `AuditLogPage.css` 3 · `customers.css` 3 · `SettingsPage.css` 3 ·
`payments.css` 2 · `RoutesCyclesWizards.css` 1 · `finance.css` 1 · `reads.css` 1 ·
`global.css` 1. **That is why round 2 migrated these three and not others** — they
are the ones holding none. The OQ-279 row is amended with this, dated; nothing was
chosen there.

**2 · A DESCENDANT VARIANT IS (0,1,1) AND A CELL'S OWN UTILITY IS (0,1,0).**
`[&_td]:text-left` on a table out-specifies `text-right` on the cell, and
`[&_td]:font-normal` out-specifies `font-semibold` on a total row. Both would have
been silent regressions with every test green — the ageing table has exactly those
two shapes. So a rule a CHILD ever overrides is written **on the child**, and
`Panel`'s `[&_h3]:` pattern is right only where nothing overrides it. The bill
run's deleted `.brun-gap-rule` carried two `!important`s for precisely this
reason, which is the same lesson from the stylesheet side.

**3 · A COMPOSED CLASS PAIR NEEDS THE BUILT SHEET, NOT THE SOURCE.**
`className="settings-tabs brun-tabs"` had both classes setting `margin-bottom`;
which one shipped is decided by the ORDER OF THE STYLESHEETS in the bundle, and
`dist/assets/*.css` answers it in one grep (`.bil-*` at 44197, `.settings-tabs` at
75927 → SettingsPage.css is later, so its 24px won and only the top margin came
from `.brun-tabs`). The port is `mt-3`; `my-3` would have shrunk a gap nobody
asked to change, invisibly. **Check any composed pair this way before porting it.**

### Defects filed (never folded in — §6)

* **DEF-562** — *a migrated screen's module-level utility constant is checked by
  nobody.* `routeBUtilities.test.ts`'s kit-constant case selects files by NAME
  (`*Kit.ts`) rather than by the Route B ledger, so a typo hoisted into a `const`
  in a migrated SCREEN is skipped by G31 (migrated) and by the kit case (name).
  **Measured, not feared:** `itmes-center` in a const of `AssetDetailPage.tsx`
  gave 9 passed and G31 PASS / 0 undeclared. Widening the loop was **tried and
  reverted** — the all-or-nothing heuristic reported 8+ false positives on
  ordinary screen constants (i18n keys, status ids, an element id), and a check
  with false positives gets switched off (DEF-323). **Workaround this round: every
  utility string is INLINE at its `className=` site**, where `classTokens` does
  check it. Round 3 should keep doing that until DEF-562 is fixed.
* **DEF-564** — *G31 is RED on the branch and it is not this CR's doing.*
  `features/metering/CommonAreasTab.tsx:428` asks for `met-row-actions`, a class
  deleted on 2026-08-20 when five per-feature row-action containers became
  `components/RowActions.tsx`. One line, in a directory this lane must not touch.

### Also changed, deliberately, and each is a strengthening

* **`components/PageHeader.css` now declares `.page-header`** — the shared
  component's own root class, which **nothing had ever declared**: `assets.css`
  was its only declaration site, through `.ast-page .page-header`. Deleting that
  file took a SHARED class undeclared and turned G31 red on a file the assets
  migration never touched. The rule is empty and says why: any property there
  moves pixels on every screen. One declaration site replaced another.
* **`dashboard.test.tsx` d.3 changed its METHOD.** `expect(html).not.toMatch(/\b0\b/)`
  scanned the whole markup for a digit, and utilities put digits in `class=`
  (`m-0`, `gap-2`). It strips the tags first now and asks what the PO's ruling was
  actually about — does the operator READ a zero. Re-proved RED with `count: 0`.
* **One interpolated `className` left `BillRunWizard.tsx`** — `` `side-item${a ? " active" : ""}` ``
  is invisible to Tailwind's scanner and `routeBUtilities` refuses one in a
  migrated file. `.side-item`/`.active` are AppShell.css's and stay classes; only
  the spelling changed, to one whole string literal per branch.

### ⚠ THE HEADLINE, AND ROUND 4 MUST READ IT BEFORE PLANNING ANYTHING

**OQ-279 WAS RULED AND IT UNBLOCKED ONE STYLESHEET, NOT THIRTEEN.** Round 2's
finding was that 23 `line-height` literals across 9 stylesheets were the binding
constraint. The ruling named four `--leading-*` values. Measured against the code
the moment they landed:

| the 23 literals are | sites | is it reachable now? |
|---|---|---|
| **1.45** | 2 | ✅ `--leading-relaxed` |
| **1.6** | **16** | ❌ nothing |
| **1.7** | 3 | ❌ nothing |
| **1.9** | 2 | ❌ nothing |

`--leading-none` (1), `--leading-tight` (1.2) and `--leading-snug` (1.4) close
**none** of the 23 — every one of those three values was **already reachable**
(`leading-none` is Tailwind's own, 1.2 is `--leading-btn`, 1.4 is
`--leading-screen-id`), so what they add is a role-generic ALIAS. Worth having;
not a new value. The three numbers that actually hold the long tail — 1.6, 1.7,
1.9 — were never put in front of the PO, because the question was written about
the six font sizes and the leading half was added as an amendment.

**This is now OQ-337, OPEN**, with the site-by-site count and three options; the
closed OQ-279 row is stamped with the correction, dated, so the next lane does
not read "thirteen stylesheets unblocked" and plan a round on it. **Seven of the
eighteen remaining stylesheets are blocked on it**, `SettingsPage.css` (1,115
lines) and `billing.css` (583) among them — and it holds `--text-panel`'s two
ruled 24px answers hostage inside two of those same files, which is why G34
stopped at 5 rather than 3.

### THE THREE THINGS ROUND 4 SHOULD READ NEXT

**1 · A `@theme` `--animate-*` KEY IS A TRANSCRIPTION, AND THE KEYFRAMES MUST GO
INSIDE THE BLOCK.** Round 2 listed `SignupWizard.css` as "unblocked by a single
decision: whether `@theme` may declare an `--animate-*` key". It is not a
decision when the animation already exists in the stylesheet being deleted — the
same argument `--leading-btn` was added under in Phase 3, and the same one round
1 used for `--tracking-label` and `--tracking-screen-id`. Copy the timing and the
keyframes byte for byte, say so in the theme file, and no value has been chosen.
Two mechanics that are not obvious: **`--animate-*` is not one of the cleared
namespaces**, so the key sits beside Tailwind's own `animate-spin`; and **v4
emits the `@keyframes` only when it is declared INSIDE `@theme`** — put it
outside and the utility compiles to an animation nothing defines, the element
stops moving, and no test or gate says a word. `tailwindTheme.test.ts` stays
green because its drift check runs tokens.css → `@theme`, so a theme-only key is
lawful. **This also half-unblocks `StateFrame.css`** (`@keyframes state-shimmer`);
what is left there is its nine assertions in excluded directories.

**2 · A HEADING STEP CARRIES FOUR PROPERTIES, AND THREE OF THEM ARE INVISIBLE
UNTIL THE MIGRATION.** `text-h3` is not "font-size: 25px" — it is size + weight +
leading + tracking as v4 modifiers. A CSS rule that wrote `font-size:
var(--text-h3)` and inherited the BODY leading becomes 1.12 the moment it is a
utility, and at 25px that is an 11px shorter line box on every plan card. So for
every `font-size: var(--text-h*)` in a stylesheet, ask what the element's leading
and tracking are TODAY: if they are inherited, the port is `text-h3 leading-body
tracking-normal`, three classes, not one. **Where the site wants no heading
semantics at all, `--text-lead` (16px) is now the right answer** — `SignupWizard`'s
plan name is exactly that shape and takes it in one class.

**3 · SPECIFICITY IS THE THING NO GATE IN THIS REPO READS, AND IT DECIDED TWO
RULES THIS ROUND.** Round 2's lesson was that a descendant variant out-specifies
a child's own utility. The public nav is the mirror image: `.public-nav a` is
(0,1,1) and **every button utility is (0,1,0)**, both unlayered, so the page has
always overridden the design system — the primary CTA's `text-bg` never applied.
Reproducing that faithfully needed the same descendant shape plus a `:not()`
carve-out for the wordmark, which had (0,2,0) of its own. **Before porting any
`.parent child` rule, work out which of the two the browser is actually
obeying** — `dist/assets/*.css` plus a specificity count answers it, and the
source alone never does.

### Defect filed (never folded in — §6)

* **DEF-573** — *a page descendant rule overrides the primary button's own colour
  and size, on both public screens.* `.public-nav a { font-size: var(--text-base);

  request. Nothing could have caught it: only a computed-style read in a browser

### ⚠ THE HEADLINE — FOUR DEAD DECLARATIONS, THREE MECHANISMS, AND ROUND 5 WILL FIND MORE

Every migration in rounds 1–3 asked "what does this rule say?". Round 4 asked
"**and is it still winning?**", and four times in three files the answer was no.
None of them is a Tailwind problem; all four predate this CR.

**1 · A PAGE RULE THAT USED TO BEAT A SHARED COMPONENT NOW LOSES TO IT.**
Phases 3 and 4a moved the button kit and `PlainTable` out of component
stylesheets and into utility strings — which live in the LAST sheet in the
bundle. A page rule at (0,1,0) that used to override `.btn-ghost` now ties with
`px-1` and loses on source order. Three instances, all filed:

| what | was | is | filed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.audit-retention-link { padding-left: 0 }` | flush left | 4px indent (`px-1`) | DEF-581 |
| `.rcw-exit { padding-inline: 0; font-size: 13px }` | flush, 13px | 4px, 14px (`px-1`, `text-btn`) | DEF-581 (the census it asked for) |
| `.bil-linegroup th { padding-top: 12px }` | 12px | 8px (`PlainTable`'s `[&_th]:p-2`) | DEF-585 |

⚠ **The third is the worst-shaped**, because `PlainTable` writes padding as a
SHORTHAND: a caller cannot add top padding to a plain-table header cell at all,
whatever they write, unless they win on emit order. Prefer longhands in a shared
kit (`py-2 px-2`, not `p-2`) so a caller's single-side override is a real
override. **PlainTable has 51 call sites and the button kit ~250; every page
rule that overrode a property either sets is in the same position.**

**2 · A RULE THAT LOSES TO ITS OWN FILE.** `.rcw-empty { text-align: center;
padding: 24px 8px }` is (0,1,0) and is only ever used on a `<td>` inside
`.rcw-table`, whose `td` rule is (0,1,1) and sets both properties. B14 rule 17's
empty state has never been centred, on three wizard pickers. Two rules, one
file, both look intentional — filed as DEF-582.

**3 · AND THE MIRROR IMAGE, WHICH IS THE NEAR-MISS OF THE ROUND.**
`.rcw-table .cell-num` LOOKED redundant with the shared `.cell-num` three other
stylesheets declare. Its tnum half is. **Its `text-align: right` is not**: a bare
`.cell-num` is (0,1,0) and `.rcw-table td` was (0,1,1), so the wizard's own
(0,2,0) rule was the only thing right-aligning the Units and Meters columns.
Dropping it and writing `[&_td]:text-left` — also (0,1,1) — would have
left-aligned every number in both pickers **with every test green**. It crosses
as `[&_.cell-num]:text-right`, the same rank it had.

**The rule round 5 should work by: for every rule you are about to port, find
what else sets the same property on the same element, and compare RANKS — not
just what is written in the file you are deleting.** `dist/assets/*.css` plus a
specificity count answers it; the source alone never does.

### THE THREE OTHER THINGS ROUND 5 SHOULD READ

**1 · `font: inherit` GOES TWO DIFFERENT WAYS AND THE NEIGHBOURING CLASSES
DECIDE.** `.audit-open` had no size utility beside it, so `[font:inherit]` — the
arbitrary PROPERTY, which G34 does not ban (it bans `font-[…]`) — is exact and
explicit. `.rcw-input` and `.rcw-chip` DO sit beside `text-sm`, and
`[font:inherit]` is emitted at byte 125151 against `text-sm` at 118478 — LATER,
so the shorthand would eat the size (the trap `Surfaces.tsx` documented in
Phase 3). There, Preflight's own `button,input,select,textarea { font: inherit }`
is the identical declaration in `layer(base)`, nothing unlayered contests font on
those elements, so it supplies it and the size utility still wins. **Both files
are in this round; read them side by side before choosing.**

**2 · ONE TOKEN, TWO PORTS, AND THE ELEMENT DECIDES.** Round 3's lesson 2 said a
heading step carries four properties. Round 4 found the same shape twice more and
in both tiers: `.bil-level` is a `<p>` that inherited the body leading and normal
tracking, so `--text-h5` needs `text-h5 leading-body tracking-normal`, while
`.bil-doc-band h3` is an `<h3>` that already has both from `global.css` and needs
`text-h5` alone. And `.rcw-stat-figure` is `text-metric leading-body`, because
the METRIC steps carry a `--line-height` modifier (1.1) too and that span
inherited 1.55. Same token, same pixel, different ports.

**3 · TWO INTERPOLATED CLASS NAMES AND ONE ADJACENT-SIBLING RULE, AND ALL THREE
HAVE A SHAPE NOW.** `rcw-consequence-${tone}` became a
`Record<"move"|"check", string>` of whole strings (round 3's `SignupWizard`
pattern); the chip's `${… ? " rcw-chip-active" : ""}` became two whole strings;
and `.bil-rollup-item + .bil-rollup-item::before` became
`not-first:before:content-['·']` — lawful only because every child of
`.bil-rollup` is an item and all six are unconditional, which was checked at both
call sites rather than assumed. ⚠ And when writing a tone table, **never put
`bg-transparent` beside a `bg-[color-mix(…)]` in one string**: two
background-colour utilities on one element are decided by Tailwind's emit order,
not by the order written.

### Defects filed (never folded in — §6)

* **DEF-581** — *the retention-log link button lost its `padding-left: 0` when
  the button family became utilities.* Equal specificity, and the kit's `px-1`

* **DEF-582** — *the route/cycle wizard's empty-state cell has never been centred
  and its 24px padding has never applied.* `.rcw-empty` (0,1,0) against
  `.rcw-table td` (0,1,1), in the same file.
* **DEF-585** — *the bill's per-service group header lost its extra top padding
  when `PlainTable` became utilities.* Same mechanism as DEF-581, different
  component, and worse because the kit sets padding with a shorthand.
* **DEF-586** — *an e2e assertion selects two class names that exist nowhere in
  the product.* `e2e/billing-surfaces.spec.ts` asserts `toHaveCount(5)` on
  `.bil-layout-card` and text on `.bil-layout-name`; that tab draws the shared
  `.chooser-option` pattern and always has. Not a migration regression — the
  classes were never in `billing.css`. **Nothing runs Playwright in CI**, which
  is why a spec that cannot pass has sat there; the cheap fix proposed on the row
  is to extend G31's reader to `e2e/` so a class LOCATOR naming a class no
  component writes is reported the way an undeclared `className` already is.

### Also true, and each is small

* **`--tracking-tag: 0.06em`** joins `@theme` as a TRANSCRIPTION — the fifth
  wide-tracking value in the product (after kicker 0.1, table header 0.08,

* **One INERT rule deleted rather than ported**: `.audit-filters .field

* **A census exclusion by SUBSTRING nearly lost four assertions.** The first pass

* **The prettier trap in a shared tree.** `npx prettier --write
  "src/features/billing/*.tsx"` reformatted five files this lane had no reason to
  touch, turning a one-line change into a 125-line diff. Nothing in CI checks

## CR-019 · Trash is billed PER CART, and the cart count multiplies the price (2026-08-20)

**Captured at arrival, requester's words verbatim (change-process step 0):**

> "in trash you ahve trash cans. they can be 1 ore more at csutomer locations,
> they are bill 1 trash can $15 - for example if you ahve 3 you multiple by 3 we
> will ahve to capture this in rates and plan"

**Step 1 · CLASSIFY — this is a CHANGE, not a defect.** Nothing in the repo states
a cart-count rule and nothing was built wrongly against one; the requirement is
new. It arrived during CR-013 and belongs to it in substance, so it is recorded as
its own CR and folded into CR-013's scope rather than opened as a parallel build.

**Step 2 · WHAT SIGNED STATEMENT IS REVERSED — none.** No ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure
speaks to cart counts. The $15.00 in the request is an **example the PO gave**, not
a rate to seed; the tenant sets it.

**Step 3 · WHAT THE PRODUCT ALREADY HAS — more than expected.** Three of the four
pieces exist:

* **`per cart` is already a unit of measure.** CR-013 part 1 lists the derived UoMs
  as *"kWh / kgal / therm / % of water / per cart"*.
* **Carts are already a size class.** A1 §S76 defines `meter_size_classes` as
  *"5/8″–4″ water · 1φ/3φ electric · gas classes · **carts**"*, and the list holds
  9 seeded rows.
* **Trash is one of the ten seeded services** (BR-RAT-024).

**What is missing is the QUANTITY**, and that is the whole of this CR.

**Step 4 · WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT AND IS NOW WRONG — and the blocker.**

⚠ **This requirement is blocked by `DEF-161` (CRITICAL, open):** *"A PLAN CARRYING
ANY NON-METERED SERVICE CANNOT BE BILLED AT ALL: the run demands a meter."* Trash
is the archetypal non-metered service, so the bill run refuses a trash plan today
before any cart rule could apply. **CR-019 cannot be demonstrated until DEF-161 is
fixed**, and DEF-161 is arguably the same requirement seen from the other end.

The resolution chain is the specific place it bites. **R3b derives the billable
quantity from a METER READ × multiplier** — a cart has no read. `resolution.py`
already refuses this by name: *"the plan covers {service} and the unit has no meter
for it, so there is no connection size to resolve a size row against."*

**Step 5 · THE QUESTION FOR THE PO, in plain English with the figure.** Three ways
to make three carts bill $45.00, and they differ in where the number 3 lives:

* **(A) Count the assets.** Carts are assets on the unit (metering owns assets,
  B2 r4), so the quantity is *how many active cart assets this unit has*. Adding a
  cart is an asset action and the next bill changes by itself. Costs a
  non-metered-quantity path in R3b — which DEF-161 needs anyway.
* **(B) A quantity on the plan's service line.** The account's trash service
  carries `quantity = 3`. Cheapest to build; the number is typed by staff and can
  silently disagree with the carts actually in the street.
* **(C) Model each cart as a service point with a read of 1.** Changes nothing in
  the chain — but it puts fictitious reads in `meter_reads`, and hard rule 3 says
  consumption always carries an explicit unit.

**The lane's recommendation is (A)**, because a cart is a physical thing the
utility already tracks and the count is then observed rather than re-typed. It is
also the option that makes DEF-161's fix general instead of trash-specific.

**Step 6 · WHERE IT LANDS.** Rate schedule, per §16's separation rule: *the rate
schedule prices a QUANTITY*, and a cart count is a quantity — so `Trash · Flat ·
per cart` is a rate schedule with a per-size (per cart-type) rate, and the plan
binds it like any other service. It is **not** a charge code: a charge code prices
a thing that exists, and this price multiplies.

**Step 7 · VERSION** — allocated when the build lands, per change-process §7.

**Step 8 · IMPACT.** Seed: a trash service point and 1–3 carts on at least one
fixture unit, or the case cannot be walked. E2E: a new journey — *three carts bill
$45.00, remove one and the next bill is $30.00*. Golden tests: a new case, because
no GT covers a non-metered quantity. Rollback: the plan simply cannot bind trash,
which is today's behaviour.

### CR-019 · AMENDED 2026-08-20 — THE PO RULED THE DECLARATION, NOT THE COUNT

Step 5's question went to the PO and came back **half answered**, which is the
useful half. Verbatim: *"yes we have to say service is meter or unmetered."*

**RULED (BR-RAT-081, CONFIRMED):** a service declares itself **metered or
unmetered**, and the bill run reads that declaration instead of demanding a meter.
The declaration lives on `tenant_services` (SET-03), beside `enabled` and
`revenue_account` — a property of what the utility **sells**, not of a plan, an
account or a premise, and the model's own docstring already argues that shape for
the GL attributes. **This is `DEF-161`'s fix and it is general**, not trash-specific:
every unmetered service in the ten-service seed becomes billable by the same change.

**R3b branches on it.** Metered → quantity from a read × the meter multiplier,
unchanged. Unmetered → quantity from a count, and the chain **never consults a
meter**. Both still refuse rather than default: an unmetered service whose count
cannot be determined stops the bill exactly as an unstated multiplier does.

**STILL OPEN — `OQ-283`:** where an unmetered service's count comes from. Options
A/B/C were shown with the worked figure (three carts at `$15.00` must bill
`$45.00`) and **the PO ruled only the declaration**, so a lane must not choose.
The lane's recommendation stands at **(A) count the cart assets on the unit**.

**Also settled, from the same session:** CR-019 lands on the **rate schedule**, now
under a ratified rule rather than a lane's reading — **BR-RAT-080**, *"the rate
schedule prices a QUANTITY; the charge code prices a THING."* A cart count is a
quantity and the price multiplies, which a charge code never does.

### CR-019 · BUILT 2026-08-21 (v2.29.55) — steps 6, 7 and 8, and what step 8 could not reach

**PO instruction:** *"CR-019 I can build now - lets do it"*. BR-RAT-090 had already
ruled the shape, so this build chose no rule.

**Step 6 · WHERE IT LANDED — the rate schedule, as step 6 said.** BR-RAT-080's
separation held up under the first real test of it: a cart count is a QUANTITY and
its price multiplies, so it is schedule work and not a charge code. Nothing about
the charge-code side moved.

**Step 7 · VERSION — `2.29.55`.**

**Step 8 · IMPACT, against what step 8 predicted:**

| Predicted | Actual |
|---|---|
| a non-metered-quantity path in R3b | ✅ `counted_quantity` + `AssetCountFacts` + `AssetCountUnavailable` |
| the count comes from assets | ✅ `assets.selectors.billable_asset_count`, reached through a rating seam |
| seed: carts on a fixture unit | ❌ **blocked on `OQ-303`** — see below |
| E2E: three carts bill $45.00 | ❌ same blocker |
| a golden case for a non-metered quantity | ❌ same blocker |

**WHAT THE COUNT ACTUALLY READS, because step 5 option A only said "count the
assets" and three predicates had to be chosen:**

* **Dated**, from `AssetAssignment` (append-only, BR-AST-017), at the
  service-period end date — so a cart delivered on the 20th does not retro-bill
  the whole cycle, and one removed mid-cycle still billed while it was there.
* **In service**, by the lifecycle stage's `behavior_class` and never its label,
  which is BR-AST-031's own rule. A tenant who renames *Installed/Active* to
  *Deployed* must not thereby stop billing.
* **For this service**, through the asset's service point. A unit with three carts
  and a water meter counts three for trash, not four.

**⚠ THE ONE NUMBER — `OQ-303`, and this is why the seed is empty.** CR-019's step 2
already recorded that the PO's `$15.00` is *"an example the PO gave, not a rate to
seed"*. The only trash figure in the billing workbook is §1's *"Trash flat $18"*,
and that is a **MONTHLY BASE** — `TRASH_FLAT` seeds as a plan base charge and the
trash schedule's unit price is `$0.00`. Re-reading the `$18` as a per-cart rate
would bill a three-cart household **`$54.00`** where the workbook says **`$18.00`**,
which is a signed figure quietly changing meaning. Spec rule 7 forbids the seeder
choosing, so the question is minted with three costed options and nothing is seeded.

**⚠ AND A LARGER FINDING THIS BUILD SURFACED — `DEF-438`, CRITICAL.** Looking for
the caller that would count the carts turned up that **there is no caller.**
`apps/rating/resolution.py` is 1,150 lines implementing the whole of design §A2 and
`grep` finds ZERO production imports of it. So CR-019's cart count, BR-RAT-088's
`$23,069.50`/month base fix and BR-RAT-081's unmetered declaration are all correct,
all tested, and **none of them can be reached from an invoice.** That is a bigger
gap than CR-019 itself and it is filed as such.


## CR-025 · Every import offers a sample CSV to download at step 1 (2026-08-21)

**Step 0 · CAPTURE — the requester's words verbatim:**

> "also we will need sample CSV files to be downloaded at every import at step 1"

**Step 1 · CLASSIFY — a CHANGE, and a small one.** Nothing is broken and nothing
we built is wrong; this is a capability neither r10 nor B15 asked for. r10's
stage 1 draws the four source cards, the drop zone and the four fields, and no
sample-file link anywhere.

**Step 2 · WHAT SIGNED STATEMENT IS REVERSED — none.** No rule says an import
must not offer a template. `BR-MET-088` (the MAPS TO list is the target's REAL
columns) is the rule this LEANS ON rather than reverses: a sample file is only
truthful if its header row is generated from the same target columns the
mapping stage offers. A hand-written sample would drift the first time a column
was added, which is `DEF-521`'s shape one level up.

**Step 3 · SCOPE — "every import", so it is the RUNNER's feature, not a
screen's.** `BR-MET-096` rules one workflow for premises and units, so the
sample belongs to the runner and takes its target as a parameter, exactly as
the field map does. One control, two files, and a third the day a third target
lands.

**Step 4 · WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT THAT THIS TOUCHES.** `ImportWorkflowPage`
stage 1 (a link beside the drop zone) and `import_runs.target_columns`, which
already answers *"what columns does this target have"* — the sample's header row
is that answer, comma-joined. **Nothing has to be invented and nothing becomes
wrong.**

**Step 5 · THE SIZE, in plain English:** one endpoint that returns a CSV whose
header is the target's own required-and-common columns with one example row, and
one link on stage 1. **The one judgment it needs:** does the sample carry an
EXAMPLE ROW (easier to use, and someone will upload it unedited) or headers only
(safe, and less helpful)? Recorded, not decided here.

⚠ **THE FAST PATH APPLIES** (change process step 5): no rule, no money, no
stored data.

**STATUS: CAPTURED 2026-08-21. Queued behind the end-to-end verification the PO
asked for in the same exchange.**

### CR-025 · CLOSED (2026-08-22, fast path)

**The one open judgment, decided and recorded** (decision log, same date): the
sample carries **one example row**, not headers only — the repo's own precedent

`BR-MET-032`. Guessable cells carry ratified SEED codes (`apartment_complex`

## CR-020 · Contracts attached to plans — CAPTURED, DEFERRED BY THE PO (2026-08-20)

**Requester's words verbatim (change-process step 0):**

> "Please note - we did not consider contracts in this; we will need another tab
> where we attach contracts required for various plans - these will be documents
> directly attached and then we add them on the plans - hthis requirement is not
> yet handled"

**PO instruction on timing, same exchange:** *"just keep a note of this we will
handle it in the end."* **So this CR is CAPTURED and NOT SCOPED.** No estimate, no
epic, no stories — deliberately, because sizing it would mean answering the
questions in step 3 below, and the PO has not been asked them yet.

**Step 1 · CLASSIFY — a CHANGE, and a genuinely new one.** Nothing in CR-013's
five parts, in A1–A17 or in r10 mentions a plan contract. The PO is right that it
was not considered.

**Step 3 · WHAT THE PRODUCT HAS TO BUILD ON — almost nothing, and that is the
finding.** Checked rather than assumed:

* **r10 draws no contract anywhere.** Every hit in the drawing is *"contractor"* —
  the Work module's field crews, an unrelated word. One stray *"Contract"*.
* **The product has exactly ONE document table**: `discount_enrolment_documents`,
  built by `0009_cr013_discounts.py` for CR-013 part 3's proof-of-eligibility. It
  is enrolment-scoped and role-restricted (BR-RAT-079: *"income and medical proof
  restricted by role and excluded from general document lists"*), so it is not a
  general attachment store and must not be bent into one.
* **There is no file-upload surface in Plans & Rates at all**, and no generic
  document library anywhere in the ten doc modules.

So this is not "add a tab" — it is a document capability the product does not
have, plus a tab.

**Step 5 · THE QUESTIONS THAT MUST BE PUT TO THE PO BEFORE IT IS SIZED.** Recorded
now so the next session does not re-derive them, and **not answered here**:

1. **A TEMPLATE, OR AN EXECUTED DOCUMENT?** *"Contracts required for various
   plans"* reads as a blank the customer signs — one document per plan. But a
   signed contract belongs to an **account**, dated and countersigned, and there
   would be one per customer. These are different tables, different lifecycles and
   different retention. It may well be both.
2. **DOES IT GATE ANYTHING?** If a plan requires a contract, may an account be
   assigned that plan before one is attached — and does PLN-04 refuse a plan
   change when the new plan's contract is unsigned? That decides whether this is a
   document feature or a billing gate.
3. **VERSIONS.** Every other object in Plans & Rates is effective-dated and
   versioned. If the contract changes, do accounts on the old one stay on it — the
   same *"bills use the version in force"* law — or does the new one apply?
4. **WHERE DOES THE FILE LIVE?** The product streams CSV exports to a `file:`
   artifact path today and has no upload endpoint, no virus scan and no retention
   policy for customer-supplied files. That is infrastructure, not a screen.

**Step 8 · IMPACT, as far as it can be stated without those answers:** a new table
(a B2 schema change, which goes the schema route), an upload/download path with
its own guards, a seventh Plans & Rates tab, and — if question 2 is *yes* — a new
refusal in the resolution chain or in PLN-04. **Rollback is free while nothing is
built**, which is the argument for answering the four questions before any of it.

## CR-022 · Plan eligibility should BLOCK an assignment, not advise it (2026-08-21)

**Step 0 · CAPTURE — the requester's words verbatim**, walking PLN-03 step 7:

**and the difference they are pointing at is r10's own sentence**, drawn on that

has qualified it. r10 predates it.

## CR-024 · A UNIT MUST BE MOVEABLE BETWEEN PREMISES (2026-08-21)

**Step 0 · CAPTURE — the requester's words verbatim**, arriving while CR-023's
screens were being built:

> "please ensure move units works in Units; we have that functionalities - you
> can have a modal for that; bascially user has put a unit in wrong premises they
> want to move it to correct premises."

**Step 1 · CLASSIFY — a NEW REQUIREMENT that REVERSES a CONFIRMED rule.** Not a
defect. The product does exactly what it was told to do, and it was told the
opposite of this.

**Step 2 · WHAT IS BEING REVERSED — quoted, not summarised.**

> `BR-MET-046` | **Units NEVER move between premises (deactivate + recreate);
> guarantees by-premises money traceability (S59/S60, ledger)** | PO PU-19 |
> **CONFIRMED**

And it is enforced, not merely written. `apps/metering/services.update_unit`
refuses outright:

```python
if "premises_id" in data or "premises" in data:
    raise errors.BizError(
        errors.BIZ_IMMUTABLE,
        br_ref="BR-MET-046",
        message_key="metering.unit.premises_immutable",
        params={"alternative": "deactivate_and_recreate"},
    )
```

⚠ **THE PO'S OWN NOTE — *"we have that functionalities"* — IS THE ONE THING IN
THE REQUEST THAT IS NOT SO**, and it is worth stating plainly rather than
quietly building around: there is **no move service, no endpoint and no modal**.
What exists is r10 DRAWING it — a `⇄ Move` action on PRM-03, a swap icon on
PRM-02's Units tab, and a whole screen id, `PRM-05`, reserved for it. So the
design moved on and the rule did not. **That is exactly the shape hard-won law 2
warns about**: had CR-023's screen lane drawn r10's Move button faithfully, it
would have shipped a button wired to a service that refuses.

**Step 3 · THE REAL TENSION, AND IT IS NOT "SHOULD WE ALLOW IT".** The reason
BR-MET-046 gives is *by-premises money traceability*. That reason is sound and
the request is also sound — a clerk typing a unit under the wrong building is an
ordinary, frequent, honest mistake. They are only in conflict if a move is
treated as an **edit**. Two cases behave completely differently:

| Case | What a move means | Traceability cost |
|---|---|---|
| **The unit has never billed** | pure data-entry correction — nothing anywhere refers to it | **none** |
| **The unit has issued bills** | every bill already issued was billed *under the old premises* | **this is what BR-MET-046 protects** |

**Step 4 · THE SHAPE THAT SATISFIES BOTH — recommended, not decided.** A move is
an **EVENT WITH A DATE**, never a rewrite of the `premises_id` column's past:

* the unit's current premises changes from the effective date forward;
* **bills already issued keep pointing at the premises they were billed under** —
  hard rule 4 makes them immutable anyway, so this is not a new principle;
* the move writes an `audit_log` row naming both premises and the reason;
* a unit with issued bills warns, states how many, and takes an override with a
  recorded reason — the same shape the PO already ruled for a refused plan
  assignment: *"show them the exception and allow them to override with reason or
  comment"*.

**⛔ WHAT MUST NOT BE BUILT WITHOUT A RULING:** silently reassigning a unit that
has billed, which would make last month's revenue-by-premises report disagree
with itself between two runs and give no reader a way to know why.

**Step 5 · SIZE.** Small if the event shape is accepted: one service, one
endpoint, one modal, and the two row actions r10 already draws. **The rule must
be AMENDED, dated, with the PO's words** — an inline edit to a CONFIRMED rule is
forbidden; it supersedes with a reason.

Steps 6–8 to follow. **Handed to the CR-023 screen lane**, which is drawing
PRM-02 and PRM-03 as this is written and would otherwise face r10's Move button
with nothing behind it.

## CR-026 · The import must take 50,000–100,000 rows in one file (2026-08-22)

**Step 0 · CAPTURE — the requester's words verbatim:**

> "In Premises and Unit import - the sizes of CSV file scan be 50,000 or 100,000
> units or premises at a time; how you will hnadle such volume in upload"

**Step 1 · CLASSIFY — a SCALE REQUIREMENT on a shipped capability.** Nothing is
wrong at the volumes walked so far; the question names volumes the current
shape was not built for. Not a defect (no promise broken), not fast-path
(stage execution moves off the request cycle — a workflow-shape change).

**Step 2 · WHAT SIGNED STATEMENT IS REVERSED — none.** BR-MET-085 (server-side
rows + hash), BR-MET-090 (idempotent commit), the five-stage law and the
30-day rollback all HOLD unchanged; this changes WHERE stages run, not what
they do.

**Step 3 · WHERE TODAY'S BUILD STRAINS, measured against the shape of the code:**
(1) extract stages one `ImportRunRow` per CSV row in the request — 100k
single-row inserts inside one web request is minutes and a timeout; (2)
transform/validate re-walk every row in ONE request and ONE `select_for_update`
transaction — a minutes-long browser request reads as hung; (3) load writes
everything in one transaction — Postgres-feasible, request-timeout-bound. The
validator already builds its lookup World once per run, so the RULES scale;
the REQUEST SHAPE does not.

**Step 4 · THE PLAN — the five stages stay, they go into the background:**
batched staging and loading (~1,000-row chunks, `bulk_create`/`COPY`); stages
2–4 as Celery jobs (already in the stack) with a progress figure the run row
carries and the stage rail draws ("Validating… 62,000 of 100,000"); the run
table is already the come-back-later surface. Commit/receipt/rollback
semantics unchanged. One judgment to record when built: the per-chunk commit
question on load (all-or-nothing vs resumable), which BR-MET-090's idempotency
already constrains.

**Step 5 · SIZE, in plain English:** about a lane-day; no rule, no money, no
schema change beyond a progress column on `import_runs`.

**Step 3b · MEASURED, not estimated (2026-08-22, 50,000 real rows through the
real stages on live Postgres, rolled back after):** extract **6.8s** ·
transform **77.9s** · validate **50.8s** · dry-run 1.9s · load **101.5s** —
**239s total**. Three stages individually blow a web request timeout, so the
background-job half is confirmed by figures. **First half SHIPPED the same
day:** the three write paths batched (`bulk_create`/`bulk_update`,
1,000-row batches — extract went from minutes to 6.8s), and ⚠ **the cap:
BR-MET-038's CONFIRMED 10,000-row cap silently REFUSED the PO's own file
sizes** — found by step 2's own discipline while implementing; raised to
100,000 (the largest figure the PO named; a cap stays because an unbounded
upload is a DoS door). BR-MET-038's register row amendment queues behind the
master-accounts lane, which holds that file's lock. **Second half (the
background stages + progress) queues as its own lane.**

**Step 0b · SCOPE WIDENED BY THE REQUESTER, same day, verbatim:**

> "this upload size will be at Assets, Accounts, Reads, payments etc"

So the volume bar is EVERY import surface, not the premises/units pair — which
lands on the design already ruled: BR-MET-096's ONE runner, two (soon more)
targets. The background machinery is built ONCE in the runner and every target
inherits it; the legacy single-shot import paths (the reads wizard's batch
POST, the stateless premises pair B15 §7A already schedules for retirement)
migrate onto the runner rather than growing their own volume handling. The
Assets/Accounts/Payments imports arrive as new TARGETS (two dict entries and a
model each, per BR-MET-096's own note) — never as new pipelines.

lanes now running.** ⚠ SUPERSEDED BY THE SECOND-HALF SECTION BELOW — the queue
cleared the same day.

### SECOND HALF · BUILT 2026-08-22 — the three slow stages now run in a worker, and the run says how far it has got

**Step 6 · EXECUTED THROUGH r11.** What landed, and where:

* **The bar: `import_runs.ASYNC_ROW_BAR = 5_000` rows.** A file at or under it is
  **completely untouched** — same call, same synchronous answer, same 200, no job
  record, no gauge row. Over it, stages 2, 3 and 4 are handed to a BE-07 job
  (`metering.import.transform` / `.validate` / `.load`) and the endpoint answers
  **202** with the job id and where to poll (B12 r1 §3).
* **The handler registration** — three `core_jobs.set_job_handler` lines in
  `MeteringConfig.ready()`. It sits beside the enqueue because a kind with no
  registered body does not fail at enqueue; it fails LATER, in a worker, with
  `no handler registered`, on a file nobody is watching. The Celery transport is
  kind-agnostic (`apps/tenancy/tasks.py`), so registration is the whole of the
  worker-side wiring.
* **The gauge: `import_run_progress`, one row per run** (metering 0017, RLS
  ENABLE+FORCE and the B2 §3 policy in the SAME migration as the CREATE).
  Written on a **second, autocommit connection** because every stage holds
  `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on its own `import_runs` row for the whole stage — a
  progress write on that row, or on that connection, could only ever report 0%
  and then 100%. Throttled to one write per 1,000 rows AND per second, so a
  100,000-row stage writes ~100 times against 100 seconds of work.
* **The poll surface: `GET /api/{tenant}/imports/{run_id}`** — the run, its
  counts, its rules, its rejects and `progress` (`stage · done · total · pct ·
  state · message · job_id`) in ONE payload. `progress` is served on **every**
  import answer, `null` for a synchronous run, so no client can be built that
  knows about a run and not about its progress.
* **UNCHANGED, and asserted:** BR-MET-085 (stages 1–3 write nothing), BR-MET-090
  (the run's record is what it DID — the gauge is never read by a receipt), the
  commit/receipt/rollback semantics, and the **30-day** rollback point. Three
  answers are still given on the call the operator made and never by poll: an
  already-loaded run hands back its **same receipt** (hard rule 6), a run that
  never validated is refused, and BR-MET-098's approval bar (**5% or 10 rows**)
  is checked **before** anything is enqueued.

**Step 3b · RE-MEASURED, both sides, on one box, back to back
(`10-scripts/cr026_import_benchmark.py --rows 50000`, 2026-08-22, real stages on
live Postgres, each pass inside one transaction that is rolled back):**

| stage | sync (bar raised) | deferred (through `core.jobs`) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| extract | 4.7s | 4.8s | +0.1s |
| transform | **51.4s** | **52.7s** | +1.3s |
| validate | **34.6s** | **35.1s** | +0.5s |
| dry-run | 1.6s | 2.0s | +0.4s |
| load | **92.1s** | **102.0s** | +9.8s |
| **TOTAL** | **184.4s** | **196.5s** | **+12.1s (+6.6%)** |

**How to read that, because the number that matters is not in the table.** The
work costs **6.6% more** to run through a job — a job record, the handler
lookup, the tenant re-entry and ~50 gauge writes per stage. What it buys is
that **no stage blocks the browser any more**: the operator's wait on *Commit*
goes from **92 seconds staring at a page that may already have timed out** to
about **2 seconds** (the pre-flight dry run BR-MET-098's approval bar requires)
and then a progress bar. ⚠ Two honest caveats on the load's +9.8s: about 2s of
it is that pre-flight dry run, which the sync path pays *inside* its own 92.1s;
and the deferred pass runs second, over the 50,000 dead tuples the first pass's
rollback left behind, so part of the remainder is measurement order rather than
machinery.

**The 5,000-row bar still holds at today's figures.** The ratified justification
(decision log 2026-08-22) was *"at the bar the slowest stage is 5,000 × 2.03 ms
= 10.2s, inside a 30s gateway timeout with 3× margin"*. Today's slowest stage is
the load at **92.1s / 50,000 = 1.84 ms/row**, so the bar costs **9.2s** — the
ruling's own arithmetic, unmoved. `test_the_ratified_async_bar_is_5000_rows`
asserts the figure so drift goes RED.

**Gates:** `pytest tests/test_cr026_background_stages.py` **16 passed** (the
registration PROVED RED first — with the kind unregistered the same record dies
at the worker with `core.jobs.JobsError: no handler registered for job kind
'metering.import.transform'`) · the CR-023/CR-025 import suites **79 passed,
unchanged**, which is the contract that a small file did not move ·
`03-golden-verify.py` **33 PASS / 0 FAIL** · `makemigrations --check` clean ·
migrate-from-empty clean · ruff ✔ black ✔.

**Step 7 · VERSION.** Landed on the branch at **2.33.0**; the tree moved to
**2.34.0** the same afternoon under another lane's CR, and `g35_version_lockstep`

**Step 8 · ROLLBACK, stated before shipping.** Reverting is cheap and was
checked: metering 0017 CREATES a table and touches no existing one, so its
reverse drops a table whose entire contents are a progress bar (nothing audited,
nothing financial reads it). Raise `ASYNC_ROW_BAR` above the row cap and every
stage is synchronous again with no other change. **The one thing that is NOT
reversible by itself:** `import_runs.run_dict` now reads `import_run_progress`
on every import answer, so a deployment that has the CODE and not migration 0017
fails every import with `relation "import_run_progress" does not exist` — found
by running the benchmark against a database that had not migrated. Code and
migration must ship together, which is the ordinary rule and is stated here
because this is the failure it prevents.

### CLOSURE · 2026-08-22 — the screen half, walked in a browser, at **2.35.0**

**Step 6 · EXECUTED THROUGH r11 (the frontend).** What landed, and where:

* **The stage rail draws the SERVER's figures.** `07-frontend/src/features/
  metering/importProgress.tsx` — *"Mapping… 8,000 of 20,000"*, a bar at the
  percentage `import_progress.read` computed, and the state. **Nothing here
  divides `done / total`.** The server computes `pct` for a stated reason
  (*"two clients would otherwise each divide by zero their own way on a 0-row
  file"*), so the screen reads that number and never derives one — BR-MET-085's
  discipline moved from the file hash to the counts. `total: null` draws **no
  bar at all** rather than a width nobody measured.
* **The poll is `GET /imports/{run_id}` every 2s and it stops on the SERVER's
  own terminal state**, never on a poll count or a timeout. A stage that dies
  shows the worker's own message, in the worker's words, and the run does not
  advance.
* **A 202 is no longer read as a result.** `_defer()` answers the run and the
  job and NONE of the stage's output, so each `onSuccess` asks `deferred`
  first. Reading it as a result would have printed a reconcile strip of zeros,
  or *"No rules ran on this file"*, over a run the worker had not begun.
* **The run table is live** (`PremisesImportsTab.tsx`). The gauge is drawn
  **under r10's STATUS pill**, not in a tenth column — r10 draws nine and B15
  §9.8 says copy them rather than tidy them, and the fact belongs to the column
  that is already about where the run has got to. The pill reads *"File read"*
  for the whole of a two-minute load, because `import_runs` writes the new
  status when a stage COMMITS and the stage holds that row locked until then;
  the gauge is the only thing on that screen that can say otherwise.
* **Nineteen strings, in all eleven catalogues, really translated.**

**⚠ WHAT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT RENDER, because it is the regression nobody
reports:** a run under the 5,000-row bar answers `progress: null`, `deferred` is
absent, the panel returns `null` on `null` and **not one poll is issued**. A
three-row file that suddenly grew a progress bar would not be filed as a bug —
the screen would just be trusted a little less. The first case of
`ImportProgress.dom.test.tsx` asserts exactly that, by name.

**BR-MET-102 · THE CANCEL QUESTION, ASKED AND ANSWERED.** The open question this
CR raised — *may an operator cancel a running import?* — went to the PO and the
answer is **"No"**. It is a ruled NON-REQUIREMENT, so the screen draws **no
cancel control and not a disabled one**: `BR-SHL-025`'s *"disabled WITH its
reason"* exists for a control that cannot act YET, and greying out one that is
ruled never to exist invites an operator to wait for it to light up. What the
panel draws instead is the door the ruling points at — *"A run that has started
cannot be stopped. When it finishes, its receipt offers a rollback that
deactivates everything the run loaded — nothing is deleted."* The rollback
WINDOW is not typed into the string: `import_runs.ROLLBACK_DAYS` owns that
number.

**⚠ AND THE WALKTHROUGH FOUND A REAL DEFECT NO GATE COULD (hard-won law 6).**
tsc, eslint, 2,003 vitest cases and every gate were green over a run table that
polled each in-flight run **once** and then went quiet — a 6,000-row import ran
to completion beside a table that never moved. The cause is worth writing down
because it has two halves that look like opposite mistakes: the gauge is **one
row per run, overwritten in place, written per STAGE**, so `progress: null` does
not mean *"never deferred"* — it means *"no stage has deferred YET"* — and
`done` does not mean the run finished, it means one stage did. Stopping on
either loses a run that is still going. **Only the RUN's own status can stop the
poll**, and that is what it does now, bounded by a cap of three candidates.
Three DOM cases pin it, each proved RED first.

> *"premises details view does not match with this - look at button positions -
> look at tabs and details within tabs. lok at header and informationd etails in
> it ; does not match - all should be done using tailwind - why it doe snot
> match"*

> *"Details view of Unit; UI does not match with Prototype; Also in Premises and
> Unit level Audit log does not point to audit log it should audit log on that
> perticular unit or premises"*

**Step 1 · CLASSIFY — a DEFECT report, with ONE rule change inside it.** Three
rows were already filed against the measured evidence before this CR existed:
`DEF-578` (PRM-02 structure), `DEF-579` (the Audit tab), `DEF-580` (PRM-03
content). That is the right classification and the change process says so — *"when
it is ambiguous it is a DEFECT, not a change, because filing our misunderstanding
as a 'change' quietly converts our error into the customer's new requirement"*.
The PO did not ask for anything new; they asked for what r10 already draws.

**The CR exists for the one part that IS a change**, and for one sentence that
must not be re-litigated.

---

### ⚠ THE SENTENCE THAT MUST NOT BE RE-LITIGATED: TAILWIND IS NOT WHY IT DID NOT MATCH

The PO wrote *"all should be done using tailwind - why it doe snot match"* as one
breath, and the two halves are unrelated facts:

* **They are right about the styling.** New UI is written in Tailwind utilities
  and adds no class to a stylesheet — B14 rule 21, Route B, PO 2026-08-19. Both
  detail screens are now handed to `routeBUtilities.test.ts`, which asks the
  STRICTER question (every class token must be declared by a stylesheet *or*
  compile through the real Tailwind compiler); `g31` stays at 0 undeclared and
  its ceiling was never raised.
* **And Tailwind is not the cause of a single thing they photographed.** Every
  divergence was STRUCTURAL: a sixth tab r10 does not draw; an Audit tab that
  rendered a link instead of the entity's rows; a header holding its number,
  address and description in each other's slots; a one-column fact list where
  r10 draws two; a bullet list where r10 draws a table. **Tailwind governs HOW a
  style is written and never WHICH tabs exist or WHERE a button sits.** Writing
  the same six tabs in utilities would have matched nothing.

Both halves are done. The distinction is written here so the next lane reading
*"all should be done using tailwind"* does not conclude that a CSS migration was
the fix, and so nobody re-opens it as one.

---

**Step 2 · WHAT SIGNED STATEMENT IS BEING REVERSED.** One, and it is not frozen.

`BR-MET-045` (CONFIRMED, source **PO PU-16/17/18**) read:

> *"Premises detail (Units/Assets/Accounts/Audit tabs) and Unit detail
> (Overview/Assets/Account history/Plan history/Audit) per PU-16/17; list
> capability row per PU-18"*

PU-16/17 was a PO walkthrough of the **previous design**. r10 draws PRM-02 as
**five** tabs with no `Accounts`, and PRM-03 as **six** with `Audit log`.
CLAUDE.md's standing ruling of 2026-08-16 governs: r10 is THE reference, and
*"where A1–A17's screen description contradicts r10, r10 is right and the spec is
stale"*. **AMENDED, dated, with the PO's sentence quoted, in
`04-docs/05-modules/04-metering/02-business-rules.md`.** No ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5
figure is touched, so this is not a re-sign; no money rule moves.

**AND ONE RULE WAS NOT AMENDED BECAUSE IT WAS ALREADY RIGHT AND WAS NOT OBEYED.**
`BR-AUD-010` (CONFIRMED) reads *"Per-entity Audit tabs … are read-only WINDOWS
into `audit_log` scoped to the entity … owning modules render; every tab links to
S61 pre-filtered ('full log')"*. **Render AND link.** The shipped tab did only the
second half, and the page's own exceptions trailer recorded that as a deliberate
deferral — which is exactly why no gate and no reviewer ever questioned it.
`DEF-579` is therefore a conformance fix against a ratified rule, not a change.

**Step 3 · IMPACT.** Ten surfaces. The tab removal touches the screen, its story's
test cases, the rule, the register and eleven catalogues; it touches **no
endpoint, no schema, no migration and no data**. The demo fixture is unaffected —
`brazosbend` renders both screens correctly and was walked. Open questions move in

(`DEF-583`, `DEF-584`, `DEF-590`–`DEF-595`), every one of them a thing r10 draws

**Step 5 · SIZE, in plain English with a figure.** Three screens' worth of markup

**Step 6 · EXECUTE** through r11 — done, in three commits, one per defect, each

**Step 7 · VERSION — 2.35.2 → 2.35.3.** All four literals together; the screen

**Step 1 · CLASSIFY.** A **CHANGE**, not a defect: Routes & Cycles were built by
CR-006 to the then-current design; the PO has since rebuilt the prototype's route
and cycle surfaces from two design instructions this session produced, and ruled
thirteen open decisions plus a pre-CR grouping-only rule. New requirements, new
screens, and one reversal (bill/due-day placement) — all of it agreed, none of it
our misunderstanding.

**Step 2 · WHAT SIGNED STATEMENT IS BEING REVERSED.** No ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure
is touched — **money never enters these surfaces and this CR hardens that**. The
statements amended:

* `BR-MET-078` (no money on routes/cycles) — **hardened, not reversed**: the PO's
  own words, *"routes and cycles are grouping only - so we will not tag late fees
  , etc"*, and the upgraded prototype states it as product copy on four screens.
* The cycle's schedule vocabulary — the legacy calendar-date columns and the
  current day-of-month generation are both **superseded** by three fields:
  start day · frequency (eight one-word business names) · days to complete.
  The reading window becomes **derived, never stored**.
* `BR-MET-082 Am.1` (membership resolves at run time) — **finally implemented**,
  not changed: ruled long ago, never built; D4 below closes that gap.
* The route's single-service model — **reversed** by D10: a route serves a
  service *set*.

**Step 3–4 · IMPACT AND WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT AND NOW WRONG.** Recorded in full
in the design record `04-docs/02-decisions/17-cr029-routes-cycles-design.md`
(B17): ten surfaces, the dynamism audit, the 14 endpoints, the two open
high-severity defects this closes by construction, and the seven-screen
divergence table where the PO's rulings **supersede the upgraded prototype's own
claims**. No lane is building on these tables today (CR-028 closed).

**Step 5 · SIZE.** Six waves, 28 tasks + the rulings' amendments. Not a fast-path
change: it touches rules, the billing calendar and the schema.

### The rulings — the PO's words, verbatim, 2026-08-23

Received in one message, answering the thirteen open items this session prepared:

> *"G0 - Yes now; SHOTS - provided D1 - yes; D2 - Yes D3 - Confirmed; D4 yes
> member resolve at run time; D5 Rt-001 is good; D6 - not required; D7 Yes -
> please do it; D8 ; what makes a cycle "completed - dont build it; ② which date
> "closes in 4 days" counts to - Next cycle date; ③ what due date a cycle-less
> one-time bill gets - it will be capture at the time of bulk billing - not here;
> ④ its proration denominator (the current guess OVER-CHARGES while it stands). -
> this is not required. D9 - when we configure Cycle we are provideing default
> values; mostly it wil remain as it is but user can over ride them during
> billing ; d10- yes it will be multi service ; D11 - Per premises ; D12 - not
> required; D13 - Cycles are not directlya ssing to accounts it is derived and
> determined at the time of bill run;"*

And the pre-CR ruling that framed the whole design, received earlier in the same
session:

> *"routes and cycles are grouping only - so we will not tag late fees , etc - we
> can capture start day, frequency, monthly, weekly daily, biweekly, once in two
> months , quaterly etc and days to complete it ; give business names to
> frequence - 1 word."*

### What each ruling means in build terms

| # | Ruled | Build consequence |
|---|---|---|
| **G0** | *"Yes now"* | This CR opens; the waves start immediately. |
| **D1** | *"yes"* | **Build the period generator.** Start day + frequency + days-to-complete + first-run date derive the next N windows; the run wizard **offers, never forces**. The writerless `read_schedules` table retires. |
| **D2** | *"Yes"* | **Unify the two cycle column generations.** Every reader (bill-run picker, due-date math, ops Cycles tab, exports) moves to the new fields; legacy calendar columns deprecated then dropped. |
| **D3** | *"Confirmed"* | **Build the sequence surface**: route detail + drag-to-reorder + printable route sheet. `walk_order` gets its first writer since it was created. |
| **D4** | *"yes member resolve at run time"* | **Membership derives live** through the tags (area→routes · premises→units · unit→service & account) at the moment Reads or Billing asks. Stored rows keep only human choices (picked premises, exclusions, walk order) and immutable history (the route stamped on each collected read). Closes both open high-severity defects by construction. |
| **D5** | *"Rt-001 is good"* | **The `RT-001` / `CY-001` grammar is the product's**, everywhere, replacing "Route 1..7" / "SCW-*" / "Cycle 08-A". ⚠ The second half of D5 — whether SET-04's "Areas & sub-areas" list stops duplicating the routes registry — **was not answered and is NOT guessed**: minted as an OQ, and the build keeps today's shape (areas are reference geography; the routes registry owns routes). |
| **D6** | *"not required"* | **Reader/device assignment is OUT of this CR** — even though the upgraded prototype draws it in the wizard, on the landing column and as an inline edit on the detail rail. **The ruling supersedes the screenshots**; the reader surfaces are not built, and the existing `routes.assigned_to` column stays as-is. ⚠ **PARTLY SUPERSEDED 2026-10-24 (PO, MQ-033; decision log of that date):** the reader IS assigned and reassigned on **Reads → cycle → Routes** (`DEF-MET-10591`, `POST /routes/reader`). The Settings surfaces this row names — the wizard field, the SET-05 column, the SET-06D rail edit — stay reader-free. |
| **D7** | *"Yes - please do it"* | Server-side pagination + sorting on both list endpoints, the N+1 derivations batched, seeded routes get real service/area, and the four open cosmetic defect rows close. |
| **D8①** | *"dont build it"* | **"Cycle completed" is not defined and not built.** The dashboard stops claiming it rather than guessing. |
| **D8②** | *"Next cycle date"* | "Closes in 4 days" counts to **the next cycle date**. |
| **D8③** | *"it will be capture at the time of bulk billing - not here"* | A cycle-less one-time bill takes its due date **from the bulk-billing run**, not from any cycle rule. |
| **D8④** | *"this is not required"* | The proration denominator question is **withdrawn** — no rule to build. |
| **D9** | *"when we configure Cycle we are provideing default values; mostly it wil remain as it is but user can over ride them during billing"* | **Bill day and due days STAY ON THE CYCLE as defaults**, and the **run may override them**. ⚠ **This supersedes the upgraded prototype**, whose SET-07.3/07.4 footnotes say *"Bill and due dates belong to the run, not the cycle"* — three screens carry that sentence and it is now wrong; the copy changes to "defaults, overridable at the run". |
| **D10** | *"yes it will be multi service"* | **A route serves a service SET.** Schema change; the single-service column is superseded. |
| **D11** | *"Per premises"* | **Sequence grain is PER PREMISES** — one stop, many meters. The Premises tab's per-unit numbering (0142/0143 on 1408 Elm) is the wrong reading; Cedar Ct's three units sharing 0145 is right. Today's per-unit `walk_order` column is superseded. |
| **D12** | *"not required"* | **The Balance column is dropped** from the route's Accounts tab. Grouping-only wins; the tab stays status-only. **Supersedes the screenshot.** |
| **D13** | *"Cycles are not directlya ssing to accounts it is derived and determined at the time of bill run"* | **No account-level cycle assignment exists.** An account's cycle is derived — account → unit → route → cycle — **at bill-run time** (D4's mechanism, applied). ⚠ **Supersedes the screenshot**: SET-07D.coverage's per-row *"Assign a cycle →"* action is not built; uncovered accounts are shown with what they lack (a route), and the fix is to route them. |

### Where the rulings SUPERSEDE the upgraded prototype — read this before building a screen

The PO's word outranks the screenshots. Four places the new design must NOT be
copied literally:

1. **D6** — no reader/device field in the wizard, no reader column on the
   landing, no inline reader edit on the route detail's Facts rail.
   (Still true of those Settings surfaces. ⚠ 2026-10-24, PO, MQ-033: the
   reader IS assigned on Reads → cycle → Routes — `DEF-MET-10591`.)
2. **D9** — the "bill and due dates belong to the run, not the cycle" footnotes
   (SET-07.3, SET-07.4, SET-07D Facts rail) are **wrong**; the cycle holds them
   as defaults and the run overrides.
3. **D12** — no Balance column on SET-06D.accounts.
4. **D13** — no "Assign a cycle →" row action on SET-07D.coverage.

Everything else in the upgraded prototype is the reference and r10 is history for
these surfaces.

### Step 7 · VERSION

`<release>.<change>.<fix>` — CR-029 opens at **2.40.0**; each wave bumps the fix
digit and the CR closes on the version the screen shows.

### Step 1 · CLASSIFY

**CHANGE**, with three clauses that are DEFECT-LED and are filed as defects in
their own right rather than being absorbed here (§1's rule: filing our own
misunderstanding as a "change" converts our error into the customer's new
requirement).

| Clause | Kind | Why |
|---|---|---|
| The request object, the eight tabs, the four job lists | **CHANGE** | New capability. Nothing says the product should already do this. |
| Customer has no number | **DEFECT** | Every carry-forward, offset and "other accounts" claim in the shipped product rests on an identifier that does not exist. The product does not do what its own rules say. |
| Move-in step 3 shows reads but not the assets at the unit | **DEFECT** | BR-CUS-021 and the S19 contract both assume the clerk can see what is installed. |
| Move-in step 4 shows a plan NAME and one figure, not its rates | **CHANGE** | No signed rule requires the rate detail; it is new. |
| Move-out closes without deciding the shortfall or the unit's occupancy | **DEFECT** | BR-CUS-030 stops dunning at close, so an unrecovered balance goes silent. That is a money-losing behaviour, not a missing feature. |

**Urgency:** raised as design work, not flagged urgent. Explicitly sequenced by
the requester behind nothing — it opens now.

### Step 2 · WHAT IS BEING REVERSED — quoted, never summarised

**Nothing in B4 or B5 is touched.** No money-math rule, no golden figure, no
frozen line. This CR moves no signed arithmetic and needs no finance re-sign.

**What IS reversed, and it is one thing:**

**The Accounts landing's action set**, as shipped since CR-003. Today the header
carries five equal-weight buttons — `Export · ↑ Import CSV · Move-out · Move-in ·
+ New account` — and `+ New account` is the primary. The premise of that layout
is that **work starts by creating an account**. This CR reverses that premise:
work starts by logging a request, and the account is an outcome. `+ New request`
becomes primary; the four jobs move behind a launcher; `Import CSV` leaves the
header for its own tab.

**Supersedes chain:** CR-002 → CR-003 (Settings and shell matched to r10) set the
header shape; this amends it for Accounts only and leaves every other module's
header untouched.

**What is NOT reversed, stated because a lane will assume otherwise:**

* **BR-CUS-018's six-step New Account wizard stands.** It is not replaced by the
  request. A walk-up customer at a vacant unit can still be handled directly.
* **The move-in wizard's FIVE step names stand** — *Find unit · Customer · Start
  & read · Plan & deposit · Review*. Steps 3 and 4 gain content; no step is
  renamed, added or removed. (Requester, verbatim: *"We will keep wizard only."*)
* **The move-out wizard's FOUR step names stand** — *Find account · Date & final
  read · Final bill & deposit · Close-out*. Steps 3 and 4 gain content.
* **BR-CUS-068 stands and is BUILT ON, not reversed.** Master accounts already
  exist as `accounts.kind='master'` (PO 2026-08-22). This CR does not invent an
  account hierarchy; it uses the one that landed.

### Step 5 · SIZE IT AND CONFIRM — in plain English, with a figure

**NOT a fast-path candidate.** It touches rules, money and data.

**What the PO is being asked to confirm, with the figures:**

1. **A customer gets a number.** Today a customer has a name and, if imported, the
   old system's reference. Accounts, premises, units, bills, payments and work
   orders all have numbers; **customers are the only thing in the product that
   does not.** Every deposit carry-forward and every "they owe money on another
   account" check rests on a clerk matching a name. Worked: a returning customer
   holding **$153.50** on a closed account gets it carried across — or does not,
   because nobody found them.
2. **A request is logged before anything else.** One numbered record per
   application, whatever channel it arrived by, holding the documents. Today a
   form and a driving licence sit on a desk until somebody has time, and nobody
   can answer *"how many are waiting?"*
3. **The customer fills in the form, not the clerk's version of it.** Name,
   address, what they need. **The system classifies** it as a new connection or a
   move-in by resolving the address — the applicant is never asked to choose
   between utility terms.
4. **Eight tabs on Accounts**, each a list of open work.
5. **Every wizard can be parked mid-way** with a reason from a fixed list, and
   resumed where it stopped.
6. **A connection can produce many work orders** — water 3, gas 4, solar 3–4,
   storm water 0 — and multi-unit work batches: **25 units produce 7 orders, not
   76.**
7. **A move-out that comes up short forces a decision.** Worked: outstanding
   **$328.70**, deposit and interest **$153.50**, **short by $175.20** — pursue,
   recover from another account, or write off. Today the account closes, dunning
   stops, and the debt goes quiet.

**Size:** the largest CR raised so far. Larger than CR-013 (Plans & Rates).
Delivered in waves — see step 6.

---

### Step 6 · EXECUTE — through r11, in seven waves

Ordered so the cheapest structural work lands first and each wave unlocks the
next. Waves W0–W2 are data-model changes and are **cheaper before production
data than after**.

| Wave | What | Why here |
|---|---|---|
| **W0** | `customers.customer_no` + the `customer` number series | Every identity claim depends on it. One catalog row, one migration. |
| **W1** | `premises.owner_customer_id` beside the free-text owner | Unlocks the connection invoice, the between-tenants question and the shortfall option, all at once. |
| **W2** | Contacts re-homed from account to customer | Makes identity matching work and makes "one edit updates all their accounts" true. |
| **W3** | The service request — object, lifecycle, list, detail, application form, processing wizard | The front door. Every wizard behind it gets shorter. |
| **W4** | The eight tabs, the revised Accounts landing, and the four job lists | The shell the rest hangs on. |
| **W5** | Move-in and move-out widened; park and resume on every wizard | Amends what is built rather than replacing it. |
| **W6** | New Connect — 8 steps, the connection record, work orders, service characteristics | The largest single build. Needs W0, W1 and W3 in place. |
| **W7** | Transfer, then Disconnect and reconnect | Transfer is mostly stitching. Disconnect needs its protections gate and its notice wording. |

**Out of scope, stated so it is not assumed:**
* The customer portal — the request must be clerk-raiseable without it.
* Work-order scheduling, dispatch, crews and the map — R5, per OQ-249.
* The outbound delivery adapter — a prerequisite this CR names but does not build.
* Add-a-service — designed, deliberately deferred to its own CR.

---

### Step 7 · VERSION

Each wave bumps `<change>` under CR-030 and moves **both** literals in one commit
(`07-frontend/package.json` and `06-backend/pyproject.toml`), which have agreed at
**2.40.3** since CR-018 Phase 2b. W0 opens at **`2.41.0`**. The closing wave
carries the CR's own row and the version it landed in.

---

### Step 8 · CLOSE — and the rollback, stated before shipping

**The closure bar (§8, PO 2026-08-18):** a person performs the task in a browser
against a booted stack. For CR-030 that means, per wave: log a request from the
customer form and process it through to an approved decision · open a New Connect
from an approved request and follow the link chain back · park a move-in at step 3
and resume it · settle a move-out that comes up short. **A green suite is not a
closure.**

**Rollback, per wave:**
* W0–W2 are additive migrations — a customer number, an FK, a re-home. Reversible
  by migration; no data is destroyed.
* W3–W7 are new tables and new screens. Rollback is a feature flag on the tab
  strip: the eight tabs collapse to `Accounts │ Imports` and the existing wizards
  are reached exactly as they are today.
* **The one irreversible thing is the contacts re-home (W2)** — plan it as
  copy-then-cut with both readable during the overlap, not a move.
