## CR-031 · The service request is a CLERK-DECIDED front door, and it hands off to move-in or new-connect

**Arrived** 2026-08-24, in the working session, mid-W2. **Requester:** Product Owner.
**Classification:** CHANGE (a new requirement, and — see §4 — a **reversal of an
unratified proposal in B18 §5.3**, caught at arrival rather than after the build).
**Urgency:** not stated. Screenshots promised: *"I will provide update dscreenshots
for Request and new connect workflows"* — so this CR is **OPEN pending those**, and
nothing in W4 should be built from this text alone.

### 0 · The requester's words, verbatim and unedited

> Please keep these notes on service request - we wil take a service request ={
> Consumer name, address, documents services etc} and issue SR #; then Utility
> clark will review all documents , details, verify address etc and then take a
> decision ={MOve -in , New connec or refusal} - also confirm all communcation to
> be sent as part of SR. If it is refusal then it close here; if it is move in
> then move in request with basica details are created and all documents are
> transfer to move in request; if it is new connect then new conenct request is
> created with basic details; we need to figure out how to link Sr and these next
> stage request; all these request can happen in 1 go or dur to pratical cases
> only step will be executed in such case we have to give save and exit opition t
> utility clark. I will provide update dscreenshots for Request and new connect
> workflows

### 1 · What it says, structured — the burden of structuring is ours

| # | Statement | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | A service request captures **consumer name, address, documents, services** and is issued an **SR #** | capture |
| 2 | A **utility clerk reviews** the documents and details and **verifies the address** | process |
| 3 | The **clerk decides**: **move-in · new connect · refusal** | ⚠ decision authority |
| 4 | **All communication is sent as part of the SR** | ⚠ see §3, ambiguous |
| 5 | **Refusal closes the SR** — it ends there | lifecycle |
| 6 | **Move-in** → a move-in request is created with basic details, and **all documents transfer to it** | hand-off |
| 7 | **New connect** → a new-connect request is created with basic details | hand-off |
| 8 | **How the SR links to the downstream request is UNDECIDED** — *"we need to figure out"* | open, handed to us |
| 9 | The whole chain may run **in one go**, or one step at a time — so the clerk gets **SAVE AND EXIT** | ⚠ practicality requirement |

### 2 · What is already built that this touches

Nothing. The request object does not exist: no `service_requests` table, no
lifecycle, no screen. W4 is where it lands, and W4 has not started. **This CR is
therefore cheap right now and expensive in three waves' time** — which is the
argument for settling §3 and §4 before W4 is packeted.

### 3 · The one ambiguity, surfaced rather than resolved

*"also confirm all communcation to be sent as part of SR"* reads two ways:

* **(a) an instruction** — every notice, email and letter about this application
  is recorded against the SR, so the SR is the communication record; or
* **(b) a question to us** — *"confirm that all communication will be sent as part
  of the SR"*.

They are not the same: (a) is a requirement with a table behind it, (b) is a
confirmation. **The change process is explicit that an ambiguity is not resolved by
guessing** — and it matters more than usual here, because if communication belongs
to the SR and the SR closes at hand-off, then a notice sent during the *move-in*
still has to find its way back. Put to the requester with the screenshots.

### 4 · ⚠ WHAT SIGNED STATEMENT THIS REVERSES — the reason this was worth catching at arrival

**B18 §6.4 proposes BR-CUS-071:**

> **The system classifies**, by address resolution: vacant unit → move-in ·
> nothing → new connection · live account → refused

**The requester has now said the CLERK decides**, after reviewing documents and
verifying the address. Those are different products: one is an automatic
classifier the clerk may override, the other is a human decision the system may
*advise*. They imply different screens, a different lifecycle, and a different
audit story about who is accountable for the outcome.

✅ **BR-CUS-071 is `NEW` — a proposal in a design document stamped DRAFT FOR PO
REVIEW, and it is NOT in `04-docs/05-modules/03-customers/02-business-rules.md`.**
So this is **not** a reversal of a signed rule and needs no re-sign: it is the PO
ruling on a proposal before it was ratified, which is the process working. It IS
recorded here so that nobody builds §6.4's classifier from the design document
without reading this CR first. **BR-CUS-069, 070, 072, 073 and 074 are unaffected**
— numbering at submission, the immutable `address_as_given`, keeping refused
requests, documents carrying over (statement 6 above *strengthens* it), and
threshold-checked approval all stand.

### 5 · The linking question (statement 8), with a proposal rather than a shrug

The requester handed this to us explicitly. The shape that fits the rules already
in this repo:

* the downstream request carries **`origin_service_request_id`** — the SR is the
  parent and the child points at it, so one SR can only ever produce one live
  child per decision, and the child is never orphaned;
* the SR keeps **`outcome`** (`move_in` · `new_connect` · `refused`) and
  **`outcome_ref`**, so the SR alone answers *"what happened to this application"*
  without scanning two other tables;
* documents **move by reference, not by copy** (BR-CUS-073's *"carry over… and are
  not re-uploaded"*), so one uploaded file is one row and the audit trail of who
  supplied it survives the hand-off;
* **SAVE AND EXIT is a `draft` state on the CHILD**, not a fourth outcome on the
  SR — the SR is decided the moment the clerk decides; the child being unfinished
  is the child's business. This is what makes *"all in one go"* and *"one step at a
  time"* the same code path rather than two.

**Not built, not decided — a proposal for the requester to rule on with the
screenshots.**

### 6 · Impact

Screens S83/S84/S85 (+ the four unnumbered ones, decision D1) · the six W4 tables ·
BR-CUS-069…074 · the W4 task list (§11, 17 tasks) · journey J26 · the demo fixture ·
**OQ-351** (which documents are mandatory) is now load-bearing, because the clerk's
review is the gate. **Waves W5 and W6 depend on W4 and are not yet started, so
nothing is being built on the old assumption right now.**

### 7 · Status

**OPEN — awaiting the promised screenshots and a ruling on §3 and §5.** No code, no
tables, no stories. Recorded at arrival per the change process, verbatim, so the
next agent reads the requirement and not a summary of it.


### CR-031 · AMENDMENT 1 — five points from the PO, 2026-08-24

Raised in the working session after the REQ-01/02/03 screenshots. **Verbatim, unedited:**

> Pleas note -  also what if billing clark wants to make changes to application
> correct name or add documents etc - currenlty it does not allow to make anyc
> ahnges to applcaition, Plus what if theyw ant to keep anote on the request. -
> how you will ahndel these changes ; also it is not necessary request will be
> approve in 1 go; hence save and exit option should be given; billing clark
> should allow to add one or more fees from drop down and then forn the how much
> fees to be collected + option to ask for payment now or later; how you will
> ahndle this; Select utility services - we will allow only utility services that
> are actiavted for that Utility/tenant

#### The five points, and where each stands

| # | The point | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Edit the application** — correct a name, add documents | ✅ **Already drawn in REQ-02**, which the PO may not have seen when writing this: the Applicant panel and the Location panel each carry an `Edit` control, the review step carries `Edit step 1…5`, and the Documents tab has `Attach another` — *"Anything the applicant sends later"*. So the capability is specified; what is NOT specified is what an edit does to a SUBMITTED request (see below). |
| 2 | **Keep a note on the request** | ✅ **Already drawn** — the History tab's `Add a note`, badged **`Internal · never shown to the customer`**, with a note-type dropdown, landing on a combined `History and notes` timeline beside the `System` rows. |
| 3 | **Save and exit** — not approved in one go | ✅ **Already drawn, and as TWO controls**: `Save & exit` leaves quietly; **`Park — waiting on`** records what is awaited, a note, and a `Remind me on` date, and surfaces on the list's `WAITING ON` column. Already ruled once, as CR-031 statement 9. |
| 4 | **Add one or more fees from a dropdown, total them, and choose pay-now or pay-later** | ✅ **Already drawn in REQ-03.5** — `Choose a fee…` + `+ Add to the list`, a running total, and `When is it being paid?` offering **`Collect now`** (Card · Cash · Cheque · Waive with a reason) or **`Collect later`** (invoice, `Due by`, and the unpaid fee listed as a blocking condition at review). ⛔ **BUT see DEF-637** — the capture totals $130.00 and the detail and receipt both show $25.00. |
| 5 | **Only services ACTIVATED for that tenant may be selected** | ⛔ **NEW, and the prototype contradicts it — see DEF-640.** |

#### ⚠ What points 1 and 2 leave genuinely unruled

The controls are drawn. What they MEAN is not, and it matters more than it looks:

* **An edit after submission changes the thing a decision was made on.** BR-CUS-070
  already rules that `address_as_given` is immutable after submission and the
  resolution writes BESIDE it, never over it. Nothing rules the equivalent for the
  applicant's NAME, and the customer match is made on identity plus date of birth —
  so editing a name after a `strong` match could silently invalidate the match that
  authorised moving a **$153.50** deposit.
* **Adding a document after verification** re-opens the approval gate: REQ-02 says
  *"Approval is blocked until somebody checks each one"* and `2 of 3 verified`.
  Attaching a fourth must return the request to `waiting on documents`; nothing says so.
* **A note is internal and never shown to the customer** — drawn on the badge — so
  it is NOT the acknowledgement channel of BR-CUS-079. Two different things that
  both look like "communication on the request".

**Proposed, not decided:** an edit to a SUBMITTED request is an append — the prior
value is kept and the change lands on the History timeline as a `System` row with
its actor, exactly as `Document attached — plot/parcel deed, verified` already
does. That makes edits auditable without a second table, and it is the same
posture hard rule 4 takes on money. **Put to the PO before W4 builds it.**

## CR-032 · "INSTEAD OF ENERGISE CAN WE USE ACTIVATED" — ONE WORD, TEN SERVICES (2026-08-25)

**0 · CAPTURED AT ARRIVAL, IN THE REQUESTER'S WORDS.** PO, 2026-08-25, verbatim:

> *"instead of energise can we use activated"*

It arrived inside an answer about `OQ-368`, alongside *"I didnot udnerstand what
did you ask me"* — so **two separate things arrived in one sentence** and they are
handled separately: the terminology is this CR; the misunderstood question is
`OQ-368`, which stays OPEN and is **re-put in plain English**, because a question
the requester could not read is our failure to ask it, not their failure to answer.

**1 · CLASSIFY — a CHANGE, and a small one.** Not a defect: nothing is broken and
nobody misunderstood a requirement. It is a **vocabulary change to a state token
and its user-facing copy**, requested by the PO.

**2 · WHAT SIGNED STATEMENT IS BEING REVERSED — none.** `energised` was never put
to the PO and never ruled on. It entered the repo through the r10 prototype's own
copy (`NCT-01`'s *"Partly energised"*, the History tab's *"Electric energised —
gate WO-4904 passed"*) and `connections.py` took it from the screens. **No ❄️
FROZEN B4/B5 figure is touched, so no re-sign is required.** `BR-MET-110` uses the
phrase *"service goes live"* in its own text, which is already the neutral wording.

**3 · WHY THE PO IS RIGHT, STATED SO IT IS NOT LOST.** *Energise* is **electric
jargon**. The platform seeds **ten services** and only Electric, Solar and Battery
are energised in any literal sense — **water is turned on, gas is lit, broadband is
provisioned, trash is scheduled, sewer is connected.** A single state token has to
cover all ten, and *activated* is the only one of the two that is true of every
service. The rule that names it, `BR-MET-110`, already avoids the word.

**4 · IMPACT — measured, not estimated.**

| Surface | Count | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Backend `.py` | **3 files**, 88 occurrences | Almost all in `connections.py` docstrings; the tokens are `ENERGISED`, `PARTLY_ENERGISED`, `SVC_ENERGISED` |
| DB columns | **2** — `connections.energised_at`, `connection_services.energised_at` | Needs a `RenameField` migration |
| DB CHECK constraints | **0** | The token is not in a constraint (migration `0026` verified) — so no constraint rewrite |
| Locale catalogues | **1 key × 11 languages** | |
| Docs `.md` | **5 files** | B18 §5.4.x, the metering rules, the module docs |
| Rows already written | **0** | Nothing has shipped; no tenant holds a connection |

**5 · SIZE — FAST PATH.** It touches **no signed rule, no money and no data
already written**, which is exactly what the change process's fast path is for.
⚠ It is NOT zero-risk, and the one risk is named: the state token is stored on
`connections.state`, so the rename must be a **migration**, not a find-and-replace,
or a fresh database and an existing one disagree about a value silently.

**6 · EXECUTE — through r11, unchanged.** Backend tokens + `RenameField` migration ·
locale key · the drawn copy in B18 · a test asserting no `energis` string survives
in the shipped tokens, proved RED before it is trusted.

**7 · VERSION.** A `<release>.<change>.<fix>` bump on the change digit.

**8 · ROLLBACK, stated before shipping:** the reverse `RenameField` and the reverse
string swap. No data is lost either way, because no row exists to lose.

**STATUS: ✅ DONE — shipped in `2.46.0`, 2026-08-25.**

**What actually landed**, against the impact table above:

| Surface | Predicted | Landed |
|---|---|---|
| Backend tokens | 3 files | `connections.py` — `ACTIVATED`, `PARTLY_ACTIVATED`, `SVC_ACTIVATED`; the old names are GONE, not aliased, and a test asserts `not hasattr(w6, "ENERGISED")` because a "harmless" compat alias is exactly how a renamed token comes back |
| DB columns | 2 | `RenameField` ×2 in `metering/0027_cr030_w6_rulings.py` |
| DB CHECK constraints | 0 | 0, as verified |
| Stored VALUES | *(not in the original table — the omission that mattered)* | `RunPython(forwards_states, backwards_states)` over an explicit `old → new` map. **Explicit because a naive `replace("energised","activated")` produces `partly_activated` BY LUCK** and would corrupt any value where the old word is a substring |

## CR-033 · "APPLY AS" SHOULD OFFER THE CUSTOMER CATEGORIES FROM SETTINGS (2026-08-25)

**0 · CAPTURED AT ARRIVAL, IN THE REQUESTER'S WORDS.** PO, 2026-08-25, looking at
`/requests/new` step 1 on **v2.46.0**:

> *"on this screen - apply as - we need customer categories that we have from
> settings - ehre as drop down"*

**1 · CLASSIFY — a CHANGE.** Nothing is broken; the control does what it was built
to do. The PO wants a different control in that position.

**2 · WHAT IS BEING CHANGED.** Step 1 draws **`Applying as`** as a two-way
segmented control — **`A person` · `A business`** — backed by
`APPLICANT_KINDS = ["person", "business"]`, a hardcoded pair in
`serviceRequestEndpoints.ts` and `models.py`. The PO wants the **customer
categories** there instead, as a dropdown, read from **Settings**.

**3 · THE IMPORTANT FINDING: THE CATEGORY ALREADY EXISTS, AND IT IS A SEPARATE,
LATER STEP.** `account_types` is the platform customer-category catalogue (B2 r5
#12 [D5], migration 0003), it is what Settings shows, and
`service_request_service.set_customer_category(...)` already attaches one to a
request. The PO created a request and the category was never asked for.

⛔ **CORRECTION, 2026-08-25 — THIS SECTION ORIGINALLY SAID THAT IS WHY THE LIST
READS `NOT YET CLASSIFIED`, AND THAT WAS WRONG.** The lane building this change
checked the read path instead of trusting the CR, and found: `NOT YET CLASSIFIED`
is the **TYPE** column, and it is not the customer category at all.
`service_request_reads.list_row` serves `"type": request.outcome if
request.outcome in _SR.JOB_OUTCOMES` with a `type_absence` of
`not_yet_classified` — **that is the JOB the request becomes**
(`new_connection · move_in · move_out · transfer · disconnect`), decided by a
clerk at review. `set_customer_category` writes `account_type` /
`account_subtype` and **never touches `outcome`**.

**So asking the category at capture will NOT clear the badge on `SR-26-0001` or
on any new request.** The change is still right — it stops every request arriving
uncategorised, and `BR-MET-111` already assumes a request carries a category —
but **the badge needs its own fix**, and anyone reading this CR expecting the two
to be connected would have been misled. The wrong sentence is left above with
this correction under it rather than deleted, because the next reader needs to
know the claim was made and withdrawn. ⚠ **The lesson is the general one: a CR is
written from a reading of the code, and a reading is not the code.** The lane
that disagreed with its own brief is what caught it.

So the ask is not *"swap a control"*. It is: **ask for the category at capture,
where the person filling the form already knows the answer**, instead of leaving
every new request unclassified for someone else to come back to.

✅ **AND A SIGNED RULE ALREADY WANTED THIS.** `BR-MET-111` (2026-08-25) says the
owner captured on a New Connect is classified *"from **the same set the service
request uses**, so a request and a build classify alike"*. That sentence assumes
the request carries a category. Today it can, and usually does not.

**4 · WHAT `applicant_kind` IS FOR, BECAUSE IT MUST NOT BE DROPPED BY ACCIDENT.**
It is stored on `service_requests`, validated against its pair, and read back as
`person_or_company`. It is **not** the same fact as the category: a *residential*
account can be held by *a business* (a landlord), and a sole trader is *a person*
on a *commercial* account. **Two facts, and collapsing them would lose one.**

**5 · SIZE — small, and it touches no money and no signed figure.** One dropdown
sourced from an existing catalogue, one payload field already accepted by the
backend's `classify` path, one seed/fixture pass.

⚠ **SUPERSEDED THE SAME DAY BY THE PO'S SECOND SENTENCE.** This section said the
category dropdown would go in the position pointed at and `A person / A business`
would be **kept below it**. The PO then sent the **New Account** step 1 (`ACC-03`)
and said *"why don you make request staep 1 simialr to this one -"*. **ACC-03 has
no person/business control at all**, so mirroring it means the toggle goes.

**It is removed from the FORM only.** `applicant_kind` stays in the database, in
`CAPTURE_FIELDS`, in the server validation and in `APPLICANT_KINDS` — nothing is
deleted, and **nothing derives it from the category**, because §4 above is right
that they are two facts and a derivation would be an invention.

⚠ **ONE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PO TO RULE ON, and it is one line of copy.**
`ServiceRequestDetailPage` renders a null `person_or_company` as **"Not
supplied"**. On requests captured from today that reads as *the applicant did not
give one*, when the truth is *we stopped asking*. Those are different statements
and hard-won law 1 says the screen must not make the first one. Until it is
ruled, the detail page must state the second.

⚠ **AND THE PO SAID "drop down" WHILE ACC-03 USES A SEGMENTED CONTROL.** The
second sentence — *"similar to this one"* — is taken as the governing one, so a
segmented control is what shipped. If the word was meant literally it is a
one-component swap.

**6 · EXECUTE** through r11 · **7 · VERSION** on the change digit · **8 ·
ROLLBACK:** restore the segmented control; no data is lost either way, because
the category column already exists and an unset category is the state every
request is in today.

**STATUS: ✅ DONE — shipped in `2.47.0`, commit `555feb2d`.** ⚠ This line read **CAPTURED** until 2026-08-26, a day after the work landed — the exact staleness the change process's step 0 exists to catch. `Applying as` (`A person · A business`) is REPLACED by the customer-category field on `/requests/new` step 1, the step's `validate` moved with it so a request cannot leave step 1 uncategorised, and DEF-684 (2026-08-26) then made every OTHER screen read the same platform catalogue instead of a hardcoded four. ⛔ **What this CR got WRONG survives in the code's own docstring and is NOT quietly dropped:** §3 says the list's `NOT YET CLASSIFIED` badge is there because the category was never asked for. It is not — that badge is the JOB the request becomes (`new_connection · move_in · move_out · transfer · disconnect`), a clerk's decision at review, and asking for the category does not clear it.

## DEF-664 · ESCALATED BY THE PO ON A LIVE BUILD (2026-08-25)

Not a new change — a defect already on the register, now **reported from
production** on **v2.46.0**:

> *"When I click on service request nothing is shoing, but I ahve created one
> request - it shows up on another scren"*

**Accounts → Requests** renders a panel saying the list *"is still to come"* with a
button to `/requests`, where `SR-26-0001` is sitting. The panel is **true** and it
is still the wrong thing to show somebody who has just created a request.

⚠ **THE STATED BLOCKER WAS REAL AND IS NOW SOLVED THE OTHER WAY ROUND.** DEF-664
says embedding is not a one-line job because `ServiceRequestsListPage` and
`AccountsListPage` **both serialise their table state into the same query
string**, so nesting them has each one's `?page=`/`?sort=` overwrite the other's —
and that namespacing is URL grammar, BR-SHL-011's to settle, not a lane's.
**That is still true, and the embed does not need it:** the embedded copy does not
own the URL. It keeps its table state in component state and leaves the query
string entirely to the page it sits inside. **No URL grammar is decided, and the
standalone screen at `/requests` keeps its shareable links unchanged.**

## CR-034 — the Plan tab should UNFOLD what actually applies to this unit

**Arrived** 2026-08-25, from the PO on the live build (`v2.47.0`), looking at
`PRM-03` → Plan for `SCW-U-001 · Unit 1`.

**Requester's words, verbatim:**
> *"this is all good; so when i view the unit - in plan section, you are showing
> ; we are unable to see this unfold - it might be dynamic so when i go on this
> screen it should show me what all details from plan are applicable"*

…quoting back the R1–R7 worked example they had just been shown (plan version
in force · one rate schedule per service · the size row · the meter multiplier
on the quantity · charge codes · the premises factor · discounts · taxes).

**1 · CLASSIFY.** A **CHANGE**, not a defect: the screen does what it was
specified to do — B18/PRM-03 asks for the plan, its effective date and its rate
schedules, and all three render correctly. The PO is asking for MORE than was
specified, having seen what the engine can narrow.

**2 · WHAT SIGNED STATEMENT IS REVERSED.** None. No ❄️ B4/B5 figure is touched
and nothing here changes a price — this is a READ of decisions already made.

**3 · WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT — and this is the finding.** ⚠ **The unfold mostly
EXISTS and this screen does not call it.** `GET /units/{id}/pricing` is mounted
(`apps/metering/api.py:1351`), `selectors.unit_pricing` serves *"plan, rate
schedules with blocks, charge codes, taxes"*, and
`07-frontend/src/features/customers/UnitPricingPanel.tsx` (707 lines) already
RENDERS it — **for the Move-in wizard only.** `UnitDetailPage.tsx`'s Plan tab
never mounts it. Hard-won law 2 in its third shape: not built-and-unwired, but
**built, wired somewhere else, and absent from the screen that needs it.**

**4 · WHAT IS GENUINELY NOT BUILT.** The **worked month** — the priced example
with the multiplier, the outside-city factor, the discount and the taxes as
NUMBERS. `unit_pricing` says so in its own payload and the reason is structural:
**no callable prices a plan outside a bill run.** `engine.price_bill` and
`price_period` are pure functions fed by `billing/gather.py`, which is keyed on
an ACCOUNT and a service period. Serving a worked month here means building an
assembly that takes a UNIT and a hypothetical period — a real story, and the
place a second implementation of billing math would be born if anyone rushed
it. **Every figure the panel shows today is a STORED value forwarded verbatim;
it performs no arithmetic, and that must survive this change.**

**5 · SIZE.** Two slices, and they should not be one commit:
  * **(a) mount the existing panel on the Plan tab** — small, no new math, no
    new endpoint. This is the bulk of what was asked for.
  * **(b) the worked month** — its own story, needs a unit-and-period pricing
    assembly, and touches ❄️ frozen math. Not started; not to be guessed at.

**Also visible on the same screenshot, already honest and unchanged by this CR:**
*"Nothing checks a plan's eligibility rules yet"* and *"no endpoint reads
[plan history] back yet"* — two stated absences that stay stated.

**Status:** (a) ✅ **DONE** `edbbc8e3` · (b) ✅ **DONE 2026-08-26, version `2.49.0`** — the re-scope below is what shipped; the close-out is at the end of this entry.

### ⚠ SLICE (b) WAS RE-SCOPED BY THE PO ON 2026-08-25, AND THE RE-SCOPE DISSOLVES THE BLOCKER

Slice (b) was written up above as *"the worked month"* — the priced example with
the multiplier, the city factor, the discount and the taxes **as computed
numbers**. That framing was mine, and it made the slice expensive for one
reason: **no callable prices a plan outside a bill run**, so serving it meant
building a unit-and-hypothetical-period assembly beside ❄️ FROZEN math — the
place a second implementation of billing math gets born.

**The PO removed the problem rather than paying for it.** Verbatim:

> *"this can be resolved by showing in - what period youa re reporting data for
> and you can point exact details for plan name, utility services on unit, rates
> scheudle for those services, minimum charges, charge code, discounts, taxes,
> contract ( you cna have placehodler) - thse will be sections and you can have
> real values for all these"*

**So slice (b) is a RESOLUTION DISPLAY, not a priced bill:** *"for this period,
here is exactly what applies to this unit"*, in sections, each carrying real
resolved values. **Nothing is computed.** That is the posture
`selectors.unit_pricing` already takes — stored values forwarded verbatim —
extended to the sections it does not yet cover.

**Why this is the better answer and not merely the cheaper one:** a computed
worked month needs a **consumption figure**, and for a hypothetical period there
isn't one. Any number chosen would have been an invention presented in the shape
of a bill — and a figure that *looks* like what the customer will pay, but is
built on a guessed quantity, is worse than no figure at all. The re-scope means
every value on the screen is one the product actually holds.

**The sections, in the PO's own order:**

| # | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **The period being reported for** | Stated at the top. **This is the load-bearing one** — R1 turns on *the plan version in force on the service date*, so the period is what makes everything below unambiguous rather than decorative. Change the period, and the answer must change with it. |
| 2 | Plan name and version | |
| 3 | Utility services on this unit | |
| 4 | Rate schedule per service | |
| 5 | Minimum charges | |
| 6 | Charge codes | |
| 7 | Discounts | ⚠ `resolve_discounts` distinguishes *"cannot express"* from *"has none"*; those must not render the same |
| 8 | Taxes | |
| 9 | **Contract** | **A placeholder is explicitly authorised by the PO.** Label it as not built; do not invent a contract model. |

**Still binding, unchanged:** no second implementation of billing math; golden
**33/33** before and after; never fabricate a value — `null` with its reason
where the chain cannot answer; money 4dp stored / 6dp percentages / DISPLAY 2;
the endpoint is a READ and writes nothing.

**Now genuinely in scope, and was not before:** the **period selector** itself,
and sections **5, 7 and 9**. Several of those may already be served and simply
not rendered — that has been the pattern on this screen all day, and slice (a)
was exactly that.

### CR-034 (b) · CLOSED 2026-08-26 — WHAT SHIPPED (version `2.49.0`)

The re-scope was right about the pattern: **five of the nine sections were
already stored and served, and simply not rendered.** Every figure on the screen
is a stored value forwarded verbatim from rating's own selectors — no sum, no
rounding, no proration, no tax. Golden **33/33** before and after, `pytest -m
golden` 23 passed / 1 xfailed both times.

| § | What shipped | Where it came from |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The period, and `as_of` = its END date | BR-RAT-007 — *"the plan version in force on the SERVICE-PERIOD END DATE"* |
| 2 | The plan, **plus every plan STRETCH inside the period** and the dates a bill would split on | BR-RAT-114 / DEF-504, through the existing `rating.selectors.unit_plan_assignments_in` |
| 3 | Services and their base charges | already served, already rendered |
| 4 | The rate schedule per service, **resolved on the service date** | `schedule_card` has accepted a date since it was written; `schedule_detail` never passed one — one argument |
| 5 | **Minimum charges** — the plan's, the plan-service line's and the schedule version's | all three were already in the payload and none was rendered as a section |
| 6 | Charge codes **with the code's own amount** | `plan_detail`'s projection carried `amount_override` and nothing else |
| 7 | **Discounts the plan OFFERS**; the GRANT is a stated absence | BR-RAT-069 — a plan binding grants a discount to nobody |
| 8 | Taxes, **and that they are not the final set** | DEF-273 — the set narrows again by the account's customer class |
| 9 | **Contract** — a stated absence citing `CR-020` | see below |

**§7 got the distinction the CR asked for, in its stronger form.** The CR warned
that *"cannot express"* and *"has none"* must not render the same. On a UNIT the
live distinction is a third one: **OFFERED is not GRANTED.** The grant needs an
enrolment, an enrolment belongs to an ACCOUNT, and a unit has none — so
`discounts.granted` is `{served:false, reason:"unit_has_no_account"}` and never
`[]`. Rating's `enrolled` count is **dropped rather than captioned**, because it
is tenant-wide and a number on a unit screen is read as that unit's however it
is worded.

**Three judgments, each in the decision log (2026-08-26) with its worked case:**
no period is invented when the caller states none · a mid-period plan change is
reported and never collapsed · which minimum FLOOR wins is not decided by a read.

**⚠ THE CONTRACT SECTION FOUND ITS OWN ROW, AND IT IS `CR-020` ABOVE.** The lane
was about to report that an open question was owed for *"what is a contract
here"*. **It is not owed** — the PO captured contracts-on-plans as CR-020 on
2026-08-20 and HELD it on 2026-08-21 (*"hold on dont proceed"*), and
`apps/rating/selectors.py` already states the same fact one module over
(*"CR-020, deferred by the PO"*). Minting an OQ beside a live CR would have been
one question under two ids — OQ-197's failure from the other direction.

**A tension for the PO rather than a bug:** this CR's section list asks the
screen for contracts, and CR-020 is the row that says contracts are paused. The
screen therefore says the work is *written down and paused* rather than drawing
an *arrives-with a later story* box over work the requester stopped.

**`OQ-363` IS UNTOUCHED AND STAYS OPEN.** The worked month is still not served,
the panel still says so, and neither of its two blockers moved.

### ⚠ AMENDED 2026-08-26 — SECTION 7 (DISCOUNTS) IS SPECIFIED, AND IT IS MORE THAN WAS BUILT

CR-034's section list said *"discounts"*. The PO has now said what that means:

> *"We should show all discount plan offer and what condition are required to
> avail that discount ; when account is attached it will avail those discounts"*

**Three requirements, and the second is the new one:**

1. **ALL discounts the plan offers** — not just the ones a reader might guess at.
2. **THE CONDITIONS required to avail each one.** This is the addition. What was
   built shows *that* a senior discount is offered at **10.00%**; it does not
   show what a customer must satisfy to get it.
3. **When an account is attached, it avails those discounts** — so the screen is
   read as a statement about what WILL apply once there is an account, not a
   list of things that merely exist.

**What is already stored, checked rather than assumed** (`apps/rating/discounts.py`):
`cap_per_bill` · `cap_per_year` · `cap_lifetime` · `bill_floor_amount` (default
`0.000000`, and the docstring is explicit that a discount may take a bill to
zero but never below, because a negative bill is a CREDIT — a different object
with a different ledger posting) · `stack_order` (**data, not code order**, and
Silver Creek runs SENIOR, CAP, PAPERLESS and AUTOPAY on the same accounts) ·
`applies_to` / `applies_to_service` / `applies_to_charge_codes` ·
`DiscountEnrolmentDocument`, so **required proof is modelled**.

**So this is largely a RENDERING gap, which is the pattern this whole CR has
followed.** The one thing to establish before building: whether the eligibility
CONDITIONS a customer must meet are stored anywhere a screen can read, or only
as `rate_plans.eligibility` — which `US-RAT-002 §5` marks **ADVISORY ONLY,
never gates assignment**, and which the live build already reports honestly as
*"Nothing checks a plan's eligibility rules yet."* ⚠ **Advisory text is not a
condition, and rendering it as one would tell a clerk the product enforces
something it does not.** If that is the only source, the conditions section
states what it can and names the gap.

**Still binding, unchanged:** nothing is computed; the GRANT still cannot be
answered without an account (`resolve_discounts`' `modelled: False` precedent
distinguishes *cannot express* from *has none*); the tenant-wide `enrolled`
count stays off a unit screen.

**Status:** ✅ **DONE 2026-08-26, version `2.50.0`** — the close-out follows.

### CR-034 §7 · CLOSED 2026-08-26 — WHAT SHIPPED (version `2.50.0`)

**FIRST, THE THING THAT HAD TO BE ESTABLISHED BEFORE A LINE WAS WRITTEN, AND
THE ANSWER IS YES — WITH ONE HALF MISSING.** The amendment asked whether the
eligibility CONDITIONS are stored anywhere a screen may read, or only as
`rate_plans.eligibility`, which is advisory. **They are stored, and they are a
different object one level down:** `discount_versions` carries
`eligibility_summary` — the plain-English sentence (`apps/rating/discounts.py:401`;
Silver Creek's five read *Age 65+ · Program enrolment · E-bill on · Autopay
enrolled · Veteran ID*) — beside the whole enrolment-and-proof block:
`enrolment_mode`, `verification_method`, `proof_required`,
`accepted_proof_kinds`, `proof_before_first_reduction`, `recertification_*`,
`lapse_behaviour`, the three caps, `bill_floor_amount`, `stacks_with_others`,
`exclusivity_group` and `stacking_precedence`. **So this was a rendering gap,
exactly as the amendment predicted:** `_offered_discounts` was already
forwarding `eligibility` and the panel drew three columns and never printed it.

**WHAT IS GENUINELY ABSENT IS THE EVALUATION, AND IT IS STATED ON EVERY ROW.**
`eligibility_rule` — the DIS-02 rule builder's document — is stored as authored
and **nothing in this product evaluates it** (`discounts.py:395-398`;
`discount_services.py:42` — *"It does not evaluate eligibility"*). So the
payload carries `terms.eligibility_checked = {served:false, reason:
"no_code_evaluates_a_discount_eligibility_rule"}` and the screen says *"Nothing
in this product checks this condition. Staff confirm it when the account is
enrolled."* ⚠ **The rule DOCUMENT itself is not shipped to the client at all** —
printing its clauses as bullet points would be the same false reassurance in a
different font.

| Requirement | What shipped |
|---|---|
| 1 · ALL discounts the plan offers | Unchanged and already true — every `plan_discount_rules` row renders, draft ones included |
| 2 · **The conditions to avail each** | `terms`, twelve stored columns per discount, in a block per discount below the table |
| 3 · Read as *what WILL apply* | A framing line above the table — ⚠ and it says **enrolled**, not *attached*: BR-RAT-069, a plan grants a discount to nobody |

**Three judgments, each in the decision log (2026-08-26) with its worked case:**
the conditions are shown as RECORDED and never as ENFORCED · the programme's
tenant-wide `budget_cap` is dropped at source, like `enrolled` before it · the
service date now reaches the discount VERSION, so one date governs the whole
answer.

**ALSO IN THIS RELEASE, AND IT IS A REVERSAL OF THIS LANE'S OWN
RECOMMENDATION:** the PO ruled *"B Default to this month"* on the review-ledger
question the CR-034 (b) lane raised. The staff Plan tab opens on the current
month; **the move-in wizard is unchanged and still answers as of today**, and
the endpoint's no-period answer is byte-identical. Two guards in opposite
directions pin that split.

**NOTHING WAS COMPUTED, AND `CR-020` IS STILL THE CONTRACT ROW.** Golden 33/33
by exit code before and after; no OQ was minted (`CR-020` covers contracts and
this amendment raised nothing new).

## CR-035 — Park has to actually work, on every wizard

**Arrived** 2026-08-26, from the PO in the working chat session, immediately
after being told (on this session's own report) that Park on the Transfer wizard
does nothing because the flow has nowhere to park to.

**Requester's words, verbatim:**
> *"Park to actually work on the wizards - it should work ; in pratcicail life
> all these request does not close in  day, hence user genrllay park them - and
> we need to adopt that behaviour and help them to work on these request as per
> their pace hence we need park functionalities"*

**Urgency:** stated as a requirement, not a thought — *"it should work"*. Not
stamped urgent by the requester; treated as the next substantial build, not a
hotfix.

**0 · CAPTURE — the sentence under the sentence.** The reason given is the
requirement: *"in practical life all these requests do not close in a day"*. A
clerk with 1–2 staff serving under 3,000 connections is interrupted; a move-in
waits on a deposit, a new connect waits on an inspection, a transfer waits on
the customer. **The product currently forces every one of those flows to be
finished in a single sitting or abandoned**, which is a working-pattern
mismatch, not a missing button.

**1 · CLASSIFY — a CHANGE, and only just.** The line is genuinely close to a
defect, because BR-SHL-047 (PO 2026-08-24, closing DEF-649, verbatim *"Park
it"*) already ruled that **EVERY wizard parks, move-out included**, and the
control is on every wizard today. What is missing is the STORE behind it for
five of the six flows. Under the change process's own rule — *"when it is
ambiguous it is a DEFECT, not a change"* — the honest reading is:
  · the CONTROL being inert where a signed rule says it must act is a **defect**
    (filed, see below), and
  · the STORE that has to exist for it to act was never specified, sized or
    built, and building it is a **change**.
So this CR carries the build, and the defect row carries the contradiction.
Filing it only as a "change" would convert our own gap into the customer's new
requirement, which is the exact thing step 1 exists to prevent.

**STATUS: ✅ DONE — shipped in `2.51.0`, 2026-08-26.** (Ruled the same day; see step 5.)
The impact survey, the three shapes and the recommendation are recorded below as
they are established.

**2 · WHAT SIGNED STATEMENT IS BEING REVERSED — none.** Nothing frozen is
touched. **BR-SHL-047** (PO 2026-08-24, closing DEF-649, verbatim *"Park it"*)
already says EVERY wizard parks; this CR does not reverse it, it makes it true.
**B19 §12.2** draws the two controls and this CR keeps both distinct: `Save &
exit` leaves quietly and writes nothing; `Park` records WHAT is awaited, a note
and a reminder date. No ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure is in scope — a parked wizard
computes no money.

**3 · IMPACT — MEASURED, not estimated (2026-08-26).**

| Surface | State today |
|---|---|
| The park PANEL, nine reasons, note, reminder date | **BUILT** in `WizardFrame.tsx`, wired by all five wizards |
| `wizardParkPort()` in `moveShared.tsx` | returns **`null`** — its own docstring says *"Returning a port here is the whole switch"* |
| Wizards with the control and no store | **5** — Move-in, Move-out, Transfer, Disconnect, New connect |
| Steps those five hold between them | **30** (5 · 6 · 5 · 5 · 9) |
| The one flow where Park already works | **Service requests** — `park()` / `unpark()` in `service_request_service.py`, columns `waiting_on`, `park_note`, `remind_on`, `parked_at`, `parked_by` on `customers.ServiceRequest` |
| A store for the other five | **NONE.** `models.py` has no move-in, move-out, transfer, disconnect or new-connect job table. A move-in in progress is not a row; it is component state over an account that does not exist yet |
| API | no park endpoint for any of the five |
| Open questions | none blocking; this CR mints the shape question itself |
| Demo fixture | a seeded parked example is owed once the shape is ruled |

**So the frontend half is DONE and the whole cost is the store, its endpoints,
the port and resume.** That is the finding that changes the sizing.

**4 · WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT AND IS NOW WRONG.** Nothing shipped becomes wrong;
five disabled buttons become enabled. The sentence under them
(`parkStoreBlockedReason`) is deleted when the port returns non-null — it is
already written to disappear on exactly that condition. **No lane is building in
these files right now.**

**5 · SIZE AND SHAPE — three, and the difference is not effort, it is what the
rest of the product believes while a wizard sits parked.** Put to the PO
2026-08-26; recorded here when ruled.

**5 · RULED — 2026-08-26, PO, verbatim:** *"Option A - Unitl move in executed,
no records updates."*

Shape **A**. A parked wizard is a saved draft of a form and nothing more.
Between 26 August and 2 September **Unit 12 reads Vacant**, no account exists,
no occupancy begins, no bill changes; the parked work appears in the clerk's own
"Waiting on" list and nowhere else. Written up as **BR-SHL-048 CONFIRMED**, with
the three consequences the ruling forces — no foreign key from a draft to the
record it names, re-validation at execution rather than trust from the park, and
BR-SHL-047's open unit-blocking half now **moot** because a parked wizard holds
nothing. The cost the ruling accepts is stated, not hidden: a parked move-out is
invisible, so that account keeps billing.

**6 · EXECUTE — through r11, unchanged.** Scope, in build order:

| # | Part | What |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | store | one table of parked drafts: flow kind, step reached, the typed values, the nine reasons, note, remind-on, who and when. `tenant_id` and the parking user are the only FKs (BR-SHL-048 (a)) |
| 2 | service + API | park · list · resume · unpark · discard, tenant-scoped, RLS FORCE like every other table |
| 3 | the port | `wizardParkPort()` returns non-null — *"the whole switch"*; the five disabled buttons act and `parkStoreBlockedReason` deletes itself |
| 4 | resume | each wizard rehydrates what was typed and lands on the step it was parked at; every check re-runs before commit (BR-SHL-048 (b)) |
| 5 | the list | one "Waiting on" surface with the reason, the note, the reminder date and the **age**, which is the only thing that stops a draft sitting forever |
| 6 | fixture | a seeded parked example, so the screen is not empty on a demo |

**7 · VERSION — `2.51.0`.** `<release>.<change>.<fix>`: a CHANGE, because the
release ships a capability the product did not have — a store, a service, an API,
the port, resume, and a list. The close-out lands in the same release: `S17.2`,
`US-CUS-031`, the B18 §4 amendment and the seeded fixture.

**8 · CLOSE + ROLLBACK — stated before shipping, as the process requires.**
**The rollback is one `return`:** `wizardParkPort()` goes back to returning
`null`. The five `Park` buttons re-disable and carry `parkStoreBlockedReason`
again — that function is already written to say the right thing on exactly that
condition — the Waiting-on tab drops out of `ACCOUNTS_BUILT_TABS`, and any
`wizard_parks` rows are orphaned but harmless.

⚠ **AND THE REASON THE ROLLBACK IS THAT CHEAP IS BR-SHL-048 ITSELF.** *"Until
move-in executed, no records updates"* means no other table was ever written, so
**there is no data migration to revert** — nothing else in the product reads a
parked draft, by construction rather than by care (it carries no foreign key to
anything it names). A ruling made for a clerk's sake turned out to be what makes
the feature safe to withdraw.

**⚠ WHAT THE CLOSE-OUT DOES NOT COVER, said plainly rather than implied:**
`EP-CUS-11` closes hard-won law 8 for the LIST half only. The store, the
service and API, the port, and the five wizards' resume all shipped in `2.51.0`

## CR-036 — services must be taggable per premise at import, for whatever services THIS utility sells

**Arrived** 2026-08-26, from the PO on the live deployment
`smartbillhub.bynry.com/ottumwa-water-works`, after creating a NEW tenant,
completing settings, activating **three** services (Water · Sewer · Trash) and
importing **9,881 premises** from a CSV (`WFL-01` mapping screen, `PRM-01` list).

**Requester's words, verbatim:**
> *"Raise new CR - I have created new tenant/utility  ; Ihave completed setting;
> I am trying to load Premises it loaded 9881 premises ; I have have Activated 3
> Services  Water, Sewer, Trash  for this Utility . At The time of Upload CSV
> File Provide only one Utility Service  . I was not able Provide remaining two
> Services and When data is upload services are not taged to that premises .
> Here are the Screenshots  .How to rectify this also note different tenant
> utility gas one to many different utility services activated  so utility
> service tagging should be dynamic  at the time of upload . because the data is
> not imported correctly I have to overrride again do you have option  how to do
> it ."*

**Evidence supplied (two screenshots).** `PRM-01` shows imported premises
`P-10000`…`P-10005` reading **`No services`** in the SERVICES column, beside
seeded rows `P-00043`/`P-00044` carrying **W · S · T** chips. `WFL-01` stage 2
shows the column `services_available` **mapped to `Services available` and
marked `Matched`** — so the operator did map it, and the load produced nothing.
Total on file: **1–50 of 9,925**.

**THREE DISTINCT ASKS, and they are not the same kind of thing.** Separating
them is the point of this entry:

| | The ask | First reading |
|---|---|---|
| **(i)** | 9,881 premises imported with **no services at all**, from a file whose services column was mapped and Matched | a **DEFECT**, not a change — the screen accepted a column and the load did not produce its effect. Under the change process's own rule, an ambiguous case is a defect, because filing our gap as a "change" converts our error into the customer's new requirement |
| **(ii)** | *"utility service tagging should be dynamic at the time of upload"* — this tenant sells three, another sells ten, and the importer must offer whatever THIS tenant activated | a genuine **CHANGE**. The current shape is one column of comma-separated codes; what the PO describes is the importer knowing the tenant's own activated services and letting a row carry any subset |
| **(iii)** | *"I have to override again do you have option how to do it"* | **a question with an answer that already exists** — see below |

**(iii) IS ANSWERABLE NOW AND DOES NOT WAIT FOR THE OTHER TWO.** The importer
ships **three write modes** (`WRITE_MODES = ("insert", "upsert", "replace")`)
and the file already carries `premise_no` (`P-10000`…), which is the key the
loader matches on (`_key_of` → `_existing_index`). So the same file re-run in
**Insert & update** updates the 9,881 rows in place rather than duplicating
them. **It is only worth re-running once (i) is fixed** — re-running today would
re-apply the same empty result.

**STATUS: CAPTURED 2026-08-26. Root cause of (i) under investigation — NOT yet
established, and not guessed at here.** The tempting reading is a target-name
mismatch (`importers.py` stages `_value(raw, mapping, "services")` while the
mapping vocabulary's target id is `services_available`), and the repo has TWO
importer paths, so which one this deployment ran must be MEASURED before a fix
is written. This module has form for exactly this shape: **DEF-542** — *"the
mapped area was checked and then silently DROPPED: stage 2 carried `area_name`,
stage 3 proved it exists, and the load stripped it — a migration would lose
every district assignment while every rule reported green."*

### CR-036 · AMENDMENT 2 — (g) the write mode belongs at stage 1 or 2

**PO, 2026-08-26, verbatim**, answering where the re-import option lives after
being told it is on stage 4:
> *"you need at step 1 or 2 itself - this is important decision how you will
> process the data and upload it"*

**A CHANGE — with a defect underneath it.** Stage 4 does what it was specified
to do. But the PO's reason is the finding: **the write mode is not a
confirmation, it is a PREMISE.** It decides what the file MEANS — a load, a
correction or a replacement — and stages 2 and 3 already report against an
assumption about it that the operator was never asked to make.

Their own screenshots prove it twice over:

| On stage 3 | Why it depends on a mode the operator has not chosen |
|---|---|
| `PRM.ADDRESS_ON_FILE` — *"No premises is already on file at this address"* — **9,881 hits**, action **Skip on load** | Under `insert` that is a real warning. Under `upsert` "already on file" is the EXPECTED state of every row, and a skip would defeat the mode entirely |
| *"This premise ID is already on file — **the write mode decides what happens to it**"* | The screen names the write mode as the deciding factor while still refusing to show it |

**Scope:** move the mode choice to stage 1 or 2; re-evaluate stage 3 against the
CHOSEN mode; keep the stage-4 dry run as the last chance to change it (a
premise you cannot revise before committing is a trap, not a decision). The
severity and the action of a rule may legitimately DEPEND on the write mode —
`PRM.ADDRESS_ON_FILE` is the first candidate and is not to be changed until the
measurement in (i) below establishes whether its skip fires at all.

⚠ **BLOCKED ON A MEASUREMENT, deliberately.** Whether `skip_on_load` is honoured
at load is unresolved and the repo contradicts itself about it — `import_rules.py`
says the action *"is performed at stage 4, which is P5 and unbuilt"*, while
`ImportWorkflowPage.tsx` says *"STAGE 4 COMMITS NOW … this note used to say the
opposite"*. One of those has outlived its truth. Building (g) on the wrong one
would move a control into a stage whose verdict is still computed against an
assumption nobody has verified.

### CR-036 · MEASURED, 2026-08-26 — and (i)'s stated hypothesis is WRONG

⛔ **CORRECTION TO THIS ENTRY'S OWN §(i), recorded rather than edited away.** The
capture above names a *"tempting reading"* — that `importers.py` stages
`_value(raw, mapping, "services")` while the mapping vocabulary's target id is
`services_available`. **Measured: that is not a bug, and a lane acting on it
would have "fixed" working code.** There are two live importer paths with two
*different but each self-consistent* vocabularies:

| Path | Reached from | Its target id |
|---|---|---|
| `import_runs.py` | the **WFL-01 wizard** — what the PO used | `services_available` |
| `importers.py` | `AddPremisesWizard` → `POST /premises/imports` | `"services"`, aliases `("services", "services available")`, and it writes `row["data"]["services_available"]` |

Both correct. Neither dead. **This correction stays here because the CR's text
would otherwise send the next lane to patch a non-bug.**

**WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED — established by exhaustion, over 11 realistic operator
values through the live path:**

| Cell | Result |
|---|---|
| `water,sewer,trash` · `Water, Sewer, Trash` · `WATER` · `water;sewer` · `water\|sewer` | 0 errors, correct codes land |
| `W,S,T` | rejected, by name: *"This utility does not sell w, s, t."* |
| `Water Service` · `Trash Collection` · `water,electric` | rejected, named |
| **`""` (empty)** | **0 errors, the row loads, services `[]` → "No services"** |

**No code drops a value. An unrecognised token rejects the row loudly. So the
ONLY way to reach 9,881 loaded rows with zero errors and no services is an EMPTY
CELL in the mapped column** — and the product's own sample is one route there:
`sample_csv` emits `""` for every `KIND_LIST` column, so a file built from the
shipped premises sample carries the header, maps it, shows `Matched`, and fills
nothing.

The opposite hypothesis is ruled out too: `selectors.py` serves the column,
`ServiceTags` draws "No services" only on an empty array, and the PO's own
screenshot shows seeded rows drawing W·S·T through that same renderer. **The
chips work. The data is empty.**

**⚠ THE ONE THING THAT WOULD CLOSE THIS OUTRIGHT: one row of the PO's actual
CSV.** Exhaustion plus the sample route is strong; it is not the file itself.

**(a) WAS ALREADY RULED AND BUILT — `BR-MET-117`, CONFIRMED.** No sniffing
anywhere: `_parse_date` tries ISO, then **only** the tenant's declared pattern,
read from `TenantSettings.date_format` at stage 2. `01/02/2026` pins to 2 Jan
under `MM/DD/YYYY` and 1 Feb under `DD/MM/YYYY`; an undeclared format returns
`None` — refuse, never guess. **The format IS reachable at stage 2, so the "stop
and report options" branch was not needed.** ⚠ Its third clause is served and
rendered by nothing (DEF-751).

**(g) IS UNBLOCKED. MEASURED: `skip_on_load` does not fire.** The rule hits 3 of
3 rows, declares the action, and the upsert updates all 3 anyway — receipt
`created 0 · updated 3 · skipped 0`. `SKIP_ON_LOAD` is assigned once and **read
nowhere** in the backend. **So the PO's re-import in `Insert & update` WILL reach
all 9,881 rows** — and the screen promising "Skip on load" on every one of them
is the worse of the two possible defects (DEF-750).

**⚠ (c) / (ii) NEEDS A SCHEMA RULING BEFORE ANY IMPORTER WORK, and this is the
finding that changes its size.** **`Unit` has NO `services_available` field.**
Only `Premises` does; a unit reaches services through `servicepoint` /
`connectionservice`. So "the unit import should allow multi utility service
tagging" is **a B2 schema change, not an importer column** — what does it MEAN
for a unit to carry services when the connection records already say so? That is
the PO's question, and it is not answerable by the importer.

## CR-037 — a unit carries its own services, so it can diverge from its premises

**Arrived** 2026-08-26, from the PO, answering the schema question CR-036 (c)
raised. It is recorded as its own CR because the answer is **a B2 schema
change**, not the importer column CR-036 (c) assumed.

**Requester's words, verbatim:**
> *"we should have services details on unit - so later any changes that are
> differnt from premises we cna maintain it on units"*

**1 · CLASSIFY — a CHANGE, and the reason is in the sentence.** Nothing is
broken; the PO is specifying a capability the schema does not have. The purpose
they give is **divergence over time**: a unit starts out like its building and
later stops being like it, and that difference has to live somewhere.

**2 · WHAT IS BEING CHANGED — and what already exists, measured.**

| Level | Today | Means |
|---|---|---|
| `Premises.services_available` | **EXISTS** — a JSON list of service codes | what this ADDRESS can get |
| `Unit` | **NOTHING** — no services field of any kind | — |
| `ServicePoint` (`unit_id` + `service_id`) | EXISTS | *"one METERED service at a unit"* — a physical point with a meter and a connection |

**⚠ `ServicePoint` IS NOT THE ANSWER AND SUBSTITUTING IT WOULD BE THE MISTAKE.**
It records a service that has been **realised** — metered, connected, billable.
The PO is asking for the **declaration**: what this unit gets, which must be
sayable *before* a meter exists and must survive a service being disconnected.
Reading services off `ServicePoint` would mean a unit "loses" a service the
moment its meter is pulled, which is exactly the divergence they want to record,
inverted.

**So the shape is THREE levels, and each answers a different question:**

    Premises.services_available   what this address CAN have      (offer)
    Unit.services_available       what this unit DOES have        (declaration)  ← NEW
    ServicePoint                  what is metered and connected   (realisation)

**3 · THE INHERITANCE, which is the whole point of the change.** A unit with no
declaration of its own **inherits its premises' list** — nothing is re-keyed for
a building whose units are all alike, which is the ordinary case. A unit that
declares its own list **overrides**, and that override is the *"changes that are
different from premises"* the PO asked to be able to maintain. This is the same
shape as the plan inheritance already ruled on: the parent supplies, the child
may refine, and the refinement is visible.

**⚠ ONE QUESTION THE RULING DOES NOT SETTLE, and the assumption being built
under, stated so it can be overruled cheaply rather than discovered later.**

> **Can a unit declare a service its premises does not offer?**

**Assumed: NO — the unit's list must be a SUBSET of the premises' list.**
Worked: premises `500 Main St` offers **water · sewer · trash**. Unit 12 may
declare *water · sewer* (it has no bin collection). Unit 12 may **not** declare
*gas*, because the building has no gas — the fix for that is to correct the
premises, not to let a unit invent a service its address does not have.

The cost of the assumption if it is wrong: a utility that keeps a deliberately
narrow premises list would be blocked from recording a real unit-level service
until they widen the address first. **Say so and it becomes a warning instead of
a refusal** — the change is one line either way, which is why it is not worth
blocking on.

**4 · IMPACT — what this touches.** A migration on `units` · the unit
serialisers and PRM-03 · the unit import (which is where CR-036 (c) started, and
which cannot proceed until this lands) · the premises import's own service
column, which must keep meaning the OFFER · anything today that infers a unit's
services from its premises or from `ServicePoint`, each of which must be found
and pointed at the new answer.

**5 · STATUS: CAPTURED AND RULED 2026-08-26. Written up as BR-MET-118.** The
build is queued behind the CR-035 and CR-036 work already in flight.

### CR-037 · WITHDRAWN 2026-08-26, by the requester, the same day it was ruled

**PO, verbatim, two messages:**
> *"I think - lets stay with rule premises services = Unit services = we will not
> change it yet"*
> *"so we dont need CR37"*

**THE RULE IS THEREFORE: a unit's services ARE its premises' services.** No
unit-level column, no override, no divergence.

⚠ **READ THE WORD "YET".** This is a **deferral, not a rejection.** The PO
described a real need — *"later any changes that are different from premises we
cna maintain it on units"* — and then decided not to pay for it now. Everything
above stays in this entry on purpose: the three-level model, the reason
`ServicePoint` is not a substitute, and the subset question. **When this returns,
whoever picks it up should not have to re-derive any of it.** Deleting the entry
would convert a considered deferral into a forgotten idea.

**⚠ THE MOST IMPORTANT THING TO CARRY FORWARD, because it is the trap:** if this
is revived, the answer is still **not** `ServicePoint`. That table records a
service already REALISED — metered, connected, billable — so deriving a unit's
services from it means a unit silently loses a service the moment its meter is
pulled. That is the divergence case backwards, and it will look like a shortcut
to whoever comes next.

**What this changes elsewhere:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **BR-MET-118** | **WITHDRAWN** the day it was written. Not deleted — stamped, with the PO's words and the date |
| **CR-036 (c)** — *"Unit import should allow multi utility service tagging"* | **ANSWERED WITHOUT CODE.** A unit's services are its premises'; the premises import already carries the services column, so a unit import needs no services column at all. The tagging happens once, at the address |
| Lane UNITSVC | **STOPPED** mid-build. Its measurement of where the product reads a unit's services today is kept; its schema work is unwound |

**⚠ AND ONE THING TO CHECK RATHER THAN ASSUME, because the new rule makes it
load-bearing:** with `Unit.services_available` never existing, **every read of a
unit's services must resolve through its premises** — and nothing has verified
that every such read does so today. If some screen or service infers a unit's
services from `ServicePoint` instead, it now disagrees with the ruling rather
than merely duplicating it. That is what lane UNITSVC was asked to measure
before it was stopped, and its answer is worth having whether or not the column
is ever built.

### CR-036 · (h) — a premises' services must be settable on screen · RULED 2026-08-26

**PO, verbatim:**
> *"No screen can set a premises' services. The Add-Premises wizard and the edit
> modal both omit the field — only the CSV importer ever fills it. So every
> address you create by hand has none. - we will ahve to fix that keep them in
> CR36 only"*

**Ruled: FIX IT, and it stays inside CR-036** rather than becoming its own CR —
the requester's call, and the right one: it is the same import-and-onboarding
surface, and splitting it would put the cause and the cure in two places.

**This is DEF-756, promoted to a scoped item.** Measured 2026-08-26 by lane
UNITSVC: `premises.services_available` is READ in four places
(`selectors.py:138`, `exports.py:112`, `PremisesListPage.tsx:255`,
`PremisesDetailPage.tsx:599`) and **written by no screen at all** —
`AddPremisesWizard.singlePayload` (456-485) omits it and `PremisesEditModal`'s
form state (504-512) has no such field.

**⚠ WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS, and it is the reason it belongs in this
CR:** the PO has just ruled that **a unit's services are its premises'
services**. Read as a derivation, that resolves to **no services at all** for the
units of every hand-built premises — while those units genuinely hold meters and
service points. So this item is the **precondition** for the rule the PO set an
hour earlier. Building the derivation first would have shipped a product that
shows a metered unit as having nothing.

**⚠ AND THE DEMO TENANT HIDES IT COMPLETELY.** `sample_data.py` and `seed_demo.py`
write the same list by hand to `premises.services_available` **and** to each
unit, so the two always agree in seeded data and can only diverge in a tenant
built through the UI or by import. **Green in the demo, wrong in production** —
which is why no one saw it until a real utility created a real address.

**Scope:**

| | |
|---|---|
| `AddPremisesWizard` | offer the services, send them |
| `PremisesEditModal` | offer the services, send them |
| The choices offered | **the tenant's own ENABLED services** — never a hardcoded list (BR-MET-003: a premises may only offer services this utility sells, and the importer already refuses others by name) |
| The write path | must refuse a service the tenant does not sell, the same way the importer does, and say which |
| Existing rows | ⚠ **premises already on file have `NULL`, and that is not the same as "none"** — it is *never asked*. Do not backfill it to an empty list, which would make an unanswered question look like an answered one |

**What it unblocks: OQ-387.** That question — is *"unit services = premises
services"* a read-time derivation or an invariant the write paths enforce? — was
recorded as unanswerable-in-practice while premises services were unwritable.
This removes that obstacle; the question itself still needs the PO.

### CR-035 · AMENDMENT 1 — the Waiting-on TAB is folded into the six worklists

**PO, 2026-08-26, verbatim:**
> *"We dont need seperate tab for this - this will be directly on each request
> Request, Connect, Move IN move Out, Trasnfr, Disconnect - seperate queue not
> reequired - what do you think?"* … and, on the analysis below: **"yyes"**

**Ruled: FOLD IT IN.** A parked job appears on the tab for its own kind of work.
The ninth tab (`S17.2`) comes out.

**The PO is right, and the product already proved it:** a parked **service
request** stays in the Requests list with its waiting-on value beside it (B19
§12.2 — park *"moves no state"*). The separate tab was the inconsistency, not
the fix. It also returns the screen to the **eight tabs B18 §4 draws**, and
dissolves the mine-versus-everyone's question entirely (DEF-769's neighbour: the
tab opened on `?mine=1` because BR-SHL-048's phrase *"the clerk's own Waiting on
list"* was read as a filter, when it meant *there and nowhere else*).

**⚠ THE ASYMMETRY THAT DECIDES WHETHER THIS WORKS, and it is not obvious:**

| Flow | A parked one is… |
|---|---|
| **Service request** | the **same row**, annotated — it exists and is numbered from creation |
| **Move-in · move-out · transfer · disconnect · new connect** | **not a row at all** — no account, no occupancy, nothing committed. That is precisely why `wizard_parks` had to be built |

So on Requests, park is a **column**. On the other five, the tab must show **two
different things in one list**: records that happened, and drafts that have not.
That is lawful — BR-SHL-048 forbids a draft appearing on the **unit, premises or
account**, and a worklist is none of those — but it is the whole risk.

**Therefore, and these are requirements rather than preferences:**
1. **A draft row must be unmistakably a draft.** Pinned at the top (it is the one
   needing chasing), visually distinct, carrying the reason, the note, the
   reminder and the **age**.
2. **The tab count must not lie.** If a Move-ins tab reads `12` and three never
   happened, that number is wrong in a way that reaches reports. Exclude drafts
   or state both — `9 · 3 parked`.
3. **Nothing else changes.** The store, service, API, port and resume all stay;
   only the presentation moves.

**⚠ WHAT IS LOST, KNOWINGLY:** a single place answering *"what is waiting, across
everything?"* With six tabs a clerk covering the desk opens six. If that turns
out to matter, the honest home is the **Dashboard**, not a ninth tab — and it is
not being built now.

**Cost:** small, and smaller than it looks. `S17.2`, `US-CUS-031` and the B18 §4
amendment were written **hours before this ruling** — the close-out is not wasted
so much as re-pointed: the story describes the behaviour, and the behaviour is
keeping its home rather than its own screen.

### CR-035 · AMENDMENT 2 — the PANEL is removed; a parked draft is a ROW of its own flow's list

**PO, 2026-09-20, verbatim:**
> *"remove it - it is anyway in the list so we dont need it sepretely - if it is
> not in list add it"*

**Ruled: REMOVE THE PANEL, WIDEN THE LISTS.** Filed and built as
`DEF-CUS-5994`.

**THE SUPERSESSION CHAIN, STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED:** `CR-035` →
**AMENDMENT 1** (PO 2026-08-26, *"this will be directly on each request …
seperate queue not reequired"*) → **AMENDMENT 2** (this). Amendment 1 put parked
work **on each flow tab** and said nothing about **where on the tab**;
`parkedDrafts.tsx` chose a pinned panel and argued for it in its §1. **This
settles the placement amendment 1 left open, and nothing else moves:** a draft
still belongs to its own flow, there is still no ninth queue, and the store, the
service, the API, the port and the resume are all untouched.

**⚠ THE RULING HAS TWO HALVES AND ONLY ONE IS A REMOVAL.** *"if it is not in
list add it"* is the larger half by work:

| Flow | Before 2026-09-20 | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Move-outs** | already unioned `wizard_parks` (PO `yes`, 2026-09-19, `BR-CUS-1077` shape) — **the panel above it was pure duplication** | panel removed, nothing else needed; gains `parked_by_name` and a Discard |
| **Move-ins** | the list said outright a parked draft *"is not a ROW OF THIS LIST … and it lives on the panel above this table"* | a THIRD union arm beside accounts and pending jobs |
| **Transfers** | no drafts at all | a two-arm union; `DEF-CUS-6004` fixed in passing |
| **Disconnects** | no drafts at all | a two-arm union |
| **New connects** | no drafts at all | a two-arm union; metering gains its own `wizard_parks` seam |

**⚠ THE OLD OBJECTION IS OVERTAKEN, NOT IGNORED — and this is the part worth
keeping.** `parkedDrafts.tsx` §1 rejected table rows on one argument: *"a
`MoveInRow` and a `WizardParkRow` share not one field"*. Two facts answered it,
neither of them an opinion:

1. **The tables already render a row with nothing in those cells, and it is the
   DRAWING'S OWN ROW.** B18 §5.5.2 draws `SR-26-0012` with account *"— draft"*,
   unit *"—"* and *"Step not recorded"*; `BR-CUS-1077` put it on the Move-ins
   list on 2026-09-16 with a NAMED ABSENCE in each empty cell rather than a
   dash. *"Four cells would be empty"* stopped being an argument the day the
   list learned to say WHY a cell is empty.
2. **The Move-outs list did it and it works** — one day before this ruling.

**⚠ THE ONE CONSTRAINT FROM AMENDMENT 1 SURVIVES INTACT, AND IT INVERTED.**
Requirement 2 was *"the count must not lie"*, and the panel honoured it by
keeping drafts OUT of `total`. They are rows now, so `total` must COUNT them —
and it must be the SERVER's figure over one window. **Every list unions in SQL**
(`_move_in_page_keys`, `_move_out_page_keys`, `transfer_reads._page_keys`,
`disconnect_reads._page_keys`, `connection_reads`' inline union): nothing is
spliced into a server-paged list in JavaScript and no number on any tab is a sum
computed in two places. `NFR-3` and `NFR-5` are why.

**⚠ WHAT WOULD HAVE BEEN LOST BY REMOVING THE SURFACE, AND WAS NOT.** Two
things lived on that panel and only one of them existed anywhere else:

* **`Parked by`** — which is what amendment 1 put in place of the
  mine/everyone's toggle it dissolved. Dropping it would have quietly re-opened
  a question that ruling closed. It is served on the row now, and had to be
  **ADDED** to the move-out row, which never carried it.
* **DISCARD** — and this one existed **nowhere else at all**. The Move-outs row
  had a Resume and no way to throw a draft away. Deleting the panel without
  re-homing it would have removed a live capability from the product **with
  nothing to notice**: no gate, test or type reads a control that is no longer
  there (`DEF-CUS-3653` — an absence is invisible to every check this repo has).
  `ParkedDraftActions` is one implementation for all five tabs.

**⚠ AND ONE THING WAS DELIBERATELY NOT CARRIED OVER.** The panel's last
sentence, *"Nothing here has changed anything yet."*, is RATIONALE, which B14
rule 33 puts at **zero words on screen** — the kind of line the PO has struck
off six screens. The badge says `Draft` or `Parked` in one word and the STEP
cell shows how far the clerk got; `BR-SHL-048` is where the reason lives.

**THE IMPROVEMENT THIS BUYS, rather than the tidy-up:** a parked draft HAS a
real step and now shows it. `MoveStepBar`'s docstring is explicit that `reached`
is the SERVER's answer and the component never derives one, drawing empty with a
reason wherever it is null — so a record that was never walked keeps its
absence, and a draft prints `3 of 6`. **Two answers on one list, each true of
its own row.**

**Cost:** four backend windows widened, one new metering seam, five tabs, one
test file rewritten, two render-checks re-pointed. **Rollback:** revert the
frontend commits alone and the panel returns with the lists still carrying the
drafts — the two halves are independent, and that is deliberate.

and `RDS-04` (read detail).

**Requester's words, verbatim, in order:**

**Classification (step 1): a CHANGE — with four rulings already inside it and
eight open questions it makes urgent.** Nothing here is ambiguous enough to be a
defect; the product does what its stories said, and the PO is changing the
agreement.

### What these words RULE (each confirmed back to the PO in the session)

| # | Ruling | What it answers |
|---|---|---|
| **R1** | **Reads move onto the shared five-stage runner** — *"We need to follow tailwind wizard that we are using - i believe we are using same code for various."* The belief is verified true: `ImportWorkflowPage` + `components/workflow/**` is ONE codebase reused by premises, units, meters/assets (`AssetImportWorkflow`) and accounts (`AccountImportWorkflow`). Reads join it as targets on the same rail, following the endorsed `WFL-01.reads.1`–`.4` screens; the older `UploadReadsWizard` retires in one commit that names what it retires. | The Blueprint's **Open 8** — one rail, decided now, before W2–W5 are built twice |
| **R2** | **Write mode — Insert new only · Insert & update · Replace the batch — applies to reads**, chosen early in the wizard per **CR-036 (g)** (PO: *"you need at step 1 or 2 itself"*), revisable at the stage-4 dry run. ⚠ For reads the modes NEVER edit a committed row (hard rule 4): *insert* refuses committed duplicates; *insert & update* SUPERSEDES a committed duplicate as a correction, reason stamped; *replace* supersedes everything the file carries. | The PO's *"insert, insert update, repalce option in step 1"* — placement already ruled by CR-036 (g), semantics constrained by financial immutability |
| **R3** | **The read detail opens as a PAGE, not a side drawer** — *"i want page to be open for consitency - we dont open side panel."* Supersedes the S29 "drawer" presentation wherever it is described; the r10 `RDS-04` overlay is superseded on this point by the PO's words (CLAUDE.md: where spec and design diverge from a ruling, the ruling wins). | The reads list row-click target. ⚠ Scope beyond reads (other detail drawers in the product) is NOT assumed — asked as Q-scope below |
| **R4** | **The read-method vocabulary is the PO's five words: Manual · Walk-by · AMI · AMR · Mobile** — *"we also have read sources - manual, Walk by, AMI, AMR, mobile reads all read methods."* These already exist as the meter-side list; the reading, the file and the batch adopt them, with a mapping for rows already stored under `ami|manual|import`. Presented back with the worked figure; treated as ruled unless the PO objects to the mapping cost. | The Blueprint's **Open 3** |

### What the import will DO for each case the PO named (the design answer, stated once)

1. **All metered services, uploaded per cycle:** the batch is tagged with the
   cycle at stage 1 (unchanged); one file may carry electric + water + gas rows
   because a route legitimately serves a service set. The file format already
   copes — the SETTINGS are what fail a mixed cycle (see Open 5/6 below).
2. **Rate types:** flat/tiered/seasonal need one `total` row per meter; TOU
   needs one row per configured window; demand adds a `demand` (kW) row with a
   reset marker; net adds `export`. The import gains the **plan-driven
   expected-register rule (BR-MET-049, signed, unbuilt — Blueprint W1)** so a
   TOU meter given only a total row is flagged AT UPLOAD, not at the bill run
   three weeks later. Seasonal needs nothing extra at import.
3. **Read methods:** a `read_method` column on the template and the staged row,
   inheriting the batch's stage-1 choice unless the row overrides
   (BR-MET-014 already permits exactly this), carried onto the committed read,
   shown on the list and the detail. Half-AMI/half-walked cycles become sayable.
4. **Mixed meters in one cycle:** per-service absolute floors (needs Open 5
   figures) · interval bounds derived from the cycle's own frequency (needs
   Open 6 yes) · a cycle-membership rule (needs Open 1: flag or refuse) · a
   service-coherence rule (row's service vs the meter's real service) · a
   per-service batch summary at review ("412 electric · 380 water · 388 gas").
5. **Sub-meters:** nothing new needed in the file — sub-meter-ness is derived
   from the meter, and master-vs-Σ(subs) already flags the master past the
   tolerance during validation. What the 460-kWh gap IS remains Open 9/OQ-327.
6. **Devices:** a solar inverter has NO register today; whether device figures
   ride this file at all is scope (**Open 7**) — built only after the ruling.

### Still OWED by the PO before the blocked waves start (asked in plain English in-session)

| Open | The question | Recommendation on file |

| 2 | May a clerk post an incomplete cycle (1,180 of 1,240)? | allow; shortfall shown, chase list produced |
| 4 | Real AMI head-end feed in scope now? | file-only; remove the refusing option |

| 7 | Do device readings come in this file, and into what? | scope — cannot be guessed |

| 10 | The reading AFTER a corrected one — recompute, flag, or leave (bills twice today)? | flag at minimum |
| **Q-replace-billed** | Replace mode meets a BILLED read — refuse, or auto-open the money correction? | new with R2 |
| **Q-scope** | Does *"we dont open side panel"* bind the whole product (a B14 amendment) or the reads detail only? | reads now; product-wide needs its own ratification |

**Sizing (step 5):** this is the Blueprint's W1 + W7 (both now unblocked) with

rulings. Execution through r11 starts on the PO's go, not before; **step 7
