### CR-038 · AMENDMENT 1 — the VEE rules become a Settings surface, per service, with a default on every rule

**PO, 2026-08-26, verbatim**, after being shown that `read_validation_settings`
has no endpoint, no screen, and per-service floors for only electric and water:
> *"What if Utility want to edit the VEE rules ? how are going to alow them to
> edit and it will be as per Utility services?"*
> …and, on the answer: *"So we have to add tasks related to these we will ahev
> to set these rules in settings and take it from there, we will provide
> default value to start with on all these rules"*

**RULED (three parts):**
1. **The VEE rules are utility-editable in Settings** — screen **S64** ("Read
   validation & estimation rules", Settings → Reference data), which the spec
   reserved and nobody built. A full page (CR-038 R3), Tailwind (B14 r21).
2. **Scoped per utility service** — the settings move from one row per tenant
   to one row per **(tenant, service)** for the service-shaped values, each
   floor in the service's OWN unit, shown only for services the tenant has
   enabled.
3. **Every rule ships a seeded default** — *"default value to start with on all
   these rules."* No service starts empty. ⚠ The default FIGURES for the eight
   services beyond electric/water are unratified — they are put to the PO in
   plain English with concrete numbers (sign-off rule 2026-08-11); BR-MET-020's
   fail-safe (absent figure → rule skipped and reported, never guessed) stays
   the engine's law for any figure the PO strikes rather than ratifies.

**Working assumption, flagged for confirmation:** thresholds are editable and
every rule always RUNS — no per-service kill switch. (The integrity rules —
unknown_meter, retired_meter, unit_missing, negative_usage, rollover,
duplicate, export_not_net — are shown on S64 and locked: a utility cannot turn
off "the meter must exist" or "a reading cannot go backwards.")

**The tasks (the S64 wave — slots beside W2, shares its per-service floors):**
1. **Schema** — per-service validation settings keyed `(tenant, service)`,
   unit-aware floor columns; existing `high_abs_kwh`/`high_abs_kgal` stay
   lawful containers; migration ordering is a 🔒 sensitive path →
   `HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING` + review-ledger row (G7).
2. **Seed + backfill** — ratified defaults written for every ENABLED service at
   provisioning, and a backfill for existing tenants; the seeded figures are
   exactly the ratified table, nothing invented.
3. **Endpoints** — role-safe GET/PUT (Owner/Admin write; clerks read), every
   change writes `audit_log` (thresholds decide what posts; what posts becomes
   money).
4. **Screen S64** — one panel per enabled service; integrity rules visible and
   locked; editable thresholds with their units; the fail-safe state ("no
   figure — rule skipped") rendered honestly; form refuses nonsense (hard
   bounds must contain flag bounds, percentages positive).
5. **Engine** — `validation.py` resolves thresholds from the (tenant, service)
   row; fail-safe skip unchanged for absent figures.
6. **History untouched** — a threshold edit affects the NEXT batch only; every
   read keeps the figure it was judged against (already how outcomes are
   stored — asserted by a test, not assumed).
7. **Tests + red-proof** — per-service resolution proven RED first (gas row
   judged by a gas floor, not electric's), RLS isolation probe on the new
   table, audit-row test.

**Estimation params** (`est_method`, `est_max_consecutive`) stay tenant-wide on
S64's general panel — nothing in the ruling asks for per-service estimation.

**Still owed before the seeds can be written: the ratified figures.** Proposed
defaults were put to the PO in-session (high-usage absolute floors per service
in each service's own unit; the 200%/25% percentages and day bounds carried
unchanged as the all-service defaults). Their ruling lands here and in the
review ledger when given; until then the eight new services' floors are
PROPOSED, not seeded.

**PO, 2026-08-26, verbatim, three messages:**
> *"We also have reading coming when move in move out, transfer, disconnect
> etc. at the time of new conenct; have you taken those task as part of build"*

> *"I want you to take a very close look at all aspect that we need to cosnider

> *"update the CR, update the HTml document and tell how many tasks and waves

**The event-reads answer, measured first:** NO — they were not in the build,

commit through metering's own append-only service** — the rule EXISTS and the
metering side of it was never built); `MoveOutWizard` draws the per-meter
final-read table and refuses `final_reads` the same way; `transfers.py` states

   disclosed, capped — never a silent zero.

### CR-038 · ADDITION, 2026-08-26 — bulk operations on reads, and the period/cycle sanity statement (W5 task 7; 11 waves · 59 tasks)

**PO, verbatim:**
> *"We will need bulk operation; also note read are for perticualr period and
> they need to be part of read cycle or bill cycle - how we are going to keep
> the sanity"*

**Part 1 — bulk operations (W5 · task 7).** Bulk already exists at the two
review gates (the import review's dispositions; the bill run's bulk apply,
BR-BIL-060 — the PO's own earlier ruling: *"it is impossible for user to do
this manually account by account"*). What has none is the READS LIST: task 7
gives S25 row selection + bulk actions — bulk-accept flagged reads WITH ONE
REASON (recorded per row), bulk-estimate the missing set (needs W1's missing
list), bulk clear-selection to export. Same law as everywhere: bulk APPLY
exists, bulk destructive/waive-shaped actions do not; every bulk act writes
its per-row trail.

**Part 2 — period/cycle sanity, the mechanism stated once (design principle,
not new code beyond the waves already planned):**
1. **The read date is the truth; the batch tag is the intent.** Every read
   stores `read_at`; every batch is tagged cycle + period at stage 1
   (mandatory today). Period membership is DERIVED from `read_at` against the
   cycle's calendar — never typed, never guessed.
2. **Four rules reconcile truth against intent:** `out_of_window` (date
   outside the tagged cycle's reading window) · `days_threshold` (interval
   bounds; per-cycle-frequency once Open 6 is ruled) · the `duplicate` unique
   `(asset, read_at, channel)` · cycle-membership (meter not in the tagged
   cycle — Open 1, flag vs refuse pending). W1's completeness closes the loop:
   expected-vs-received PER CYCLE PER PERIOD.
3. **Billing never selects by batch.** The bill run picks cycle + period and
   gathers committed reads FOR THE PERIOD per meter — so a late-posted read
   still lands in its right period, a missing one is an exception a human
   decides (BR-BIL-015), and one that arrives after billing goes through
   true-up or the billed-correction door. The issued bill locks its reads and
   each line carries its `read_id`.
4. **Every entry path carries the same context:** the quick single-read modal
   (task 6) DERIVES cycle + period from the read date and the meter's cycle
   assignment and SHOWS them (the clerk confirms, never types); event reads
   (W9) take their period from the event date; corrections inherit the
   original route stamp so history never migrates onto today's route.

**⚙ PART 1 BUILT 2026-08-26** by the CR-038 W5 tasks 6/7/8 lane.

**It closes DEF-046's second finding, open since 2026-08-11** — *"fix_
disposition/fix_reason/fixed_by exist with no writer and no route, so
US-MET-012 TC-3..7 have nothing to call"*. Three columns in the schema and in
`read_dict`'s served field list that nothing ever wrote. These are their writer.

**Backend** — `services.bulk_fix_reads` + `bulk_estimate_reads`, `POST
/reads/bulk-fix` and `POST /reads/bulk-estimate`.

**The PO's accountability rule is what shapes every line of it** (2026-08-26,
verbatim): *"keep the rule — speed comes from the bulk button… an auditor asking
'who chose to estimate M-4412?' gets a name"*. So a bulk action here is a LOOP
over rows that each get the full trail — `fixed_by` (the acting user),
`fix_reason`, and ONE `audit_log` row PER READ — never a single statement
touching many rows anonymously. Two tests ask the auditor's question from two
directions (over `meter_reads.fixed_by` and over `audit_log`) and assert a name
comes back.

**Only ACCEPT is bulk, and that is a boundary rather than an omission.**
BR-MET-023 lists more fix verbs (override · investigate · check · field-visit ·
prorate · change-multiplier) and none belongs on a bulk button: an override is a
SUPERSEDE needing a new value and its own reason for each read, and one reason
typed once about forty different readings would be untrue of thirty-nine. The
screen SAYS so rather than leaving a clerk hunting for Override.

**BR-MET-129 bounds what it can do:** a warned reading already POSTED and stays
posted. Accepting records a judgment after commit (clause 3); it neither posts a
reading nor holds one out, and no ERROR is ever cleared by it.

**Frontend** — row selection on S25 (a checkbox CELL in the S25 table config,
as `AssetRegistryPage` already does it — B14's one table type) plus
`features/metering/ReadsBulkBar.tsx`. A row the action cannot touch renders a
DISABLED checkbox WITH its reason (BR-SHL-025). A refused row comes back NAMED
— *"M-4413 — superseded by a newer reading"* — never folded into "38 of 40",
because a count is not something a clerk can act on. A sort, page or filter
change CLEARS the selection.

**⚠ BULK ESTIMATE IS SERVED AND HAS NO CONTROL ON THIS SCREEN.** The missing set
it operates on is the DERIVED `f.status=pending` list, whose rows carry
`id: null` and are a different selection model from the stored rows this bar
owns. One selection meaning two different things is how a clerk estimates the
wrong meter. REPORTED and left to W1's completeness surface, which owns that
list. **Part 2 (the period/cycle sanity mechanism) needed no new code beyond the
waves already planned, as this section itself states** — the quick-entry modal's
clause-4 obligation is built in task 6 above.

### CR-038 · ADDITION, 2026-08-26 — trailing-12-month consumption on account AND meter (W5 task 8; 11 waves · 60 tasks)

**PO, verbatim:**
> *"We ahve to calcualet last 12 month consumption from these readings and
> display it on account and meters"*

**Measured:** the ACCOUNT side is SERVED — S21's Usage tab draws a 12/24-month
chart with `Avg/month · last 12 months`, peak, low and YoY over the STORED
monthly usage (BR-MET-106: computed from reads once, stored, restated on a
correction, absent when unread, estimates marked). The METER side is the gap:
S50's Reads tab lists individual readings and no 12-month rollup exists there.

**The task (W5 · task 8):** a trailing-12-month consumption strip on the asset
detail (per register where the meter has several — a TOU meter's windows are
not blended), read from the SAME stored monthly-usage source the account tab
uses — one source of truth, never recomputed by a screen; months with no read
render absent, never zero; estimates carry their mark. Sub-meters get it free
(they are assets). Devices: with W6/Open 7, as everything device-shaped.

**⚙ BUILT 2026-08-26** by the CR-038 W5 tasks 6/7/8 lane — **and it fixed
DEF-798 at the source first, because the chart could not be correct over a
broken figure.**

**DEF-798, measured and now closed:** `monthly_usage` summed across REGISTERS
unit-blind, so a demand peak-delta landed in the kWh energy total and a TOU
meter's windows were counted on top of its own `total`. **The reported case was
684 + 14 = 698 kWh where the truth is 684 kWh; after the fix the stored July
figure is 684.000000.** RED-PROVED by disabling the new selection, which
reproduced 698 exactly. `monthly_usage.select_consumption_facts` now makes the
choice PER ASSET — never `export`/`generation`/`demand`, and `total` OR the TOU
windows, never both — and an unclassified register RAISES rather than joining
the sum by default (`generation` was minted the same morning; a default branch
would have added a solar device's production to every site's usage with nothing
failing).

**Backend** — `apps/metering/asset_usage.py` + `GET /assets/{id}/usage`. ONE
SERIES PER REGISTER, each carrying its own unit; there is no "meter total" and
no code path that could produce one.

**⚠ ONE DIVERGENCE FROM THIS SECTION'S WORDING, STATED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED.**
This task asks for the *"SAME stored monthly-usage source"*. **The RULES are
literally the same code** — `monthly_usage`'s own functions, not a copy, and a
test pins the two surfaces against each other on the single-meter case so a
drift goes red. **The stored ROW cannot serve a meter:** `monthly_usage` is keyed
(account, service, month) and has no asset or channel grain, and adding one is a
migration on a table BR-MET-106 signed. So the meter figures are COMPUTED
server-side and the payload SAYS so (`source: "computed_from_reads"` +
`stored_source_absent`), the screen repeats it in one line, and **`OQ-418`** asks
the PO whether the stored month should gain that dimension. Nothing is
recomputed *by a screen*; what it is not is *stored*.

**Frontend** — `features/assets/AssetUsageStrip.tsx`, mounted at the head of
S50's Reads tab (law 2). A non-consumption register is DRAWN and LABELLED *"Not
consumption — never added to usage"* rather than hidden: hiding it would leave a
clerk looking at a demand meter an empty chart. An unread month draws NO bar and
the count is stated (BR-MET-106); an estimated month is marked. Sub-meters get it
free, as this section says — they are assets and the same tab renders.

**Tests:** `tests/test_def_798_register_blind_usage.py`, 10 cases, and
`AssetUsageStrip.test.tsx`, 7 — whose central assertion is that the string `698`
appears nowhere in the rendered markup. RED-PROVED by blending the registers.

### CR-038 · BUILT, 2026-08-26 — the BR-MET-136 follow-up: a rule can be switched off, and it says so

BR-MET-136 was CONFIRMED on 2026-08-26 and its own last column said what was
missing: *"This amends what the S64 lane shipped today, which has no enabled
flag at all: the column, its default, its S64 control and its audit row are a
follow-up task."* That task is closed.

**What the tenant gets.** `read_validation_service_settings.rule_enabled` — a
JSONB map of check → on/off, per (tenant, service). **13** checks are switchable;
**7** are not. Every existing row acquired the column EMPTY, and empty means
every check runs, so nothing was silently turned off by the upgrade.

**The four clauses, and where each is enforced.**

| Clause | Where | The thing that would break it |
|---|---|---|
| **1 · a flag per (tenant, service)** | the column + `validation.JUDGMENT_RULES` (`ALL_RULES` − `INTEGRITY_RULES`, by subtraction) | a rule added to the engine landing in neither list — a test asserts the two partition the vocabulary |
| **2 · default ALL ENABLED, provisioning AND backfill** | the column default `{}` plus the absent-means-enabled convention in `rule_switches` | a `default=lambda: {"zero": False}` slip — proved RED, `electric shipped with zero disabled` |
| **3 · an enabled rule ALWAYS runs** | there is NO skip branch: every rule is computed, and `switch_outcome` is the ONE place a verdict can be replaced (plus `switch_group_outcome` for the three group rules) | a per-batch bypass — a test asserts one rule off leaves the other twelve reporting |
| **4 · the 7 integrity rules are NOT switchable** | refused at the API BY NAME (422, the rule in `params`) AND forced back on inside `rule_switches` | a row written by a shell — proved RED, an unknown meter posting `disabled` instead of `error` |

**And the clause that is easiest to miss.** *"A disabled rule must state on the
read that it was disabled rather than vanish."* It is REPLACED, never dropped:
a new severity **`disabled`** with reason `disabled_by_tenant_setting`, ranked
below `not_evaluated` so it can never decide a row, carried into stored
`rule_outcomes` and summarised on the batch as `disabled_rules` — **beside**
`unevaluated_rules`, never inside it. A gap a clerk should chase and a check the
utility retired are different facts; the argument is written out at the
`DISABLED` constant.

**Version.** Shipped at `2.52.0` — deliberately NOT bumped by this lane. Eleven
CR-038 lanes are in flight on the same two literals (`package.json` /
`pyproject.toml`, G35's pair), and a per-lane `fix` digit would be eleven
conflicts over one number. The CR-038 close-out owns step 7.

**Raised, not chosen: `OQ-417`.** `generation_channel` is the mirror image of
`export_not_net` — same shape, same severity, no threshold — and the PO locked
seven checks by name, not eight. It is switchable today because that is what the
ruling says. The worked case for the sitting: *a solar inverter reports 612 kWh;
a utility can currently switch off the check that stops that being filed as a
customer's consumption.*

**Also filed:** `DEF-806` (a lost `/**` in `endpoints.ts` made every frontend
test unable to COLLECT — no gate in this repo parses TypeScript) and `DEF-807`
(this lane wrote to the shared checkout from an isolated worktree for twenty
minutes; restored by reverse-applying each edit and verified file by file).

**Classification (step 1): a CHANGE, with one live DEFECT inside it** — the
reads not landing on 2–3 tenants is reported behaviour, not a new requirement,
and is filed separately rather than folded in (see "the live one" below).

### What the trace established (measured, not assumed)

⚠ **A correction the trace made about ITSELF, recorded because the same class
of error is what this CR exists to prevent:** the first version reported
**eleven** writes inside the provisioning transaction. There are **SIXTEEN** —
the bill template, notice templates, notification settings, security policy and
read-validation thresholds were all missing from it, and all five are wired.
The count was wrong because the trace read only the opening stretch of the
function. **Answering the PO's question ("dont you have to create templates
and notification data") is what found it.**

| # | Finding | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **The sample estate is water · sewer · trash ONLY** — 49 water meters, three months of water reads | An electric+gas tenant signs up successfully and gets **nothing**; the seeder correctly refuses to plant services the utility does not sell. **The most likely cause of the reported reads gap** |
| 2 | **Signup offers 6 of the 10 services** (electric · water · gas · sewer · trash · broadband) | Storm water, **solar**, thermal and battery cannot be chosen at signup — and a solar utility is being onboarded now |
| 3 | **Jurisdiction (inside/outside city) can be written by NOTHING** | It decides an outside-city surcharge on every bill at an address; the bill run treats it unstated as an exception. Read side built, write side absent |
| 4 | **A premises owner is ONE free-text field** — no kind, no contact, no link | Three of the five occupancy states name an owner as the party who PAYS, so money is routed at an owner the product cannot identify |
| 5 | **Transfer and disconnect have tables and no number; move-in and move-out have NO RECORD AT ALL** | A clerk cannot quote a reference; nothing on a bill can point at the job that caused a change |
| 6 | **Size classes cover 4 services of 10** | A base charge is selected by service → account type → size class, so a service with no class cannot price by size |
| 7 | **Sub-areas are fully built, ruled and never demonstrated** — depth-two enforced, all 4 seeded rows top-level | The filter the PO asked for has nothing to filter; nobody discovers it works |
| 8 | **A failed block is recorded and NOT SURFACED** — outcomes live in `sample_data_runs`, no screen reads them | A tenant whose reads failed is indistinguishable from one that never asked for them |
| 9 | **The audit log carries TOTALS ONLY** for a run — no failing module, no reason, no code | The permanent trail can say a run went badly and cannot say what failed |
| 10 | Term, implementation and add-ons have **no column, table or screen** | Three of the four commercial dimensions sold have nowhere to live |
| 11 | Import accepts fields the seed never sends: coordinates, floor, square feet, state | Map has nothing to plot; the demo does not exercise those columns |
| 12 | The numbering docstring says **twenty-two**; the catalogue holds **twenty-five** | A comment that drifted — the behaviour is correct |

### What is ALREADY right, and must not be "fixed"

Recorded because a later lane could easily undo these thinking them gaps:
**block isolation works** (each block its own transaction, a failure is caught,
recorded and the loop continues — "one module must not stop the rest");
**the plant can never roll back the tenant**; **every block is
insert-what-is-missing**, so a re-run cannot double a utility's data; **money
rows are keyed** so a replay writes nothing; **occupancy is derived**, not
stored, so its absence on a unit is correct; **taxes are rate-less outside
Texas** deliberately; **the net meter and sub-meters are never read** on
purpose, so the ready-to-run billing month gains no phantom missing reads.

⚠⚠ **TWO OF THE TEN WERE NOT RATIFIED AND ARE NOT SEEDED.** Steam was put as
*"steam by thousand pounds per hour"* and battery as *"by kW and kWh together …
the pair is the class"* — a unit and a shape, with not one boundary named on

covers only what was shown (PO 2026-08-11). **OQ-560** and **OQ-561** are minted
and `apps/tenancy/service_size_classes.py` raises `NotImplementedError` naming
each. **A band boundary decides which base charge a customer pays; inventing one
is inventing money** — a 12,000 lb/hr hospital steam header and a 900 lb/hr
office riser pay the same base charge today, and so do a 5 kW / 13 kWh home
battery and a 100 kW / 400 kWh commercial pack.

**And the design consequence is the reusable part.** Three services seed zero
rows for three different reasons, and in a flat `{code, name}` fixture all three
look identical. `service_size_classes.UNBANDED_SERVICE_DIMENSIONS` is what keeps
them apart in code: **sewer RETURNS an empty tuple** (ruled to have none) and the
other two **RAISE** (nobody has said). Without that distinction the next lane
"finishes the list".

with 41 rows, not 40**, and switches the orphan off on S8. And `G-250` keeps its
"(residential)" suffix, because BR-TEN-072 forbids renames in seed data.

### Step 4 · THE CELERY QUESTION, ANSWERED — no cron jobs are needed, and here is why

The PO's sentence assumes two billing cycles need *"multiple cron jobs run by
celery"*. **They do not, and the reason is worth stating plainly because it also
says what celery IS for here.**

* **A bill run is an INLINE service call, not a scheduled job.**
  `apps/billing/runs.py` says so in its own docstring: *"It runs INLINE. There is
  no job runner in this project."* All five phases — create → prepare → apply
  decisions → calculate → release gate → issue — are ordinary function calls that
  return when they are done.
* **The seeder ALREADY drives all five**, through the same doors S31 uses:
  `create_run` → `prepare_run` → `calculate_run` → `authorise_release` →
  `release_run`. It does not write invoice rows. **So a second cycle is a second
  pass of a loop that already exists** — `_periods_to_bill()` returns the periods
  marked `billed`, and today exactly one is.
* **Celery's real job here is the SEED ITSELF.** `apps/tenancy/tasks.py` puts the
  whole sample load on a worker so signup returns immediately (CR-017). One job,
  walking blocks in dependency order — which is precisely the ordering the PO's
  sentence describes.
* **Beat/cron is deliberately NOT configured** and that is recorded, not
  accidental. Scheduled billing for a live tenant is a different feature with a
  run-exactly-once constraint; a demo seed is a one-off.

**So the answer to *"how will you handle this"*: one background job, two
sequential inline runs, with the money cases written between them — not two
cron schedules.** The ordering the PO gave IS the implementation order.

money case must be written at the stage where a clerk would have written it** —
a refund seeded after both runs is a row; a refund seeded between them is a
history.

| 1b | Customers block | **master + its sub-accounts** | The master must exist before the run that consolidates it |
| 2 | Reads block, month 1 | ✅ *(exists)* | — |
| 3 | **Billing run 1** | ✅ *(exists — June)* | — |

| 5 | Reads block, month 2 | **new** | The PO's *"add meter reading for second month"* |
| 6 | **Billing run 2** | **new** — flip July's `billed` flag | The second cycle now bills an estate carrying a credit, a refund and a correction, which is the whole point |
| 7 | Reads block, month 3 | ✅ *(exists — August, committed and unbilled)* | **Left for the PO to run.** Acceptance item 4, unchanged |

## CR-041 — the list toolbar behaves the same way on every screen

**Arrived** 2026-08-27, from the PO, twice, in escalating terms.

> *"can you run the - where else is this class used the same way - and fix the
> issues - actually fix the bug dont only write it"*

> *"tool bar - descrption, search, filter, column seelctor, pagination, export -
> - we need to ensure it behavios in a simialr way everywhere - currently it is
> lot differnt that many places - you ahve to do - where else is this class used
> the same way. and create a task list and fix all those not just report it"*

### The sweep they asked for, RUN — `.met-filters`

**Three live sites. Two were found separately, a day apart, and neither swept the
others. The third had never been looked at.**

| Site | Found | State |
|---|---|---|
| `UnitsListPage` | 2026-08-26 | fixed then, with the conclusion written into the file |
| `ReadsListPage` | 2026-08-27 | fixed by the reads lane — **the PO reported it as a defect first** |
| `UploadReadsWizard` | **2026-08-27, by this sweep** | ✅ **fixed now** |

`.met-filters` is `display:grid` with
`grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr))`. On a **filter
panel**, which is what it was written for, that is right. On anything else it
stretches each child to a 200px column: on two list screens it consumed the whole
toolbar row; in the upload wizard it spread four segment pills across the panel
instead of grouping them. **Same class, same misuse, three screens, three
separate discoveries.**

⚠ **`grep` FOR THE CLASS TAKES FOUR SECONDS. Nothing in this repo does it.** The
first two fixes each wrote down the diagnosis and neither asked *where else*.

### ⚠ AND THE FIRST MEASUREMENT OF THE WIDER PROBLEM WAS WRONG

A grep for `table-toolbar` in each page file found it on **2 of 11** list pages
and suggested every other screen hand-rolls its toolbar. **That is false.**
`DataTable` **renders the toolbar itself** — search, the filter slot, a spacer,
the download slot and the column chooser — so every list that uses `DataTable`
gets the same row by construction. Recorded because it is the shape of error this
CR exists to fix: *the first measurement of a consistency problem was itself
inconsistent with the code.*

### The real inconsistency, measured across all 28 tables

The toolbar is shared. **What differs is what each page hands it.**

| Capability | Tables with it | The gap |
|---|---|---|
| Search | **24 / 28** | — |
| **`searchPlaceholder`** | **7 / 24** | ⚠ **THE BIG ONE.** Seventeen searchable lists print the generic *"Search this list"*, so the box never says what it matches. B14 rule 19 (DEF-510) already requires the list's own prompt. One line per page |
| `filterBarSlot` | 15 / 28 | The five customer-flow tabs — Disconnects, Move-ins, Move-outs, New connects, Transfers — have search and no filter while their sibling list pages have both |
| `downloadSlot` | 15 / 28 | Same five, plus Service requests, Template catalog and Discounts, cannot export while their siblings can |
| Column chooser | 28 / 28 | ✅ `DataTable` always renders it |
| Pagination | `DataTable`'s | ✅ shared |
| Description at 80% | mixed | `max-w-prose` survives in `WizardFrame`, `SettingsSampleData`, `UnitPricingPanel`, `moveReadsCapture` — the wrong cap, which is DEF-900's own finding one screen over |

### The task list

| # | Task | Size |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | ✅ **DONE** — `.met-filters`' third site swept | one div |
| **2** | Every searchable list declares its own `searchPlaceholder`, naming the fields it actually matches — **and where the config cannot match what the prompt would claim, the prompt says what is true and the gap is filed** (the reads lane's own precedent, DEF-950) | 17 pages |
| **3** | The five customer-flow tabs gain the filter their sibling list pages have, or state why not | 5 tabs |
| **4** | The eight tables with no export gain one, or state why not | 8 tables |
| **5** | `max-w-prose` → `max-w-measure` wherever it caps a description (B14 rule 18) | 4 files |
| **6** | **A guard, because this is the whole point.** A list that declares `searchFields` and no `searchPlaceholder` fails — the same shape as G31's ceiling. Without it, task 2 is undone by the next new screen | 1 gate |

thing that was fixed once and recurred somewhere else, because nothing asked the

* **`_refuse_replace_for_assets` / OQ-326** — correct, and now redundant because the
  general refusal covers it.
* **Lanes building right now:** checked against `git log` on the integration branch
  and the four in-flight worktrees. No lane holds `write_modes.py`,
  `import_runs.py`'s stage-4 block, `readsImportRail.tsx` or `ImportWorkflowPage.tsx`.
  Nothing to stop or let land.

### ⚖️ THE JUDGMENT CALL, MADE AND WRITTEN DOWN — the option goes, the behaviour stays

The PO's sentence is about an **option**: *"replace **option** is not required"*.
It is not a statement that the deactivate-what-is-missing behaviour was wrong —
they ruled that behaviour into existence six days earlier with a worked figure.

For **reads** the two come apart cleanly, because `replace` there does *nothing
that `upsert` does not do* (that is the whole of OQ-418). Removing it removes
nothing. It is deleted outright.

For **premises and units** they do NOT come apart: `replace` is the only thing in
this product that retires a record the utility's file no longer carries. So:

* **the OPTION is withdrawn from every screen and refused at the API boundary by
  name**, so no caller can reach it and there is no unsafe default (hard-won law 3);
* **the BEHAVIOUR is left standing in `import_runs.py`**, unreachable, with
  BR-MET-099 amended to say exactly that;
* **`OQ-580` asks the PO the question the removal raises** — *how does a utility
  retire premises it no longer serves?* — with the three options and the figure.

**Why not simply delete it:** destroying a signed capability on an inferred scope
is not reversible in one line, and the PO's sentence does not say the behaviour
was wrong. **Why not simply leave the mode reachable by API:** a mode no screen
offers but any POST can reach is a control with no consequence preview in front
of it, which is the opposite of what BR-MET-099 itself requires. The refusal is
the honest middle, and it is the **exact shape already ratified for the assets
targets** (OQ-326), generalised rather than invented.

### Step 5 · SIZED

**Not a fast path** — it touches a signed rule and it changes what the server
accepts. Six tasks:

| # | Task | Size |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Backend: both constants drop to two; `replace` refused **by name**, naming OQ-580; BR-MET-099's branch kept and documented as unreachable | 2 files |
| 2 | Frontend: **ONE shared write-mode control**, born Route B, used by BOTH rails — the same two options, the same order, the same words, the same place | 1 new component + 3 files |
| 3 | Catalogues: 8 keys retired × 11 locales | 11 files |
| 4 | Tests, RED first: the constant, the refusal, the control, and the historical row that still renders | 2 suites |
| 5 | Rules: BR-MET-099 amended · BR-MET-127 reworded · **BR-MET-210 minted** · OQ-580 · OQ-326 moot · DEF-1020 | 4 files |
| 6 | **Step 7 — VERSION** `2.63.0 → 2.64.0`, four literals + `CHANGELOG.md` | 5 files |

**In plain English, with the figure, for the PO:** *today every import offers three
choices and the third one — "Replace, and retire what is missing" — is the only
thing that can deactivate the 28 premises in your file's district that your
spreadsheet no longer lists. After this change every import offers two, in the
same words, in the same place, on step 1. The 28 premises are then retired one at
a time by hand, unless you tell us otherwise (OQ-580).*

### Step 8 · ROLLBACK, STATED BEFORE SHIPPING

One revert of this CR's commits restores the third option on both rails. **No data
migration either way** — the mode is a `TextField` with no `choices`, historical
rows keep whatever they were written with, and BR-MET-099's implementation is
never removed, so re-offering it is re-adding a string to two tuples and one list.

> corner"*

> whera re base charges, discounts, refunds, credit, - if there are nothing to
> report we have to show nothing to report; Im also ging you screenshot of

---

### Step 1 · CLASSIFY — and the two "absence" statements are NOT the same statement

The PO said two things about empty sections in two different messages, and read
in isolation each looks like the opposite of the other:

> *"you ahve to remove - Filters that arrive later … Export and column choices"*

> *"if there are nothing to report we have to show nothing to report"*

**They are consistent, and the distinction they draw is the useful part of this
CR.** Two kinds of emptiness have been rendered the same way:

| The emptiness | What the screen currently says | The PO's ruling |
|---|---|---|
| **A FEATURE WE HAVE NOT BUILT** — "the design also filters by cycle, by billing run and by a date range … each their own piece of work" | a titled panel explaining our backlog to a utility clerk | **REMOVE IT.** A clerk cannot act on it, did not ask for it, and it occupies the screen every single visit |
| **A SECTION WITH NO DATA IN IT** — this bill has no corrections, no discounts, no refunds, no credits | in some places a sentence, in others the section is simply absent | **SAY "nothing to report".** An absent section is indistinguishable from a broken page |

⚠ **A LANE THAT READS ONLY THE FIRST MESSAGE WILL DELETE THE WRONG THINGS.** The
Corrections tab's *"No credit note or replacement bill is recorded against this
bill"* is the second kind and is **exactly right** — it is the model for what the
other sections should do, not a candidate for removal.

⚠ **AND THIS NARROWS `ArrivesWith`, WHICH IS REPO-WIDE.** `G38` counts stated
absences (`UNTRACKED_BASELINE = 71`) and hard-won law 2 is why they exist: a
component that renders nothing is a feature that silently does not exist. The
ruling does not repeal that — it says **where the note is allowed to live**. An
unbuilt feature is stated in the REGISTER (a defect row, an OQ, a story), not on
the customer-facing screen. That is a change to an established convention and is
recorded as such below.

⚠ **G38 CANNOT TELL A PAID DEBT FROM A DELETED NOTICE.** Its baseline "may only
fall", and deleting a panel lowers the count exactly as building the feature
would. So every removal under this CR must land with the defect row that now
carries the absence, named in the commit — otherwise the ratchet records progress
that did not happen.

### CR-040 · WAVE E TASK 17 — LANDED 2026-08-27. The panel names ONE cause again

**Appended, not edited** — this register is append-only. The wave E table above
is amended in place for E17's STATE only, which is `DEF-978`'s own rule applied
to the defect that taught it.

**The task read:** *"The seeding panel names the new blocks rather than reporting
a module short."*

⚠ **WHAT WAS ACTUALLY SHORT WAS NOT THE PANEL. IT WAS THE GRAPH BEHIND IT, AND
MEASURING THAT FIRST IS WHAT KEPT THIS TO FIVE EDGES.** The Sample data panel
(S8 → Company profile) has rendered one line per BLOCK since CR-039 wave B, so
the three blocks waves C and D added — a refund, an overcharge correction and a
second billing cycle — **did each get a line**. What they did not get is an
**edge**. `BLOCK_DEPENDENCIES` held ten of the fourteen blocks and named none of
them.

`_root_for` walks declared edges only, and its own docstring chooses that
direction deliberately: *"a missing edge makes a block look like a ROOT, never
like a consequence"*. So on the commonest real failure — a first bill run that
cannot issue because a tax authority has no liability account — the panel drew
**four "Start here" markers over one cause**, on the screen whose entire job is
to say which line to read first. Wave B built it to answer the PO's *"we need to
look at what of 1 job fails"*; two waves later it was answering it four times.

**Delivered:**

| | What landed |
|---|---|
| **Five edges** | `payments:seed_sample_refund` → the Accounts and Payments blocks · `billing:seed_sample_correction` → the Accounts and first Bills blocks · `billing:seed_sample_second_cycle` → the Meter reads block. **Every quote was already in the code** — each is the sentence its own seeder prints at a person when it refuses — so CR-039 wave B's standard (*"do NOT invent a dependency graph nobody ratified"*) holds, and `test_cr039__every_declared_edge_is_quoted_from_the_file_it_cites` greps all five back out |
| **`ROOT_BLOCKS`** | The four blocks that genuinely depend on nothing, declared. In a dict that only holds edges, *"this block needs nothing"* and *"nobody has looked at this block"* are the **same absence** — which is exactly how three blocks landed edgeless with two tests over the graph and neither able to object: both ask *is every declared edge TRUE?*, and a graph can be perfectly honest and half empty |
| **The ratchet** | `06-backend/tests/test_cr040_e17_seeding_panel_blocks.py`, 4 cases. A fifteenth block that is neither edged nor declared a root goes RED, and so does a block that is somehow both |
| **The screen, proved** | 3 cases in `SettingsSampleDataBlocks.test.tsx` over the four-block money cascade: all four named on their own lines (billing and payments each appear **twice**, which a per-module render collapses), **one** *"Start here"*, three consequences naming the bill run, and three *"fix the part it is waiting on first"* notes |
| **A stale comment corrected** | `SettingsSampleData.tsx` said *"Four of the eleven blocks share a module with another"*. It is **eleven of fourteen** — metering has two, customers, billing and payments three each — so the comment understated the very problem it exists to describe, by a factor of three (hard-won law 1) |

⚠ **THE EDGE THAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT IS THE DECISION.** The obvious one is
`billing:seed_sample_second_cycle → billing:seed_sample_records`, and it is
**wrong**. Both billing blocks call the same `_preconditions`, so a tenant with
no cycle, no attributable actor or an unmapped tax authority fails **both** — but
that is a **COMMON CAUSE, not a dependency**. July bills from July's own reads
and needs no June invoice; the second cycle exists to bill an estate with a
financial past, which is a matter of ORDER (task D14) and not of prerequisite.
The wrong edge would have told an operator that fixing the first run fixes the
second and marked cycle two a CONSEQUENCE — *"retry the root first"* — when what
fixes both is the setup fact underneath them. **Two roots and one fix is the
honest report.** Recorded as this lane's judgment in the decision log, not as a
ruling.

**FOUND ON THE WAY — `DEF-1090`, and it had been RED for a day.**
`test_cr039__a_retry_that_fails_again_records_the_new_failure` asserted
`len(row.blocks) == 1` on the **billing MODULE's** ledger row. Billing owned one
block when that was written and has owned three since waves C and D, so the suite
guarding this very panel read `3 == 1` over a product behaving perfectly. Its own
failure message was always about the RETRIED block; that is what it asserts now,
plus a second assertion — derived from `SAMPLE_MODULES`, not typed — that a retry
does not quietly drop the module's other blocks off the row. **The same shape as
`DEF-976` three days earlier: a test restating a count that is owned elsewhere.**

⚠ **SEVEN ENTRIES WERE WRITTEN, NOT EIGHT, AND WHAT HAPPENED TWICE WHILE THEY
WERE BEING WRITTEN IS THE MORE USEFUL FINDING.** CR-042's `2.64.0` was cut by its
own lane, and CR-041's `2.65.0` by the integrator, **both between this lane's

the rule working, and it is the same shape as `DEF-932` on the same day (*"the
2.64.1 that two lanes cut and the merge lost"*).
**The lesson for the next reconciliation, and it is cheap: take the measurement
AND the digits in ONE commit, and push it before writing a word of prose.** A
version number is a shared resource that any lane can claim while you are
describing it. Both renumbers were mechanical and no wave's entry changed a word.

`2.63.0`.** The version was written down in three places and taken in none. That
is `13-change-process.md` step 7 in one commit: *"the one usually skipped"*, and
the reason a gate refuses a CR marked done with no version. ⚠ **It was then taken,

> *"One time bill, budget bill, fix bill, can you define suer friendly process -
> workflows - that take carae of bill generation data, steps, data colelctions,
> impact of such action on finance, reading open balance etc - you also need to fien
> UI for it as per tailwind components - test it it works"*

### Step 1 · CLASSIFY — a CHANGE, and the three are not in the same state

This is a **change**: three surfaces exist and none of them was designed as a
workflow. It is not a defect — nothing here is broken against a signed rule; what
is missing is the process itself.

### Step 0 · THE MEASUREMENT, TAKEN BEFORE ANY DESIGN

All three tabs are **built and partly working**, not stubs — and each already
states, in its own words, the one thing that stops it being a workflow:

| Tab | Lines | Endpoints wired | What it says it cannot do — verbatim from the shipped copy |
|---|---|---|---|
| **One-time bill** | 736 | 4 | *"A one-time bill can be drafted but not sent yet. The due date comes from the billing cycle's payment terms, and a one-time bill belongs to no cycle — so there is no rule yet for when it falls due, and a guessed due date would decide when a late fee starts."* · and *"Charge lines are never typed by hand on any bill. Every line comes from the customer's plan or from one of your charge codes."* |
| **Budget bills** | 491 | 8 | *"Enrolling everybody at once and importing a list are not here: no account records which plan it is on, so there is nothing to work through. The yearly-increase cap is a setting and lives in Settings."* |
| **Fix a bill** | 679 | 9 | *"Cancelling a bill outright is a different act with its own rule and is not offered here. Adding your own reason codes needs the reference table that is not built yet."* |

⚠ **THE THREE BLOCKERS ARE OF THREE DIFFERENT KINDS, and that decides the shape of
this CR.** One-time bill is blocked on a **RULE THE PO HAS NOT GIVEN** (when does a
cycle-less bill fall due). Budget bills is blocked on **MISSING DATA** (nothing
records which budget plan an account is on). Fix a bill is blocked on a **SCOPE
DECISION** (is cancelling part of this workflow or its own act). Only the first
needs the PO before anything can be built.

### Step 3 · WHAT THE PO ASKED FOR, unpacked into the five things they named

For **each** of the three:

1. **Bill generation data** — what the workflow needs before it can produce a bill,
   and where each field comes from.
2. **Steps** — the wizard, in the house shape (`WizardFrame`, one primary per step,
   one transactional commit, BR-SHL-018/019).
3. **Data collection** — what a clerk types, what is derived, and what is refused.
   ⚠ Bounded by a rule this product already has: *"Charge lines are never typed by
   hand on any bill"* — so a one-time bill's lines come from charge codes, never from
   free text, and the workflow must make that easy rather than fight it.
4. **Impact on finance** — every one of these three MOVES MONEY, so each step must
   say what it will post before it commits (B14 rule 11, the consequence preview),
   and the ledger effect must be stated in the review-ledger row in plain English
   with a figure.
5. **Reading open balances** — ⚠ **this one is not free.** `DEF-1081`, filed today,
   records that the bill run's own step 2 **cannot show what a customer already
   owes** because nothing gathers it. The same gather is what these three workflows
   need, so it is one piece of work serving four surfaces, not four.

Plus **UI in Tailwind components** per B14 — ⚠ and rule 21's migration clause is per
file: a utility in a file absent from `route-b-migrated.txt` renders as **nothing**
(`DEF-974`). And **tested**, which for a money path means RED-first and a golden run
before and after.

### Step 5 · WHAT NEEDS THE PO BEFORE A LINE IS WRITTEN

**One question, and it is the one the product already asked and never got an answer
to:** *when is a one-time bill due?* A cycle bill takes its due date from the cycle's
payment terms; a one-time bill belongs to no cycle. The shipped copy says a guessed
due date would decide when a late fee starts — which is why it was never guessed.

**STATUS: DESIGNED 2026-08-27 — the three workflows are defined; §4 is BUILT; one
PO ruling blocks the last step of the first third.**

### Step 6 · WHAT THE DESIGN PASS PRODUCED (2026-08-27)

**`04-docs/05-modules/07-billing/10-cr044-workflow-design.md`** answers all five
named things for each of the three tabs: bill generation data (with the source of
every field), the steps as `WizardFrame` flows under BR-SHL-018/019, what a clerk
types versus what is derived versus what is refused, the finance consequence each
commit must state before it commits, and the open balance.

**Three findings changed the shape of the work, and two of them shrank it:**

1. **"Reading open balances" is a READER, not a gather — and it is BUILT.**
   `payments_seam.prior_position_for_account` already computes the position and
   FOOTS by construction, but it answers about an INVOICE and has exactly one
   caller (`issue.py:1306`). All four surfaces have no invoice to ask about, so
   `apps/billing/open_balance.py` changes the question and delegates the
   arithmetic untouched. ❄️ WE-1's **45.00** arrears half comes back
   byte-identical to what the bill prints; ❄️ GT-16's migrated **267.30** comes
   back on an account with no invoice at all, which is the case an invoice-only
   read cannot see. 7 backend cases + 5 frontend cases, RED-proved.
   First caller wired: budget eligibility, rendered on the Budget Bills tab.
   **`DEF-1081`'s gathering half is closed; its three step-2 tabs are not this
   lane's and stay open.**
2. **The Budget Bills blocker is a WIRING gap, not missing data (`DEF-1180`).**
   The account→unit→plan chain exists and both ends are published. What is left
   is a policy call, `OQ-640`, not a schema change.
3. **Cancelling a bill is proposed as its own act (`OQ-641`)**, moved from a
   paragraph above the form to a named, disabled choice on the reason list.

**Filed:** `DEF-1180` (the wiring gap) · `DEF-1181` (enrolment keyed off a raw
account uuid, never shown back as a name) · `DEF-1182` (`file_defect.py`
allocates into an active block) · `DEF-1183` (the catalogues are off-format and
locale parity is already broken).
**Routed to the PO:** `OQ-241` (unchanged — when a one-time bill falls due) ·
`OQ-640` · `OQ-641`. **❄️ golden-verify 33 PASS / 0 FAIL, before and after.**

**NOT BUILT, and deliberately:** the three wizards themselves. The PO asked for
the process to be *defined*, and a wizard built before its shape is agreed is the
expensive way to discover it is wrong. §6 of the design gives the order of work.

## CR-045 — The toolbar standard: one search, one filter set, one download glyph, on all 27 lists

**Arrived** 2026-08-27, from the Product Owner, across four messages during a live
walk of v2.73.0.

> *"in all tool bar - we have to increase the length of search - currently it is very
> small and text insught is cutting. second for each page we need to decide what will
> be search cateria - can you show me page by page - i want search by address as well
> with other logical search by cases"*

> *"show me on screen or create HTML - look at all tool bars and lets standard it
> across application"*

> *"In tool bat you need filter also and icon forn downlon csv - please udpaste your
> document"*

> *"Standard propose by you is good with me; Search — page by page - most fo these are
> good; in account you will need phone numner of email ID also ; I agree with all -
> The standard, if you confirm it; I want to write another CR - prepare all tasks for
> all screens and excute in waves"*

### Step 1 · CLASSIFY — a CHANGE, with three DEFECTS carried inside it

**A change**, because the standard itself is new: no signed rule said the search box
had one width, that every list carries filters, or that a prompt may not name a field
the server does not match. Those are new agreements.

**But three of the findings are DEFECTS and are classified as such**, per the change
process step 1 (*"when it is ambiguous it is a DEFECT, not a change"* — filing our own
error as a "change" converts it into the customer's new requirement):

| | What | Why a defect, not a change |
|---|---|---|
| **D-1** | `.table-search input { min-width: 220px }` is orphaned — no component renders `.table-search`, so all 27 search boxes fall back to the browser default (~170px) | A declared rule stopped applying during the B14 rule 21 Tailwind migration. Nothing asked for that |
| **D-2** | Bills, Payments and both Assets tabs each name a search field the server does not match | The prompt was written before the leg it describes. Hard-won law 1: a comment claiming a guarantee is not the guarantee |
| **D-3** | Units silently searches premises address; Premises silently searches city | The mirror of D-2 — the server does more than the prompt admits, so nobody tries it |

D-1 is owned by the page-header/toolbar lane already running. D-2 and D-3 are this CR's
wave B and C.

### Step 2 · WHAT SIGNED STATEMENT IS BEING REVERSED

**None.** Nothing here contradicts a ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure — no money rule, no
rounding, no golden test. No HUMAN-GUIDE §6 re-sign is required.

Two signed statements are **extended, not reversed**:

* **B14 rule 4** (`↓` download) is already ratified and is currently UNENFORCED. This
  CR enforces it. That is applying a rule, not changing one.
* **B14 rule 19** (a list's own search prompt) already requires each list to declare a
  prompt. This CR says what a lawful prompt looks like.

One statement of MINE is corrected, and it was wrong when I published it:

> ⚠ **R7 said "at most four named terms". Service requests names FIVE — *"Search
> request #, name, address, phone, or email…"* — and I marked that row CORRECT in the
> same document.** A rule contradicted by a row the same page calls correct is not a
> rule. **R7 is amended to FIVE**, which is what the measured, working screen does.

### Step 3 · IMPACT — and the one the PO added

The PO accepted the page-by-page table with one addition:

> *"in account you will need phone numner of email ID also"*

**Measured:** `customers.selectors.account_list` matches `account_no`, `customer_no`,
contact `full_name`, and unit ids (which carry premises address and meter #). It
matches **neither phone nor email**. `Contact.email` (CITextField) and `Contact.phone`
(TextField) both exist and are both marked **PII**.

**Precedent exists and is ratified:** the service-requests list already searches
`applicant_phone` and `applicant_email`. So searching these two columns is not a new
posture, and no new open question is minted.

⚠ **THE PHONE LEG NEEDS NORMALISATION AND THIS CR STATES THE APPROACH RATHER THAN
GUESSING LATER.** A clerk types `555-1234`; the stored value may be `(555) 123-4567`.
A raw `icontains` finds nothing and reports "no results", which is worse than no
feature. **The leg strips every non-digit from BOTH the search term and the compared
column, and matches on the digits.** The email leg needs none of this — `citext`
already makes it case-insensitive.

⚠ **ACCOUNTS NOW NAMES SEVEN THINGS AND THE BOX HOLDS FIVE.** Account #, customer #,
name, address, meter #, phone, email. R7 caps the PROMPT at five; R4 forbids matching
what the prompt does not name. Both hold if the prompt names the five a clerk reaches
for and the box carries the full list where it can be read:

> **`Search account #, name, address, phone or email…`** with a help affordance stating
> *"Also finds a customer # or a meter #."*

That is this CR's one piece of new UI, and it is deliberately small.

### Step 4 · WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT AND IS NOW WRONG

* **Nothing is data-wrong.** No stored value changes; no bill, read or ledger row is
  affected. This CR writes no data at all.
* **One test changes by ruling:** `ReadsPage.test.tsx:409` asserts the Reads prompt
  does **not** contain `"address"`. That was correct when Reads searched only a meter
  number. The PO's request reverses it, so the assertion is rewritten with the ruling
  and its date cited — never deleted.
* **Lanes building right now:** the page-header/toolbar lane holds D-1 and the shared
  `DataTable`/`DownloadButton` files. **Wave A is that lane's, not a new one** — a
  second lane in those files is the shared-tree failure CLAUDE.md law 11 documents
  seven times.

### Step 5 · SIZE, IN PLAIN ENGLISH WITH A FIGURE

**27 lists · 6 waves · 26 tasks.** The two changes that fix all 27 screens at once are
one CSS declaration and one shared component. The real work is the seven filter sets
and the six server search legs — everything else is copy.

⚠ **AMENDED 2026-08-27 (DEF-1702): 6 waves · 34 tasks.** Wave D was sized at seven
filter sets from a walk of the screens. A mechanised sweep of every screen rendering a
`DataTable` — printed inside wave D so it can be re-run rather than re-walked — measures
**28 such screens, 11 of them with no filter control of any kind**, and only three of
those eleven were in the wave. Wave D is 15 tasks, so this CR is 34. **The figure that
was wrong is the one that was counted by looking.**

### Step 6 · EXECUTE — the waves

**Wave order is a dependency, not a preference.** Every later wave assumes a search box
wide enough to hold its prompt and a toolbar with room for its filters, so **A lands
first**. B–E are independent of each other with ONE exception, stated below.

⚠ **THE LOCALE FILES ARE THE COLLISION POINT.** Eleven catalogues
(`07-frontend/src/i18n/locales/*.json`) are touched by waves B, C, D and E. Four lanes
editing eleven shared JSON files is DEF-165's mechanism with extra steps. **Rule of
execution: a wave's locale keys are written by that wave's own lane, in ONE commit, at
the END of the wave** — never incrementally, never by two lanes at once.

⚠ **AND R3 SETS THE ORDER WITHIN WAVE C: the server leg lands BEFORE the prompt that
names it.** A prompt shipped first is a promise the product does not keep, which is the
exact defect (D-2) this CR exists to remove. One commit may carry both; the prompt may
never lead.

#### Wave A — the shared frame · 4 tasks · fixes all 27 screens

| Task | What |
|---|---|
| **A.1** | The search box: `flex: 1 1 20rem; min-width: 15rem; max-width: 32rem` in the shared toolbar. Wants 320px, shrinks to 240px before anything wraps, never exceeds 512px. Assert the clear ✕ tracks the new width |
| **A.2** | Delete the orphaned `.table-search`, `.table-search input`, `.table-search-clear` rules; lower G31's declared-class ceiling by the number removed |
| **A.3** | `DownloadButton` → `↓` icon-only, `Download CSV` as `aria-label` + `title`, both the plain and the CSV/PDF menu variants. Glyph imported from `components/icons.tsx` (B14 rule 15 / G37), never inline |
| **A.4** | Toolbar slot ORDER fixed in `DataTable`: search · filters · spacer · ↓ · ▥ |

#### Wave B — copy only, where the server is already right · 3 tasks

**STATUS 2026-08-27 (v2.79.0): B.1 and B.2 are BUILT. B.3 is NOT, and cannot be
— see DEF-1705.**

| Task | What | State |
|---|---|---|
| **B.1** | Grammar fixes to `Search <term>, <term> or <term>…`: Routes, Cycles, Templates, Chart of accounts | ✅ BUILT. Each prompt was measured against its own selector rather than assumed: Routes and Cycles match `code \| name`; the template catalogue matches name, code, category and used-by; the chart of accounts filters client-side on code and name. All four name four terms or fewer (R7) |
| **B.2** | Prompts that now tell the truth about legs that already exist: Premises (+ city), Units (+ address) — this closes **D-3** | ✅ BUILT, and **D-3 is closed**. `premises_queryset` really does match `city__icontains` and `units_list` really does match `premises__address_line` — both since long before this CR, both unsaid until now |
| **B.3** | ~~Rate schedules: name `code`, which the server already matches~~ | ⛔ **UNBUILDABLE — DEF-1705** |

⚠ **B.3 WAS WRONG WHEN I WROTE IT, AND IT IS WRONG IN A WAY THIS CR EXISTS TO
PREVENT.** `rating.selectors.schedule_list` filters on `name__icontains` alone;
one layer deeper, **`Tariff` has no `code` column at all** — its fields are
tenant, name, service, account_type_id, is_sample and the timestamps. The
`code` this row means belongs to `Plan` and to `Charge`, which are different
tables and really do search `code | name`. Rate schedules sit on screen right
beside both, which is very likely how the row got written: **it is true of its
neighbours and false of itself.**

Both ways of closing it were refused and the reasons are the rule:

* **Ship the copy** → that is **D-2**, a prompt naming a field the server does
  not match, recreated by the wave written to remove D-2.
* **Add the leg** → `Q(code__icontains=…)` on `Tariff` is a `FieldError` at
  runtime. Making it real is a column, a migration, a per-tenant uniqueness
  rule and a decision about what code every existing schedule gets. That is a
  change with a schema in it, and choosing the answer is a prime-directive
  violation.

So `rating.rates.searchPlaceholder` and `searchFields: ["name"]` are left
**exactly as they are, because they are already exactly true**, and the finding
is recorded in `schedule_list`'s own docstring where the next lane will look.

⚠ **AND THE PREVENTION IS ALREADY IN THIS CR, IN THE WRONG ORDER.** Task **F.1**
is a gate that reads each list's declared prompt terms against its server match
fields and fails when they disagree — it would have refused B.3 on the commit
that wrote it. F.1 is scheduled in the LAST wave, after every copy wave it
would have protected. **A gate that checks a wave belongs before that wave.**

| **C.6** | **Reads — address, account # and unit legs.** The PO's original request. Rewrites `ReadsPage.test.tsx:409` citing this ruling |

#### Wave D — filters for the **NINE** lists that have none · 15 tasks

⚠ **THIS LINE READ "the seven lists that have none · 7 tasks" UNTIL 2026-08-27,
AND IT WAS SHORT BY TWO SCREENS AND WRONG ABOUT FOUR MORE (DEF-1702).** The seven
were sized from a WALK of the screens; the number below is from a SWEEP of the
code, and the sweep is printed here so the count can be re-derived instead of
re-walked. That re-derivation IS the prevention DEF-1702 asks for.

**THE SWEEP — run it, do not trust this paragraph.** One line per screen under
`07-frontend/src/features` that renders `<DataTable`, asking two questions of
each: does its `TableConfig` declare `filters:`, and does the file render a
`<FilterBar`?

```bash
cd 07-frontend/src && for f in $(grep -rl '<DataTable' features --include='*.tsx' \
      | grep -v '\.test\.'); do
  printf '%-58s decl=%s fbar=%s\n' "$f" \
    "$(grep -cE '^\s*filters:\s*(\[|\w+,)' "$f")" \
    "$(grep -c '<FilterBar' "$f")"
done | sort
```

above, which asks only whether a `<FilterBar` is rendered and so scores an
inert control identically to a bare screen, and scores a working bespoke panel

**`10-scripts/cr045_toolbar_sweep.py` replaces that one-liner** and reports a
SHAPE per screen — `wired` · `custom` · `declared` · `inert` · `bare` —
because those five have five different owners. Measured at `21498f1`:

Every wave is independently revertable and none writes data. A is one CSS declaration
and one component; B is copy; C adds OR-legs that can be removed without touching what
they were added beside; D and E add capabilities that render only when declared, so
reverting a declaration removes the control. **No migration, no data write, no money
path.** The riskiest single change is C.1's phone normalisation, and its blast radius
is one OR-leg on one list.

meter-upload walkthrough. The fourth confirmed the logic and asked for the work.

### ⚠ THE FIFTH MESSAGE WIDENED THIS FROM ONE UPLOAD TO FOUR, AND IT IS THE ANSWER TO A QUESTION WE RAISED

The meter ruling's decision-log entry closed with: *"Premises, units and accounts all have numbering series
too, and all three still take their identifier from the file. The reasoning reads across, and applying it
would be widening a scope the PO did not widen."* It was raised on the walkthrough page as one line for the
PO to settle. **They have settled it: the same logic applies to all four.** Recorded here so nobody later
reads the widening as a lane's initiative.

**All four series exist already** (`core.numbering.SERIES_CATALOG`): `premises` (`P-{00000}`), `unit`
(`U-{00000}`), `asset`, `account` (`AC-{YYYY}-{00000}`). Nothing new has to be invented for any of them —
this change makes each series the ONLY path rather than the fallback.

### Step 1 · CLASSIFY — a **CHANGE**, in three clauses, and none of them is a defect

| # | The statement | Kind | Why not a defect |
|---|---|---|---|
| i | The identifier is issued by the tenant's series, never taken from the file — **on all four uploads** | **New requirement** | The old behaviour was ruled, built and correct; this reverses the ruling, it does not correct a mistake |
| ii | A blank unit still loads, into inventory | **Reversal, then withdrawn** | The PO reversed `BR-AST-045` and then reversed the reversal in the same exchange. Net effect: **nothing changes.** Recorded so the round trip is visible, not hidden |
| iii | A row naming a record already on file is **rejected** in Insert new only | **New requirement** | `AST.NUMBER_ON_FILE` warns today *by design* (`DEF-543`) — the mode was unknown at stage 3. That was a correct build against a constraint that has since moved |
| iv | Four separate documents instead of one | **UI / copy only** | Still real work, and the fast path applies: no rule, no money, no data |

### Step 2 · WHAT IS BEING REVERSED — quoted

**`BR-AST-026`** (per-type prefixes from the tenant's asset number series) said the series allocates
**when the column is left blank**. It now allocates **always**, on this target. Amend, do not supersede —
the prefixes and the series are untouched.

**`BR-AST-045`** — *"If they dont provide unit, its okay, we will still accept them and later we can
update it."* **CONFIRMED, NOT REVERSED.** Re-stamp with today's date; change nothing. `OQ-840` carries
the round trip.

**`DEF-543`'s reasoning** — *"the write mode decides, and stage 3 does not know it"* — is **no longer
true**, and this is the finding that makes clause (iii) buildable rather than an argument.
**`CR-042` moved the write-mode choice from step 4 to step 1.** Stage 3 runs after step 1. The obstacle
DEF-543 correctly described has been removed by a different change, and nobody noticed because the two
were never read together.

**No ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure is touched.** No money moves. Golden-verify must stay 33 PASS / 0 FAIL.

### Step 3 · IMPACT

the dry-run figures · the load path · the assets create/update services · one migration · the import
wizard's three screens · eleven i18n catalogues · `BR-AST-026/033/045/049` · `CR-028` design §4.7a ·
two walkthrough documents · `OQ-840` (closed).

**Open questions, both directions:** `OQ-840` closes. **Nothing new is minted** — the three remaining
uploads (premises, units, accounts) still take their identifier from the file and are **explicitly out
of scope**; the PO was shown the same question for them on the walkthrough page and has not ruled it.

**The demo fixture:** r10's 1,262-row `meter_fleet_2026.csv` is the worked case. 1,243 rows name a unit,
12 do not, and **all 12 must still load** — that is clause (ii)'s regression test.

### Step 4 · WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT, AND BY WHOM

A lane dispatched at 14:5x is **in flight on wave A** and has already landed the template half. Its work
is listed as done below rather than re-scoped, because re-issuing work in flight is how two lanes end up
reverting each other.

### Step 5 · SIZE — eight waves, 34 tasks, four targets

⚠ **"FOUR TARGETS" IS WRONG AND THE PRODUCT HAS SIX** (`import_runs.TARGETS`: premises · units · meters · sub-meters · devices · accounts). Kept as written because it is what was sized and signed; **the two it omits are wave I, which this CR's closure does NOT close.** Verified against the code by wave H, 2026-08-27.

**The shape, applied identically to all four uploads.** Stated once here so no wave restates it:

1. The record's **own identifier is never taken from the file for a new record** — it is issued from that
   entity's series in Settings › Numbering, **inside the write transaction**, so a rejected row burns no number
   and a rollback returns the counter.
2. The identifier column **stays** on the template with a new meaning: *"an EXISTING number, if this row updates
   a record already in SMARTBillHub — blank for a new one."* Blank is the normal case.
3. That column is the **match key**, and it decides the row's fate by write mode:
   **Insert new only → REJECT** · **Insert & update → update the details.**
4. The utility's own legacy reference goes in **External reference**, never overloaded onto anything else.
5. The dry run **projects** what it will issue and **states the status** each row will land in.

### CR-040 · THE TIE-OUT — the hard part nobody gave a task row, measured 2026-08-27

**Why this section exists.** CR-040's own step 5 puts payments, a refund and an
overcharge correction *between* two billing runs. Every one of those posts to
the ledger, and **hard rule 5** requires balanced pairs written only by the
posting service. **The CR sized eighteen tasks and not one of them asks whether
the resulting books foot.** A demo whose books do not tie out teaches a utility
that ours do not, and it would do it silently — the seeder does not fail, it
just leaves a drift behind.

**Two suites nearly covered it and neither did**, which is why it survived five
merged waves:

| Suite | What it proves | What it does not ask |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/test_us_led_004_tie_out.py` | BR-LED-007's check WORKS — against hand-built LE fixtures (`brazos`, `dana`), a three-entry book authored to make the panel's own states reachable | anything about the estate the PO clicks on |
| `tests/test_cr040_two_cycles.py` | the real seeder on a real tenant issues two cycles | **it never opens the ledger** — it counts invoices |

**So the product's own release blocker had never been pointed at the fixture it
ships with.** It has now.

#### The measurement — a full plant, `tie_out.tie_outs()`, the product's own door

```
JE = 155 entries · 506 lines · issued: June 47 · July 46 · August 0
refunds settled 1 · corrections executed 1

accounts_receivable   AGREED     GL 5,171.18  register 5,171.18  drift    0.00
deposit_liability     DRIFTING   GL     0.00  register   750.00  drift -750.00
tax_payable           DRIFTING   GL   242.30  register   242.99  drift   -0.69
```

**✅ THE ROW CR-040 MOST NEEDED IS CLEAN.** All 155 entries balance — hard rule 5
holds — and the receivables control agrees with the customer subledger **to the
cent, at zero drift**, on a book carrying two issued cycles, payments, a carried
credit, a refund and a corrected overcharge. *The money the bills claim is the
money the ledger carries.* That was the open question and the answer is yes.

**⚠ THE OTHER TWO ROWS DRIFT, AND NEITHER IS AN UNBALANCED BOOK.**

* **`deposit_liability`, −750.00 → filed as `DEF-1713`, and it is the MIRROR of
  `DEF-177`.** DEF-177 (open since 2026-08-16) says the register column is never
  written while payments credits the GL — *books 150.00 / register 0.00*. The
  seeded estate shows the **opposite**: the migrated deposits arrive through
  `services.create_from_import` (`IMPORT_ACCOUNT_FIELDS`, US-CUS-023 — *"a
  migrated deposit arrives WITH its original receipt date"*), which writes
  `accounts.deposit_on_file` and **posts nothing**. Same column, opposite
  direction, different cause — and nobody checked whether a door existed that
  produced the reverse, because DEF-177's own prevention text predicts only the
  one direction. ⚠ **Note the asymmetry INSIDE one import:** the opening
  receivable posts a balanced opening JE (`CR030_OPENING_BATCH_KEY`, ❄️ GT-16
  pins it) and the deposit half of the same row posts nothing at all. **A
  migrated deposit is money the utility owes back**, so a balance sheet that
  omits it understates liabilities.
* **`tax_payable`, −0.69** — a basis mismatch the product names itself
  (`tax_outstanding_is_the_billed_basis_only`). Not a lost 69 cents.

#### What landed — `06-backend/tests/test_cr040_seeded_books_tie_out.py`, 5 cases

**It asserts a SHAPE, never a total**, and the choice is deliberate: a fixture's
receivables total is not a signed number — nothing in ❄️ B4/B5 says what a demo's
books should come to — and a guard that reddens every time a lane adds a case to
the estate is a guard people are trained to edit. **An edited tie-out guard is no
guard.**

1. the estate really is a financial history (two issued cycles, a settled refund,
   an executed correction, more entries than the chart has accounts) — the
   non-vacuity witnesses, asserted **first and separately** so that if they fail
   the reader knows every green below is meaningless;
2. **every journal entry balances, PER ENTRY** — not the grand total, because a
   book netting to zero can hold two entries each wrong by the same amount in
   opposite directions, which is exactly what a posting bug produces;
3. AR is `AGREED` at **exactly zero drift with both sides NON-ZERO** — because
   `AGREED` over 0.00 against 0.00 is a row that agreed with itself about
   nothing, and `tie_outs()` returns precisely that for an empty book;
4. the drifting set is **EXACTLY** `{deposit_liability, tax_payable}`, each still
   naming its cause;
5. the books are asked at the **June boundary too** — a drift introduced by cycle
   one and cancelled by cycle two would pass an end-state check, and the money
   cases sit between the runs by design (D14).

⚠ **CASE 4 IS A STATED ABSENCE IN B7's SHAPE, AND IT REDDENS BOTH WAYS:** red if
a **third** subledger starts drifting (a new fault — what this file is for), and
red **the day DEF-177/DEF-1713 or the tax basis is fixed**, which is the day the
guard should be tightened to demand a clean book and `release_blocked is False`.
A test that merely tolerated *"some drift"* would do neither and would go quietly
green over a demo whose books had stopped footing.

⚠ **WHAT WAS NOT DONE, AND WHY.** The deposit posting was **not** written.
Ledger posting is a CLAUDE.md 🔒 sensitive path, and a migrated deposit's opening
credit needs the same finance-visible treatment the opening receivable already
has — so it is filed, not guessed. **And the comparison was NOT loosened to make
the row green**, which is what DEF-177's own prevention text warns against:
substituting a register that IS maintained would compare the ledger against
itself, and that is not a tie-out.

**❄️ NO FROZEN FIGURE MOVED.** `golden-verify` read **33 PASS / 0 FAIL** before
and after, exit 0. Checked rather than assumed, because seeding a second cycle
was the obvious way to move one.

### CR-040 · A COLLISION FOUND AT r11 STEP 0 — `DEF-1712`

**Running step 0 against a CR whose waves are already merged found a
contradiction no gate can see.** CR-040's arrival capture is the PO, verbatim:
*"you need credit and refunds cases, overcharge cases, creit cases"*. Wave D
built exactly that at `9b815d7` (**07:11 UTC**) — `seed_sample_refund` and
`seed_sample_correction`, both registered blocks with edges in the seeding
panel's dependency graph.

**Six hours later, at `ce1ef58` (13:30 UTC)**, the decision log records the
three-months ruling and elaborates: *"WHAT THIS RULING DOES NOT COMMISSION, and a
lane may not add it because it would make a nicer demo: no collections ladder, no
payment plan mid-flight, no disconnection and reconnection, **no refund, no
credit note**."*

**Both forbidden things are seeded, merged and green** — and the correction
necessarily issues a credit note, because that is how a class-R restatement
works.

⚠ **WHERE THE FAULT ACTUALLY IS, and it is the reusable half.** The PO's own
words in that ruling are only *"this si corerct - Three months — enough to make
last bill and balance forward mean something, and little else"*. **They answered
a question about HOW MUCH HISTORY.** The exclusion list is the *lane's* inference
about what the smallest option implies, written into the decision log **in the
same authoritative register as the ruling**, where the next reader cannot tell
the two apart. CLAUDE.md is explicit that **a signature covers only what was
shown** (PO 2026-08-11) — and a refund was never shown as a thing being given up;
it was asked for by name in the same CR six hours earlier.

**So the likely reading is that the exclusion list OVERREACHED, not that the PO
reversed themselves within six hours. NOTHING WAS RIPPED OUT on that reading** —
the fix is either deleting two merged seed blocks or amending a paragraph that
records a PO ruling, and **a lane may do neither on its own authority.**

**Recommendation, for the PO in one sentence:** keep wave D, and amend the
exclusion list to name **months** rather than **cases**. ⚠ **This is NOT a re-ask
of the three-months question** — that is ruled and stays ruled (law 13); it is the
supersession-must-be-stated case, which CLAUDE.md lists as legitimately reaching
the PO.

**Durable half, and it is not a gate:** when a ruling is written up, the PO's
verbatim words and the lane's inference from them must be **typographically
separated**. This entry quoted verbatim in bold and then continued in the same
voice for three paragraphs the PO never said. A future lane greps *"no refund"*,
finds it in the decision log, and deletes working code.
