## CR-047 — the account upload loads one record at a time, inherits from the unit unconditionally, and hands back two files

**Arrived** 2026-08-29, from the Product Owner, across three messages during a live read of the
account-upload walkthrough. The first asked for the change; the second and third ruled on the two
questions it raised.

> *"2.15  Accounts are on file either wayNames, units, contacts — all usable now -> after this stage -
> record is uploaded to system - it is either succes or failed; in case of success you read next record;
> in case of faile you stop the process; we need to make changes, if it is success then you read next
> record, if it is fail - you display on screen shich record failed and why (dont write to dB) and
> continue to uplaod next record; at the end we need 2 CsV file 1 for success record and other for failed
> records; - please modifu the document and show me what changes you will do the process; also when you
> upload the record  what all data you ahve to inherit from units - Utility services, plan (all details
> required for account), meters/assets, any other details, currently im not sure whether youa re
> inheriting it - please check factauully and also these detaisla re dynamic that means you ahve to save
> it by reference - please udpaet the diagram accoridngly"*

> *"if account is created then we need to inherit details form units - otherwise upadling it later will be
> big tasks"*

> *"if account is created then money is also lands"*

### ⚠ READ THIS BEFORE THE TASK LIST — MOST OF THIS CR IS A DEFECT, NOT A CHANGE

Step 1 of `13-change-process.md` says *"when it is ambiguous it is a DEFECT, not a change, because filing
our misunderstanding as a 'change' quietly converts our error into the customer's new requirement."*
It is not even ambiguous here. **`BR-CUS-051` is CONFIRMED and has been since the account import was
specified**, verbatim:

> Import mechanics = the standard: staged → per-row errors → **skip-errors ON** → **"N created · N failed"
> summary** → 10,000-row cap

*Skip-errors ON* and *"N created · N failed"* **is** what the PO asked for. What shipped is one
transaction around the whole file that reports a single error and creates nothing. **That is `DEF-2519`
(critical), not a new requirement**, and the CR is written that way so the record does not credit us with
a rule we already owed.

### Step 1 · CLASSIFY

| # | The statement | Kind | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| i | A refused record is skipped, named on screen with its reason, and the run continues | **DEFECT** (`DEF-2519`) | `BR-CUS-051` already says exactly this, CONFIRMED. The code does not do it |
| ii | Two files at the end — one for what loaded, one for what did not | **New requirement** | Nothing signed asks for a download of either kind, on any of the six uploads |
| iii | An account that is created inherits from its unit whatever its status | **New requirement** (and it closes `DEF-2518`) | No signed rule says it either way. The current behaviour is an implementation choice inherited from the S18/S19 door, not a ruling — so this is a new rule, **not a reversal** |
| iv | If the account lands, its money lands | **Confirms the existing design** | See step 2. Nothing moves |

### Step 2 · WHAT SIGNED STATEMENT IS BEING REVERSED — and the ❄️ FROZEN check

**One frozen figure is in range and it was checked before anything else was written.**
`GT-16` (B5 ❄️, finance-signed 2026-08-08) carries the batch rule verbatim:

> batch check: Σ of all opening JEs = Σ of all imported buckets (fixture batch: 1,213 accounts →
> clearing credit = total migrated AR $184,320.55); re-posting the same batch is idempotent (no second JE
> set)

**It does not move, and the reasoning is recorded here rather than assumed.** The four `ob_*` buckets are
written by `import_writer.write_opening_buckets` **only for an account that was created**. So under a
partial load both sides of the identity shrink together: a row that failed produced no account, therefore
no buckets, therefore nothing on either side of the equation. Σ JEs = Σ buckets holds exactly. What
changes is that the **file** may now contain rows that contributed to neither side — which the equation
never mentioned. The fixture's **$184,320.55** is unchanged because that file has no failing rows.

The idempotency clause is untouched too: re-running `failures.csv` is a **different run with a different
batch id**, so it posts its own entry set. That is not a re-post of the same batch.

**Therefore: NO finance re-sign is required, and HUMAN-GUIDE §6 is not entered.** If a later lane thinks
otherwise, it must re-derive the two sentences above before acting — do not take this paragraph on trust.

**Nothing else in range is signed against the new behaviour.** `BR-MET-040`'s own text already says *"Plan
is REQUIRED at account **activation**"*; moving the check out of the import path and onto activation makes
the code agree with the rule it cites, so it is a **correction of the application point**, not an
amendment of the rule. Recorded as such in the rule's row.

### Step 3 · IMPACT

| Surface | What it costs |
|---|---|
| Business rules | Two new (`BR-CUS-672`, `BR-CUS-673`); one application-point note on `BR-MET-040` |
| Backend · metering | Savepoint per record, refusal sentences, two new stage-3 rules, one CSV endpoint |
| Backend · customers | Inheritance split from the occupancy guards; the plan check moves to activation |
| Frontend | Failure list, two downloads, an inherited-services figure, and the changeover door **both halves** |
| Open questions | None minted. Nothing here needed a value chosen (law 13) |
| Demo fixture | Unchanged — `bbu-accounts-cutover.csv` has no write-time failures |
| Golden tests | `GT-16` re-read and confirmed unmoved; no re-sign |
| Defects closed | `DEF-2519`, `DEF-2518` |
| Documents | The PO-facing walkthrough artifact, rewritten the same day |

### Step 4 · WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT AND IS NOW WRONG

**Code shipped.** `CR-030 W1` built the accounts target on the shared runner and `CR-046 C4/C5` reworked
its identifier and write-mode handling. **Both are CLOSED, so neither is edited** — each takes a
superseded-by pointer to this CR. The all-or-nothing transaction was correct for the runner's other five
targets, which have no write-time business refusals; accounts are the first target that does, and nobody
noticed the assumption change under them.

**Data already written.** None. No tenant has run an account import that hit a write-time refusal —
had one, it would have written nothing, which is the defect.

**Lanes building right now.** Three, dispatched by this CR, module-scoped so no two touch one file.

### Step 5 · SIZE — nineteen tasks, in four groups

Record (7) · backend metering (4) · backend customers (2) · frontend (4) · tests and close (2).
The two carrying real risk are the savepoint and the changeover door; the rest is mechanical.

**Fast path does NOT apply** — this touches a rule, money and data.


### CR-047 · SUPERSEDES POINTERS — `CR-030 W1` and `CR-046` are CLOSED and are NOT edited

Both CRs made statements about the accounts loader that `CR-047` changes. **Neither body is touched** —
a closed CR is a record of what was decided then, and editing it would destroy the only evidence of the
assumption that broke. Each takes a pointer instead:

| Closed CR | What it said | What `CR-047` changes |
|---|---|---|
| `CR-030 W1` | Built accounts as the sixth target on the ONE ETL runner (`BR-MET-096`) — *"a new import is a TARGET, never a new pipeline"* | The shape is right and stands. What it inherited without noticing is the runner's **all-or-nothing transaction**, which was correct for its other five targets *because none of them has a write-time business refusal*. Accounts are the first that does. `CR-047` narrows the transaction to one row |
| `CR-046 C4/C5` | The account number is the utility's, taken from the file verbatim; the write mode decides what a known record does | Unchanged and still correct. `CR-047` only changes what happens when a record the write mode ACCEPTED is then refused by the writer |

⚠ **The assumption that broke is worth naming, because it is the kind that breaks silently.**
`CR-030 W1` did not make a wrong decision — it reused a proven runner, which is exactly what
`BR-MET-096` asks for. The runner's one-transaction property was *load-bearing* for premises, units and
the three assets targets and *harmful* for accounts, and nothing in the repository records a property as
belonging to some targets and not others. A lane adding a seventh target inherits the same silence.


### ⚠ CR-047 · WIDENED 2026-08-29 TO ALL SIX UPLOADS — AND A SENTENCE IN THIS CR'S OWN STEP 4 WAS WRONG

**PO instruction, verbatim:** *"Can you update the CR47, write down all tasks related to … and then execute
all these tasks and close CR 47"*, over the table this lane put on screen. The PO chose to **widen this CR
rather than raise a second one**, which is their call and is recorded so nobody reads the widening as a
lane's initiative.

#### THE CORRECTION FIRST, BECAUSE IT IS THE REASON THE CR WIDENED

Step 4 above says the all-or-nothing transaction *"was correct for the runner's other five targets, which
have no write-time business refusals"*. **THAT IS FALSE FOR THE THREE ASSETS TARGETS, and this lane wrote
it without opening the assets writer.** `apps/assets/services._create_asset_inner` refuses **four** ways,
by name, and `_load_assets_rows` has no `try`, no `except` and no savepoint anywhere in its row loop —
byte for byte the shape of `DEF-2519`:

| The refusal | Rule | Raised as |
|---|---|---|
| The asset number is already on file | `BR-AST-033` (hard block) | `BizError` `BIZ_STATE` |
| The legacy reference is already used | `BR-AST-049` (unique per tenant) | field refusal |
| An assigned-on-create asset has no install date | `BR-AST-011` | `VAL_REQUIRED` |
| A lookup value is not one of the tenant's own | — | `VAL_UNKNOWN_LOOKUP` |

**These are ordinary contents of a real meter-fleet file**, not edge cases — so the same defect is live on
three more uploads with a HIGHER probability of firing than on accounts.

**Premises and units are exposed by a different mechanism and it is worth stating separately.** They are
written straight through the ORM (`model.objects.create(...)`, no guard), so what escapes is a
**database** refusal — a unique index or NOT NULL that stage 3 does not model, or a genuine race where
another user takes the same premise number between the rehearsal and the commit. Lower probability,
identical consequence. ⚠ **And PostgreSQL makes the savepoint mandatory rather than merely tidy there:
once a statement fails inside a transaction the whole transaction is poisoned, so catching the error and
carrying on is not possible without one.**

**A statement about what the product CANNOT do decays fastest** — this lane has now recorded that lesson
three times and made the mistake a fourth. The rule it keeps failing: **re-measure a "cannot" at the moment
of writing it down, not at the moment you formed the belief.**

#### WHAT DOES *NOT* GENERALISE — CHECKED SPECIFICALLY, BECAUSE IT LOOKS LIKE IT SHOULD

| Change | Applies beyond accounts? | Why not |
|---|---|---|
| **Inherit from the parent unconditionally** (`BR-CUS-672`) | **NO** | An asset's links to its unit and service are conditional on **the data** — a unit and a service in the file — not on a status the operator can silently leave blank. And a meter with no unit going to **inventory** is ruled behaviour with its own named stage-3 warning (`AST.UNIT_BLANK_TO_INVENTORY`). That is nothing like `DEF-2518`, where a blank OPTIONAL cell produced a wired-to-nothing record and reported it a success. Premises and units have no parent to inherit from |
| **The changeover date and the money door** | **NO** | Accounts are the only upload that reaches the ledger |

⚠ **"Inventory" is NOT a seventh upload** and was named as one in the PO's question. It is the
DESTINATION a meter takes when its row names no unit. Nothing to build, nothing to change.

#### THE WIDENING TASKS — 20 to 25

| # | Task | Targets | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | Savepoint per record + a reason and a fix on every failed row, on the **assets** loader | meters · sub-meters · devices | `_load_assets_rows`. Catch the four refusals above by their error base, not by `Exception` |
| 21 | The same on the **generic** loader | premises · units | `_load_locked`'s ORM write path. Catch the database refusal; the savepoint is what makes continuing possible at all |
| 22 | A **per-target column map** for the two result files | all six | ⚠ **This is a gap in THIS LANE'S OWN SPEC, not the metering lane's.** Task 13 specified accounts-shaped columns (*account number, customer name, unit reference, opening balance*) for an endpoint that is keyed by RUN and therefore already serves all six. One map, six entries, declared beside the existing column sets |
| 23 | Four new stage-3 rules on the assets targets | meters · sub-meters · devices | `AST.NUMBER_NOT_ALREADY_ON_FILE` · `AST.EXTERNAL_REF_FREE` · `AST.INSTALL_DATE_REQUIRED_WHEN_ASSIGNED` · `AST.LOOKUPS_RESOLVE`. Same reason the three account ones moved: a rule caught in the rehearsal is a row the operator fixes BEFORE committing |
| 24 | Tests, each proved RED first | all six | Per target: a file with one refused row still loads the other N−1 |
| 25 | Close the record — version, changelog, review ledger | — | Change-process step 7 |

**Why the cost is far below six times the work:** the five non-account targets share ONE runner, so tasks
20 and 21 are two functions in one file, not five implementations. Task 22 is a table. Only task 23 is
genuinely per-target, and it is four rules written once against three targets that share a column set.

## CR-049 — A sent legal document is FROZEN as the document, not re-rendered from data

### Step 0 · CAPTURE — the requester's words, verbatim, at arrival

> *"One thing we should keep in mind any legal document when send - it is freezed - we should keep all
> underline data, but actual leter and PDF should be freeze - any changes to tempalte or any items hsould
> be noted as changed; that way it will keep the santity of the legal documents; otherwie everytime we
> reproduce it using data in table, we might change something about it and that is not correct"*
> — the Product Owner, 2026-08-30, in the working chat session, replying to the `CR-048` E9 business
> example (a regulator asking to see the exact disconnection letter a customer was sent last July).

### Step 1 · CLASSIFY — this is a DEFECT and a requirement, and the split is deliberate

The change process says **when it is ambiguous it is a DEFECT, not a change**, because filing our
misunderstanding as a "change" quietly converts our error into the customer's new requirement. Applying
that honestly splits this in two:

| Half | Classification | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **No document this product sends is stored as sent — not the notice, and NOT THE BILL** | **DEFECT** | ⚠ **This row first said the bill was already frozen and only the notice was not. That was wrong** — see the correction below. `NFR-33` and `NFR-35` (ratified, in `04-docs/02-decisions/06-non-functional-requirements.md`) already require STORED ARTIFACTS for *"anything that cannot be re-rendered or is legally executed"*, with write-once immutable-object-lock and seven-year retention, and `BR-SHL-031` carries the same into the shell rules. **The rule is signed and has ZERO implementation.** That is `DEF-193`'s class exactly — a ruling that reached every document and no code — and it is our gap, not a new ask. |
| **A change to a template or an item must be NOTED AS CHANGED** | **New requirement** | Nothing signed says this. It is a genuinely new obligation — an audit trail on the wording itself, not only on the documents that used it. |

⚠⚠ **CORRECTION, THE SAME DAY, AND IT WIDENS THIS CR: THE BILL DOES NOT FREEZE EITHER.** The first draft of
this CR — and what was said to the PO — was *"Bills already freeze. Notices don't."* **`BR-BIL-030` freezes
the INPUTS, not the output.** `invoices.bill_payload` + `custom_snapshot` are the DATA a bill is assembled
from, held immutable by a database trigger; `documents.RenderedDocument`, which carries the HTML and the
PDF bytes, **is a dataclass and not a model**, and `_pdf()` re-runs on every request. **No stored PDF or
HTML exists for any bill anywhere in this product.** `BR-BIL-030`'s phrase *"a complete document instance"*
means a complete DATA instance; reading it as the document is the mistake, and it was made twice — in this
CR and out loud to the PO.

### Step 5d · THE ENGINEERING JUDGMENTS, MADE AND WRITTEN DOWN RATHER THAN ASKED

Hard-won law 13: a judgment where the rules ran out is ours, recorded with its worked figure.

**(a) THE BYTES GO BEHIND A SEAM; THE GUARANTEE DOES NOT.** The metadata — tenant, document kind, source
ref, channel, storage key, `content_hash`, byte length, `stored_at` — lives in a Postgres table with RLS
`FORCE` and a write-once trigger, the same shape as the invoice immutability trigger already in
`billing/migrations/0006`. **The BYTES live behind a storage seam**, exactly the idiom `provider_seam.py`
and the integrations seam already use.

⚠ **AMENDED THE SAME DAY BY PO RULING: THE PRODUCTION BACKEND IS CLOUD OBJECT STORAGE, NOT POSTGRES.** This
clause first said *"a Postgres-backed implementation shipped"*, with an object store as a later swap. PO
verbatim: *"we will need storage - on cloud - define proper engineering for it; later document retrival
become an issue - look at volume, performance, speed, cost, you will ahve to save link in DB for PDF links,
also you ahve to see tenant wise seperations"*. **The seam survives the amendment unchanged and is what
made it cheap** — what changes is which implementation ships, not the shape. The full design is (e) below.

**(b) THE WORKED FIGURE, so the storage decision is not made on a hunch.** A utility at the top of our
stated range — 3,000 connections — produces roughly **36,000 bills a year at ~60 KB**, **~36,000 receipts
at ~30 KB**, and a few thousand notices: call it **~3.4 GB a year, ~24 GB over the seven years `NFR-35`
requires**. **A hundred such utilities averaging half that is on the order of a terabyte.** In Postgres
that terabyte sits in every backup, every restore and every vacuum; in object storage it is roughly
**$25–30 a month** at standard rates and materially less once a lifecycle rule moves anything older than a
year to cold storage. That is the whole argument, and it is why (a) was amended rather than defended.

**(c) WHAT IS STORED PER CHANNEL.** Print → the PDF bytes. Email → the rendered subject and body as sent.
SMS → the text as sent. In-app → nothing new; it already stores its render and the PO has ruled it out of
scope.

**(d) THE FREEZE IS A PRECONDITION, NOT A CUTOVER** — see step 4. Nothing has been sent to a customer, so
the dispatcher can refuse to mark anything `sent` without an artefact, with no exceptions and no era
before it. **This option expires at go-live.**

**(e) THE CLOUD STORAGE DESIGN, in the seven decisions the PO's ruling asks for.**

| # | Decision | Why, in one line |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **AWS FIRST, MULTI-CLOUD BY CONSTRUCTION** | ⚠ **PO ruling 2026-08-30:** *"curently we will start with AWS, but we need to keep it multi cloud - google or any other cloud - in future we mght have differnt requirements"*. So the shipped adapter is **AWS S3** and the interface stays vendor-neutral. ⚠⚠ **AND HERE IS WHERE "S3-COMPATIBLE" LEAKS, SAID NOW RATHER THAN DISCOVERED ON THE DAY WE ADD A SECOND CLOUD:** the S3 API is genuinely portable for the COMMON operations — put, get, pre-sign, checksum — and Google's interop mode and MinIO both speak it. It is **NOT** portable for the COMPLIANCE features this rule depends on: **object lock / WORM, lifecycle transitions and customer-managed encryption keys are spelled differently on every cloud**, and Azure needs a real adapter rather than an endpoint swap. **So the seam is drawn at INTENT, not mechanism** — the interface says *store this immutably for seven years*, and each cloud's adapter decides whether that is S3 Object Lock in compliance mode, a GCS bucket retention policy, or an Azure immutability policy. An interface carrying `set_object_lock(mode="COMPLIANCE")` would be an AWS interface wearing a neutral name, and the second cloud would be a rewrite rather than an addition. ⚠ **And a backend that CANNOT express immutable retention must REFUSE to be configured for production rather than silently storing a deletable object** — law 3, and it matters more here than anywhere, because a guarantee is the entire point of this store. |
| 2 | **A filesystem backend for tests and local dev**, same interface, chosen by settings | The suite must not need a network or a bucket. ⚠ **CLAUDE.md law 3 — defaults fail closed:** a missing bucket configuration REFUSES loudly; it must never silently fall back to local disk in production. ⚠ **AND THE AWS CLIENT IS A RUNTIME DEPENDENCY, NOT A DEV ONE.** `06-backend/pyproject.toml` carries a comment about exactly this mistake — `cryptography` sat under `dev`, every local test passed, and the SHIPPED IMAGE raised `ModuleNotFoundError`. The filesystem backend needs no dependency at all, which is what keeps the suite honest without a cloud account. |
| 3 | **Key layout `t/<tenant_id>/<yyyy>/<mm>/<document_id>`** ⚠ **SUPERSEDED 2026-10-02 by `CR-160-BRC10` (PO) → `t/<utility web name>/<module>/<yyyy>/<mm>/<file id>[.ext]`, one bucket per environment; old keys still load, nothing moved** | Tenant first so a prefix IS a tenant; dated so a lifecycle rule moves cold objects without reading the database. |
| 4 | ⚠ **TENANT SEPARATION IS THE DATABASE ROW, NOT THE PREFIX** | The prefix is a naming convention and nothing more. What prevents a cross-tenant read is that **the only way to learn a key is an RLS-scoped row**. So: never list the bucket, never derive a key from a tenant id a caller supplied, never accept a key as an input. A caller in tenant A asking for tenant B's document gets the same answer as one asking for a document that does not exist. |
| 5 | **Delivery is a PRE-SIGNED URL that expires in FOUR HOURS**, issued only after the row is resolved and the caller authorised | ⚠ **PO ruling 2026-08-30, and it reversed this lane's first answer.** This said *"minutes, not hours"*; the PO ruled: *"dont expire it in minutes - exprise it in 3 or 4 hours"*. **They are right, and the reason is the bulk export in (f) below** — a manifest of half a million pre-signed URLs fetched in parallel takes longer than minutes to work through, so a minutes-long TTL would have made the export they asked for in the same breath impossible. A four-hour link also survives a person opening a bill, being interrupted, and coming back. **The cost, stated rather than buried: the URL is a bearer token for that one document, so a link forwarded in an email is readable by whoever receives it for four hours.** That is a real exposure and it is the PO's to accept — it is bounded, it reaches ONE document, and it cannot be used to discover another. Never a public object, never a permanent link; the TTL is a setting so it can be shortened without a deploy. |
| 6 | **Server-side encryption on; object lock (WORM) with `NFR-35`'s seven-year retention** ⚠ **LOCK SUSPENDED 2026-10-02 by `CR-160-BRC10` (PO: *"dont lock it"*) — no object lock, no expiry tag; encryption unchanged** | The cloud-native form of write-once, **beside the database trigger and not instead of it**: the trigger protects the record, the lock protects the bytes. |
| 7 | **The content hash is stored as the object's checksum as well as in the row, and verified on read** | A silent byte change is exactly what this rule exists to prevent. |

**RETRIEVAL — the half the PO named specifically.** The common case is one person opening one document:
an indexed lookup in the metadata table plus one object GET, tens of milliseconds. **Listing is ALWAYS a
database query and never a bucket listing** — the day somebody reaches for a bucket list is the day this
gets slow and starts crossing tenants, and it is the one performance rule worth stating in the code.

**(f) BULK EXPORT — *"if we want to just download all documents for given utility, we should able to do it
quickly"* (PO 2026-08-30). ⚠ THE ANSWER IS THAT THE TENANT-SEPARATION RULE DOES NOT BLOCK THIS — IT IS
WHAT MAKES IT FAST AND USABLE.**

The rule says *never list the bucket to discover what exists*. It does not say a caller may not fetch many
objects. **The metadata table IS the index, and it is a better one than a bucket listing could ever be:** a
bucket listing returns keys and byte counts; the table returns *this is the March bill for account
ACC-1042, stored on 3 April, hash abc…*. **That difference is the whole reason an export is usable rather
than a folder of half a million files named after UUIDs.**

**THE ARITHMETIC, and it is the argument.** A 3,000-connection utility seven years in holds roughly
**525,000 documents (~24 GB)** — 36,000 bills and 36,000 receipts a year plus a few thousand notices.

| How | What it costs |
|---|---|
| **Serially, one object at a time** at ~30 ms each | **≈ 4.4 HOURS of pure latency**, before a single byte of transfer |
| **In parallel, 100 at a time** | **≈ 2.5 minutes of latency** |
| Bytes proxied **through the application** | Doubles the transfer and makes the app the bottleneck at exactly the moment it is carrying 24 GB |
| Bytes fetched **direct from storage** by pre-signed URL | The app moves a manifest, not a terabyte |

**So "quickly" is decided by three choices, and none of them is the folder layout:** enumerate from the
DATABASE, fetch in PARALLEL, and never proxy the bytes.

**THE SHAPE:** it is a background job, not a request — 24 GB cannot stream through one, and this repo
already has the pattern (`Job`, `ASYNC_ROW_BAR`, the import runner's 202-then-poll). The job writes **a
MANIFEST first** — one row per document with its kind, date, account, source reference, hash and a
HUMAN-READABLE filename — and then either hands over pre-signed URLs for a parallel client fetch, or builds
one archive and hands over a single URL. **The manifest is the deliverable either way**; the bytes are
almost incidental.

**TWO THINGS THIS ADDS TO THE TABLE IN (a), and they are cheap now and a migration later:**
1. **An index on `(tenant, stored_at)` and `(tenant, kind)`.** The manifest query is the export; an
   unindexed scan of half a million rows is where the four hours would come back.
2. **A HUMAN-READABLE NAME on the row** — `bills/2026/03/ACC-1042-INV-000123.pdf`. Without it the export is
   a folder of UUIDs and the utility cannot use what we handed them. **The database is the only place that
   knows the human name; the object store never will.**

**AND `stored_at` MAKES IT INCREMENTAL.** The first export is 24 GB; every one after it is *what is new
since last time*, which is the difference between a quarterly job and an annual ordeal.

**ONE THING WE DO NOT CONTROL, said plainly rather than promised away:** 24 GB has a transfer floor set by
the link, not by us — roughly half an hour at 100 Mbps no matter how well this is built. **What our design
decides is whether four hours of avoidable latency sits on top of that.**

⚠ **AND IT IS THE MOST SENSITIVE OPERATION IN THE PRODUCT** — every document a utility ever sent, in one
archive. System Admin only, audited, tenant-scoped like everything else, and the archive itself expires.

**TASK 1 IS LANDED — `v2.82.0`, 2026-08-30. THERE IS NOW SOMEWHERE TO PUT A DOCUMENT**, which is the
sentence step 5c says everything else on this CR is waiting for. What exists:

| | |

| Its isolation and its freeze | `tenancy/migrations/0026_rls_document_store.py` — the table, RLS `ENABLE + FORCE` with B2 §3's signed predicate, and a trigger refusing **every** UPDATE and **every** DELETE, all in ONE migration. |
| The bytes | `document_storage.py` — the seam. `AwsS3Storage` (the one cloud adapter) and `FilesystemStorage` (tests and local dev, no dependency). |

**WHAT TASK 2 INHERITS, so its lane does not have to derive it.** Call
`apps.tenancy.document_store.store(kind=…, source_type="outbound_message", source_id=<the queue row>,
channel=<pdf_print|email|sms>, content_type=…, display_name=…, payload=<bytes>, process=
"notifications.dispatcher")` inside the tenant's own context. It returns a `StoredDocumentRef`. It **refuses**
an empty payload, a missing `display_name`, a missing author and an unruled kind, and there is **one artefact
per (source, channel, content type)** — a second store of the same three is a unique-constraint violation, not
a second copy. `for_source(...)` answers `document_not_stored` when there is none, which is what task 7's
*"re-rendered from data, not the original"* is built on.

⚠ **THREE THINGS TASK 2's LANE MUST NOT REDERIVE.** (a) The bytes are written BEFORE the row, deliberately —
do not wrap the upload in the transaction; the row can never be deleted, so a failed upload would leave a
permanent record of a document that does not exist. (b) A caller never sees or supplies a storage key. (c)
Enumeration is always a database query; the seam has no `list()` and must never grow one.

⚠ **AND ONE THING NO CODE IN THIS REPO CAN DO, which belongs on the deployment checklist rather than in a
task:** the bucket must be **created** with Object Lock enabled — AWS cannot switch it on afterwards — and a
lifecycle rule moving year-old objects to cold storage is the difference between **$27** and **$8** a month
for a hundred utilities. Both are in `document_storage.py`'s docstring and in the review-ledger row.

**NEW RUNTIME DEPENDENCY:** `boto3` in `06-backend/pyproject.toml`. It is **not installed in the authoring
environment**, so the AWS adapter is proved against an injected client — the request is verified, a real round
trip is not.

**TASKS 2, 5 AND 7 ARE LANDED — `v2.84.0`, 2026-08-30. NOTHING LEAVES THIS BUILDING WITHOUT A COPY OF IT
BEING KEPT.** Task 1 gave us somewhere to put a document; this is the first thing that writes into it.

| | |
|---|---|
| The write (task 2) | `06-backend/apps/notifications/frozen_documents.py` + the dispatcher. It renders, **FREEZES**, and only then hands the batch to a provider. Print stores the letter text it hands the vendor, email a minimal RFC 5322 message carrying the subject and body as sent, SMS the text. |
| The precondition | `dispatcher._mark_sent` takes the freeze answer as a **REQUIRED argument** and refuses a row without one. The ORDER is the first guarantee — an unfrozen row is released and never reaches a provider — and `require_frozen` is the second, because a guarantee resting on the order of two statements is one refactor from being gone. |
| `DEF-2504` (task 5) | **CLOSED, and proved RED first.** Serve the 48-hour certified notice, edit the dispute-rights clause, reproduce the notice — the reproduction carries the ORIGINAL wording. With the freeze absent it answered `document_not_stored`. |
| The honest half (task 7) | `frozen_documents.reproduce` answers `original` or `re_rendered_from_data_not_the_original` — never an empty success — carrying the store's own `document_not_stored` code and an i18n key. Four keys, eleven catalogues. |

**FOUR JUDGMENTS MADE AND WRITTEN DOWN**, all five rows in `12-governance/02-decision-log.md`, 2026-08-30:

1. **Freeze BEFORE the hand-off, not after.** Freezing after would create the one state this rule cannot
   describe — a posted letter with no copy of it, and a row that must either be marked `sent` (breaking the
   guarantee) or left `queued` (lying about a message the customer is holding).
2. **Print freezes the TEXT we hand the vendor, not a PDF — and that is NOT task 6's answer.** Step 5d(c)
   says *"Print → the PDF bytes"* and there are none: no page-render library exists (`OQ-149`) and the
   printable classes render text. **Rendering a PDF at freeze time would freeze a document the customer
   never received**, which is the substitution `BR-NOT-027` exists to forbid. The media type follows the
   payload, so the day a renderer lands `application/pdf` is what gets kept with no change to the rule.
   **Whether a separate PDF rendition must ALSO be frozen stays task 6's.**
3. **The kind map is keyed on the pinned TEMPLATE CLASS, not `event_key`** — which is NULL on every row
   this product writes today, so an `event_key` map would have answered *"unruled"* for the very notice
   `DEF-2504` is about.
4. **A retry whose fresh render disagrees with the frozen copy HOLDS the row.** Neither copy may be sent
   silently: the fresh render breaks the rule, and the frozen bytes hide a wording change from the System
   Admin who made it.

⚠ **WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, AND THE FIRST ONE MATTERS MOST.** **The guarantee is worth only what the ROUTE

### Step 5b-bis · THE SCOPE TABLE GREW FROM 21 CLASSES TO 40 (PO ruling, 2026-08-30)

**`OQ-1164` IS CLOSED AND THOSE NINETEEN CLASSES NOW DISPATCH.** The PO was shown, in plain English with
the count, that the product has 41 kinds of letter and message, that their own step-5b scope table named
21, and that the other 20 had never been ruled on — together with the recommendation to keep all of them,
because storage is a few kilobytes a message and the risk runs one way only: keeping a document you did
not need costs almost nothing, and failing to keep one you did need loses it permanently. They ruled,
verbatim:

> *"My recommendation is to keep all of them. - OKY KEEP THEM"*

**NINETEEN, NOT TWENTY.** The twentieth is `staff_bulk_summary`, the in-app staff summary, which the same
PO ruled out by CHANNEL on 2026-08-26 (*"we dont have to worry about in-app message those are mostly FYI ;
hence we dont have worry about them"*). **A ruling on a LIST does not overturn a ruling on a CHANNEL**, and
a lane that read the newer sentence and swept the in-app class in would have manufactured two genuine PO
answers that disagree — the failure hard-won law 13 exists to prevent. The exclusion is asserted BY NAME in
the test file so it cannot be undone quietly.

**NINETEEN CLASSES, SEVENTEEN FILING CATEGORIES, 16 → 33 ON THE CONSTRAINT.** `kind` names the DOCUMENT and
`channel` is its own column, so the printed statement and the statement email share one kind (A19 rule 1
legislates for both in one sentence), as do bill-ready on email and on SMS — the same collapse the twelve
existing kinds already use for the four disconnection tiers. That is a lane judgement recorded with both
figures in `12-governance/02-decision-log.md`; it changes nothing the PO can observe, since all nineteen
classes are kept either way, and it is written into the human-review ledger row as one of three things to
confirm because a signature covers only what was shown.

**WHAT IT COST:** one migration, `tenancy/0028_oq1164_every_customer_document_kind`, widening the
`ck_stored_documents_kind` CHECK constraint. Widening only — no row the table already holds can become
invalid — and its reverse REFUSES if any row uses one of the 17 new kinds, because migration `0026`'s
write-once trigger means such a row could never be deleted to make room. `HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING`.

**WHAT IT DID NOT DO.** The freeze is unweakened: `_mark_sent` still takes the freeze answer as a required
argument, and a class with no ruled kind still HOLDS rather than being guessed. **The four field-service
classes got a kind and nothing else** — the flow that would send them is R5 (`OQ-249`) and this ruling
explicitly does not authorise building it. ~~Task 3's reprint route is still unbuilt, so the first sentence
of this section's warning stands unchanged.~~ **Task 3 landed the same day — see step 6-bis.**

the customer is not. **The fix is one key in the snapshot each writer already builds**, and it belongs to
the writers rather than to this module.

1. **A single-document read FETCHES as well as linking.** Decisions 5 and 7 pull opposite

2. **A tampered document is REPORTED, never softened into "re-rendered from data".** Those

   seven-year record behind a reassuring caption.
3. **The date range's upper bound is SQL**, which is why tenancy's published service grew
   rather than being reached around (B2 §2).

call `BR-BIL-033` already made, and the same bytes `GET /invoices/{id}/document.pdf`
already served to a clerk. That is why the bill freezes a PDF where the LETTER freezes
text: for the letter there are no PDF bytes to keep and inventing them would freeze a

⚠ **`OQ-149` IS UNTOUCHED AND STILL OPEN.** The kept page is the Base-14 print FLOOR —
no logo, no usage graph, no barcode, no tenant CSS. **What is kept is what is produced**,

**A real PostgreSQL refuses it**, by `billing_template_version_frozen` (billing migration

rewrite what those customers were sent without touching a single invoice row."* So the
bill's data and the tenant's chosen template ROW were both already protected; **what was
protected by nothing is the CODE that draws the page and the platform's LIBRARY of
layouts** — a deploy moves the first, a rollback moves the second, and an already-pinned
bill then prints on `_layout_for`'s named stand-in. The freeze is still necessary and the

second costume: the suite's database is not the product's, so a case can be green and
wrong about production.**

**FIVE JUDGEMENTS, all in `12-governance/02-decision-log.md`, 2026-08-30:** (1) the bill
freezes a PDF and the letter does not, and it is a fact about the code rather than a
preference; (2) the due date is put on the in-memory row BEFORE the render, because
`_meta` reads it and a draft has none — freezing the pre-issue render would have frozen
a bill with a dash where the due date belongs; (3) the pointer lives on
`stored_documents.source_id`, never on the invoice, so keeping a bill touches no
financial row and hard rule 4 is never approached; (4) `require_frozen` checks the
ARTEFACTS as well as the verdict — the opposite of its notifications counterpart, which
must not, because a letter has exempt cases and a bill has none; (5) the S30 bands stay
and are labelled, where the notifications panel draws nothing — same rule, two answers,
because the two screens are for different things.

**THE MEASURED COST, so the storage decision is not a hunch.** 2,368 bytes of HTML and
3,680 bytes of page per bill — **6 KB**. A 3,000-connection utility billed monthly is
**~210 MB a year and 1.4 GB over `NFR-35`'s seven years**; a hundred of them is ~142 GB.
Step 5d(b) estimated 60 KB a bill against a designed PDF that does not exist yet, so the
real figure is an order of magnitude smaller — and will rise when `OQ-149` closes.

### Step 6-quater · TASK 8 IS LANDED — `v2.89.0`, 2026-08-30. THE WORDING NOW CARRIES A TRAIL

**This is the task this CR called *"the genuinely new requirement"*** — everything else on the
list was making an existing promise true. It is the PO's middle clause: *"any changes to
tempalte or any items hsould be noted as changed"*.

⚠ **THE QUESTION IT HAD TO ANSWER FIRST: what does this add that VERSION HISTORY does not?**
The product already versions a template well — `BR-BIL-026` makes every edit a new append-only
row, both bodies are kept, migration `0006`'s trigger refuses to let a published one move, and
the history table lists every version with its date, its author id and a pin count. **Measured
against the tree, two things were missing and the second is the one the PO's sentence is
about.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **WHAT MOVED** | **Nothing in this product diffed two versions.** Neither did the audit trail — and `OQ-255` says otherwise, which is why it is written down: `template_service.save_draft`'s `audit_log` row held the class, the variant, the version number, the status and the effective date, **and not one character of the wording.** True of the ROW, false of the WORDING. A person asked *"did last March's edit touch the dispute-rights paragraph?"* opened two versions and compared them by eye. |
| **WHO IS HOLDING THE OLD WORDING** | The history's `pinned_by` cell was a bare integer — *"pinned by 3,412 sent"* — **with no way to reach one of them.** A version list can say HOW MANY; it cannot say WHICH, and WHICH is what a regulator and a complaining customer ask. ⚠ **It became answerable only today**: tasks 2, 3 and 4 gave every sent document a kept copy with an id, so an impact row hands over the letter itself. |

| | |
|---|---|
| The service | `06-backend/apps/notifications/template_changes.py` — **DERIVED, and there is no second table.** Which of `subject` / `preheader` / `body` moved and by how many lines; which already-sent documents are pinned to the superseded version, each with the id of its kept copy. |
| Why derived | Both inputs are **immutable by database trigger** — a published version's wording cannot be updated (`notifications/0006`), and a pin is frozen for ever with the version undeletable (`BR-NOT-025`, `notifications/0017`). So a diff computed today is the diff of the day of the edit, for ever, and a stored copy could only drift from the rows it came from (hard-won law 5). `BR-NOT-028`, written **PROPOSED and not ratified**: `BR-NOT-027` part 3 is the PO's rule, HOW to note a change is ours. |
| Hard rule 7 | **No new audit row and no new table.** The `template.saved` row an edit already wrote now also names `changed_fields` and `changed_from_version` — and the wording is deliberately NOT copied in, asserted by a test that fails if `body` or `subject` ever appear in the blob. |
| The route | `GET /template-catalog/{code}/changes/{version_id}` — System Admin, like every door on this screen, and it is the most sensitive read on it because it names the customers who received a particular letter. It serves a document ID, never a storage key. |
| The screen | The version history gains a **Changed** cell — *"Letter"*, *"Subject · Letter"* — with the sentence on hover and the line counts plus the affected letters in the detail it opens. **Mounted and clicked**, through `TemplateDetailPanel` and the real history page. |
| The proof | `tests/test_cr049_t8_template_change_trail.py` (13 + 1 `requires_postgres`) and `templateChangeTrail.dom.test.tsx` (7). 73 pass across the six closest backend suites, unchanged; the whole frontend suite is 3,424 passing across 213 files. |

**FIVE JUDGEMENTS, all in `12-governance/02-decision-log.md`, 2026-08-30:** (1) the trail is
DERIVED and the argument is a trigger rather than a preference; (2) the audit row an edit
already wrote gains what moved, and the bodies stay out; (3) *"already sent"* is a `sent_at`
stamp rather than a status word, with the in-app alert and the send test excluded by importing
`frozen_documents`' own scope rather than restating it; (4) *"the previous version"* is the row
below, never `version - 1`, because a deleted draft leaves a chain reading 1, 3; (5) the
Changed cell has THREE states — the wording arriving, an edit that moved nothing, and a backend
that has not answered — and collapsing any two is a false statement on a legal trail.

⚠ **WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, and both are recorded rather than left to be found.**
**(a) NOBODY IS ASKED WHY THEY CHANGED IT.** *"Softened wording"* is a judgement a person makes,
has no column anywhere, and is `OQ-255`(b) — still with the PO. The screen goes on saying *"no
change note recorded"* beside the derived facts, deliberately, so a reader cannot mistake a
diff for an author's note. **(b) NOTIFICATION TEMPLATES ONLY.** A bill template version holds a
`layout_key` and options — which of five platform layouts, not wording (`BR-NOT-026`) — so
*"the wording changed"* has nothing to point at there. Filed as **`OQ-1165`** with the three
shapes it could take, rather than guessed at.

## CR-048 — Templates & Notifications: wired end to end, not screens over a dead engine

**Arrived** 2026-08-29, from the Product Owner, with a 35-page teardown of the three screens
(`616e6390-Templates__Notifications_Teardown_v1.pdf`, traced against `v2.79.13` on
`smartbillhub.bynry.com/silver-creek-water`).

> *"please read this document - create cR and start making these changes"*

> *"in CR-048 - we ahve to implent forntend backend and wired the code so that it start wrking in the
> product"*

### ⚠ THE SECOND MESSAGE IS THE SCOPE RULING, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT ORDERS EVERYTHING

**Frontend AND backend AND wired.** Not a screen refresh, not an engine with no surface — the three
together, working in the product. That instruction happens to agree with the teardown's own headline,
which is why it reorders the task list rather than adding to it.

### Step 1 · CLASSIFY

| # | The statement | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| i | **The queue never reads the notification rule** | **DEFECT** — the rules are stored, editable and ignored |
| ii | Sixteen customer messages have wording seeded and no rule to send them | **DEFECT** for three of them (move-in, move-out, missed payment-plan instalment); **new requirement** for the rest |
| iii | No preview on a screen that authors regulated notices | **Requirement not met** |
| iv | The two-letter fallback mark, ruled 2026-08-16, was never built | **Ruled, not built** |
| v | Two template systems must become one | **New ruling** — needs writing down before anyone builds against it |
| vi | Five files are legacy CSS hosting a converted Tailwind table | **Structural**, and the root cause of seven visible defects |
| vii | Text escaping its card, cells wrapping to four lines, 60px pickers | **Visible defects** |

### ⚠ THE HEADLINE, AND WHY EVERY SCREEN TASK WAITS BEHIND ONE BACKEND TASK

**Switching *"Bill ready — email"* off on the settings screen changes nothing at all.** `notification_rules`
and `notification_rule_channels` are written and editable; the one write path into the queue takes its
channel list from **whichever module called it** and never consults the rule. The only thing added on the
way through is the print floor.

Everything else is built: the single write path, the transaction, the pinning, the audit row, the batch
claim, the idempotency key, the provider seam that refuses honestly. **138 messages are queued on the
PO's own screenshot because that machinery works.** One box is missing — *read the rule* — and it is the
difference between a settings screen that works and one that is decoration.

**This is what the PO's ruling means in practice: the wiring IS the change.** A CR that rebuilt all three
screens and skipped it would ship a prettier decoration.

### Step 2 · WHAT SIGNED STATEMENT IS BEING REVERSED

**None, and one ❄️ check is not needed:** nothing here touches B4/B5 money math. `GT-16` and the billing
contract are untouched — notifications compose and queue documents, they do not price them.

**Two things must be WRITTEN DOWN as rules before anyone builds against them**, and the teardown says so
itself — *"a page can be closed, and the next person to build against this will read the repository"*:

1. **Templates live in ONE place — and the PO ruled 2026-08-30 that the place is the SCREEN AND THE
   SERVICE, NOT THE SCHEMA (`BR-NOT-026`, closes `OQ-842`).** Verbatim: *"Yes, Go with option B; I agree"*.
   A person opens Templates once, sees notification templates and bill templates listed together, and edits
   either through the same draft → publish flow. **Both table pairs survive and NO ROW MOVES.**

   ⚠ **THIS PARAGRAPH USED TO SAY THE OPPOSITE, AND IT WAS HALF WRONG.** It read: *"Notification templates
   … and bill templates … become one system. Both already follow the same draft → publish, append-only,
   pinned-at-send pattern, so this is a merge of two things built alike, not a reconciliation of two
   designs."* **The LIFECYCLES are alike; the CONTENT MODELS are not.**
   `notification_template_versions` holds `subject`, `preheader` and `body` — words a person typed.
   `bill_template_versions` holds `layout_key` + an `options` blob — which of **five** pre-built platform
   layouts to use, with **no body text on that side at all**. Merging the tables would have meant a column
   meaningless on one side of every row, bought with a migration over rows a sent bill and a sent letter
   both point at.

   **The finding that decided it, measured before the question was put:** both pins are LOOSE COLUMNS, not
   foreign keys, so a migration that dropped a version row would raise no error and break no test — and the
   damage is asymmetric. A bill is locked at issue into `custom_snapshot`, so an orphaned pin there costs
   the provenance answer, not the document; a notification re-render is handed the pinned version and takes
   its body from that row, so orphaning one means a letter sent last July can never be produced again.

   **The cost the PO accepted:** *"one place"* is a promise about the PRODUCT, not the database. A future
   engineer opening the schema finds two table pairs behind one screen, so the unified service's own
   docstring carries that fact and the guard that matters asserts **both pairs still exist** — a later lane
   "finishing the merge" goes red rather than quietly doing what this ruling declined.
2. **A version pinned by a sent document survives any merge.** A sent document points at the exact version
   it rendered from; that version may be archived and never deleted. **This makes the merge a MIGRATION
   rather than a delete-and-recreate**, and it is the constraint that decides the whole shape of T10.

### Step 3 · IMPACT

| Surface | What it costs |
|---|---|
| Backend · notifications | The rule join at queue time; the event key on existing callers; the catalogue's missing events; the dispatch schedule |
| Backend · tenancy | Serve the logo bytes; draw the two-letter mark |
| Backend · billing | Queue bills as their EVENT, not as a source type |
| Frontend | Five files migrated to Tailwind FIRST; the designer rebuilt output-first; the notifications list and rule page |
| Business rules | Two new (one system for templates; a pinned version survives) |
| Screens | SET-09 · SET-12 · SET-12D · the ten designers S91–S106 |
| Decisions | **Five, and they are the PO's** — see step 5 |
| Deliberately NOT in scope | Any email/SMS/print provider adapter (PO instruction — the queue fills, nothing leaves the building) · delivered/bounced counts (they can only be true once something is sent) · rasterising the mark for PDF · the customer portal · the Work module |

### Step 4 · WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT AND IS NOW WRONG

**Nothing is wrong. Almost everything is right and unreached.** That is the unusual shape of this CR and
it is worth stating plainly: 37 templates are seeded, seven tables exist, eighteen endpoints serve them,
the queue holds real rows, and **in-app is the one channel that genuinely delivers today** — to staff,
not customers. The gap is not quality; it is the last hop and one missing join.

⚠ **One correction carried in from the teardown, affecting a document already published:** the database
diagram says 141 tables. That count read only each module's main model file, and several modules keep
tables elsewhere. Notifications is one of them: **7, not 3.**

⚠ **AND THE CORRECTION ITSELF DECAYED IN TWO DAYS — IT SAID 178 AND THE MEASURED NUMBER IS 180 (merge
lane, 2026-08-30).** The teardown's 178 was right when the teardown was written; `meter_read_asset_monthly_usage`
(BR-MET-141, 2026-08-27) and one sibling landed after it. **So the figure is not written down here as a
figure — it is written down as the WAY TO GET IT**, because that is the only form of it that cannot go
stale:

```
DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=config.settings.local python -c "
import django; django.setup()
from django.apps import apps
own = {'assets','audit','billing','customers','identity','ledger','metering',
       'notifications','payments','rating','tenancy'}
print(len({m._meta.db_table for m in apps.get_models()
           if m._meta.app_label in own and not m._meta.proxy}))"
```

**Measured 2026-08-30: 180** — metering 35 · rating 31 · tenancy 28 · customers 24 · payments 16 ·
billing 15 · assets 9 · **notifications 7** · identity 7 · ledger 6 · audit 2. Django's own `auth` (3)
and `contenttypes` (1) are excluded: they are the framework's tables, not this product's, and counting
them is how 184 becomes a fourth number in circulation. **The published diagram is outside this repo**,
so the correction is reported to the PO rather than applied — nothing in the tree can reach it.

### ⚑ WHERE IT STANDS — 2026-08-30, verified by the merge lane against the code, not taken from lane reports

**36 of 37 built. One part-built. Nothing outstanding that a lane could start today.**

| Wave | Tasks | State |
|---|---|---|
| **A** — the rule join | A1 | ✅ built. The queue reads the utility's own switches; suppressions are reported in a sentence. |
| **B** — every event fires | B1–B11 | ✅ **all eleven built.** Events **18 → 30**; the seeded-wording-with-no-rule gap **13 → 0**, computed and not typed. Seven of B11's thirteen have a live trigger; five are drawn and REFUSED by name with an open question each (`OQ-1160`–`OQ-1163`, `OQ-249`), which is the honest state and not an omission. |
| **C** — the Tailwind migration | C1 | ✅ built. All five notification/template files migrated; two visible defects fell out of it. |
| **D** — logo and mark | D1 · D2 | ✅ built. |

### ⚑ WAVE I — THE DECLUTTER, 2026-08-30 (v2.85.0)

**Wave H fixed the SHAPE of these screens; the PO then read the WORDS on them and found the same fault ten
times in one sitting.** Every one is a sentence rendered inside a table cell. A sentence in a cell sets the
height of its whole row and wraps at whatever width the column happens to be, so an explanation that is
correct, honest and required by a signed rule still turns a list you can scan into a wall you have to read.

**Nothing here could see it either, and for the same reason wave H's shape defects were invisible:** every
gate reads SOURCE, and a paragraph compiles exactly like a number. `DEF-2476` carries that escape reason.

**The ten, with the number before and the number after** (Chromium, 1728×1080, against the running app):

| # | The PO's words | Before → after |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | *"why we are showing two names under template name"* | the grouped cell drew the event as a heading AND the row's own name, so a template that is its own event printed the same words twice → **0 rows print a doubled name**; a row's name now comes from one place |
| 2 | *"autopay - why you are howing text - this is internal not required"* | four rows carried a scrolling danger box of the platform's own reasoning, **137–160px tall, the longest 499 characters** → **no row of the list holds a `data-refusal` box at all**; the fact is a status chip and the words are on its tooltip |
| 3 | *"used by - why so much text - just show some status"* | longest value **123 characters, six line boxes** → **19 characters, one line**, as one of five short statuses |
| 4 | *"past-due reminder - you created email SMS print, you can also do that by havng action button for each type"* | *"Past-due reminder"* was **3 rows**, *"Disconnect notice"* 4, *"Payment receipt"* 3, *"Payment plan"* 3, *"Bill ready"* 2 → **one row each, with a control per surface in the Kind column**; the list is **28 rows where it was 38** |
| 5 | *"Send-time elections"* — *"i agree - please remove"* | four switches, **three of which said in their own text that nothing read them** → section gone; the **one live switch moved** to the Payment received rule page and its three dormant siblings keep their columns |
| 6 | *"Which letter each tone sends"* — *"i agree - please remove"* | a third copy of the collections ladder → gone |
| 7 | *"Letters this utility can produce"* — *"i agree - please remove"* | the Templates screen, duplicated → gone |
| 8 | *"'Messages needing attention' gets its own tab"* | the worklist sat under six cards of configuration → its own tab, with its counts beside it |
| 9 | *"keep the fact, kill the paragraph"* (the unfireable-event note) | **3 line boxes, 78px, danger tier, no tooltip**, on twelve rows → **1 line, 18px, muted, the whole 95-character sentence on `title`** and on the event's own page |
| 10 | *"on this screen for KInd - can you use Icons"* | **4 line boxes, 0 of 38 cells drawn as icons, tallest row 235px** → **1 line box, 28 of 28 icons, tallest row 52px**; every glyph keeps the server's own word as its accessible name |
| 11 | *"this sentence is too long"* (the Templates caption) | **138 characters**, three sentences → **40 characters**, one line |

⚠ **THE KIND COLUMN'S WIDTH WENT UP, 100px → 166px, AND THAT IS NOT A FAILURE.** The words never widened
that column — they wrapped inside it — so width was the wrong evidence and the first draft of the check
used it and passed on the broken screen. Height is the evidence, and the check reports width without
asserting it. That is the DEF-182 shape (a check whose output cannot distinguish pass from fail) caught
before it shipped rather than after.

⚠ **NOTHING WAS DELETED TO ACHIEVE ANY OF THIS.** `BR-NOT-018` (an event nothing fires is DRAWN and REFUSED
BY NAME) and `BR-SHL-025` (a dead control carries its reason) are unchanged and still enforced: every
sentence taken off a row is still in the DOM on that row's `title`, still read out in full by a screen
reader, and still on the page the row opens. The switch on an unfireable event is still disabled with that
sentence as its tooltip. What changed is how much of a row a sentence may take.

**Step 7 · VERSION — `2.85.0`.** Taken as `2.85.0` and not `2.84.0` because the template-detail lane took
`2.84.0` on the tip while this wave was building, and one version covering two changes cannot answer

**Step 8 · ROLLBACK, stated before shipping:** the wave is frontend-only — no migration, no server change,
no data written — so reverting the two commits restores the previous screens exactly. The one thing a

### ⚑ WAVE H — THE SCREEN REPAIR, 2026-08-30 (v2.82.1)

**The PO reported these three screens as wrong for about three weeks and every round of fixes failed to
converge. The reason is now measured rather than guessed at, and it is ONE thing:** all three render their
body inside `settingsShared.PanelGrid` → `.settings-grid`, which is `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(320px, 1fr))`
— a legacy EQUAL-COLUMN card grid. Every previous fix was made INSIDE the redesigned components; the thing
squashing them was the page wrapper one level up that no lane owned. **And nothing in this repo could see
it**: every gate reads source, every screen test runs in jsdom, which performs no layout at all, so a
control rail collapsed to 108px satisfies every assertion that its class is present — and the class IS
present and IS correct.

**What each of the seven turned out to be, with the number before and the number after** (Chromium,
1728×1080, against the running app):

| # | The PO's words | Real? | Before → after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | *"Next Counter header wraps to two lines"* | **yes** | the label needs 146px, the column was declared 130px, so the whole header row was 54px where one line is 35px → column 152px, every header cell no-wrap, header row **35px** |
| 2 | *"label beside the field, should be stacked"* | **NOT REPRODUCED** | 29 label/field pairs on Numbering and 31 on Notifications, measured at 1728, 1440, 1280, 1100 and 900 — **300 pairs, every one stacked, zero side by side**. Most likely read from a screenshot of the crushed 108px and 330px columns. Nothing changed; `DEF-2482` records the measurement so nobody hunts it twice |
| 3 | *"Number formats and How they appear together scroll away"* | **yes, and the reported cause was wrong** | `align-items: start` is NOT the fault — a grid item's containing block is its grid AREA, so the rail has 1,944px of travel and pins correctly through a 2,154px scroll at 1728×1080 and 1440×900. At **1366×768 and 1280×720** the 729px rail is taller than the 712px/664px window, so **41px and 89px of its foot can never be reached** → it now scrolls inside itself once it outgrows the window, fully visible at both |
| 4 | *"Templates: the red placeholder box is unbounded"* | **yes** | four boxes 372px wide × 137–217px tall carrying 266–499 characters, all `max-height: none` → capped at 7.5rem with their own scroll, **nothing truncated** |
| 5 | *"Notifications: same box, same fault"* | **yes** | 238×318px, 414 characters → **819×97** from the layout fix alone, and capped as well so the next long sentence cannot repeat it |
| 6 | *"pagination shows more than 10 rows"* | **half** | see the box below — two tables genuinely had NO footer; the page SIZE is a signed figure and is not ours to move |
| 7 | *"the rules table overflows behind the next card"* | **yes** | five tables were 14px, 76px, 200px, 323px and **692px** wider than their own section → **every table on all four screens escapes by 0px**, and no page scrolls sideways |

**The root cause and the three screens after it:** the designer frame **448px → 1392px**, its control rail
**108px → 344px**, its rendered document **324px → 1032px**; SET-12 from **ten sections all 330px,
widest:narrowest 1.00:1** to a full-width channel strip, a full-width rules matrix and a body:rail of
**3.30:1**; SET-12D's body column from **336px 336px 336px** to one stacked column. `.settings-grid` itself
is deliberately unchanged and Company, Security and Regional still measure **448px 448px 448px** before and
after — that is asserted, not assumed.

### ⚠ ONE THING FOR THE PO, AND IT IS A COLLISION WITH THEIR OWN SIGNED RULING — NOT A QUESTION WE CHOSE TO ASK

**The report says these lists should page at 10 rows. The ratified page-size ladder is 50 / 100 / 200 / 500 /
1000, default 50** — PO ruling **2026-08-09** (A11 r2 Lane C, verbatim in the decision log: *"page sizes
50/100/200/500/1000, default 50"*), carried by **B14 rule 16** and built into `components/tableTypes.ts`,
which every list in the product reads. So the two halves of item 6 were handled differently, on purpose:

* **the half that is a defect is FIXED.** The letter library was rendering all 38 kinds of document and the
  queue all 50 messages **with no footer at all** — no range, no page arrows, no rows-per-page. Both now
  carry the shared `ListPager`. That is B14 rule 16 being met, and it needed no ruling.
* **the half that is a signed figure is NOT touched.** Adding 10 to the ladder, or defaulting to it, changes
  **every list in the product** — accounts, premises, reads, bills, payments — against a number the PO set
  themselves. Hard-won law 13 puts exactly this case on the short list of what legitimately reaches them:
  *a ruling that collides with a signed rule; the supersession must be stated, never assumed.*

**Put in plain English with the figure, which is how it should be asked:** *"You asked for these lists to
show 10 rows a page. Every list in the product currently offers 50, 100, 200, 500 or 1000 and starts at 50,
which is what you decided on 9 August. Do you want 10 added everywhere and made the starting choice — or
only on these two screens?"* **Nothing is built either way until they answer**, and the render-check
deliberately asserts that a footer EXISTS without asserting what size it offers, so the gate does not
quietly freeze the current ladder in place.

### THE DURABLE HALF, WHICH IS WHY THIS WAVE EXISTS AT ALL

`10-scripts/render-checks/cr048-notifications-geometry.mjs` printed every number above and **asserted none of
them**. It now carries **50 assertions** and exits non-zero: no `.settings-grid` on the three screens, the
designer's three widths, the body-to-rail ratio, no table past its card, no page scrolling sideways, a
footer on every list over ten rows (and deliberately not on a table of typed fields with one Save), no
danger-tier box over 170px, no wrapped column label, the numbering rail reachable at 1280×720, and the three
sibling tabs still on the shared card grid. **Proved RED before being trusted green** (hard-won law 7): with
the five fixes backed out it reports ten failures and reproduces the original figures exactly — header row
54px, 89px of rail below the window, refusals at 217px and 197px, designer frame 330px.

**The one gap it does not close, stated rather than left to be discovered:** it needs a running stack, so it
is not in `run_gates` and nothing runs it automatically. Wiring a browser check into the gate run is a
separate piece of work and a bigger one than this lane.

### ⚠ FIVE DECISIONS ARE THE PO'S, AND THREE OF THEM BLOCK TASKS

| The decision | Blocks | Why only they can make it |
|---|---|---|
| What happens when a utility picks two colours that make its own bill unreadable | D3 | A recommendation is on the table: keep their accent, let the product choose black or white text — so a utility is never told its brand colours are wrong and a bill is never unreadable |
| Who receives a staff alert | F8 · the SLA event | *"Owner"* is not one of this product's three roles, and the ruling on who may CHANGE a rule does not answer who GETS one |
| Whether a doubled reading should tell a customer before anyone has checked the meter | the high-usage event | **A stuck meter is the commonest cause of a doubled reading** |
| Which template tables survive the merge, and what happens to pinned versions | E9 | Engineering proposal, the PO's sign-off |
| What the generated mark does at print resolution | D3 on PDF only | Engineering, once a renderer exists — not blocking the screen half |

## CR-050 — Anything over 100 records goes to the background worker

### Step 0 · CAPTURE — the requester's words, verbatim, at arrival

> *"can we run anything above 100 recors directly using worker batch job"*
> — the Product Owner, 2026-08-30, in the working chat session, immediately after the
> `DEF-2487` demo failure: utility `ottumwa-water-works`, build `v2.81.1`, 1,048 accounts,
> a clean dry run and then *"Something went wrong. Nothing was saved — try again."*

### Step 1 · CLASSIFY — a DEFECT with a change riding on it, and the split matters

| Half | Classification | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **A 1,048-account commit is killed by the 60-second web-worker timeout** | **DEFECT** (`DEF-2487`, critical) | Nothing signed ever said an accounts row costs what a premises row costs. `ASYNC_ROW_BAR = 5,000` was ratified on a measurement taken on PREMISES rows (2.03 ms/row) and then applied to every target. That is our arithmetic, not the customer's requirement. |
| **The bar comes down to 100 for a batch that goes to a worker** | **CHANGE** | The requester named a number. It is theirs, it is what this CR carries, and the measurement below confirms it rather than choosing it. |

### Step 2 · WHAT SIGNED STATEMENT IS BEING REVERSED

**`CR-026`'s bar is NARROWED, not reversed.** The decision log of 2026-08-22 records:
*"at 5,000 rows the slowest stage is 5,000 x 2.03 ms = 10.2s, inside a 30s gateway timeout
with 3x margin; the 5,001st row goes to a worker."* Every word of that stays true **of the
target it was measured on**. What changes is that the bar is no longer ONE number for all
five targets: `ASYNC_ROW_BAR` remains 5,000 as the default and the accounts LOAD gets its
own, measured, bar of 100.

❄️ **No FROZEN B4/B5 figure is touched.** Nothing here is money math — the ledger posting the
accounts load performs is unchanged in every respect.

### Step 3 · THE MEASUREMENT, because a bar chosen without one is what caused this

`10-scripts/def2487_accounts_bar_benchmark.py`, live PostgreSQL, one transaction per size,
rolled back:

| accounts | load stage | per row | against the 60s web-worker timeout |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 100 | 12.7 s | 127 ms | 4.7x — comfortable |
| 500 | 60.5 s | 121 ms | 1.0x — level with the wall |
| 1,048 | 130.6 s | 125 ms | 0.5x — the worker is killed |

The cost per row is flat across a tenfold range, so the bar decides only how many of them run
inside a request. **There is no useful bar between 100 and 500**, which is why the requester's
own number is also the right one.

⚠ **THE BAR IS PER STAGE AS WELL AS PER TARGET, and that is measured too.** On the same
1,048-row file, transform took 0.2 s and validate 0.2 s. A bar of 100 on all three stages
would push a 101-row file's fifth-of-a-second validate into a worker and make somebody poll
for it. Only the LOAD carries the accounts cost, so only the LOAD gets the low bar.

### Step 4 · WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT AND IS NOW DIFFERENT

* **Nothing shipped is wrong.** The async path, the job record, the poll and the progress gauge
  were all built by `CR-026`; this changes WHEN that path is taken, not what it does.
* **One behaviour changes for existing users:** an accounts file of 101–5,000 rows used to
  answer 200 with a receipt and now answers 202 and finishes in a worker. That is the point.
* **No data already written is affected**; no migration; nothing to backfill.

### Step 5 · THE PRECONDITION, WHICH IS BIGGER THAN THE NUMBER

⚠ **Moving traffic to the queue is only safe if something is consuming the queue.** In
production `JOBS_EAGER` is False and `apps/tenancy/tasks.send` swallows a broker failure by
design — *"the record stays queued and is picked up by the next worker that sees it"* — which
is correct for work already recorded and catastrophic for work a person is waiting on. On a
deployment with no worker running, the lower bar would have turned a visible 500 into an
upload that reports success and never happens.

So the change ships with three things beside it, and none of them is optional:

1. **The promise is checked before it is made.** `core.jobs.dispatch_is_ready()` asks a probe
   registered by tenancy, which pings Celery's own control channel; no reply means the stage
   is REFUSED — *"Nothing is running to process a file this size. Start the background worker
   and try again, or upload a smaller file."* — and no job record is created. Verified live
   against a real Redis with the worker stopped: refused, 0 jobs created, run left `validated`.
2. **A queued stage nothing has claimed says so on screen.** A worker can die in the second
   after it answers the ping. Past 30 seconds the gauge reports `stalled` and stage 4 draws a
   warning whose first fact is the one a person actually needs: *nothing has been written*.
3. **The whole accounts load path was walked for role gates.** A deferred stage runs as
   `_JobActor`, which carries an id and no role by design; `DEF-2515` was one `@require_role`
   on one function that path calls, and it only ever fired above 5,000 rows. Lowering the bar
   moves nearly every real migration onto that path, so the load was RUN end to end as the
   worker runs it — with an opening balance and a deposit, so the ledger posting is included —
   and again through a real Celery worker on 1,048 accounts.

### Step 6 · EXECUTED THROUGH r11 — see `DEF-2487` in the defect register

### Step 7 · VERSION — `2.83.0`

A change (`<release>.<change>.<fix>`), so the middle number moves and the fix number resets.

### Step 8 · CLOSE, and the rollback stated before shipping

**Rollback is one line and needs no deploy of anything else:** empty
`import_runs.ASYNC_ROW_BAR_BY_TARGET` and every target is back on the default 5,000, exactly
as before. The refusal, the stalled flag and the stage-4 download are independent of it and
each rolls back on its own.

**What is NOT closed by this CR, stated rather than left to be found:** the accounts load
still costs ~125 ms and 45 queries per row, and a large part of that is that every created
account is snapshotted for its audit row through the whole account-detail payload — which
reaches into the ledger for an AR position on an account that cannot have one yet, and is
built TWICE per account in `apps/customers/services._open_account`. Moving the work to a
worker means nobody is waiting on it, so this is now slow rather than broken. It is worth its
own piece of work and is filed as `DEF-2480` rather than fixed here.

triage, which is the greppable trace of the reversal.

**So the last figure this repo records for the backend suite is 2 standing reds, and neither
of those two is still red.** ⚠ **That is NOT the same as saying the suite is green.** Twelve
backend test files changed between the triage and this tip — `test_cr049_t3_reprint_route.py`,
`test_cr049_t3_tamper_diagnostic.py`, `test_cr049_t4_bill_freeze.py`,
`test_def2473_a_queue_row_matches_its_class.py`, `journey_cohort_fixtures.py` and seven more —
and no recorded run covers them. **The honest state is: unmeasured since 12:44.**

⚠ **A figure of "3 failures, two of which have owners" is circulating today. It has no source
in this repository** — the only recorded triage says 2, and both of those are closed. Reported
rather than repeated.

⚠ **AND THE MEASUREMENT ITSELF HAS A HAZARD WORTH RECORDING, because it is this repo's own
recurring shape on a resource nobody thinks of as shared.** A full-suite run was attempted
from this lane and did not complete in 50 minutes, against a frontend suite that finishes in
244 seconds. `ps` shows why: **two lanes were running the whole backend suite against the same
PostgreSQL at once** — one in the main tree with no `--reuse-db` (so it creates and drops the
test database) and one in a worktree with `--reuse-db` (so it depends on that database
existing). Both processes were live and computing, neither deadlocked. **A `git worktree`
isolates files and refs; it does not isolate the DATABASE**, which is the same lesson
`check_head_current.sh`'s own header records about refs. A lane that needs a trustworthy suite
number needs its own database name, not just its own directory.

Three corrections in under two hours, each one accurate when written and overtaken within the
hour. **A status report on a branch moving at 135 commits a day has a half-life measured in
minutes, and chasing it produces a register entry that is mostly its own errata.** The next
reader should **re-measure**, not read further corrections.

**What makes the original section still useful despite that** is the one thing it did right
and the thing every finding in §4 was about: **every figure carries the commit and the clock
time it was taken at.** *"No commit names task 8 at 15:20 UTC at `4f87530`"* is permanently
true and self-dating; *"task 8 is not built"* would have been wrong within fifteen minutes.
**That is the transferable lesson, and it is cheaper than any gate:** a measured claim states
WHEN and AGAINST WHAT, or it becomes one of the nine stale sentences this report was written
to find.

**The findings in §4 are NOT affected by any of this.** All ten are about statements that were
wrong at the moment they were measured — a defect row saying `open` over a fix on the branch,
a wave heading counting ten rows in a table of eleven, a wave with no section at all. Those do
not decay; they are still there.
