### CR-060 · 5 · SIZE, AND THE PLAIN-ENGLISH CONFIRMATION

For reading aloud: *"The books are correct for everything a customer owes us and everything they pay.
What is missing is the other half. We record what we paid our suppliers for the water and power we
resell, and none of it reaches the books — so the accounts show income with almost no cost against it.
We also never book the revenue for water somebody has used but not yet been billed for. Fix those two
and a bookkeeper can sign the accounts; fix neither and what we have is a list of who owes us money
that calls itself accounting. Separately, the product does not know whether the customer using it is a
utility, a sub-metering company or an HOA — so everyone gets the utility's screen, and the one number a
sub-metering company exists to watch is calculated in a way that is useless to them."*

**The figures to quote.**
* **Today: 7 posting paths credit revenue and 3 debit cost.** With C1 and C15 that becomes **7 against
  about 20** — *"and the twenty include purchased power, purchased water and purchased gas, the money
  the utility actually spends to have something to sell. That is the difference between a receivables
  ledger and a book. Nothing else on the change list moves that line."*
* **Bought-versus-billed:** bought 1,000,000 gallons, billed 910,000 → **9% unaccounted for**, which
  is leak, meter under-registration or theft. **Computed per service per tenant today** — so a
  sub-metering company running forty buildings gets an average that *"describes neither and points at
  nothing anyone can go and fix."*
* **Scale:** at ~150 journal lines and ~180 invoice lines per account-year, 3,000 accounts is 450 K
  lines a year; **80,000 accounts is 12 M a year and 120 M after ten** — *"fine for PostgreSQL; not
  fine for the staffing premise."*
* **A capitalised asset booked as an expense:** a **$40,000** truck overstates this year's costs by
  $40,000, understates the next five years' by the depreciation that never happens, and leaves the
  asset off the balance sheet entirely. **The most common bookkeeping error at this size of utility.**

### CR-060 · 6 · HOW THE FINANCE MODULE WORKS TODAY — the facts every task below depends on

Reproduced so the tasks are buildable without the source page.

**EVERYTHING FUNNELS THROUGH ONE WRITER.** Six money events reach the books through
`apps/ledger/posting.py` and nothing else: **a bill run issuing an invoice** (billing, five phases) ·
**a payment clearing** (payments — cash, cheque, ACH) · **a reversal, refund or write-off** (payments
— NSF, bad debt) · **a deposit batch reconciled** (payments — bank line matched) · **a manual journal
entry or opening balance** (ledger, staff-authored) · **a supplier invoice captured** (ledger, cost of
service). The module seams — `billing/posting_seam.py`, `payments/ledger_seam.py`,
`ledger/journal.py` + `opening_balances.py`, `ledger/cost_capture.py` — **carry figures and documents
across the boundary, never a journal line.** `posting.post()` refuses unbalanced pairs (debits =
credits, or `PostingError`), keys one entry per source event, requires the tenant GUC (`app.tenant_id`,
RLS FORCE), refuses more than 2 dp at posting (`BR-LED-025`), **REFUSES an entry dated inside a
CLOSED fiscal period** ⚠ **CORRECTED 2026-09-02 (`DEF-3202`) — this sentence read *"resolves the entry
date to an **OPEN fiscal period** (`close.resolve_entry_date`)"*, and it was not true: `post()` did no
period check at all, and an entry dated 31 July posted into a CLOSED July, moving a month the books
promise cannot move. It refuses now. The FORWARD is still `close.resolve_entry_date`'s and the CALLER
calls it, because only the caller knows whether moving a date is right — a payment that genuinely
arrived late should move (`BR-TEN-038`, LE-9); a month-end accrual must never (this CR's own T7
judgment). A writer that forwarded by default would have silently done the wrong one of those for
every caller nobody has written yet.** — and writes the audit row (hard rule 7). **The expense
side is deliberately severed** — cost capture stops before the writer and writes to a **register the
reports read directly.**

**IS THERE A DELAY BEFORE THE WRITER RUNS? BETWEEN THE MONEY EVENT AND ITS JOURNAL ENTRY, NONE AT
ALL.** It is the **same database transaction**. `post_bill_issue` is called inside the issue
transaction, and the payment path's `_allocate_and_post` **carries an explicit warning in its own
docstring that it is not a second transaction boundary and must never be called from anywhere else.**
If the posting refuses, the invoice or payment **rolls back with it.** The reason is written into the
code: **money in the system that never reached the books is the state nothing can repair — because the
payment row is immutable the instant it commits.** There is **no outbox, no queue and no nightly
posting sweep.**

**But two other delays are real and both are deliberate.** *The clerk waits, sometimes:* bill-run
calculate, issue and release can run as background jobs — the request body carries `background: true`
and the API answers **202 with a job id to poll** instead of 201; **production defaults `JOBS_EAGER`
to false**, so a real run goes to a Celery worker on billing's own named queue. **The invoice and its
journal entry still appear together, atomically, inside it.** *The money waits for the bank:* three
gates hold an entry back until the cash is real — **a payment with no clearing date is `processing`
and posts nothing** · **a deposit batch posts at RECONCILE, when the bank confirms, not when the batch
is cut** · **an event dated into a closed period is moved forward rather than reopening the month.**

**TWO DATES, BECAUSE THEY ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS.** `entry_date` is the **book date** — what the
trial balance groups by. `posted_at` is the **wall clock** — when it became immutable. *Worked case: a
cheque dated 30 Jul, July's books closed 5 Aug, the clerk records it cleared on 7 Aug →
`resolve_entry_date()` moves the book date to the first open day, `posted_at` is 7 Aug, and **July's
trial balance is byte-identical before and after.***

**THE BILL RUN — a staged pipeline a clerk drives, not a button that does everything.**
**1 · Gather & check** — cycle scope, subscriptions, reads, balances, credits, overcharges.
**Read-only**; the S31.2 sub-tabs re-run it on every refresh. (`POST /billing/runs`,
`GET /billing/runs/{id}/summary`) · **2 · Resolve exceptions** — per-case tables with bulk actions: no
reads published, unit with no billable account, account held by a disputed read; each break can be
**held for the catch-up queue or retried.** · **3 · Calculate** — rating resolves the plan and rate
schedule, prices consumption, applies taxes, discounts and fees, drafts the invoice with **stamped
lines**. · **4 · Issue — the one transaction that matters.** Invoice lines are frozen, the document
snapshot is locked, and `posting_seam.post_bill_issue` is called **inside the same transaction — a
posting refusal refuses the whole issue.** · **5 · Release** — delivery hands off to notifications:
print set, email, portal.

**WHAT THE ISSUE ENTRY ACTUALLY POSTS — NOT THE BILL'S TOTAL.** `posting_buckets()` sums the **stamped
invoice lines** into GL buckets: one debit to **1200 Accounts receivable** against credits to the
per-service revenue accounts, the tax payable series, fee revenue and contra-revenue discounts.
**Prior balance and total due are presentation and are deliberately excluded** — *prior balance is
already in AR from its own bill, so posting it again would double the receivable.* **One bill issue
produces exactly ONE journal entry however many lines the invoice has**; the worked case in the code:
**15 invoice lines collapse to 9 buckets, so the entry has 10 lines.**

**PER ACCOUNT PER YEAR:** 12 monthly bills ≈ 12 entries / 108 lines · 12 payments cleared ≈ 12 / 36 ·
occasional fee, correction, write-off ≈ 2 / 6 → **≈ 26 entries and ≈ 150 lines per account-year.**
*(The oft-quoted "20–30" is right for an account-MONTH across everything, not for one bill.)*

**THE POSTING CONTRACT.** A module builds a `PostingRequest`: a posting key, a book date, a wall-clock
moment, a currency, and a tuple of `PostingLine`s. It hands that to `post()`. **It gets back a
`PostingResult` echoing the debits and credits that landed, so the caller can tie out what it asked for
against what happened — at the moment of posting, rather than a month later on the trial balance.**
**Every line carries its provenance:** `source_type` and `source_id` are **required on every single
line**, so any figure traces back to the document that produced it; five more dimensions (service,
account, premises, unit, tax authority) are optional **because they don't all apply — a cash line names
no service.** **The idempotency key is COMPOSED, never hand-written:**
`posting_key(source_type, source_id, event)` **refuses a missing part rather than building a short
key**, because two different payments both keyed `"payment||cleared"` would collide — *which is
precisely the double-post the guard exists to prevent.* **A replay returns `created=False` as a
RESULT, not an exception:** a resumed batch replaying is the correct outcome, not an error.

**THE CHART — 35 accounts seeded per tenant, and only for services that tenant actually sells.**
1000–1210 asset (Cash · Undeposited funds · Accounts receivable · **Unbilled AR**) · 2200 liability
(tax payable series, **generated per authority, never re-let**) · 2300–2400 liability (customer deposit
liability · customer credit balances) · 3000 equity (opening balance clearing) · 4100–4170 revenue (ten
services, **base and usage split where it applies**) · 4180–4300 revenue (budget variance · minimum-bill
adjustment · late fee · NSF & other fee · **customer discounts, contra**) · 5100–5300 expense (cost of
service — purchased power, water, gas · treatment · hauling · transport · O&M · infrastructure) ·
6800–6950 expense (bank fees · bad debt · deposit interest).

**THE THREE TABLES THE BOOKS ARE MADE OF.** Money is `NUMERIC(18,6)` — **a lawful container for the
4-decimal rule, displayed at 2.**
* **`journal_entries`** — `id` (uuid7, time-ordered) · `tenant_id` (RLS scope, PROTECT on delete) ·
  **`entry_date`** (the book date) · **`posted_at`** (the wall clock) · `type` (standard · accrual ·
  reversing) · `status` (**a draft may be unbalanced; a post may not**) · `source_type` + `source_id`
  (**no FK — polymorphic**) · `posting_key` (**partial unique index — NULL for a manual JE, which has
  no upstream event**) · `number` (`JE-000104`, **stamped at post; a draft has none and gaps happen**) ·
  `currency` **on the entry, not the line — a mixed-currency entry cannot balance** · `memo` ·
  `reversal_of` (**unique — one mirror, ever**) · `auto_reverse_entry_id` (set on the accrual, pointing
  forward at its day-1 reversal) · `created_at`/`updated_at`.
* **`journal_lines`** — `id` (uuid7, **partitioned by year**) · `tenant_id` · `journal_entry_id` ·
  `ledger_account_id` · **`side`** (debit/credit — **sign lives here, never in the amount**) ·
  `amount` (`numeric(18,6)`, **always ≥ 0**) · `source_type`/`source_id` **required on every line** ·
  the five optional dimensions — **and a line that names a customer account and cannot resolve its
  premises is REFUSED, not written NULL.**
* **`ledger_accounts`** — `code` (**free-form, unique per tenant; two tenants may both run a 4100;
  frozen once posted against**) · `name` (editable) · `type` (**exactly five: asset · liability ·
  equity · revenue · expense; frozen once posted against**) · **`designation`** (the semantic handle
  code resolves by — `accounts_receivable`, `bank_fees`, `write_off` — **this is the indirection that
  lets a tenant renumber**) · `qbo_ref`/`xero_ref` · `deleted_at` (**deactivate-first; delete refuses
  when any reference is unreadable**).

**⚠ THE FIVE-TYPE VOCABULARY IS THE LOAD-BEARING CONSTRAINT.** There is **no fund, no contra type, no
function or activity column**, and the line's dimension set is **a fixed column list rather than a
configurable one.** Everything in the framework question below follows from that single fact.

**MONTH-END CLOSE.** `close.py` computes a **five-item checklist live** and closes on
**warn-and-confirm**: an incomplete close is **refused without a reason and recorded with one**, with
the incomplete items **snapshotted**. **Only a System Admin reopens.** Once closed,
`resolve_entry_date()` pushes a late-dated event forward, **so a closed month's trial balance is
byte-identical before and after.** The accounting export then runs **four gates in order**: the window
must be closed · must not already be covered by another batch · **must foot** · and every row must
carry the target system's reference. **The payload is stored, so the file is hash-stable and a later
mapping edit cannot silently rewrite a batch that was already sent.**

**RECONCILING AGAINST THE BANK — 6 tables, 9 endpoints, S37–S40.** `bank_accounts` ·
`deposit_batches` · `deposit_batch_events` · `bank_statement_imports` · `bank_lines` ·
`bank_rec_resolutions`. **Reconciliation runs on deposit batches, not on individual payments — which
is how a bank actually presents the money.** Cut the batch (day × tender) → import the statement (CSV
to bank lines, **SHA-256 fingerprint so the same statement cannot be imported twice**) → auto-match
then match by hand → **explain the difference** (a gap is a resolution with a **named cause**, not a
silent adjustment; `derive_processor_fee()` books the fee to **6800 Bank fees**) → reconcile (**DR the
bank account, CR 1010 Undeposited funds**, with the fee leg where one applies). **Unreconciling posts
NOTHING.** It is a status change, not a reversal — **because the cash genuinely did move. Reversing the
entry would misstate the bank account.**

**GL MAPPING — ONE RESOLUTION, SIX PLACES TO CONFIGURE IT.** **The mapping logic is NOT duplicated.**
There is exactly one function that decides a line's GL account — `issue._gl_account_for()` — **it runs
once, at issue, and stamps the answer onto `invoice_lines.gl_account_id`.** The posting seam then reads
that stamp and **deliberately refuses to re-resolve it**, with the reason in its docstring: *resolving
it again here would be a second implementation of that rule sitting downstream of the first, and the
two would disagree eventually — with the books holding the copy that was wrong.* **That is the correct
design and it is already built.** **The CONFIGURATION surface, though, is scattered — and the code says
so itself: eleven columns across five modules can hold a GL account, and a human sets them on six
different screens under two different top-level sections:** Settings → Services
(`tenant_services.revenue_account`, `.base_revenue_account`) · Settings → Accounting (**13
designations**, `ledger_accounts.designation`) · Plans & Rates → Charge Codes S12
(`charges.gl_account_id`, `plan_services.gl_account_id`) · Plans & Rates → Taxes & Fees S13
(`taxes.liability_gl_account_id`, `.collection_allowance_gl_account_id`) · Settings → Configure
(`payment_methods.clearing_gl_account_id`, `reason_codes.default_gl_account_id`) · Settings → Company →
Regional (`fy_start_month`, `fy_start_day`, `close_cadence`, `close_day`). **`GET /ledger/gl-mappings`
is served and shows all six. `PUT` is NOT served, because half of what it would write is tenancy's
column and a cross-module write is forbidden.**

**THE EXPENSE SIDE — captured, deliberately not posted.** The product captures the cost of service and
**processes none of it: no approvals, no payment runs, no vendor master, no cheque printing. Full
accounts payable was explicitly declined.** Each captured invoice carries an **optional volume**, and
**that is what earns the feature its keep**: it computes the one figure no accounting package can —
bought 1,000,000 gallons, billed 910,000, **9% unaccounted for.** The figure is **all-or-nothing per
service per period** and is **reported absent with its reason rather than derived from a partial
denominator.** `post_capture_to_journal()` is a deliberate no-op **and the reason is a RULE rather than
a preference**: posting `DR cost-of-service / CR accounts payable` would create **a liability this
product forbids anyone to drain** — twelve months at $3,100 of purchased water would leave **$37,200
standing** for invoices the utility had actually settled by cheque, **and a growing false number is
worse than an absent true one.** So **no `2500 Accounts payable` is proposed in the chart**, the
export's cost section is labelled **register-derived**, and **the function stays present-but-empty with
a test asserting it posts zero lines — so the day supplier payments exist, the test that must change is
standing in the right place.** *Corrections after a period closes are permitted, but only with a
reason; a corrected row whose money has already left in an export carries an explicit flag saying so.*

**IS THERE AN ACCOUNTING-METHOD CONTROL? NO — AND THE REASON IS SHARPER THAN "not yet".** There WAS
one. **The PO removed it**, and the source records why: **it had zero readers.** *(⚠ See §0c finding 1
— that is no longer true.)* **So the chart of accounts is identical for every tenant and the product is
hard-wired ACCRUAL:** revenue recognises at bill issue — DR receivable, CR revenue — **never at cash
receipt. A cash-basis utility using this product is keeping accrual books.** **One real basis switch
exists and it is much narrower than a method:** `tax_remitting_basis_by_authority` lets a tenant say,
**per tax authority**, whether remittance is reported on **what was billed** or **what was collected**.
**It changes a report, not a posting** — the correct shape for cash-vs-accrual VAT/GST schemes, **and
the only place in the product where a basis is a setting.**

**⚠ AND ONE OF ITS TWO VALUES CANNOT BE COMPUTED.** The **billed** basis is exact. The **collected**
basis asks how much tax sits inside the payments received — **and `allocations` records only payment,
invoice and amount. It does not record which charge classes the money met.** The report **correctly
returns absent with its reason** rather than showing the billed figure, *which would have a utility
remit tax on money nobody has paid.* **And the ruling that declared it computable rests on an
allocation order the product does not use:** it was justified on the ground that a partial payment
**covers tax first** — a $100 payment against a $247.87 bill clearing all **$20.97** of tax before the
utility keeps anything. **The shipped default order is usage and base first, then taxes, and the order
is a tenant setting besides.** **On one partial payment the same bill's collected tax is 0.00, 12.69 or
20.97 depending on the order — a 20.97 spread on a single bill, filed monthly across four
authorities.** *So this is not a reporting gap to fill in; **two signed rulings disagree, and the data
cannot settle it either way.***

**WHAT THE BOOK CAN ANSWER — four of five statement levels, and the fifth is ruled.**
*Regular account* — **yes**; every line carries `account_id` and `ix_journal_lines_account` indexes it.
*Master account* — **yes**; a master is **not a parent**, it is an ordinary account with `kind='master'`
billed directly, **so its statement is just an account statement and there are no child accounts to
roll up.** *Premises* — **yes**; `premises_id` is stamped at posting and indexed. **This is the
by-premises summary that was designed and never built.** *Unit* — **yes, unindexed** *(⚠ §0c finding 2:
service and tax authority are unindexed too)*. *Customer* — **yes, RULED**; no `customer_id` on a
journal line, **so it is a join through `customer_accounts`.**
**THE APPORTIONMENT QUESTION DISSOLVES RATHER THAN NEEDING A SPLIT, and the rule is one sentence: sum
within a customer, never across customers.** A customer statement lists that customer's linked
accounts, each at its own balance, and totals them as *"across N accounts"*. **A jointly-held account
appears at FULL VALUE on each holder's statement — which is not a double-count but the correct
presentation of joint and several liability, where each party is liable for the whole.** *The
double-count only appears if someone sums two customers together, and nobody asks for that figure.*
**Liability stays where it already is: on the account**, which is what the bill was issued against and
what every journal line points at. **The statement presents; it never re-attributes.** *(The link table
already carries the pair, the confidence tier — strong · probable · weak — and the person who confirmed
it, and says in its own words that "the uniqueness is on the PAIR, not on the account, so nothing here
forbids a jointly-held account".)*

**HOW MANY WAYS DOES EACH KIND OF MONEY ARISE?** **Revenue: 16 accounts, 7 posting paths** — all seven
fire **inside one entry, the bill issue**: usage · base · fee (the charge code's own GL) · minimum-bill
adjustment · budget variance · late fee · NSF fee; **plus discount, which is contra-revenue and posts
as a debit.** **Cost: 11 accounts, 3 paths today** — bank fees (deposit reconcile) · bad debt
(write-off) · deposit interest (final bill); **the eight cost-of-service accounts have no posting path
at all.** **Tax: 1 account per authority, 2 paths** — credited at bill issue, debited at remittance.
**Revenue is the elaborate side and cost is nearly empty, and that asymmetry is the single clearest
statement of what the books currently are: a receivables ledger with an expense footnote.**

**⚠ AND C1 ALONE LEAVES THE TWO SIDES ON DIFFERENT BASES, WHICH IS WORTH NAMING RATHER THAN
DISCOVERING.** Revenue is recognised **when it is billed**; under C1 cost is recognised **when it is
paid**. *A supplier invoice received on the 28th and paid on the 5th sits in no month at all — the
commodity was sold in one period and its cost lands in the next.* **The fix is the mechanism already
being built for the other side: C17 accrues unpaid supplier invoices at close and reverses on day one
— the same code path as C2 pointed the other way — giving true matching WITHOUT creating the standing
payables balance the PO rejected, because the accrual undoes itself before anyone could mistake it for
a liability to pay.**

**HOW BIG DOES IT GET? FOUR SCENARIOS, BECAUSE THE CEILING IS DISPUTED — and this is T1.**
**The repository contradicts itself and the partition decision was justified against the smaller
number.** The project brief says *"<3,000 connections, 1–2 staff"*. The non-functional requirements say
*"~5,000 and above — indicative, not a hard cap"*, that the Starter/Growth/Scale tiers are
*"commercial, not technical ceilings"*, and in as many words: **"design must not hard-limit"**. *So
60,000–80,000 accounts is not out of scope by the requirement — it is 16× to 27× the market
description, and the two documents cannot both be steering.*

| Accounts | Journal lines/yr | After 10 yrs | Invoice lines/yr | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **3,000** · the brief | 450 K | 4.5 M | 540 K | Small. A single unpartitioned table would do. |
| 20,000 | 3.0 M | 30 M | 3.6 M | Comfortable, with the partition key fixed. |
| 60,000 | 9.0 M | 90 M | 10.8 M | **Yearly partitions are now too coarse.** |
| 80,000 | 12.0 M | 120 M | 14.4 M | Fine for PostgreSQL; **not fine for the staffing premise.** |

**What gives way, in the order it gives way — and only the last is not a database problem.**
1. **Partition granularity — first to break, cheapest to fix.** The *"by year"* ruling records its own
   justification: *"at this product's declared ceiling of utilities under 3,000 connections a year of
   lines is a small partition"* — **explicitly scoped to 3,000.** At 80,000 a yearly partition holds
   12 M lines per tenant, **and partitions are not tenant-scoped, so the real partition is that
   multiplied by every tenant in it.** **The fix is reverting to what the requirement originally
   said** — monthly was the option put to the PO and was superseded by the yearly ruling. **⚠ Note the
   inconsistency it left behind: `audit_log` and `meter_reads` stayed MONTHLY, so the two largest
   financial tables ended up with the COARSEST partitions in the product.**
2. **The partition key — no pruning at all.** At 3,000 accounts a full-partition scan is invisible; **at
   80,000 it means a one-month trial balance reads a year of lines.** *Fixing the granularity without
   fixing the key buys much less than it looks.*
3. **The bill run — wall clock, not correctness.** The transaction boundary is right and scales: issue
   is **per invoice under a `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` row lock**, so 80,000 bills are 80,000 small
   transactions rather than one enormous one, **and two workers racing the same draft serialise
   correctly.** The resume checkpoint is per-account. **Two things still need attention:** the gather
   loop is a plain `for account in accounts` **with no `.iterator()`, so the queryset materialises — at
   80,000 rows that is memory nobody budgeted**; and 80,000 sequential issue transactions is a long wall
   clock on one worker — **the queue and the scope key exist, so the work is parallelising the run, not
   redesigning it.**
4. **Onboarding — an arithmetic limit, already stated.** Imports are capped at **10,000 rows per run**
   for accounts and assets, and unit-pattern generation at **3,000 per run**. **Loading 80,000 accounts
   is therefore eight import runs minimum** — a stated design limit rather than a defect, **but a
   migration plan nobody has written.**
5. **The staffing premise — the one that is not a database problem.** The requirement says **1–2 staff
   per tenant.** The exception queue scales linearly with accounts and the staff does not. **At a 2%
   exception rate, an 80,000-account run produces 1,600 exceptions for one clerk.** *Bulk actions are
   what make this survivable rather than impossible, which is exactly why they were required — but this
   is where the product premise gives way well before PostgreSQL does, and no index fixes it.*

**⚠ AND ONE THAT WOULD BE A REWRITE, WORTH ASKING ABOUT NOW.** Everything above assumes **monthly**
meter reads. **The read-method list already includes AMI**, and if interval data is ever in scope the
arithmetic **changes character rather than degree: hourly reads at 80,000 meters is 700 million rows a
year, which dwarfs every table discussed here combined.** Nothing in the code suggests interval storage
is intended — frequency is free text and reads arrive through cycles and batches. **So the question to
settle is not how to store it, but whether it is in scope at all, because that answer changes the
storage design rather than tuning it.**

**FIT AGAINST THE TEN REGULATORY FRAMEWORKS — 0 of 10 appear in the codebase.** None is named anywhere
— not in code, not in tests, not in the decision log. *(The two apparent hits are substring accidents:
every "FERC" is inside `TransferCommitPlan`, and every "Ind AS" is inside phrases like "…behind as…".)*
**That is not automatically a defect.** The honest description of what exists is **a framework-neutral
meter-to-cash sub-ledger that exports to an accounting system** — and the design says so deliberately:
**cost capture posts nothing precisely because it would create a liability this product forbids anyone
to drain.** The statutory reporting is meant to happen in QuickBooks, Xero or the ERP downstream.
**The question is whether that stays true as you move into these markets.**

**What genuinely travels to all ten:** double-entry with **enforced** balanced pairs (a database
trigger, not a convention) · accrual recognition at issue · **a configurable fiscal calendar** (start
month and day, monthly or quarterly cadence — covering April for UK/India/Canadian public sector, July
for Australia and many US municipals, and January, **without a code change**) · period close with lock,
reopen and audit, **and forward-dating rather than reopening** · immutable entries with corrections as
new rows · **a tenant-owned, free-form, importable chart** (a customer can key in a FERC or GASB code
set today, because code is text and unique only per tenant) · **the designation indirection**, so
application logic never names a number.

**What each framework needs that is not there:** fund / fund-balance dimension (**GASB · PSAS** —
absent; five account types only, no fund column) · **FERC Uniform System of Accounts** — function,
activity, plant accounts (**FERC · NARUC** — absent; the chart is commercial 1000/4000 and lines carry
no function) · utility plant, CWIP, depreciation (absent) · regulatory assets & liabilities, deferrals
(absent) · **allowance for doubtful accounts / ECL** (**IFRS 9 · Ind AS 109** — absent; write-off is
direct, `DR 6900 / CR 1200`, **no contra-asset account exists**) · **unbilled revenue accrual**
(**seeded, unused** — `1210` exists and nothing posts to it) · multi-currency / FX translation (absent;
one currency per entry, no rate, no translation) · multi-book / parallel GAAP (absent) · budgetary
accounting and encumbrances (absent) · modified accrual option (absent) · segment reporting
(**partial** — a service dimension exists on every line, no segment concept above it) ·
**cash-vs-accrual tax remittance basis (BUILT** — per authority, both bases always computed).

**⚠ THE ONE STRUCTURAL BLOCKER, IF YOU WANT TO MOVE UPMARKET.** A journal line's dimensions are **a
fixed column list** — service, account, premises, unit, tax authority — **declared on the table AND on
the frozen `PostingLine` contract.** GASB and PSAS need a fund; FERC needs a function. **Adding either
is a schema migration plus a change to the one contract every posting caller depends on, not a
configuration.** *Everything else on that list is chart content, which the tenant can already supply.*

**⚠ AND THAT IS WHY THE FUND DIMENSION IS A DECISION WITH A DEADLINE RATHER THAN A BACKLOG ITEM (T1b).**
**Journal lines are immutable — corrections are new rows and nothing updates a posted line. So a
dimension added later is NULL on every line already posted, permanently.** A utility that adopts fund
reporting in year three gets **fund-accurate books from year three and a silent discontinuity before
it, and no migration can repair that, because repairing it would mean editing history the product
exists to protect.** **So the cost of this decision rises with every row posted, and the cheapest moment
to say yes is before the first tenant goes live in one of those markets. Saying no is entirely
reasonable — it is a different product — but it should be said, dated, and revisited when a GASB or
PSAS customer actually appears, rather than discovered at that point.**

> ### ⚠ CORRECTION, 2026-09-01 — THE DEADLINE ABOVE IS REAL BUT MUCH NARROWER THAN THIS CR STATED
>
> The paragraph above is written as though the discontinuity were global. **It is not. Every journal
> line belongs to ONE utility** — `journal_lines.tenant_id` is a FK to `tenancy.Tenant`, with RLS
> FORCE — **so a customer who signs in year three has NO lines before year three.**
>
> **Which means the case the paragraph is actually worried about does not exist.** Add the fund tag
> the day a government utility becomes a customer and **they get fund-accurate books from their very
> first bill.** The blank history is *other utilities'* history, and nobody will ever run a fund
> report over it.
>
> **The real exposure is ONE case, and it is much narrower:** a utility **already using the product**
> whose auditor starts requiring fund reporting **mid-stream**. That utility gets fund-accurate books
> from the day the column lands and a gap before it. Real, but narrow — and it is the only thing the
> deadline is about.
>
> **What does NOT change:** the migration cost itself (a schema change plus a change to the frozen
> `PostingLine` contract every posting caller depends on), and the fact that a decision unmade is a
> decision made by default at the worst moment. **T1b still needs one sentence and a date.**
>
> **Why this correction is here rather than an edit:** the original paragraph was checked against the
> schema and found overstated. It is kept verbatim so the next reader sees the change and not only the
> conclusion — the same discipline this register applies to a superseded PO ruling.

**THE FINDING THAT REFRAMES EVERYTHING ELSE — verified in code.** **The product does not know which
kind of customer it is serving.** The rule names three — utility, sub-metering company, HOA — **and
there is no tenant-type field anywhere.** *"HOA" exists in the database only as a **premises owner
category**, describing who owns a building, not who is running the software.* **So nothing can adapt:
not the tiles, not the vocabulary, not the defaults. Every tenant gets the utility's screen.** And **the
one figure a sub-metering company exists to watch is computed at a grain that is useless to it**:
bought-versus-billed is calculated **per service, per period, across the whole tenant**, and a
sub-metering company runs forty buildings — **blending a leaking building with a tight one produces an
average that describes neither and points at nothing anyone can go and fix.** **The cause is ONE MISSING
COLUMN:** `supplier_invoices` carries a service, an amount and a volume — **and no premises, no unit, no
meter.** *The receivable side already carries premises on every journal line. Only the cost side cannot
say where the money went.*

**CAN COSTS ACCEPT EVERYTHING — PAYROLL, CAPITAL ASSETS, ALL OF IT? Yes to most, no to one.** **Yes for
operating costs, and it is a small change:** the category list today is **the tenant's live service list
plus exactly two others — O&M and Infrastructure — and that second half is HARDCODED in the chart.** *A
tenant cannot record payroll, insurance, a legal bill, fuel or rent anywhere in this product.* **So the
promise of "one place" is not yet true, and closing that is mostly seeding chart accounts.**
**NO for capital assets, and this is the one that would do real damage.** **A $40,000 truck is not an
expense.** Recorded as one it overstates this year's costs by $40,000, understates the next five years'
by the depreciation that never happens, **and leaves the asset off the balance sheet entirely** — *the
most common bookkeeping error at this size of utility.* **And it does not need solving, because it is
already solved elsewhere:** the assets module already carries `purchase_cost`, `depreciation_method`,
`expected_life_years` and a computed `book_value_amount`. **Capital spending has a home; it simply is
not this tab.** **The right move on the Costs screen is a REFUSAL that points there —** *"this looks
like equipment: record it on the asset instead"* **— not a category that quietly accepts it.**
**⚠ AND THE EXPOSURE BECOMES REAL THE DAY C1 LANDS.** While capture posts nothing, a miscategorised row
is a tidy-up. **Once costs post on settlement, a capitalised asset recorded as a cost posts a wrong
number into the trial balance — and by then it is a signed figure in a closed month, not a report you
can re-run. So decide the capital boundary BEFORE you post costs, not after.**

**A CATEGORY LIST THAT MATCHES A US UTILITY OPERATING STATEMENT** (grouped so the export lands in
recognisable buckets rather than one flat "costs" total): **Cost of service** — *built* — purchased
power · water · gas · sewer treatment · trash hauling · broadband transport (**the six that carry a
volume and drive bought-versus-billed**) · **Operations & maintenance** — *partly*; one flat O&M bucket
exists, **split it: labour · materials & supplies · contract services** · **Customer accounts** —
*missing*; billing and collection costs, postage, printing, meter reading · **Administrative &
general** — *missing*; payroll and benefits · insurance · professional fees · office and rent ·
vehicles and fuel · **Taxes other than income** — *missing*; property, franchise and payroll taxes,
**distinct from the customer taxes the Taxes tab remits** · **Depreciation** — *elsewhere*; comes from
the asset's own life and book value, **never captured as an invoice** · **Capital spending** —
*elsewhere*; belongs on the asset.
**⚠ ONE CAUTION ON PAYROLL SPECIFICALLY.** A single figure — *"payroll, $12,000"* — is fine as a record
of what left the bank, **and that is all this product claims to be. But it is not payroll accounting:
the withholdings a utility holds back for the employee and remits to the government are a liability,
and a one-line record does not carry them.** **Label the category so nobody mistakes it for a payroll
system, and keep the posture already ruled for AP — capture, hold, reconcile, export, and process
nothing.**

**THE SURFACE, COUNTED FROM CODE.** **118** finance API operations (of the product's 472) · **38**
finance DB tables (billing 16 · payments 16 · ledger 6; of 181) · **20** wired finance routes (of 103)
· **46** finance migrations (billing 27 · payments 10 · ledger 9) · **21** A1 screens (S30–S43,
S56–S60, S73–S74; of 102) · **1,402** backend finance test functions across 109 files (of 7,443 in 595)
· **441** executable Playwright E2E blocks (101 specs, 8 finance-named) · **308** E2E journey documents.
**⚠ TWO OF THOSE NUMBERS ARE NOT WHAT THEY LOOK LIKE.** The **308 journey documents are written
specifications with handoff contracts between steps — they are NOT executed by a runner**; the
executable suite is the **441** Playwright blocks. And **the golden billing figures: the harness
everyone quotes as `33/33` checks that B4/B5 agree with themselves and imports no application code, so
it can never go red when the engine drifts. What runs the rating engine is 14 of the 61 signed golden
tests — roughly three quarters of the signed billing figures have no test that exercises the engine.**

### CR-060 · 7 · THE TWENTY CHANGES, IN FULL

Weights are the source document's own: **Must · Should · Decision.**

---

#### C1 · Post supplier costs on settlement — **MUST · the core change**
* **Why.** The PO's objection to posting was that **`CR accounts payable` creates a liability nobody
  can drain.** **Posting `DR cost / CR cash` on the day it is PAID never creates one.** One new field
  — **`paid on`** — and the books finally carry the cost of service.
* **⚠ THIS IS A PROPOSAL, NOT A RULING, AND IT DOES NOT START UNTIL IT IS RECORDED.** The standing
  ruling is that capture posts nothing in R2, **with the reasoning written into the code — and that
  reasoning was about posting on RECEIPT, which C1 does not do.** It deserves an **explicit decision**
  rather than being folded in as an implementation detail, **because it changes what the trial balance
  says.**
* **Rule.** `BR-LED-028` — **AMEND**, and it needs a ruling. *A supersession to record, not a
  contradiction to argue.*
* **Backend.** `PATCH /finance/cost-of-service/{id}` accepts `paid_on`. **Setting it triggers the
  settlement posting; clearing it is refused once posted.**
* **Data.** `supplier_invoices` **+ `paid_on`** — nullable date. **Its presence is what makes the row
  postable.**
* **What it unlocks.** Posting on settlement **wakes the eight dormant cost-of-service accounts.** With
  C15 the ratio moves from **7 credit paths against 3 debit paths to 7 against about 20** — *and the
  twenty include purchased power, purchased water and purchased gas.*
* **Proof.** Settlement posts DR cost / CR cash · **an unset `paid_on` posts nothing** · a second
  settlement is a **replay no-op** · settlement into a closed period **books forward** · **and the
  existing "capture posts zero lines" test must be REWRITTEN, not deleted — it is the standing record
  of the old ruling.**
* **⚠ Prove on PostgreSQL, not the SQLite suite** (hard-won law 14).

#### C2 · Accrue unbilled revenue at close — **MUST**
* **Why.** **`1210 Unbilled AR` is seeded in every chart and nothing has ever posted to it.**
  Consumption between the last read and period end is **real revenue absent from the books.** *It is
  the first thing any reviewer finds.*
* **Rule.** `BR-LED-006` — **AMEND**: the close checklist gains a step **that can actually be
  completed**, plus a new rule for **how unbilled revenue is measured and priced.**
* **Backend.** `POST /finance/accruals/unbilled` (compute and post the period's unbilled revenue) and
  `GET /finance/accruals/unbilled` (**preview before posting — the figure, and the reads it came
  from**). **Reuses the existing accrual entry type and its day-one auto-reversal — the machinery
  already exists.** `GET /finance/close-checklist`'s `accruals_posted` item **must stop answering
  `unknown`.**
* **Proof.** The accrual amount from reads after the last bill · **auto-reverses on day one** · **a
  closed period is byte-identical before and after** · the checklist item flips from `unknown` to done.

#### C17 · Accrue unpaid supplier costs at close — **MUST · the mirror of C2, and it is what makes C1 honest**
* **Why.** **Without it, revenue is recognised when BILLED and cost when PAID**, so a commodity sold in
  one month can have its cost land in the next. **Accruing at close and reversing on day one gives true
  matching AND creates no standing payables balance, because the entry undoes itself.** *Same code path
  as C2, pointed the other way.*
* **Rule.** `BR-LED-006` — **AMEND, the same rule as C2. Worth writing the two as ONE rule about period
  matching rather than two unrelated steps — they are the same idea applied to each side.**
* **Backend.** `POST /finance/accruals/unpaid-costs` — **new.**
* **Proof.** An unpaid invoice at close **accrues** · **it reverses on day one** · **settling it
  afterwards posts ONCE, not twice** · **the accrual and the settlement together never double-count the
  cost, which is the failure this pairing exists to prevent.**
* **⚠ SHIP IT WITH C1, NOT AFTER.** *Settlement posting alone puts revenue on an accrual basis and cost
  on a paid basis — a defect somebody finds in a signed month.*

#### C19 · Make the collected tax basis computable — **MUST · a reconciliation, not a choice**
* **Why.** A tenant can already choose to file on **what they collected**, and **the product cannot
  produce that figure.** `allocations` records an amount **and not which charge classes it met.**
* **Rule.** `BR-LED-002` · `BR-PAY-010` — **RECONCILE. Two signed rulings disagree** (see §6).
  **Recording the breakdown makes the question moot, and THAT is the disposition to write down rather
  than choosing a winner.**
* **Backend.** **Record the class breakdown ON the allocation row.** Then collected tax is **a fact
  whatever order a tenant chooses**, and the two rulings stop needing to agree. `GET /finance/taxes`'s
  collected column stops returning absent — **and its refusal text is RETIRED, not reworded, because it
  describes a limit that will no longer hold.**
* **Data.** `allocations` **+ a per-class breakdown — the ONE genuinely new structure in this
  document.** Either four nullable amount columns **or a child row per class**; *the child row survives
  a fifth class being added, which the tenant-defined class makes likely.*
* **Proof.** A full-coverage payment reproduces the signed **20.97** · **the same partial payment under
  three different class orders yields three different, correct collected-tax figures — the case that
  proves the breakdown is READ and not assumed** · two authorities on different bases in one month
  still file correctly.
* **Interim, and cheap (T7e).** **Warn where the basis is CHOSEN, not where it is filed.** Today a
  tenant picks *collected* in settings and **discovers at filing time that the figure is absent.**

#### C20 · Post depreciation — **SHOULD · and unusually, the number already exists**
* **Why.** The assets module **already computes accumulated depreciation and book value** from the
  purchase cost, method and expected life, **and shows them on screen. Nothing posts them.** Once C1
  puts cost in the books, **this is the last piece of a real operating statement.**
* **Backend.** A posting path and a period trigger — **not a calculation.**
* **⚠ Order.** **After C1** — *depreciation in books that carry no cost is an odd half-picture.*

#### C3 · Give the supplier invoice a premises — **MUST**
* **Why.** Without it, **bought-versus-billed cannot be computed per building, and for a sub-metering
  company that IS the product.**
* **Rule.** `BR-LED-030` / `BR-LED-031` — **AMEND: all-or-nothing moves from per-service-per-period to
  per-service-per-PREMISES-per-period. The refusal text changes with it.**
* **Backend.** `POST /finance/cost-of-service` accepts `premises_id`.
* **Data.** `supplier_invoices` **+ `premises_id`** — nullable UUID, **deferred FK to metering, matching
  how every other cross-module pointer here is declared.**
* **Cost.** *One nullable column, one field on the form, one grouping on the report.*

#### C4 · Opening · movement · closing on the trial balance — **SHOULD**
* **Why.** Today it shows **period debit and credit only.** *Every accountant reads a trial balance as
  position-then-movement-then-position; without the opening column they cannot tie this month to last
  month's signed statement without exporting.*
* **Backend.** `GET /ledger/trial-balance` response gains **opening** and **closing** per account.
* **Proof.** **Opening + movement = closing, per account and in total** · **opening on a fresh chart is
  ZERO, not null.**

#### C5 · Decide on an allowance for doubtful debts — **DECISION · ❄️ FROZEN**
* **Why.** Write-off is **direct** today: `DR bad debt / CR receivable`, **no contra-asset account.**
  **Fine for US municipal and sub-metering. Not acceptable under IFRS 9 or Ind AS 109**, which need an
  expected-credit-loss estimate.
* **⚠ STOP — `B4` / `B5` FROZEN.** An allowance **changes signed money math. Finance re-sign through the
  change process, NEVER an inline edit.**
* **Disposition.** **A market-entry decision, not a bug — but decide it BEFORE selling into those
  markets, not after.** Only if IFRS or Ind AS markets are in scope.

#### C6 · Retire the dead `accounting_method` column — **SHOULD · ⚠ CORRECTED BY §0c FINDING 1**
* **Why, as written.** *"It sits in the settings table with no reader, and the demo seeder still writes
  'accrual' into it. Either delete it or make it mean something. A live column nothing consumes is how
  the next person concludes the product supports cash basis."*
* **⚠ AND IT DOES HAVE A READER AT 2.123.0.** `tenancy/selectors.py:470` requires it for the
  **`fiscal_billing` onboarding-checklist item**, while `tenancy/services.py:879` **deliberately leaves
  it unset at provisioning** — **so that item can never complete for any tenant provisioned since
  CR-008, and no screen can set it.** **C6 must fix the checklist condition in the same change**, and a
  **defect row is owed either way.**
* **Data.** `tenant_settings` — retire `accounting_method` **in the same migration as C7's
  `organisation_type`.**

#### C16 · Customer statement — **MUST · RULED, apportionment settled**
* **Why.** One customer, their accounts, each balance, **a total across them.**
* **ZERO SCHEMA.** *"The link table already carries the pair, the confidence tier and the confirmer.
  The customer statement is a read over a table that has been ready the whole time."*
* **Rule.** `BR-CUS-054` — **AMEND** with what the link means for money: **sum within a customer, never
  across; a jointly-held account is shown in full to each holder** — *which is joint and several
  liability correctly presented*; **a weak or untiered link is shown and MARKED, never silently merged
  and never silently dropped** — *the tier already refuses to carry a deposit, and a statement should be
  no braver than that.*
* **Backend.** `GET /reports/customer-statement` — **new.** Reads the existing link table; the
  per-account figures are the account-ledger read it already has. **Totalled as *"across N accounts"*.**
* **Proof.** One customer with three accounts sums to their total · **a jointly-held account appears at
  FULL VALUE on BOTH holders' statements** · **no query sums across customers** · a weak or untiered
  link is listed and marked · **a customer with no live account gets an empty statement, not an error.**

#### C7 · Organisation type on Settings → Company → Details — **MUST · RULED, placement decided**
* **Why.** **Everything else in this section depends on it.** Three values: **utility · sub-metering
  company · HOA.**
* **Where, and why there.** On the **Utility details panel of Company → Profile, beside legal name and
  DBA — it is an identity FACT and that is where identity lives.** *Not a finance tab, and not a signup
  wizard a tenant sees once and never returns to.* **A setting also has one advantage over a signup
  question that matters here: every existing tenant can fix it in one click. Asked only at signup, the
  answer would be missing for everyone already on the platform and would need a backfill.**
* **Seed it to `utility` at provisioning** rather than leaving it null — **following the precedent
  already ratified for the eleven regional fields that sat empty until a human opened the tab** — so **no
  tenant is ever in an unknown state and every existing tenant gets a correct default.**
* **Rule.** `BR-TEN-*` — **MINT**: the type, its three values, its seeded default, and what each type
  shows.
* **Backend.** `PATCH /tenants/{id}` accepts `organisation_type`.
* **Data.** `tenant_settings` **+ `organisation_type`** — text, seeded `utility`. *(Retire
  `accounting_method` in the same migration — C6, with §0c finding 1's caveat.)*
* **⚠ ONE CONSEQUENCE WORTH TAKING WHILE YOU ARE IN THERE.** The panel is titled **"Utility details"**
  and the logo placeholder reads **"Utility logo"**. **For an HOA or a sub-metering company those labels
  are simply WRONG — the product is calling them something they are not, on the screen where they state
  who they are.** Once the field exists, both labels can follow it: **"Organisation details"** as the
  neutral heading, or the tenant's own type once chosen.
* **What it unlocks, and nothing more.** **This one field is what C8 and C9 read.** *It changes no
  money, no posting and no book. It is the cheapest change on the list and the one the other two wait
  on.*

#### C8 · Swap the headline tiles by type — **MUST**
* **Why.** **A utility watches DSO and collection rate — it is GROWING revenue. A sub-metering company
  watches cost recovery — it is RECOVERING an invoice it already paid. Same books, different question.**
* **Backend.** `GET /finance/revenue-ar` — **the tile set varies by organisation type.** **⚠ The
  recovery figures are a DIFFERENT READ, not a relabelling.**
* **Screens.** **R2** (utility) keeps Billed · Collected · Collection % · Still owed · DSO · Written off
  YTD. **R3** (sub-metering) shows **Paid suppliers · Billed members · Recovery % · Unaccounted for ·
  Still owed**, with **DSO and collection-rate tiles HIDDEN — they answer a question this customer does
  not have.** *"Recovery below 100% is money gone."*
* **Proof.** Default is `utility` for a new tenant **and for an existing one** · each type renders its own
  tiles · **an unknown value falls back rather than erroring.**
* **Blocked on.** **T3 — the sub-metering demo tenant.** Nothing in the fixtures can exercise this.

#### C9 · Bought-vs-billed per building — **MUST**
* **Why.** Follows from C3. **Ranked worst-first, so the leaking building is the FIRST ROW, not an
  average. This is the screen a sub-metering company opens every month.**
* **Backend.** `GET /finance/cost-of-service/reconciliation` gains **`group_by=premises`** and
  **worst-recovery-first ordering.** **⚠ The all-or-nothing volume rule applies PER BUILDING, not per
  tenant.**
* **Proof.** Recovery per building · **a building with no volume reports absent with its reason and does
  NOT poison the others** · worst-first ordering.
* **Blocked on.** **T3.**

#### C10 · One GL mapping screen that can save — **MUST · Settings**
* **Why.** **Eleven GL columns are set across six screens; the one page that shows them all is READ-ONLY
  because half belongs to another module.**
* **The fix, and it respects the boundary.** **An orchestrating service in the tenancy module that the
  mapping screen calls — one screen, one save, several owners underneath — NOT a cross-module write.**
  *Nothing in the current design forecloses it.*
* **Rule.** `BR-LED-014` — **AMEND**: where GL mappings live and who may write them through one screen.
* **Backend.** `PUT /ledger/gl-mappings` — **previously declined, now served through the orchestrator.**
* **The simplification underneath it.** **Two things are being conflated today.** **Roles** — *"which
  account means receivables"* — are **a fixed set of thirteen, set once at setup.** **Per-object
  choices** — *"which account does THIS charge code credit"* — are **many, and genuinely belong on the
  object's own form, because that is when you decide them.** *Presenting both as one read-only "mapping"
  page is what makes the surface feel scattered.*
* **Proof.** **One save writes across modules** · **a partial failure writes NOTHING** · **a test
  asserting no cross-module ORM write, which is the rule the orchestration exists to respect.**
* **⚠ Prove the partial-failure case on PostgreSQL** (hard-won law 14).

#### C18 · Move the accounting calendar onto the Accounting screen — **SHOULD · Settings**
* **Why.** **Fiscal year start, close cadence and close day sit under Company → Regional beside the date
  and number formats. Those are DISPLAY preferences; a fiscal calendar is an ACCOUNTING decision.**
* **Cost.** **Free to move**, and it completes the one-screen picture. *Two fields and a label.*
* **⚠ Changing it re-computes every period boundary, so the current period is shown back before saving.**

#### C11 · Fix the vocabulary: *record · recorded · in the books* — **SHOULD**
* **Why.** **The product has SIX different phrasings for "held here but not in the books"** — *posts
  nowhere · moves no books · register-derived · kept apart from the totals · nothing reached the books.*
  **Pick one pair and use it everywhere.**
* **Rule.** **`B14` — MINT a UI rule.** *B14 is the right home; it already governs clerk-facing copy.*
* **Scope.** A vocabulary sweep across the **eleven locale catalogues.**

#### C12 · Put close-readiness on General Ledger — **SHOULD**
* **Why.** **The five-item checklist only appears once you are already on the Close screen deciding to
  close. A one-person finance team wants to know on the 3rd what is still outstanding, not on the 31st**
  — so it belongs on **whatever tab they land on, which is now the trial balance.**
* **Backend.** **The same `GET /finance/close-checklist` payload serves the General Ledger strip.**

#### C13 · Build the by-premises summary (S60) — **SHOULD · Reports**
* **Why.** **The ONE designed finance report with no page.** *Its data path now works — journal lines
  carry premises since the dimension stamping landed — so this is a screen over a working read, not new
  plumbing.* **It is also the utility's version of C9.**
* **Backend.** `GET /reports/by-premises` — **new**, over a read model that already exists.

#### C14 · Give General Ledger the list toolkit — **MUST · and NONE of it needs building**
* **Why.** **`components/DataTable` already ships search, sort, paging, column show/hide and column
  reorder, and `FilterBar` ships the filters — and only `PaymentsPage` uses them. Every ledger page
  hand-rolls its table instead.**
* **Backend.** `GET /ledger/trial-balance` and `GET /ledger/journal-entries` gain **the list grammar** —
  `q`, `sort`, `dir`, `page`, `per`, `f.type` — **so a filtered journal view becomes a shareable URL.**
* **Proof.** **Search, sort, filter and column preferences survive a reload · the URL round-trips.**
  (Playwright, on the built page.)
* **⚠ Both components ARE on the Tailwind migration list, so a legacy ledger page may import and render
  them safely.** See the build constraint in §8.

#### C15 · Widen the cost categories — **but NOT to capital assets — MUST**
* **Why.** **Today a tenant can record a cost only against a service they sell, plus O&M and
  Infrastructure — the non-service half is closed and hardcoded. No payroll, insurance, professional
  fees, vehicles or rent. So "everything in one place" is not yet true.**
* **Rule.** `BR-LED-029` — **AMEND**: the vocabulary widens **and gains an explicit refusal for capital
  spending.**
* **Backend.** `POST /finance/cost-of-service` accepts the widened vocabulary and **refuses a
  capital-asset category BY NAME, pointing at the asset.**
* **Data.** **Seed data, not schema** — new chart accounts for the new categories.
* **⚠ Do it BEFORE C1.** *A miscategorised row is a tidy-up until costs post, and a correction
  afterwards.*
* **⚠ Two exposures while capture posts nothing, and both are manageable.** **Bought-versus-billed** —
  *payroll has no volume, so it must NEVER enter that denominator*; the existing all-or-nothing rule
  already handles a cost with no volume, **so this needs a category FLAG rather than new logic** (T7c).
  **The accounting export** — its cost section would start carrying figures that are not cost of
  service; **it is already labelled register-derived, so the fix is GROUPING, not a warning.**

**AND THE FIVE ABSENCES THAT WERE CONSIDERED AND DECIDED AGAINST — recorded as decisions so the next
reader knows they were considered rather than missed:**

| Absence | Disposition | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Multi-currency and FX translation | **Not now** | *One currency per entry is deliberate: a mixed-currency entry cannot balance. Adding FX later is ADDITIVE — it does not spoil existing books — so it can wait for a customer who needs it.* |
| Multi-book / parallel GAAP | **DECLINED** | *A second set of books at this product's size means two things that can disagree and one or two staff to reconcile them. The accounting export is how a second basis reaches whoever needs it.* |
| Budgetary accounting, encumbrances | **DECLINED** | *Follows fund accounting. If the fund decision goes the other way this returns with it; on its own it is a different product.* |
| Regulatory assets & liabilities · FERC chart numbering | **CONFIG, not code** | *The chart is tenant-owned with free-text codes — a utility that needs these accounts can add them today. What they cannot get is the FUNCTION dimension, which is the fund decision wearing another name.* |
| Modified accrual basis · segment reporting | **With funds · partial** | *Modified accrual is a governmental-fund concept and arrives with fund accounting or not at all. Every line already carries a service, which is the segment most utilities report on.* |

**THE TWO THE DOCUMENT WOULD FIX FIRST, in order.** **1 · Post something to `1210`, or remove it.** *An
unbilled-revenue account that is seeded and never posted to is the gap that most directly undermines the
accrual claim — and the one a finance reviewer in any of the ten markets will find first. Consumption
between the last read and period end is real revenue the books currently do not show.* **2 · Decide
whether direct write-off is acceptable** (C5). *Under IFRS 9 and Ind AS 109 it is not. For US municipal
and submetering customers today, direct write-off is fine — so this is a market-entry decision, not a
bug.*

**AND THE ONE-LINE SUMMARY THE DOCUMENT PUTS ON ITSELF:** ***C1 and C2 together are the whole accounting
story. One puts costs in the books, the other puts unbilled revenue in the books. Do both and the
product genuinely holds accrual books a bookkeeper can sign. Do neither and it holds a receivables
ledger that calls itself accounting.***

### CR-060 · 8 · THE SCREENS

#### 8a · What is built today — W1–W10, ten page components, eleven wired routes

Scope is the finance surface only — every screen reached under `/finance`, plus the account-ledger
report. **Billing and the rest of Payments are deliberately not here** (payments is `CR-059`). One
component serves two routes, **because the tab lives in the URL.** *Where a screen states that
something is unavailable, that text is in the product today.*

| # | Screen | Route · ID | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| **W1** | Revenue & AR | `/finance` · **S36** · `RevenueArPage.tsx`, 1,227 lines | Billed · Collected · Collection % · Still owed · DSO · Written off YTD; revenue by service; who owes you (five age buckets); **cash position — *received not yet banked* and *confirmed by the bank*, NEVER added together**; **subledger tie-out** (receivables · customer deposits · tax payable) where **a difference cannot be dismissed — it clears when the entry behind it is fixed** |
| **W2** | Deposits & Bank | `/finance/deposits` · **S37** | *"Needs your attention — {count} deposits do not match the bank. Usually a cheque."* + unmatched bank lines |
| **W3** | Bank import wizard | `/finance/deposits/import` · **S38** | 1 File → 2 Match → 3 Confirm. **The file is fingerprinted by SHA-256, so the same statement cannot be imported twice** |
| **W4** | Deposit batch detail & reconcile | `/finance/deposits/:batchId` · **S39·S40** | **Σ explanations must equal the difference, and the difference must be zero at reconcile. Nothing plugs a residual; there is no "force match anyway"** |
| **W5** | Taxes & remittance | `/finance/taxes` · **S41** | Authority · files on · billed · collected · remitted · still owed. **The basis is never guessed for you**, and *"Bills say X. Books say Y."* is shown when the two disagree — **it is not reconciled silently** |
| **W6** | General ledger | `/finance/gl` · **S56·S57** | Trial balance & journal; **"Balanced ✓ / Out of balance by {difference}"** — *debits and credits can only differ if something is wrong.* **Two things state WHY they are unavailable:** opening an account line to its entries, and filtering by property |
| **W7** | Close the month & export | `/finance/export` · **S42·S43** | The five-item checklist; **reason required only if incomplete**; **four export blockers, each named**: the month is still open · it does not add up · already handed over · accounts with no code in your package |
| **W8** | Write-offs waiting for approval | `/finance/write-offs` | **The note is required — it is the only place anyone explains why this debt was given up.** *(No A1 screen ID — built after the inventory was extracted.)* |
| **W9** | Cost of service & bought-vs-billed | `/finance/cost-of-service` · **S73·S74** (provisional, `OQ-204`) | **Captured, not posted. Nothing here reaches the books — the export section is labelled register-derived.** Correcting after the period closes requires a reason |
| **W10** | Account ledger report | `/reports/account-ledger` · **S59** | **Read from posted journal lines only. The report never recomputes money — the reporting module imports no billing, payments or customers code** |

**Not in this set: the by-premises summary (S60)** — the one designed finance report with no built page
(**C13**). **Only one of the ten carries no screen ID** — the write-off queue. *The finance surface is
the best-covered part of the inventory, which is not true of the product as a whole: A1 was extracted
from a prototype that has since been deleted, so elsewhere it describes screens that can no longer be
opened.*

#### 8b · The proposed set — R1–R9, and the tab restructure 7 → 6

**Three moves.** **Write-offs stops being a destination and becomes an approval panel inside Revenue &
AR**, where the receivable it gives up already lives. **Cost of service becomes "Costs" — NOT "AP",
because there is no payables balance in the books and a clerk who goes looking for an ageing will not
find one.** And **Export is renamed to name the close**: the component is already called
`CloseExportPage`, **and closing the month is the bigger monthly event.**

**General Ledger leads and is the landing tab, per the PO's ruling.** *The books are the one surface
every other tab feeds, so opening on the trial balance means the first thing anyone sees is whether the
month balances — and the five tabs after it run in the order the month is actually worked.*

| | Today — 7 tabs | | Proposed — 6 tabs |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Revenue & AR | 1 | **General Ledger** · leads, and lands |
| 2 | Deposits & Bank | 2 | Revenue & AR · **write-offs move in here** |
| 3 | Taxes | 3 | Deposits & Bank |
| 4 | General ledger | 4 | Taxes & Remittances |
| 5 | Export | 5 | **Costs** · not "AP" |
| 6 | Write-offs | 6 | **Close & Export** · close is named |
| 7 | Cost of service | | |

* **R1 · General Ledger** — CHANGED (**C4 · C12 · C14**), was W6. Adds the list toolkit (search, period,
  type, account, source, state, **columns**); the **"Before you close this month · 3 of 5 done"** strip;
  and **Opening · Debit · Credit · Closing** per account. *"Opening and closing let a bookkeeper tie
  this month to last month's signed figures without exporting to a spreadsheet first."*
* **R2 · Revenue & AR — utility** — CHANGED (**C8**, write-offs move in), was W1. The write-off approval
  panel arrives as **"Write-offs waiting for you · 2"**.
* **R3 · Revenue & AR — sub-metering company** — **NEW VARIANT · same screen, different question**
  (**C7 · C8**). Tiles: **Paid suppliers · Billed members · Recovery % · Unaccounted for · Still owed.**
  A per-building table (Building · Paid · Billed · Recovery · Unaccounted), **worst building first**;
  *who owes you* **by member**. **DSO and collection-rate tiles are hidden for this organisation type.**
* **R4 · Deposits & Bank** — **UNCHANGED except the tab strip**, was W2. *"This screen is already right.
  It reconciles on batches, which is how a bank presents money, and it refuses to plug a residual."*
* **R5 · Bank import wizard** — **UNCHANGED**, was W3. *"Leave as is."*
* **R6 · Deposit batch detail & reconcile** — **UNCHANGED**, was W4. *"This is the strongest screen in
  the module."*
* **R7 · Taxes & Remittances** — **UNCHANGED except the tab label**, was W5. *"Both bases are always
  computed and the choice is never guessed. Already the right shape for VAT and GST regimes — leave it
  alone."*
* **R8 · Costs** — CHANGED (**C1 · C3 · C9 · C11 · C15**), renamed from *Cost of service*, was W9. The
  form gains **Category** (service · O&M · payroll · insurance · …), **Building / master meter**, and
  **"Paid on — blank until you pay it"**. Two states, in the C11 vocabulary: **"Recorded — held here,
  not in the books"** and **"In the books — posted when you enter *paid on*: DR cost / CR cash, one
  balanced entry, no payables balance ever created."**
* **R9 · Close & Export** — CHANGED (**C2**), renamed to name the close, was W7. Adds **"Unbilled
  revenue for this period — consumption read after the last bill, priced at the current schedule. Post
  accrual → reverses automatically on day 1 of next month."** *C2 turns a checklist item that reports
  `unknown` today into one a clerk can complete from this screen.*

**FOUR OF THE NINE ARE UNCHANGED** — Deposits & Bank, the import wizard, the batch detail and Taxes need
nothing beyond the new tab strip. **The bank-reconciliation trio in particular is the best-built part of
the module. Leave it exactly as it is.**

#### 8c · The Settings screens that build the one-screen picture — P1–P4

**Much less has to be built than it implies, because the shell is already there.** **Settings →
Accounting exists and already has three sub-tabs — chart, mapping and controls.** *So the work is not a
new screen: it is making one existing sub-tab writable, adding a fourth, and renaming two things into
plain English.* **These sit in Settings, not the Finance tabs.**

| Where | Today | Proposed |
|---|---|---|
| Settings → Accounting → **chart** | Exists | **Unchanged.** The tenant's own chart, already add/edit/retire |
| Settings → Accounting → **mapping** | **Read-only** | **Becomes writable**, and splits visibly into **Roles** and **Where money lands**. Relabelled from *"mapping"* |
| Settings → Accounting → **calendar** | **Does not exist** | **New fourth sub-tab.** Takes the fiscal fields off Company → Regional |
| Settings → Accounting → **controls** | Exists | **Unchanged.** The finance settings that are not accounts |
| Settings → Company → **Regional** | Exists | **Loses four fields** and can finally drop *"fiscal calendar"* from its own name |

* **P1 · Accounting → Where money lands** — CHANGED (**C10**), was read-only. **Roles in the books · 13**
  (*"the accounts the system needs by name. Set once at setup, rarely touched."*) and **Where money
  lands · by kind** (services · charge codes · taxes · payment methods · adjustment reasons). **One Save
  writes across five modules through an orchestrating service — all of it or none. Every row deep-links
  to the object that owns it.**
* **P2 · Accounting → Calendar** — **NEW SUB-TAB** (**C18**). Financial year start month and day · close
  cadence (monthly/quarterly) · close by day of month. **"This period" is COMPUTED, never stored** — FY
  label, period number, start, end, close-by date. **Changing it re-computes every period boundary, so
  the current period is shown back before saving.**
* **P3 · Company → Regional, after the move** — CHANGED (**C18**). *"The sub-tab is called 'Regional,
  formats & fiscal calendar' today. Once the calendar moves it is just regional formats, and the name
  can say so."*
* **P4 · Accounting → Chart of accounts** — **UNCHANGED**, shown for context. *"Already right, and the
  reason the rest works: the chart is the tenant's own, codes are free text, and application logic never
  names a number — it asks for the role."*

**Where this lands in one line:** **Settings → Accounting becomes the ONE place every accounting
decision is made** — the chart, the roles, where money lands, the calendar and the controls — **while
the object forms KEEP their GL field as the natural place to set it at creation.** *Nothing moves out of
Finance, and nothing moves into it.*

#### 8d · ⚠ THE BUILD CONSTRAINT THAT APPLIES TO EVERY SCREEN TASK IN THIS CR

**`features/ledger/` is NOT on the Tailwind migration list — ZERO of its 8 files.** Under B14 rule 21's
migration clause, **a Tailwind utility is emitted ONLY for a file listed in
`07-frontend/src/styles/route-b-migrated.txt`.** Write one in a file that is not on that list and **it
is a class no stylesheet declares: it renders as NOTHING AT ALL, while `tsc`, eslint and every
`toHaveClass` assertion pass, because the class really IS in the DOM.**

| Area | CSS route | What it means for this work |
|---|---|---|
| `features/billing/` | **Tailwind** | All 15 files migrated. Not in scope here anyway |
| **`features/ledger/`** | **Legacy CSS** | **Zero of 8 on the list. Every one uses hand-written `fin-*` classes. EVERY SCREEN IN THIS CR LIVES HERE** |
| `features/payments/` | Legacy CSS | Zero on the list. `PaymentsPage` is the one file using the shared table |
| `components/DataTable` · `FilterBar` | **Tailwind** | **Both migrated — so a legacy page may import and render them safely.** The utilities live in their files, which are on the list |

**SO THE BUILD RULE FOR EVERYTHING IN THIS CR IS ONE SENTENCE: reuse `fin-*` classes the stylesheet
already declares, or import a migrated component — and write NO Tailwind utility inside
`features/ledger/`.** *A utility written there is invisible on screen and green on every gate, which is
the exact failure G31 exists to catch and the reason two fixes on 2026-08-27 re-broke the screens they
were repairing.* **If Tailwind is wanted on these screens, migrating the file is its own piece of work,
done first and on its own — never folded into a feature change.** *(`SettingsAccountingTab.tsx` and
`ChartOfAccountsPanel.tsx` are not on the list either — same rule.)*
**C14's toolkit ask lands neatly inside that constraint: nothing needs to be written from scratch and no
utility has to be typed into a ledger file.**

### CR-060 · 9 · ENDPOINTS AND TABLES — the exact delta

**118 finance operations today · 8 change · 3 new (+2 more reads) · 1 previously declined.** *Almost
nothing here needs a new route — the work is fields on existing payloads.*

| Endpoint | Today | Change | What has to happen |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PATCH /finance/cost-of-service/{id}` | Served | **C1** | Accept `paid_on`. **Setting it triggers the settlement posting; clearing it is refused once posted** |
| `POST /finance/cost-of-service` | Served | **C3 · C15** | Accept `premises_id` and the widened category vocabulary. **Refuse a capital-asset category BY NAME, pointing at the asset** |
| `GET /finance/cost-of-service/reconciliation` | Served | **C9** | Add `group_by=premises`. **Worst-recovery-first.** The all-or-nothing volume rule applies **per building**, not per tenant |
| `GET /ledger/trial-balance` | Served | **C4 · C14** | Response gains **opening** and **closing** per account. Request gains the list grammar — `q`, `sort`, `dir`, `page`, `per`, `f.type` |
| `GET /ledger/journal-entries` | Served | **C14** | Same list grammar, **so a filtered journal view is a shareable URL** |
| `GET /finance/revenue-ar` | Served | **C8** | Tile set varies by organisation type. **The recovery figures are a different READ, not a relabelling** |
| `GET /finance/close-checklist` | Served | **C2 · C12** | The `accruals_posted` item **must stop answering `unknown`.** **The same payload serves the General Ledger strip** |

The ledger module holds **`EP-LED-01…06`** and **`US-LED-001…021`**. **Most of the work below amends a
signed rule rather than minting one — and two of them cannot be amended at all without a finance
re-sign.**

| Change | Rule | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| **C1** | `BR-LED-028` | **AMEND, and it needs a ruling.** The rule says capture processes nothing; **posting on settlement is a new statement about WHEN the books move.** Its stated reasoning was about posting on **receipt**, which this does not do — **so it is a supersession to record, not a contradiction to argue** |
| **C2** | `BR-LED-006` | **AMEND.** The close checklist gains a step **that can actually be completed.** New rule for **how unbilled revenue is measured and priced** |
| **C17** | `BR-LED-006` | **AMEND, the same rule as C2.** The checklist gains a second accrual step. **Worth writing the two as ONE rule about period matching rather than two unrelated steps — they are the same idea applied to each side** |
| **C3 · C9** | `BR-LED-030` / `031` | **AMEND.** All-or-nothing moves from **per-service-per-period** to **per-service-per-premises-per-period. The refusal text changes with it** |
| **C5** | `B4` / `B5` ❄️ | **STOP — FROZEN.** An allowance changes signed money math. **Finance re-sign through the change process, NEVER an inline edit** |

| **C16** | `BR-CUS-054` | **AMEND.** The link rule gains what it means for money: **sum within a customer, never across; a jointly-held account shown in full to each holder. A weak or untiered link is shown and MARKED, never silently merged and never silently dropped** — *the tier already refuses to carry a deposit, and a statement should be no braver than that* |

| **C10** | `BR-LED-014` | **AMEND.** Where GL mappings live and who may write them through one screen |
| **C11** | `B14` | **MINT a UI rule.** One vocabulary for *recorded* versus *in the books*. **B14 is the right home; it already governs clerk-facing copy** |
| **C15** | `BR-LED-029` | **AMEND.** The category vocabulary widens, **and gains an explicit refusal for capital spending** |
| **C6** | `CR-008` ruling 1 | **CORRECT (§0c finding 1).** *"It had zero readers"* is no longer true |

### CR-060 · 11 · TESTS, TEST DATA AND E2E

**1,402 finance test functions across 109 files today.** The additions are **small in number and
specific in kind — and two are the sort that only fail on real PostgreSQL.**

**⚠ TEST DATA IS THE GAP THAT BLOCKS TWO CHANGES.** **There is ONE demo tenant and it is a utility.**
C8 and C9 are the sub-metering variants **and nothing in the fixtures can exercise them.** Before either
can be tested, the demo spec needs **a second tenant that is a sub-metering company: a master account,
several buildings, member accounts under each, and a supplier invoice per building.** *That is a fixture
task with no code in it, and it blocks two of the three "must" changes.*

new figures belong** — a settlement posting, an unbilled accrual across a period boundary, and **a
per-building recovery with ONE building deliberately missing its volume so the absent case is exercised
rather than assumed.**

**⚠ TWO OF THESE MUST BE PROVED ON POSTGRESQL, NOT ON THE SUITE.** `config/settings/test.py` **hardcodes
in-memory SQLite**, which **has no aborted-transaction state — so any code that catches a database error
and carries on passes everything and fails on the first refused row in production** (hard-won law 14).
**C1's settlement posting and C10's partial-failure case are both exactly that shape. Run them against
real PostgreSQL before believing them.** *(Cheapest mitigation, and it is free: run these suites with
`JOBS_EAGER=false --reuse-db`.)*

### CR-060 · 13 · WHAT NOT TO TOUCH

**Three things to leave alone, stated as a deliberate scope exclusion:**

1. **The single posting service.** **One writer, balanced pairs enforced in the database, idempotent by
   construction. Every change above goes through it, none around it.**
2. **The designation indirection.** Application code asks for *"the account that means receivables"*,
   never for *"1200"*. **It is the single most portable thing in the design and the reason a tenant can
   key in their own chart.**
3. **Resolving the GL once, at issue, and stamping it.** **The posting seam deliberately refuses to
   re-resolve. Two implementations of one mapping rule would eventually disagree, and the books would
   hold the wrong one.**

**And the bank-reconciliation trio** — Deposits & Bank, the import wizard, the batch detail — **is the
best-built part of the module. It reconciles on batches, refuses to plug a residual, and has no
force-match escape hatch. Leave it exactly as it is.**

CR, so no version has moved. The product is at `2.123.0`"*. **T5 and T7c landed at `2.124.0`.**
