each task that lands bumps the change digit, and T5 and T7c shipped as **one build** — T7c is a flag
on the category T5 introduces and neither is meaningful on its own. Two bumps would have named a
version nobody can install. Both rows carry `2.124.0`.
Each task that lands bumps the **change** digit; each fix on top of a landed task bumps the **fix**
digit. **Every task row in §12 gets its landing version written into it when it closes**, and **the CR
cannot be marked done with no version.**

### CR-060 · 15 · ROLLBACK

* **T1, T1b, T6b and T15 are DECISIONS and carry no code.** They are also the ones that get more
  expensive with time: **T1b's cost rises with every journal line posted**, and **T6b must be answered
  before the first cost posts, not after.**
* **T0, T3, T5, T9, T10, T12, T13, T14, T17 and T18 are additive or presentational** and back out by
  reverting the commit. **T5 in particular is safe precisely BECAUSE it lands before T6** — a
  miscategorised row is a tidy-up while capture posts nothing.
* **T6 IS THE ONE THAT IS NOT ROLLBACK-CHEAP, and it is the reason C1 needs a recorded ruling first.**
  **Once costs post, the entries are in the books; once the month closes, they are a signed figure in a
  closed period, not a report you can re-run.** **Rolling T6 back does NOT unpost what it posted** —
  that would need reversing entries through the posting service, which is the correct mechanism and is
  not free. **So: settle T6b, land T5, and record the C1 ruling BEFORE T6 goes anywhere near a tenant.**
* **T6c is a rollback hazard in its own right and must ship WITH T6.** The export's cost section is
  labelled *register-derived* precisely because nothing posted. **If T6 lands without T6c, the same
  money leaves twice by two routes** — once from the register through the export and once from the
  books.
* **T7b must ship with T6, not after.** **Settlement posting alone puts revenue on an accrual basis and
  cost on a paid basis. That is a defect somebody finds in a signed month, and a signed month is not
  something you re-run.**
* **T7d changes the `allocations` shape on a money path.** Prefer the **child-row-per-class** form: it
  **survives a fifth class being added**, which the tenant-defined class makes likely, and it backs out
  by dropping a table rather than by dropping columns from a live money table.
* **T8's partition change is cheap NOW and expensive later**, and is **independent of everything else on
  this list** — which is exactly why it should not wait for the decisions above.
* **C5 / T15 cannot be rolled back at all in the ordinary sense**, because moving it means moving a
  ❄️ FROZEN figure. **It does not start without a finance re-sign through `HUMAN-GUIDE §6`.**

##### ✅ 0d.2 IS RESOLVED — 2026-09-03, AND BY TWO DIFFERENT AUTHORITIES

⚠ **THE PARAGRAPH DIRECTLY ABOVE IS SUPERSEDED AND IS KEPT DELIBERATELY.** It said the
question *"IS NOT RESOLVED HERE AND MUST NOT BE RESOLVED BY A LANE"*, and on the day it
was written that was right. It is resolved now. It stays on the page because a reader
who half-remembers it needs to see that it was ANSWERED rather than quietly overwritten
— and because **the two halves were settled by two different people, which is the whole
shape of law 13** and is easy to lose if the record is tidied into one sentence.

**HALF ONE — THE COUNT — IS THE PO's, AND ONLY THE PO's.** Asked directly, 2026-09-03,
verbatim: ***"C25 says six tabs. - this is correct."*** `C25` names its six — General
Ledger · Revenue & AR · Deposits & Bank · Taxes & Remittances · Costs · Close & Export —
and **Refunds is not among them.** That closes the first of the two options above: `C25`
does **not** become seven, the wireframes do not move, and the strip is six. It also
retires the reading in this CR's own `T10` row that *7 → 6* was arithmetic rather than a
target; that row is amended in place and says so.

**HALF TWO — WHERE REFUNDS GOES — WAS OURS, AND IT IS DECIDED: A PANEL INSIDE REVENUE &
AR.** This was never a question for the PO (law 13: *"a judgment call recorded in the
decision log with its reasoning is the deliverable; a question is the failure to make
one"*), and the decision is not a preference — **it is `C25`'s own stated principle
applied a second time.** `C25` folds Write-offs into Revenue & AR *"where the receivable
it gives up already lives"*; **a refund gives back money the customer's ACCOUNT holds as
credit, and the credit position lives in Revenue & AR.** So Refunds sits beside
Write-offs, in the same tab, for the same reason.

**THE ONE REAL COUNTER-ARGUMENT, RECORDED AS CONSIDERED AND DECLINED**, so nobody
re-opens it: a refund cheque appears on the bank reconciliation as an outstanding cheque
(`CS-14` states it in the statement's own arithmetic), which argues for Deposits & Bank.
**Declined** — that is the cheque **CLEARING**, which already lives in bank rec, exactly
as a payment's deposit batch lives in Deposits & Bank while the payment itself lives in
Revenue & AR. **Raising and approving a refund is an account-credit act.**

**WHAT IT COST, AND WHAT IT DID NOT.** `FINANCE_TABS` in
`07-frontend/src/features/ledger/financeShared.tsx` went from seven entries to six.
**Nothing was deleted:** `RefundsPage` shipped whole at `2.125.2` under `CR-059` task 18
and is **re-homed, not withdrawn** — `/finance/refunds` stays routed for every link
already in circulation, precisely as `/finance/write-offs` did when its own tab went, and
the page now highlights Revenue & AR because highlighting a tab the strip no longer draws
would leave the whole strip looking unselected. **Unlike the write-off fold, this one
needed code:** `RevenueArPage`'s `WriteOffQueuePanel` already existed and no refunds panel
did, so `features/payments/RefundsQueuePanel.tsx` is new. **Removing the tab without
building that panel would have left a finished five-act lifecycle reachable only by
typing a URL** — hard-won law 2, in the module that has already met it five times.

**AND THE THING THAT MADE THIS COLLISION INVISIBLE IS NOW CHECKED.** **No test in this
repository asserted the Finance strip's contents in any form** — not its length, not its
members — which is exactly why a sixth tab, a seventh and an eighth each arrived
correctly and the total was nobody's. `revenueAr.test.tsx` now names the six **in order**;
a length assertion alone would have gone green on a seventh tab that replaced a sixth.

**Full reasoning, with the collision explained rather than blamed:**
`12-governance/02-decision-log.md`, 2026-09-03.

  figure, so it does not start or reverse without a finance re-sign through
  `HUMAN-GUIDE §6`.

#### 0d.6 · HOW THIS WAS MEASURED, AND ONE ERROR IN THE MEASUREMENT

**Method:** the amended document was read for its register, its resolution table and its
counts; the tab count was verified by parsing `FINANCE_TABS` out of the source rather than
trusting either document; task statuses were counted from this CR's own rows.

⚠ **AND ONE NUMBER PUT TO THE PRODUCT OWNER WAS WRONG, WHICH IS RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN
QUIETLY CORRECTED.** They were told **eighteen** absences were now out of scope, and they
approved the update on that basis. **It is twelve** — the eighteen came from a
case-insensitive text match that counted the phrase where it appears in ordinary prose.
The distinction in `0d.4` between one RULED and eleven PROPOSED was missed in the same
pass. **A proxy that returns a plausible number is more dangerous than one that returns
none**, and this is the second time in two days that sentence has had to be written into
a reconciliation section.

**THE RULE THIS CR INHERITS FROM `CR-059`, unchanged:** *a task is not reportable until a
person has used it on screen, and any absence a source document describes gets a
specification number or an explicit, RATIFIED out-of-scope reason.*


## CR-061 — The chart of accounts needs more codes and more categories, and a discount may not be filed under revenue

### CR-061 · 0 · CAPTURE — the requester's words, verbatim, at arrival

Two statements, 2026-09-01, in the working chat session, in answer to the two yes/no questions that
had been standing on `4300`'s human-review row since **2026-08-28**:

> **(1)** *"if you need differnt number assign it - im okay with it; actually you need more GL code s
> and categories, I tried to assigned using existing code, they are not sufficiencnt"*

> **(2)** *"no, you cannot file discount under revenue"*

⚠ **STATEMENT (1) IS THE MORE IMPORTANT OF THE TWO AND IT IS NOT A REPLY TO THE QUESTION ASKED.** The
question was whether `4300` is the right number and name. The answer grants that **and reports a
FIELD FINDING**: the PO *tried to assign GL codes using the existing ones* and found them
insufficient. That is a real-usage report from the person doing the work, not a preference — and
nothing in this repo asked whether the chart was big enough, so nothing would have surfaced it.

⚠ **STATEMENT (2) REVERSES A BUILD DECISION THAT IS ALREADY SHIPPED AND POSTING.**

### CR-061 · 1 · WHAT SIGNED STATEMENT IS BEING REVERSED — quoted, never summarised

`apps/ledger/chart.py:448` records the decision now overruled, in its own words: the account is filed
under **revenue**, *"not a new sixth `LEDGER_ACCOUNT_TYPES` value"*. The reasoning given at the time
(and repeated by the coordinator when putting the question) was that a sixth kind *"would change how
every account in the product is grouped and signed on the trial-balance screen, which is much more
than the ruling asked for."*

**The PO was shown that cost and ruled the other way. That is their call and it stands.** The cost is
not waived by the ruling — it is now scoped work rather than an objection.

### CR-061 · 5 · THE REFERENCE CHART THE PO SUPPLIED — 111 ROWS, VERBATIM, AND WHAT IT COSTS

**Supplied 2026-09-01 with the words *"just as an example"*.** It is reproduced in full below because it
is the ANSWER to *"which codes were you reaching for"* — the question §3 wrongly said was open — and
because these CRs must stand alone without the chat that produced them.

**⚠ READ THE THREE FINDINGS BEFORE THE TABLE. THEY ARE WHY THIS IS NOT "ADD 75 ROWS".**

**FINDING 1 — `4300` COLLIDES, AND THE COLLISION IS THE DISCOUNT ACCOUNT ITSELF.** The reference gives
**`4300` = Electric Energy Revenue**. The product today has **`4300` = Customer discounts
(contra-revenue)** — the very account both of today's rulings were about. The PO pre-authorised the
move: *"if you need differnt number assign it - im okay with it"*.

**FINDING 2 — THE REFERENCE ANSWERS *"you cannot file discount under revenue"* IN ITS OWN STRUCTURE, and
it is NOT a sixth account type.** Rows 32-37 are a category called **Revenue Adjustments** — Billing
Adjustment `4700`, Leak Adjustment `4710`, Rate Correction `4720`, **Customer Credit `4730`**, Refunds
`4740`, Bad Debt Write-off `4750` — every one with **Normal Balance = DEBIT**. So a discount is a
**revenue ADJUSTMENT with a debit normal balance**, grouped apart from Customer Revenue. **That is
cheaper than the sixth `LEDGER_ACCOUNT_TYPES` value §2 was sizing**, and it is what the PO's own
chart does.

**FINDING 3 — THE REFERENCE CARRIES TWO COLUMNS THE PRODUCT DOES NOT STORE AT ALL.** **Normal Balance**
(Debit/Credit) and **Accounting Method** (Accrual / Fund Accounting). The second is `CR-060` **T1b** —
the fund tag the PO ruled Option B on **the same day** — arriving from the other direction: rows
104-111 (Transfers, Net Position) are marked *Fund Accounting*, so the chart itself now asserts a fund
dimension is needed for those accounts. **The two decisions are one decision.**

**THE GAP, MEASURED FROM CODE.** The product seeds **34** accounts; the reference has **111**. But the
count is the least of it — **the numbering schemes disagree at the root.** Ours groups every service
inside `41xx` (`4100` Electric usage, `4110` Water usage, `4120` Sewer); the reference gives each
service its own hundred-block (`4000` Water, `4100` Sewer, `4200` Stormwater, `4300` Electric).
**Adopting the reference renumbers accounts that already carry posted journal lines**, and hard rule 4
makes a posted line immutable — so this is a mapping-and-migration question, not a seed-data edit.

## CR-062 — The seed data for all ten services: three billing bases, real capacities, and every metered service gets its meters

### CR-062 · 0 · CAPTURE — the requester's words, verbatim, at arrival

**2026-09-02, in the working chat session.** The change arrived as seven statements across one
conversation, each one narrowing the last. They are quoted in the order they were said, because the
later ones only make sense as corrections of the earlier ones.

> **(1)** *"do you think Trash - primary unit is correct?"*

> **(2)** *"this is problem with every Utility services- why dont you se the correct data in Seed data
> and fix it - show me on screen what youa re going to set in table format first"*

> **(3)** *"Shall we consider Metered, % of service and Capacity based; Storm water - it is capacity
> based not unmetered , capaicyt is decided based on sizes of propoerty; Trash - it is capacity based
> and Cart sizes will decide price X how many Cart; Solar - is also capacity based - 1 panel capacity
> X # of Solar panels ; Broadband - It will be capacity based - ; Thermal/Heat - Metered; Battery -
> capacity based - you ahve to udpaet it - show me final table"*

> **(4)** *"panel isn't in the catalogue... that is correct - you have to decide the unit for Solar
> panels - and then it behave like Trash only"* · *"Battery — kW... Im okay with it"*

> **(5)** *"you need to make this dynamic - based on Utility services that are selected ; accordingly
> you have to seed the data for that utility services"* · *"for panels you will need various
> capacityes similarly the capacities we have created for Trash cart - you need to do it for Solar,
> Battery and Strom water also - show me all that youa re going to include in settings"* · *"you will
> ahve to set the prices for Strom water to Thermal - all these prices shoudl take effect if Utility
> services are enbaled by user at the time of Tenant creations"*

> **(6)** *"In solar youa re still not doing it correctly - For example We have 10 Types of Solar panel
> with various capaity 1 Kw, 2Kw 3Kw 4Kw so and SO forth ; on given Unit we have installed 3 panels
> with 2Kw, 4Kw and 8 Kw , it means the totla capacity will be 14 Kw ; rate will be for 1 Kw = 14 $ per
> KW then bill should be 14 X 14 = 156 $"*

> **(7)** *"Electric $12.00 base kWh read - along with base you will need rate schedule - Either
> Tiered or TOU"*

> **(8)** *"this is not correct - you cannot drop electricty or gas - can you tell me what corrections
> you will ahve to do"*

⚠ **STATEMENT (6) IS THE ONE THAT CHANGES THE MODEL, AND IT REVERSES WHAT THIS COORDINATOR HAD
PROPOSED AND THE PO HAD ALREADY APPROVED IN STATEMENT (4).** Statement (4) approved `panel` as solar's
unit — a COUNT of panels, exactly like carts. Statement (6) says that is wrong: panels come in
different capacities, they are installed together on one unit, and **the billable quantity is the SUM
of their capacities in kW, not how many there are.** Solar's unit is therefore **`kW`, not `panel`**,
and `panel` is not added to the catalogue after all.

⚠ **ITS ARITHMETIC IS OFF BY ONE PRODUCT AND THE CORRECT FIGURE IS WHAT THIS CR BUILDS.** The stated
example is *"14 X 14 = 156 $"*. 14 kW at $14.00 per kW is **$196.00**. The PO was told this in the
same session and did not dispute it. **The seeded figure and its test assert $196.00.** Recorded here
rather than silently corrected, because a wrong figure copied into a fixture becomes a wrong figure
asserted by a test, and then it is the product's answer.

⚠ **STATEMENT (8) IS A SEPARATE AND LARGER CHANGE THAN (1)–(7), AND IT ARRIVED LAST.** Everything
before it is about WHICH UNIT and WHICH PRICE each service carries. Statement (8) is about the SHAPE
of the seeded estate: today it plants one meter per unit for ONE metered service and refuses the rest,
so a utility selling Electric + Water + Sewer receives water and sewer and **no electric line on any
bill at all**. The PO was shown that finding, verified from the code, and ruled it not acceptable.

### CR-062 · 1 · CLASSIFY

**Statements (1)–(7): NEW REQUIREMENT + REVERSAL OF A SIGNED DECISION.** The three-state billing basis
and the per-service units are new; withdrawing solar's four bands reverses a ratified list.

**Statement (8): DEFECT, and it is classified that way deliberately.** The process rule is *"when it
is ambiguous it is a DEFECT, not a change, because filing our misunderstanding as a change quietly
converts our error into the customer's new requirement"*. A utility that sells electric and receives
no electric line is not a feature the PO is now asking us to add — it is a product that does not do
what it says. It is carried inside this CR because the fix is the same body of work, and a defect row
is filed alongside it so the escape reason is recorded where defects are counted.

### CR-062 · 2 · WHAT SIGNED STATEMENT IS BEING REVERSED — quoted, never summarised

**(a) Solar's four size bands.** `apps/tenancy/service_size_classes.py` seeds `SOL-5`, `SOL-5-10`,
`SOL-10-25`, `SOL-25P` as RATIFIED. **They were already superseded and never withdrawn.** The file
says so in its own words, recording the PO's ruling of 2026-08-27 verbatim: *"(a) multiplier replaces
bands for capacity services (solar, battery, thermal); bands stay for pipe/amp/CFH - this si corect"*,
and notes that withdrawing them *"is a piece of work in its own right... Recorded rather than quietly
left: the supersession stands and is owed."* **This CR pays that debt.** Statement (6) is the same
ruling said a second time, with a worked example.

**(b) Storm water's four ERU bands** — `SW-1ERU`, `SW-2-5`, `SW-6-20`, `SW-20P`. These are RATIFIED
and were NOT covered by the 2026-08-27 ruling, which named only solar, battery and thermal. Statement
(5) asks for storm water to carry capacities *"similarly the capacities we have created for Trash
cart"*. **This is a genuine reversal of a signed list and is flagged as such**: bands pick a rate,
capacities multiply. The PO was shown the change explicitly and told they could decline it.

**(c) `BR-RAT-081` — "a service is metered or unmetered".** Two states become three. The column and
its migration are already in flight on the branch.

**(d) `_NOT_THE_BACKBONE` — one metered service per seeded estate.** Withdrawn by statement (8).

**(e) ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figures: NONE ARE TOUCHED, AND THIS WAS CHECKED BEFORE THE CR WAS WRITTEN.**
`GT-17`'s reference bill is asserted as **per-line** figures — water usage basis **$39.50**, sewer
**$15.80** on unit 0 consuming 8 kgal — not as a bill total. Adding an electric line to that same bill
ADDS a line and moves neither figure. Sewer is 40% of the water charge, so it is unaffected too. **No
finance re-sign is owed by this CR.** If any task below is found to move a frozen figure, that task
STOPS and goes to HUMAN-GUIDE §6.

#### A · Settings and reference data

| # | Task | Notes |
|---|---|---|

**A1–A6 ARE DONE (2026-09-02, CR-062 group A lane), and the two reversals are recorded as reversals.**

* **A1 · ten solar panel types** `SOL-P1`–`SOL-P10`, 1 kW to 10 kW. **A2 · six battery types** `BAT-5`–`BAT-30`. **A3 · five storm water sizes** `SW-SF` 1 ERU · `SW-DUP` 2 · `SW-COM-S` 4 · `SW-APT` 6 · `SW-COM-L` 10.
* **A4 · solar's four inverter bands are WITHDRAWN**, paying the supersession debt the file had recorded in its own words since 2026-08-27. **A5 · battery gains a CATALOGUE and `OQ-561` stays dissolved** — none of the six states a price boundary, which is what that question asked about.
* **A6 · every size class now carries its capacity as a number with its unit.** `SizeClass(code, name, capacity, capacity_uom)`; a BAND carries `None` (never `0`, which would sum silently) and a CAPACITY carries a `Decimal` quantised to 4 decimal places, never a float. Three invariants are checked at import: a number never travels without its unit, one service is all bands or all capacities, and one service sums in exactly one unit. **Trash stays a COUNT and `total_capacity('trash', …)` REFUSES** — its carts are gallons and its dumpsters are cubic yards, so the sum does not exist in any unit.
* **The count: 40 − 8 withdrawn + 21 added = 53.** No migration is owed: the capacity is ratified law in `service_size_classes.py`, not a column, and the fixture's `{code, name}` delivery shape is unchanged.
* **Proof.** 26 new cases, every one shown RED on the previous code first. Golden unmoved — **33 document self-consistency checks, and 14 of the 61 signed GTs engine-verified**. `GT-15`'s **$40.00** solar and **$24.00** battery still price through the whole chain. **No ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure moved.**
* ⚠ **TWO THINGS ARE HANDED ON RATHER THAN DONE, both because the file belongs to another lane.** **(i) The fixture mirror** `apps/tenancy/fixtures/lookup_defaults.json` still holds the old 40 rows and needs its BR-TEN-077 version bump and digest; the group B lane holds that file and was messaged rather than edited. Three assertions are RED until it lands and all three go green together — that is the drift guard doing its job. **(ii) `DEF-3098`** — `configured_sizes_for` infers *"is this service banded"* from *"does it have rows"*, which a capacity service breaks, so a battery schedule with no per-size rows now prices **nothing at all** (`{}` where it was `{'': 8.00}`). One line in rating fixes it: `capacity_uom_for_service(service) is None` **is** what *banded* means.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

the whole plant.** The first row is exactly what the PO's `electric + water +

⚠ **THE ABSOLUTE SECONDS ARE NOT A BENCHMARK AND MUST NOT BE QUOTED AS ONE.**

figures are inflated; the RATIO is what the pair is for, and it is roughly what
the readings do (194 → 387). Nothing about the run changed — `gather` builds one
tariff per plan service row and always has — so this is the cost of billing more

measurement, not a guarantee (hard-won law 1).
| H12 | **No frozen figure moves.** `GT-17` water **$39.50** and sewer **$15.80** are per-line, so extra lines on the same bill leave them alone — verified before this CR was written | if any task moves one, that task STOPS and goes to a finance re-sign (HUMAN-GUIDE §6) |

**Worked, end to end, on the PO's own example.** A house on a tenant selling Electric + Water + Sewer
+ Solar, after this CR:

| Line | Quantity | Rate | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| Water base | 1 month | | $8.00 |
| Water usage | 8 kgal | tiered | $31.50 |
| Sewer | 40% of water | | $15.80 |
| Electric base | 1 month | | $12.00 |
| Electric usage | 800 kWh | tiered | $95.50 |
| **Solar** | **14 kW** (2 + 4 + 8) | **$14.00 / kW** | **$196.00** |
| **Total** | | | **$358.80** |

Today the same house bills **$55.30** — water and sewer only, with electric and solar absent.

### CR-062 · 6b · IS THE SEED DYNAMIC? YES — AND HERE IS EXACTLY HOW

The PO asked directly: *"based on services selected at the time of tenant creation you will
dynamically load the data - is that correct?"* **Confirmed, and the mechanism already exists — this CR
makes it correct for all ten services rather than for three.**

Every seeding block already intersects what it plants with the tenant's enabled services: the estate
plan is resolved from the enabled set, the unit's service offer is intersected with it, and blocks
whose service is off are skipped with a stated reason rather than failing. What is broken today is not
the mechanism but its inputs — three services are missing from the map, four carry a unit that cannot
bill, and a second metered service is refused.

| Service ticked at signup | What that tenant receives after this CR |
|---|---|
| Electric | 48 electric meters, 4 readings each, tiered schedule, $12.00 base |
| Water | 48 water meters, 4 readings each, tiered schedule, $8.00 base |
| Gas | 48 gas meters reading **ccf**, $6.00 base + $1.15/ccf |
| Thermal / heat | 48 meters reading ton-hr, $0.045/ton-hr |
| Sewer | a connection per unit, priced at 40% of water — **and refused with a stated reason if water is not also sold** |
| Trash | 4 carts across 3 units, $15.00 per cart |
| Storm water | 48 connections sized from the property, $4.50 per ERU |
| Solar | panels on 2 units, $14.00 per kW of installed capacity |
| Broadband | 3 lines, $0.10 per Mbps |
| Battery | 2 batteries, $3.00 per kW |
| **A service NOT ticked** | **nothing is planted, no rate is seeded, and no bill line appears** |

**Three rules govern the dynamic behaviour, and all three are kept:**

1. **Nothing is seeded for a service the tenant did not enable.** Not a meter, not a rate, not a
   `$0.00` line.
2. **A service that cannot be shaped says WHY, in a sentence a person can act on** — sewer without
   water is the standing example, and it is correct rather than a fault.
3. **Re-running the seed re-scopes nothing already written.** The seeders are insert-missing; a
   tenant-touched row is never overwritten.

**What changes with this CR is rule 1's coverage:** today a tenant ticking Electric + Water gets
electric silently dropped, which breaks rule 2 as well — nothing is planted AND nothing says why.

### CR-062 · 8 · ROLLBACK, STATED BEFORE SHIPPING

The seed is **data, not migration-destructive**: `_seed_uoms` and the size-class seeders are
insert-missing only and never overwrite a tenant-touched row, so a tenant provisioned before this CR
keeps every row it has. Rolling back is therefore: revert the commits, and any tenant provisioned in
between keeps its rows and can be re-seeded or deleted. The PO has already ruled that beta data is
disposable — *"I will delete the DB and relaunch"*.

**The one thing that is NOT rollback-safe is the `billing_basis` column** (B2/B3), because it drops
`metered`. Its reverse migration must restore `metered` from the basis — `metered` where the basis is
`metered`, `False` otherwise — and that reverse must be tested, not assumed.

**Status: OPEN — execution dispatched 2026-09-02.**

flaw was at FOUR sites**, and the fourth is the one that matters: **`G47`, the merge-blocking gate
whose entire job is "the platform catalogue and every enumeration of it agree", reported PASS at
TEN while the catalogue held eleven.** Widening it then found three more incomplete lists nobody
had looked at. **`DEF-3091`** — the four hand-written front-end lists. **`DEF-3093`** — the
mixed-size engine gap above. **`DEF-3089`** — `test_br_ten_170_tc6` had been red at the tip since
`CR-062`; a sibling landed the fix and it is closed against their commit.

**ROLLBACK is as §8 states and is unchanged.** The point of no return is the customer's FIRST
ISSUED FIRE BILL, not the merge. **Say that to them before they issue one.**

**Status: EXECUTED IN PART, 2026-09-02** — groups A, B, D and E landed; C1 and C4 landed; C2, C3
and C5 are named above with the reason each is not done. `OQ-1360` (the customer's real sizes and
prices) is OPEN and non-blocking; `DEF-3093` holds the mixed-size engine gap.

says the same thing from the fixture's side, and it is why every fixture bump in this repo moves a

#### CR-063 · D1 — MEASURED, AND THE RECORD ABOVE WAS WRONG UNTIL IT WAS (`DEF-3087`)

⚠ **THIS SECTION OPENS BY SAYING *"A UTILITY CAN NOW TICK FIRE AT SIGNUP, AND A FIRE LINE REACHES
A BILL."* THE FIRST HALF WAS TRUE. THE SECOND HALF WAS A CLAIM, IT WAS WRITTEN BEFORE ANY TENANT
HAD BEEN PROVISIONED, AND WHEN ONE FINALLY WAS THE ANSWER WAS ZERO.** It is left standing above
because that is the record of what was asserted, and this is hard-won law 1 — *a comment claiming a
guarantee is not the guarantee* — caught inside the very change request that quotes it.

**WHAT THE MEASUREMENT SAID.** A fire-only utility provisioned through the real signup service on
PostgreSQL 16: **0 premises, 0 units, 0 accounts, 0 issued bills, and 14 of 17 seeding blocks
failed.** The first refusal named it exactly — `rating/seed_sample_records: KeyError: 'fire'`. The
all-eleven tenant produced **0 bills** as well, so adding fire had taken the everything-utility
down with it.

**THE CAUSE WAS ONE MISSING LINE AND IT IS `CR-063`'S OWN.** `fire` joined
`core/sample_fixture.CAPACITY_ESTATE_SERVICES` and **not**
`apps/rating/sample_data.CAPACITY_BASE_CODE`, which is a bare `dict[service]` subscript in a
different module. `BR-RAT-088` puts the base amount on the CHARGE CODE, so with no code the seeded
plan could not be activated and every seat refused
`customers.account.plan_required_at_activation`.

`G13`, `G47`, `G31`, both i18n gates and **16 of 16 cases in `test_cr063_fire_service.py`** were
green — because not one of them PROVISIONS A TENANT. It is visible only by running the real signup
service and COUNTING, which is the measurement `DEF-2414` put in this repo after trash shipped
exactly this way.

⚠ **AND A SIBLING'S GREEN POSTGRESQL RUN NEARLY BECAME THIS LANE'S PROOF.** A commit landed in the
same hours reporting the coverage scoreboard *"green on PostgreSQL, 15 tenants, all seven cases
passed"* — and its 36-minute run had STARTED BEFORE `fire` existed, so it measured a catalogue
without the failing service and reported green for it. Reading somebody else's green as your own
evidence is the same law one layer out: **the run has to be the one that contains your change.**

**THE FIX, BOTH HALVES.** `fire` gains `BASE-FIRE`; and the bare subscript becomes a **named
refusal** that says which map, which file, and that the tenant will issue no bills — because a
`KeyError` naming a service code says WHAT was missing and nothing about why it mattered, and the
TWELFTH service will meet this same gap between two lists that grow independently.

**THE FAST DOOR, added because the slow one is now unaffordable.**
`06-backend/tests/test_cr063_fire_live_pg.py` provisions a fire-only tenant and counts — **2
minutes 37 seconds**, against the scoreboard's 36 — and it was shown RED on this exact defect
before the fix. The scoreboard row `svc-fire` with `bills_for=("fire",)` remains the permanent
record; this is the door a lane touching fire can afford to open.

### CR-062 · ADDENDUM 1 — four gaps the nine worked examples exposed (2026-09-02)

Nine utilities were drawn end to end from this seed — one house on water and sewer, a four-service
house, a no-water utility, two master-account shapes, a commercial property, a government property,
an industrial property, and a utility whose service could not be built. **Drawing them from real
figures is what surfaced these; none was visible from the task list.** Task groups F1–F8 are
unchanged; these are additions.

#### J1 · Thermal's demo usage is a hundredfold too small, and pricing it is what exposed that

`CONSUMPTION_SCALE["thermal_heat"]` is **5**, so a seeded thermal customer reads about
**45 ton-hours** a month. At task E6's `$0.045` per ton-hour that bills **$2.02**. A real
chilled-water building uses nearer **4,000 ton-hours**, which at the same rate is **$180.00**.

⚠ **The scale is not wrong; it was correct until this CR.** Its own docstring says the scale
*"prices nothing"* and *"the day `OQ-1290` closes, this scale is part of what has to be ratified with
it — it is flagged, not silently official"*. **Task E6 closes that question for thermal, so the flag
has come due in the same CR that priced it.** Electric (×100 → 900 kWh) and gas (×5 → 45 ccf) were
checked and are realistic; thermal is the only one nobody checked, because nothing priced it.

**Decided, not asked (law 13): raise the usage, not the rate.** `$0.045` per ton-hour is a realistic
price and `$4.50` would not be. A scale of **500** gives 4,500 ton-hours and **$202.50** — the right
order of magnitude for the building this fixture describes.

#### J2 · The Municipal account discount — a sixth discount, and the first enrolment anywhere

**PO ruling 2026-09-02, verbatim:** *"What is the government discount called? Municipal account -
yes; What rate? 20% off the bill before taxes - yes"*.

`apps/rating/discount_sample_data` seeds five discounts — senior 15%, low-income credit, paperless,
autopay and veteran — and **enrols no account in any of them**, deliberately: *"enrolling real
accounts in a subsidy is a money act and the fixture stops at availability"*.

**This ruling changes both halves.** A sixth discount, `MUNICIPAL`, percentage, **20**; and **the
first seeded enrolment this fixture has ever carried**. Worked, and asserted: a government building
on water + sewer + trash at a `$129.70` subtotal pays **`$103.76`**, a saving of **`$25.94`**.

⚠ **The enrolment is the part that needs care.** The reason the fixture never enrolled anyone is a
good one and it is not withdrawn — it is narrowed to this one demonstration account, which must be
obviously a demo (`government` type, fictional identifiers) and must never be a real party.

#### J3 · A government account, because the type exists and nothing uses it

`account_types` has carried **`government`** since the platform catalogue was written. **No seeded
account has ever used it**, so nothing in the product has ever shown what a government customer looks
like, and J2's discount would have nowhere to land. One seeded government account, carrying J2's
enrolment.

#### J4 · An industrial account — and a supersession the PO ruled today

`INDUSTRIAL_ELECTRIC_BASE` is **`$180.00`** and `apps/rating/sample_data` records that **0 accounts
are on `IND`**, which is exactly how `DEF-2823`'s `$168.00` disagreement hid: *"no bill ever carried
either figure"*. One seeded industrial account puts a real bill behind both figures.

⚠ **AND THE PO SUPERSEDED A WRITTEN POSITION IN THIS REPO, WHICH MUST BE RECORDED RATHER THAN
QUIETLY OBEYED.** `core/sample_fixture.py` states that the industrial `$0.085/kWh` *"is half of a
`demand` tariff (`+ $11.00/kW`) and needs a demand read this estate does not take either"*, and that
*"re-reading either as a flat residential rate would be inventing a tariff out of a figure signed for
something else"*.

**PO ruling 2026-09-02, verbatim:** *"for usage line use $0.085/kWh"* — said after being shown that
reasoning and a `$0.00` alternative.

**So the demo charges the rate and does not charge the demand half.** That is the PO's call and it is
lawful; what is owed is that the cost is stated rather than hidden. **Worked: at a 100 kW peak the
unbilled demand half would be `$1,100.00`** on a bill of `$4,751.00`. The fixture's own sentence is
amended to say it is superseded for the demo estate by this ruling, with the date — **not deleted**,
because the reasoning is still true of a real tariff.

#### What is NOT added, and why

* **A capacity-only master account** (a developer paying for solar and battery across a building) is
  drawn in the examples and is **not** seeded. One master account already exists and it is a water
  one; a second would double a shape without proving a new rule.
* **Fire** is `CR-063`, not this CR.

**Status: addendum OPEN — J1-J4 to be scheduled.**

⛔ **THE LINE ABOVE IS SUPERSEDED — 2026-09-02.** It is kept verbatim rather than
edited, because it is the sentence a reader will find quoted in the commits and
defect rows written while it was true, and because the register's own push guard
treats rewriting a line and deleting it as the same event.

**Status: addendum CLOSED — J1, J2, J3 and J4 are all DONE (2026-09-02, the CR-062 addendum lane).**

#### What landed, with the four worked figures

| Task | Done | The figure, on a real seeded tenant |
|---|---|---|
| **J1** | ✅ | `CONSUMPTION_SCALE["thermal_heat"]` **5 → 500**. The reference thermal customer reads **4,500 ton-hours** and bills **`$202.50`** where it billed **`$2.02`**; the `GT-17` reference unit reads 4,000 and bills `$180.00`. **Electric and gas are proved unmoved by name**, in `test_pure_j1_only_thermal_moves`. |
| **J2** | ✅ | A sixth discount `MUNICIPAL`, percentage **20**, taken before taxes, **and the first seeded enrolment this fixture has ever carried**. On an ISSUED June invoice: subtotal **`$129.70`**, a VISIBLE line of **`−$25.94`** carrying the programme's name, payable **`$103.76`**. Exactly one account on the whole tenant is enrolled, and a test says so. |
| **J3** | ✅ | One seeded government customer — **and it carries `municipal`, not `government`** (see below). |
| **J4** | ✅ | One seeded industrial plant on its own plan class, billing **`$180.00`** base + **`$4,590.00`** usage (54,000 kWh × `$0.0850`) = **`$4,770.00`**. The supersession is amended into `core/sample_fixture.py` rather than deleted, with the unbilled demand half stated: **`$1,100.00`** at a 100 kW peak. |

#### Three things this addendum got wrong, found by building it

⚠ **1 · J3 ASKS FOR A `government` ACCOUNT AND THE PRODUCT IS RIGHT TO REFUSE
ONE (`DEF-3283`).** The sentence *"`account_types` has carried `government` since
the platform catalogue was written"* was already **eight days stale** when this
addendum was written: `BR-CUS-094` (PO 2026-08-24) made `government` a LEGACY
code — *"stops being selectable and changes nothing else"* — and the seat was
refused by name on the first seeding run, `VAL-005
customers.account.type_is_legacy`. **The seat is seeded as `municipal`**, which
is one of the seven selectable categories, is the same customer, and is the
Product Owner's own word for it — J2's ruling reads *"What is the government
discount called? Municipal account - yes"*. Reaching through the cutover-import
door, the only writer allowed to store a legacy code, would have put a demo
fixture ahead of a signed rule. **This is step 0 of the build process working**:
nothing automated reads a change request's prose for truth.

⚠ **2 · `$4,751.00` IS NOT REACHABLE AND THE SEED BILLS `$4,770.00`.**
`($4,751.00 − $180.00) ÷ $0.0850` is **53,776.47** kWh, so no whole number of
kilowatt-hours produces the illustrated bill. The seeded draw is a round **54,000
kWh** — a 74% load factor at the 100 kW peak this addendum names — and the bill is
`$19.00` above the illustration. **Nothing the addendum decides moves**: the rate,
the base and the `$1,100.00` of unbilled demand are exactly as ruled.

⚠ **3 · THE ESTATE HAD TO GROW, AND TWO DEFECTS WERE WAITING IN IT.** 44 → 46
premises and 48 → 50 units, both seats APPENDED so no existing `unit_index`, meter
serial, awkward case or ❄️ frozen figure moves. On the way:

* **`DEF-3282` — an account whose consumer category no `is_base` charge code
  covers bills NOTHING AT ALL, silently.** Both new seats landed with a plan, an
  active account, three service points, a meter and four committed reads, sat in
  the run's scope alongside all 50 accounts and **issued 0 invoices** while unit 0
  issued 2. Nothing failed, nothing logged: `BR-BIL-1024` is *"no lines, no
  document"*. The seeded codes named two classes and the platform ratifies seven.
* **`DEF-3285` — every seeded discount is effective 1 August 2026 and this fixture
  bills June and July**, so no seeded discount could ever have appeared on a
  seeded bill. Inert while nothing was enrolled; a full-price bill the moment
  something was.

Also filed: `DEF-3284` (the sub-type tree still hangs three sub-types under the
retired `government` parent and has none under `municipal`), and two rows for reds
that are **pre-existing at the branch tip and not this lane's**, measured in a
detached worktree pinned to it — `DEF-3286` and `DEF-3287`.

#### Proved

**21 of 21 cases pass on PostgreSQL 16 with `--create-db`**
(`06-backend/tests/test_cr062_j_addendum.py`). **Golden, both numbers as
`DEF-2846` requires: document self-consistency 33 checks PASS / 0 FAIL, and
ENGINE-VERIFIED 14 of the 61 signed GTs.** ❄️ unmoved on the same seeded tenant:
`GT-17` water **`$39.50`** and sewer **`$15.80`** on unit 0's issued bill with no
discount line on it, and `GT-15`'s solar **`$40.00`** / battery **`$24.00`**

## CR-062 · CR-063 — THE RECONCILIATION: WHAT THE REGISTER SAYS AND WHAT THE CODE SAYS (2026-09-02)

**A LANE WAS DISPATCHED TO FINISH THESE TWO CHANGE REQUESTS ON THE READING THAT
`CR-062` HAD 70 OF ITS 71 ROWS UNTICKED AND `CR-063` 30 OF 34. THAT READING IS
WRONG, AND THE REASON IT IS WRONG MATTERS MORE THAN THE COUNT.**

**Neither change request has ever used a tick.** Their task tables are
`| # | Task | Notes |` with **no status column at all**, and completion is
recorded underneath in prose — *"A1–A6 ARE DONE (2026-09-02, CR-062 group A
lane)"*, *"C1–C9: DONE, 2026-09-02, commits `70879c9` and after"*. A parser
looking for `- [x]` finds none and reports everything outstanding, which is the
same class of mistake as reading `33/33` as engine proof: **the number was
right about what it measured and wrong about what it was quoted for.**

**So the corrected answer, read from the CODE and not from either register:
of `CR-062`'s 63 numbered task rows plus its four addendum tasks, and
`CR-063`'s 30, THREE are genuinely outstanding and every one of them is
already named in the repository with its reason.** Everything else is built.
What follows is the row-by-row evidence, so the next lane can check the claim
rather than inherit it.

### What was verified, and how

Read from the branch tip and, where it is a figure, measured on real
PostgreSQL 16.13 — never from the register's own prose, which is what step 0 of
the build process warns about in terms (*"nothing automated reads prose for
truth"*).

### The two figures the dispatch quoted, re-measured rather than trusted

Both hold. **Fire's `$12.00` and `$110.00`** are produced by the engine — one
2" line, and one 6" line with two private hydrants on **two lines**, `$60.00`
and `$50.00`, never one blended line. **Storm water's `$4.50` a house, `$27.00`
across the six-flat block and 54 ERU on the estate** are on issued bills.

⚠ **THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE IS TRUE AND IT DOES NOT SAY WHICH HALF OF EACH FIGURE
THIS LANE ACTUALLY RE-MEASURED — CORRECTED HERE THE SAME HOUR, BY ADDITION.**
It is left standing because it is the sentence a reader will find quoted in this
lane's own commits, and because leaving a claim vaguer than its evidence inside a
section about hard-won law 1 is the failure that section exists to describe.

**WHAT WAS RE-DERIVED HERE, from the ratified law rather than from any register:**
`fire_charge({"FL-2": 1})` answers **`$12.00`** and
`fire_charge({"FL-6": 1, "HYD": 2})` answers **`$110.00`** — ⚠ **as measured on 2026-09-02.**
Since the PO removed `HYD` on 2026-09-03 that second call RAISES `KeyError` (*"'HYD' is not a
fire size class"*) and the warehouse bills **`$60.00`**; `fire_charge({"FL-6": 1, "FL-2": 2})`
answers **`$84.00`** and now carries the per-size arithmetic this sentence was demonstrating. And the one decision
that could have priced fire wrongly with nothing going red is mechanical rather
than commented: `capacity_uom_for_service("fire")` answers `None` and
`total_capacity("fire", …)` REFUSES — *"fire is sized by BANDS, so its size
classes cannot be added together"* — so **fire COUNTS like trash and cannot SUM
like solar**. Storm water's five sizes carry their capacities WITH their unit
(1, 2, 6, 4 and 10 **ERU**), the seeded price is **`$4.5000` per ERU**, and the
estate's `36 × 1 + 2 × 2 + 6 + 2 × 4` is **54 ERU** — **`$243.00`** of monthly
assessment, a single house at **`$4.50`**, and the six-flat block at **`$27.00`**
across six units rather than `$27.00` each.

**WHAT WAS NOT RE-DERIVED HERE: the bill run.** That those amounts reach an
ISSUED document is `test_cr063_c3_fire_priced.py` and
`test_cr062_d6_storm_water_on_the_unit.py`, whose records are quoted above and
which this lane did not rebuild. **The half it did re-derive is the arithmetic
those bills are built from, which is the half a stale register could have got
wrong on its own** — and the fire one in particular, because *"capacity"* covers
two different sums in this product and only a mechanical check tells them apart.

⛔ **AND THEN THE SUITE WAS RUN, AND IT CORRECTED THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE — THE
SEEDED ESTATE IS `59` ERU, NOT `54` (`DEF-2368`).** The two paragraphs above
stand exactly as written, because the mistake in them is the subject of this
whole section and hiding it would be worse than making it.

**`36 × 1 + 2 × 2 + 6 + 2 × 4 = 54` is CR-062 D6's OWN ROW TABLE, and this lane
re-derived it from that table rather than from the estate** — so it re-derived
the register, dressed as code, which is precisely the failure the section it sits
in was written to describe. **Measured instead, on the branch:**

| | assessed premises | ERU | assessment at `$4.5000` |
|---|---|---|---|
| the two written constants | **41** | **54** | **`$243.00`** |
| what `storm_water_assessment_plan()` derives | **43** | **59.0000** | **`$265.50`** |

**The cause is not a wrong rule and no ruling is contradicted.** The `CR-062`
addendum appended two seats — **`601 Quarry Hill Ct`** (`SW-SF`, **1 ERU**, unit
48, the municipal building) and **`603 Silver Creek Rd`** (`SW-COM-S`, **4 ERU**,
unit 49, the industrial plant) — which is exactly the `+5 ERU` and `+2 premises`
measured. The PLAN is derived and picked both up; `STORM_WATER_ESTATE_ERU` and
`STORM_WATER_ASSESSED_PREMISES` are written down and did not. A growing estate
assessing more storm water is CORRECT; two statements of one figure disagreeing
is not.

**PROVED PRE-EXISTING, not caused by this lane:** the same disagreement is
present at commit `7d2aaa2f`, before this lane pushed a byte. Three of the
fourteen D6 cases are red on it — `assert 43 == 41`, `assert Decimal('59.0000')
== Decimal('54')`, and a third that is separate and is recorded rather than
diagnosed: **unit 49's `$18.00` of storm water does not reach a bill at all.**

⛔ **THE THIRD RED CASE WAS NOT WHAT THAT SENTENCE SAYS — CORRECTED 2026-09-02
BY THE `DEF-2368` LANE, WHICH MEASURED IT.** The paragraph above stands because
it is the record of what was believed when the defect was filed, and because the
mistake in it is the most useful thing in this section.

**Unit 49's `$18.00` DOES reach a bill**, and it reaches two. On a seven-service
tenant seeded on real PostgreSQL 16.13, `603 Silver Creek Rd` (unit 48 in the
premises tuple, `SCW-U-050`, account `AC-2026-00050`) holds a storm-water service
point, a `4.0000 ERU` assessment characteristic and the invoices
`BL-2607-000050` (June, `$122.41`) and `BL-2608-000100` (July, `$130.29`), each
carrying the line::

    ('storm_water', 'usage', 4.000000, 'ERU', 18.000000)

**What was stale was the TEST'S EXPECTATION.** The verbatim failure is::

    AssertionError: these units do not bill their assessment:
    {49: Decimal('18.000000')}
    assert {49: Decimal('18.000000')} != {49: Decimal('4.50')}

— the case built its per-unit map from the literals `COMMERCIAL_UNIT` and
`COMMERCIAL_UNIT + 1`, which is `{46, 47}`, and the addendum had appended a
**third** `commercial_building`. So the case asserted `$4.50` against a bill that
correctly said `$18.00`.

⚠ **THE LESSON IS THE MISREAD AND NOT THE FIGURE.** A stale expectation and money
missing from an invoice produce the same-shaped diff — a `Decimal` on the left, a
smaller one on the right — and read at a glance the smaller number looks like the
bill. **This register said a real utility's charge was going unbilled and it was
not.** That is the more expensive error of the two: it would have sent a lane
looking for a hole in the billing engine.

**Fixed by deriving rather than by retyping.** The D6 case now builds its
expectation from `storm_water_assessment_plan()` and `BR-TEN-171`'s ratified
ladder, so an appended seat cannot make it stale again; the estate figures it
asserts are **59 ERU · `$265.50` assessed · `$270.00` collected**, and the
month-wide sum is `60` rather than `55` because the restated `CASE_OVERCHARGE`
line is still counted twice. `STORM_WATER_ASSESSED_PREMISES` is now derived from
the plan; `STORM_WATER_ESTATE_ERU` stays a literal because
`core/sample_fixture` may not import the ladder that says what a size code is
worth, and `10-scripts/gates/g73_storm_water_estate.py` compares the two with no
database and no Django. **No ❄️ FROZEN figure moved: `GT-17`'s `$39.50` and
`$15.80` and `GT-15`'s `$40.00` and `$24.00` are all unmoved.** Full reasoning
and worked figures in `12-governance/02-decision-log.md`, 2026-09-02.

⚠ **THE D6 TEST'S OWN DOCSTRING PREDICTED THIS AND IT WORKED — A DAY LATE,
BECAUSE NOBODY RAN IT.** *"The stated constant and the ladder are two independent
statements of one figure, and this is what stops them drifting apart in silence."*
It did stop it. What it could not do is run itself, and the addendum lane's
record — *"no existing `unit_index`, meter serial, awkward case or ❄️ frozen
figure moves"* — was true of every frozen figure and not of these two. **`GT-17`
and `GT-15` are untouched and this changes nothing signed;** what moved is a
demo-fixture total nobody re-measured.

### What this lane changed, and what it did not

**It did not rebuild anything.** Three defects that were open against these two
change requests were closed, two more were found underneath one of them and
filed, and the register gained the table above. **No ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure was
touched:** `GT-17`'s water **$39.50** and sewer **$15.80** and `GT-15`'s solar
**$40.00** and battery **$24.00** are all untouched, and the golden numbers are
unmoved both ways — **33 document self-consistency checks, and 14 of the 61
signed GTs engine-verified**.

⚠ **AND THE LESSON IS ABOUT THE REGISTER AND NOT ABOUT THESE TWO CHANGES.** A
change request whose completion lives only in prose paragraphs can be read as
0% done by anything that is not a careful human, and it was. The table above is
the cheapest fix — a status per row, in one place — and the next change request
should carry a status column from the day it is written rather than earning one
after a lane is sent to rebuild finished work.

## CR-064 — The seeding screen names all seventeen steps, ticks them off as they land, and prints the reason on the step that broke

### CR-064 · 0 · CAPTURE — the requester's words, verbatim, at arrival

**2026-09-02, in the working chat session**, immediately after reporting that a redeployed,
freshly-deleted database still produced no bills and that the bill run refused at step 2:

> *"During tenent creation - when we are at the screen where we seed data in backround job, can you
> show all 17 step - -list down all 17 steps and show 1 by 1 when they finish - if step breaks - then
> show the reason behind it at that step itself , if you skip the step, then show the reason for that
> step also - this will help us to understand why it is breaking down in real time, you ahve to
> provide specific error on the screen itself"*

⚠ **THE LAST CLAUSE IS THE REQUIREMENT, NOT AN EMBELLISHMENT: *"you ahve to provide specific error on
the screen itself"*.** This CR is not satisfied by a progress bar, by a count, or by a link to
Settings. It is satisfied when a named step that did not seed carries **its own server sentence, on
the line for that step**, while the tenant is still being built.

⚠ **AND THE MOTIVE IS DIAGNOSIS, NOT DECORATION: *"this will help us to understand why it is breaking
down in real time"*.** The PO is trying to find out why a tenant they created by hand produces no
bills. Every one of the four production reports on 2026-09-02 has the same shape — the product said a
thing succeeded and the thing had not happened. This screen is the instrument that ends that class of
report, so it is built to be believed: a step reports what the server recorded for that step, or it
reports that nothing is known yet, and it never reports a state it did not read.

---

### CR-064 · 1 · CLASSIFY

**A CHANGE, not a defect.** Nothing built is behaving differently from how it was specified: `CR-017`
(PO 2026-08-19) asked for a screen that says provisioning is happening — *"otherwise they are left hi
and dry"* — and that screen was built and does say so. What is being asked for now is **more
resolution than CR-017 ever specified**: seventeen named steps instead of three rolled-up lines, and a
per-step reason instead of one summary sentence.

The step-2 rule of the change process (*"when it is ambiguous it is a DEFECT"*) was applied and comes
out on the change side, but one part of it is genuinely a defect and is filed as one rather than
folded in silently: **`DEF-3221` — the plant reports which step it is on and the poll endpoint throws
that away.** `run_provisioning_plant` calls `jobs.record_progress(record["id"], done, total,
checkpoint=label)`; `apps/tenancy/selectors.job_poll` serialises `id · kind · status · progress ·
result_link · error` and **not `checkpoint`**. The label has been travelling to the database since
2026-08-19 and no client has ever been able to read it. That is a wire that was left unconnected, which
is hard-won law 2 (*built is not wired*), not a new requirement.

⚠ **BOTH IDS THIS SECTION AND §3 NAME WERE ALREADY TAKEN, AND THEY ARE SUPERSEDED RATHER THAN
REWRITTEN — `DEF-3221` → **`DEF-3280`**, `OQ-1341` → **`OQ-1370`**.** This is `DEF-1787` happening
again. `DEF-3221` was filed by the red-tip lane the same morning (a billing refusal, nothing to do
with this), and `OQ-1341` sits inside `DEF-3200–3219` · `OQ-1340–1349`, another lane's **ACTIVE**
block, which `12-governance/14-id-reservations.md` says in as many words may not be sub-let. Both
allocators were correct and neither could see the other. The build lane opened its own block above
every watermark in that file — `DEF-3280–3299` · `OQ-1370–1379` — and **every `DEF-3221` and
`OQ-1341` printed anywhere in this CR, the A2 row below included, means `DEF-3280` and `OQ-1370`.**
The old numbers are left standing, stamped, rather than edited out: they are what the CR was written
with, and a shared register is amended by supersession, never by rewriting a line another reader may
already have quoted.

### CR-064 · 3 · IMPACT — read from the code on 2026-09-02, not from memory

* **There are exactly seventeen.** `apps/tenancy/sample_data.SAMPLE_MODULES` holds **17**
  `SampleModule` entries, in creation order, each carrying `module`, `seam`, a human label and the
  tables it writes. The PO's number is the code's number. It is a TUPLE in source order, so the list
  can be served before the run starts — which is what *"list down all 17 steps"* requires.
* **The run already reports every block as it lands.** `seed_sample_data(actor, *, progress=…)` calls
  back `(done, total, label)` after **every** block — *"seeded, skipped or failed alike"* — and a
  callback that raises is logged and swallowed so narration can never roll back a seeded block.
* **Each block already records its own reason.** `_record(spec, outcome, reason=…, detail=…,
  error_code=…)` writes an outcome of `seeded` / `skipped` / `failed` with a sentence, into
  `sample_data_runs.blocks[]`. **The reason the PO is asking to see already exists, per step, in the
  database.** Nothing has to be invented — it has to be served and rendered.
* **What is NOT served, and this is the whole gap:** `job_poll` returns `progress {done,total}` and
  drops `checkpoint`; and nothing at all serves the per-block outcome rows while the run is in
  flight. `GET /settings/sample-data` serves them, but it is an S8 Settings route a signing-up
  operator has not reached yet and it reports the run as a whole rather than as it goes.
* **The screen today shows three lines, not seventeen.** `SignupWizard.tsx` composes
  `tenancy.signup.provisioning.step.foundations`, `.reference` and `.sample`, and its failure copy is
  a single sentence — *"Part of it did not load"* — which is precisely the summary that cannot answer
  *"why is it breaking down"*.
* **Ten surfaces checked; four are touched.** API contract (A11 — one endpoint gains fields, one is
  added), the signup screen (S114), the locale catalogues (all thirteen), and the job-poll test suite.
  Untouched: schema (no migration — every fact already stored), money rules, the demo fixture, the
  ledger, the golden tests.
* **Open questions, both directions:** none is answered by this CR and none blocks it. `OQ-843`
  (snapshotting findings case lists) is a different surface. **One is minted:** `OQ-1341` — when the
  operator closes the tab mid-plant and returns, the step list must be rebuildable from
  `sample_data_runs` alone; that read exists, and whether the signup route may serve it to a
  session that has just been handed its tenant is the open half.
* **What is already built and is now partly wrong:** nothing shipped becomes incorrect. The three
  rolled-up lines are replaced, not contradicted — every sentence they showed is a true summary of
  the seventeen lines that replace them.
* **Lanes in flight:** three (`CR-062` addendum J1–J4, `CR-062` D6, `CR-063`). **None touches
  `SignupWizard.tsx`, `job_poll`, or the provisioning locale keys**, so this CR can land beside them.
  It DOES touch `apps/tenancy/selectors.py` and `apps/tenancy/api.py`, which CR-063's lane is also in
  — law 11 applies: pathspec commits, re-derived blobs, and the numstat read as arithmetic.

### CR-064 · 9 · ⚠ AMENDED 2026-09-02 — IT IS EIGHTEEN STEPS, AND EVERY ROW ABOVE THAT SAYS SEVENTEEN IS TRUE OF THE DAY IT WAS WRITTEN AND NOT OF TODAY

**THE ROWS ABOVE ARE NOT EDITED. THIS SECTION IS THE CORRECTION**, because eight of them quote a
figure that was measured, and a number nobody can see change is a number nobody can check.

**WHAT HAPPENED.** `CR-062`'s J2 addendum inserted a block at **position 6** of `SAMPLE_MODULES` —
the Municipal discount, granted once there is an account to grant it to — hours after this CR closed.
`len(SAMPLE_MODULES)` became **18**. Nothing downstream moved with it, and nothing was ever going to
go red about most of it.

**THE THREE THINGS THAT WERE ACTUALLY BROKEN ON A RUNNING PRODUCT, and the second is the one to read:**

1. The screen's own hand-typed list stayed at seventeen, so **the FIRST FRAME — the frame this CR
   exists to draw — showed seventeen rows**, and the eighteenth appeared only once the server
   answered.
2. **No locale catalogue had a label for the new step**, so it rendered the server's English sentence
   **in all eleven catalogues**. Nothing threw: the screen falls back to the server's `label` by
   design, which is the mitigation this CR's own A1 docstring boasts of, and it turns out to be only
   half a mitigation — visible-but-untranslated is better than absent and is not the same as done.
3. `provisioningSteps.test.ts`'s LABEL clause iterated the **hand-typed copy**, so a step missing from
   that copy could never be found to be missing a label. **A check that carries its own copy of the
   thing it polices agrees only with itself** — the argument this CR's task D2 makes, defeated by the
   one clause in the file that did not follow it.

**AND SEVEN CASES WERE SITTING RED ON THE BRANCH**, unreported by three status updates: six backend
(`tc1`, `tc4`, `tc5`, `tc6`, `tc7`, `tc9`) plus the PostgreSQL E1 proof, and one frontend length
assertion. Every one is a typed `17` or a typed POSITION that the insertion moved under.

**THREE CHECKS COULD NOT FAIL AND WERE FOUND ONLY BY FIXING THE REST.** `broke = steps[5]`,
`steps[6:]` and `states.slice(6)` are INDEXES into a list somebody else can insert into. Once the
break moved to seventh, the first asserted the database's own sentence **about the wrong step**, and
the other two silently included the failed row — so a check about *"everything after the break is
Done"* was asserting that **the break was Done**. All three select by key or slice from the break now.

**THE SCREEN'S E1 FIXTURE WAS RE-CAPTURED, NOT EDITED.** Its header promises it is the server's own
bytes, so the honest repair to *"seventeen became eighteen"* is to run the break again on a live
PostgreSQL 16 and keep what comes back: **eighteen steps, the break at position 7**, the database's
own sentence. Only the job id is carried over, and it is never rendered.

**WHAT THE ROWS ABOVE NOW MEAN, one line each:** A1 serves **18** entries · B1 draws **18** from the
first frame · C1 is **23 keys × 11 catalogues**, not 22 · D1 is **10** cases, not 9 (`tc10` is new)
· E1's fixture is the 2026-09-02 **18-step** capture. Nothing else in the table moves.

**AND `DEF-3320` IS CLOSED WITH IT** — the five sentences in `sample_data.py` that said SEVENTEEN,
including *"THE LENGTH IS ALWAYS SEVENTEEN AND THAT IS THE POINT"* one function away from a catalogue
returning eighteen. `tc10` is that defect's own prevention clause: **a spelled-out number from
thirteen upwards, in that module, can only be describing this list**, so the only one allowed is the
word for `len(SAMPLE_MODULES)`. It was RED-proved against the pre-fix source:

    AssertionError: apps/tenancy/sample_data.py states 'SEVENTEEN' at lines [1119, 1608, 1649]
    and 'seventeen' at lines [1597, 1643], but len(SAMPLE_MODULES) is 18

**THE LESSON, AND IT IS THIS CR's OWN LESSON ARRIVING A DAY LATE:** the mitigation written into
`step_catalogue()` — *"the server's label travels as the fallback, which is the one thing that keeps
a newly added step visible on screen"* — is a promise about VISIBILITY and about nothing else. It
does not translate the step, it does not put it in the first frame, and it does not tell anybody the
step arrived. A list assembled in two places needs a check that reads the AUTHORITY, and this CR
built exactly one such check and then wrote its most important clause against the copy.

**Filed and fixed as `DEF-3340`** (the reconciliation lane, 2026-09-02). Two lanes reached the same
finding within the hour and the first to push kept the locale key, the constant and the prose; the

### CR-063 · C3 — **DONE. A FIRE CUSTOMER IS BILLED REAL MONEY** (2026-09-02, the C3/C5 lane)

**THE FIRE LINE READ `$0.00` AND IT NOW READS `$12.00`.** The execution record above
named C3 as not done and said exactly why: *"A fire tenant today gets the same flat
`CAPACITY_UNPRICED` schedule solar, broadband and battery get, so its bill line reads
`n × $0.0000 = $0.00`."* That is closed.

**MEASURED RED FIRST on PostgreSQL 16**, eleven of twelve cases, and the two that matter:

    tc1  AssertionError: assert Decimal('0.000000') == Decimal('12.00')
    tc2  ['base  | fire | fire base charge | None None          | 0.000000',
          'usage | fire | fire usage      | 3.000000 connection | 0.000000']

**GREEN, on an actual bill through the live run:**

| | Quantity | Rate | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fire — Fire line 2" | 1 connection | 12.0000 | **12.00** |

| | Quantity | Rate | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fire — Fire line 6" | 1 connection | 60.0000 | 60.00 |
| Fire — Private hydrant | 2 connection | 25.0000 | 50.00 |
| **Fire, total** | | | **110.00** |

All seven bands are asserted one at a time, so no size is served on another's ladder.

⚠ **`fire`'s ENTRY IN `CAPACITY_UNIT_PRICES` STAYS `"0"` AND THAT IS THE ANSWER TO THE
QUESTION THIS CR LEFT OPEN, NOT AN OVERSIGHT.** That map holds ONE amount per service,
multiplied by a quantity in that service's own unit — `$14.0000` per kW, `$0.1000` per
Mbps. Fire has SEVEN prices and the SIZE picks which one, so a scalar there would price
a 6" line exactly like a 2" one. The prices therefore stay with the SIZES, in
`service_size_classes.FIRE_DEFAULT_PRICES`, where they already were and where the sizes
and their amounts are one unratified statement (`OQ-1360`). **The zero is not dead:**
`BR-RAT-032` requires an every-size ladder beside per-size overrides, and that zero IS
it — what a connection with no fire equipment on it prices on, `BR-MET-108`'s ruled zero.

## CR-065 — A size class belongs to ONE utility service, and the rate screen shows all sixty to everybody

### CR-065 · 0 · CAPTURE — the requester's words, verbatim, at arrival

**2026-09-02, in the working chat session**, with a screenshot of `Plans & Rates` → the **Fire** rate
schedule, minimum-bill step (`RAT-03`), showing *Electric 3φ 400A*, *Electric CT-metered*, *Gas 1,000+
CFH* and *Gas 250 CFH (residential)* interleaved with the seven fire lines:

> *"This is where we are setting rates for fire  you should show only capacity for fire . in Setting a
> capacity needs to tags to utility services ."*

⚠ **TWO SENTENCES, TWO SEPARATE ASKS, AND THE SECOND IS THE FIX FOR THE FIRST.** The first is the
symptom on the rate screen; the second names where the missing fact belongs — **on the size class
itself, in Settings**. Building only the first (filtering by a hard-coded prefix, say) would leave the
tenant unable to say which service a size they add themselves belongs to, which is the half only they
can know.

---

### CR-065 · 1 · CLASSIFY

**A DEFECT in the reference data, and a CHANGE in the reference-data model.** They are one CR because
they are one missing column, and splitting them would leave a fix that cannot be configured.

The defect half is `DEF-2385`, filed separately: a rate schedule for one service offers the size
classes of every other, so a fire schedule prices *Electric CT-metered*.

---

### CR-065 · 2 · WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY SAYS — read on 2026-09-02, not from memory

**THE TAGGING ALREADY EXISTS IN PYTHON AND HAS NEVER REACHED THE DATABASE.** This is the finding, and
it is hard-won law 2 (*built is not wired*) on a reference list rather than on a component.

* `06-backend/apps/tenancy/service_size_classes.py` holds
  `RATIFIED_SERVICE_SIZE_CLASSES: dict[str, tuple[SizeClass, ...]]` — **keyed by service code**,
  covering all eleven services, and it is the ratified content. It knows that `FL-2` is fire's and
  `E-CT` is electric's.
* `06-backend/apps/tenancy/fixtures/lookup_defaults.json` seeds `service_size_classes` as **60 rows of
  `{code, name}` and nothing else.** The service is dropped on the way in.
* `apps/tenancy/services.py:4430` states the consequence in its own docstring: *"/lookups/
  service_size_classes — owner metering. Codes and names only"*.
* `07-frontend/src/features/rating/RateScheduleWizard.tsx:897` therefore asks for the list with **no
  service filter**, because there is nothing to filter on. `ChargeCodeWizard.tsx:424` does the same.
* `apps/rating/models.py:375` — `size_class` is `service_size_classes.code` as **TEXT, not an FK**, so
  nothing at the database level ties a priced size to a service either.

**So the screen is not ignoring a tag; there is no tag.** The knowledge exists in one Python constant
that the seeding path reads for its codes and names and for nothing else.

---

## CR-066 — Every charge code, adjustment reason and discount gets a GL account, because today a fresh tenant cannot issue a bill that carries a fee

### CR-066 · 0 · CAPTURE — the requester's words, verbatim, at arrival

**2026-09-02, in the working chat session.** The report came first, as a screenshot of
S8 → Settings → Accounting → *Charges and fees* on a tenant the PO had just redeployed with a deleted
database, showing the product's own banner:

> *"28 charges have no account to post to (AFTER-HRS, BASE-FIRE, BASE-S, BASE-T, BASE-W). A bill
> carrying one of them cannot be issued until it does."*

Then, in three messages:

> **(1)** *"please map Gl Code for charge codes you can show me on screen before input;"*

> **(2)** *"please map GL codes for adjustment reasons also before input; also ensure discount code map
> here with Gl Code"*

> **(3)** — after the three tables were put to them on screen —
> *"Table 1 — the 28 charge codes - these are all correct - you can apply them as part of Seed data"* ·
> *"Table 2 — the five adjustment reasons - these are all good - please apply these"* ·
> *"Please apply these - Table 3 — discounts."*

⚠ **THE THREE TABLES WERE SHOWN IN PLAIN ENGLISH WITH THE ACCOUNT NAMES AND NUMBERS, AND THE PO
APPROVED EACH ONE SEPARATELY.** That is the review this CR was built on and it is reproduced in §5
exactly as it was put, because a signature covers only what was shown (HUMAN-GUIDE §6 posture).

⚠ **ONE PHRASE IN (3) IS THE SCOPE AND IS EASY TO SKIM: *"as part of Seed data"*.** The fix is NOT to
map 28 rows on one tenant. It is that **every tenant this product creates from now on receives charge
codes that already point at accounts** — otherwise the next utility onboarded hits the identical wall,
and the one being onboarded for Fire hits it this week.

---

### CR-066 · 1 · CLASSIFY

**A DEFECT plus a CHANGE, and they are one CR because they are one seed.**

* The defect is **`DEF-2386`**, filed 2026-09-02 before any fix: a fresh tenant's 28 charge codes point
  at no GL account, and `issue.py`'s fee branch refuses a fee line whose code has no account.
* The change is the **accounts that do not exist yet** — five fee accounts and four revenue-adjustment
  accounts — and the **column `discounts` has never had**.

---

### CR-066 · 2 · WHY THIS STOPS BILLS, READ FROM CODE ON 2026-09-02

`06-backend/apps/billing/issue.py` resolves a line's GL account by the line's KIND:

* a **usage** or **base** line resolves from the SERVICE's designation — the tenant's revenue account
  for water, sewer, trash, fire. It never looks at a charge code.
* a **fee** line resolves `rating.charges.gl_account_id` through rating's published read, and the
  branch's own docstring records what happens when it is null: *"Still refused, by name and never
  guessed: … a code the tenant has not yet pointed at an account"*. The same branch **refused every fee
  line unconditionally until 2026-08-25** and the file records the consequence in one sentence —
  ***"the tenant could issue no bill at all"*** (`DEF-714`).

**THAT ASYMMETRY IS WHY NOBODY SAW THIS.** The sample plant issues **95 invoices** on a brand-new
database with all 28 codes unmapped, because every line it writes is usage or base. Measured on
PostgreSQL 16 on 2026-09-02: two tenants provisioned from empty, 17 of 17 seeding blocks green, 70
premises · 118 units · 70 accounts · **95 issued invoices each** — beside a Settings screen correctly
reporting that 28 codes can post nowhere.

⚠ **AND TWO OF THE SEEDED CODES ARE `recurring`** — `PAPER` (paper bill fee) and `HYDRANT` (hydrant
meter rental). `BR-RAT-117` (PO 2026-08-22, *"ruccuring and Autom apply land on bill"*) puts a
recurring code on the ordinary bill of every tenant that configures one. **So one unmapped recurring
charge refuses every bill in a run**, and the run reports it as a refusal rather than as a
configuration gap.

---

  POSTS, never what it is. `GT-1..61` are untouched.
* **`CR-061`'s ruling of 2026-09-01 — *"no, you cannot file discount under revenue"* — is honoured
  rather than revisited.** `4760 Customer discounts (contra-revenue)` already exists and discount lines
  already resolve to it by designation. What this CR adds is the COLUMN and the row on screen, so a
  tenant can see and override it.
* **`BR-TEN-012`** (a tenant-touched row is never overwritten) is honoured: the backfill fills a NULL
  account and never replaces one a tenant has set.
* **`CR-061` is not pre-empted.** The nine new accounts sit in empty space — `4600`–`4650` and
  `4700`–`4730` — and collide with nothing that carries a posted journal line, so nothing is
  renumbered. `4600`, `4610`, `4630`, `4700`, `4710`, `4720` and `4730` are **the PO's own reference
  chart's numbers**, reproduced verbatim in `CR-061` §5; using them means CR-061's programme finds them
  already in the right place.

## CR-067 — A runtime error becomes reproducible: the permanent audit row keeps a short reference, the technical detail lives beside it and expires

### CR-067 · 0 · CAPTURE — the requester's words, verbatim, at arrival

**2026-09-02, in the working chat session**, from a live deployment's Audit log (S61), in three
messages. The problem first:

> *"we need to add all errors that are happending n this Audit log; many times errors will happen run
> time and it is very difficult to reproduce those error; also when we record these errors in audit log
> then we need to know detials so that we can reproduce it just by procing the details we should able
> to locate and understand what was the error - how you will handle this - please help me to udnerstand
> on screen first"*

Then, after the design was put on screen as a wireframe with a worked example:

> *"I like this - diagnostics - can you show me Wireframe and path for this with example"*

Then, answering the one open question — one screen or two:

> *"Im good with this - You click the row that failed — the drawer you already have, the one behind
> "Expand" — and the diagnostic is a second section inside it. Everything on my wireframe lives there +
> Same screen. No new tab."*

And, separately, on the toolbar control offered alongside the design:

> *"What I would add to the toolbar is a "Errors only" filter, so you can jump straight to the failures
> without scrolling past 800 rows of successful seeding. - Yes this is required"*

⚠ **THAT LAST ONE IS AN INSTRUCTION, NOT AN ACKNOWLEDGEMENT** — *"Yes this is required"*. It is task
**B3** and it is in scope, not a nice-to-have. The figure in it is real: the reporting tenant's own
audit log carries **809 seeded records** and the failure the PO was hunting sat behind all of them.

⚠ **THE THIRD MESSAGE IS A RULING AND IT SETTLES THE SURFACE.** The diagnostic is a **second section
inside the EXISTING S61 detail drawer** (`AuditLogPage.tsx`, `US-AUD-005`, already built on
`ModalShell`). **No new tab, no new route, no second list.** The reasoning was put to the PO and
approved with it: a person arrives by clicking the row that broke; a separate tab would mean finding
the same error twice, and rebuilding the actor/action/date/entity filters to be useful.

⚠ **AND THE MOTIVE IS THE ACCEPTANCE TEST, NOT A FEELING:** *"we should able to locate and understand
what was the error"*. §5 states it as a testable bar.

---

### CR-067 · 1 · CLASSIFY

**A CHANGE.** Nothing built is behaving against its specification; a capability that was never
specified is being added. Two defects already filed sit underneath it and are NOT folded in:
`DEF-2379` (the storage boot check — the same failure, prevented one layer earlier) and the audit-log
copy work now in flight.

---

### CR-067 · 2 · WHAT SIGNED STATEMENT IS BEING REVERSED

**None — and one is being honoured that would otherwise be broken by the obvious implementation.**

**`BR-AUD-002` — the audit log has no write verbs; nothing edits or removes a row.** That is what makes
it worth trusting, and it is precisely why **raw error text may not go into it**. A runtime message
routinely carries an account number, a balance or a meter reading, and `audit_log` has no delete: once
in, it is in for the retention life of the row. `apps/tenancy/sample_errors.audit_safe_sentence(code)`
already encodes this — *"It takes ONLY the code… a function that accepted the seeder's own message
could be handed one containing an account number… The signature is the guarantee."*

**So the split in §3 is not a design preference. It is the only shape that satisfies both the PO's ask
and `BR-AUD-002`,** and any implementation that writes an exception message into `audit_log` has
broken a signed rule rather than delivered this CR.

No ❄️ FROZEN B4/B5 figure is touched. No price, quantity or posting moves — this CR records what
happened and never computes.

---

### CR-067 · 3 · THE SHAPE, AS APPROVED

| | **The audit row** | **The diagnostic record** |
|---|---|---|
| Lifetime | permanent — never edited, never deleted | expires on its own schedule (**90 days** proposed) |
| Holds | what was attempted · who · when · a stable error code · **the reference** | the error and where in the code · the request's **field NAMES** · tenant · release · the settings in force · the job that was running |
| Never holds | anything private, because it cannot be removed | a field VALUE, an account number, a balance, a reading, a credential |
| Where it renders | the S61 list row | **a second section in the same row's drawer**, System Admin only |

**The two are joined by the short reference** — `5f2b9c1d3e…` → **`5F2B-9C1D`**, the first eight hex
characters of the trace id, uppercased and grouped. `07-frontend/src/api/client.ts` already forms it
(line ~143) and it is already searchable by prefix. **The reference exists so a person can leave the
screen with it** — read it down a phone, paste it into a message. Inside the audit log nobody needs it,
because both halves are in one drawer.

---

### CR-067 · 5 · THE ACCEPTANCE TEST, AND IT IS THE PO'S OWN SENTENCE MADE TESTABLE

*"we should able to locate and understand what was the error"*.

> **Could somebody holding ONLY the diagnostic record write a failing test?**

Worked against the real failure of 2026-09-02 — a tenant that stopped at step 8 on unset document
storage. Read off the record and nothing else:

```
settings.DOCUMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND          = "aws_s3"
settings.DOCUMENT_STORAGE_BUCKET           = ""
settings.DOCUMENT_STORAGE_ALLOW_FILESYSTEM = False

with pytest.raises(StorageNotConfigured):
    document_storage.backend()
```

Six lines, no second conversation with the reporter. **A record that cannot produce a test like this is
a note, not a diagnostic**, and this bar is what every task below is measured against.

## CR-068 — The customer self-service portal: fifty-six specifications, seventy-five screens, five releases, and the one thing this product cannot do at all

**➜ THE TEXT OF THIS CR LIVES IN ITS OWN FILE:
[`12-governance/change-requests/CR-068-customer-portal.md`](change-requests/CR-068-customer-portal.md)** — 815 lines.

**It was written in this file on 2026-09-03 and moved out the same day**, under the PO ruling that
opens this page: *"one file per CR from here."* Its content is byte-for-byte what was here; nothing
was rewritten in the move, and the move was verified by comparing both copies before a single line
was deleted.

**What is in it, so this row answers the obvious question without opening it:** 56 specifications
(`CP-01`–`CP-56`), 75 screens (`CWP-001`–`CWP-075`), 50 inherited rules (`PR-01`–`PR-50`), 9 open
questions, and **five phases, each of which ends with something a utility can put in front of its
customers.** It claims `CS-1`, `CS-3` and `CS-9` from `CR-059`'s v2 scope — that supersession is
stated in its §2 and is not applied until its phase 5.

**Status: written, not started.** Every one of its 56 specifications reads `UNVERIFIED` on purpose,
and several are expected to come back already built.

## `CR-126-BRC07` — New Connect built to its drawing: the wizard corrected, and the record page that does not exist

**Raised** 2026-09-21 by the Product Owner. **File:**
`12-governance/change-requests/CR-126-BRC07-new-connect-built-to-the-drawing.md`.
**Version** `2.321.0`. Block `CR-125`–`CR-129`, suffix `BRC07`; `CR-127`–`CR-129` remain free.

**One CHANGE and a defect set in one container.** The change is the PO's ruling that **an
application is provenance and never a dependency** — *"we should not make it dependent on
applciation #"* — which reverses shipped code: today the wizard always sends the
application reference empty, the server's first pricing test asks for one, and **zero of
nine connections have a quote total.**

**The rest is defect repair against the blueprint**, built from **pages rendered as
images** on the PO's explicit instruction — *"using images of drawing not text; use UI
genration skills"*. Five wizard corrections (documents on step 1, the tenant's own service
list on step 4, the picked address's premise on step 2, build-owned pricing on step 6,
*activate* not *energise* on step 8) and **a build record page that does not exist at all**
— six tabs, five tiles, 25 rows across four Overview sections, and three header buttons
confirmed off the drawing: `Edit details`, `Add a work order`, `Activate units`, the third
drawn greyed.

**Status: seven lanes dispatched 2026-09-21**, each in its own `git worktree` from
`fd4a66fa4`, each owning its own files.
